sources.applicability: The Anchor already satisfies the fingerprint half (radius-two 2048-bin integer Morgan counts with the generalized dot-product Tanimoto kernel), which is why that element is adopted as a confirmation and not as a change. The prior-width diagnosis is the published statement of this lineage's own measured defect (standardized error 40.72 near the archive against 6.69 far on the Anchor's own picks), and the proposals-per-selection diagnosis maps onto the inherited pool_multiplier 16 (160 candidates per announced batch of ten, so sixteen per selection). Their marginal-likelihood fitting, batch size one and 10,000-evaluation budget are not transferable: the profile epoch freezes announced batches of ten and 300 observations per task, and this lineage fits no kernel hyperparameters at all.
sources.finding: Tripp and Hernandez-Lobato (ICML 2024 AI for Science workshop) diagnose three defects in the PMO GP-BO baseline and report that fixing them makes a basic GP BO the strongest entry they measure (sum of AUC Top-10 over 23 tasks 16.303 against Genetic GFN 16.213, MolGA 14.708, REINVENT 14.196): the prior signal variance fitted by marginal likelihood on poor starting data is too small and is replaced by a declared outputscale of 1.0 for objectives in [0,1]; binary Morgan fingerprints over-smooth the Tanimoto kernel and are replaced by count fingerprints; and the acquisition was maximized over only about six proposals per selection, raised to about one thousand with batch size one. Their acquisition stays UCB with beta drawn log-uniformly from [0.01, 1]. They describe it as a pilot without ablations, so the three fixes are not separated.
sources.title: Diagnosing and fixing common problems in Bayesian optimization for molecule design

sources.applicability: Supplies the exact closed form this position needs over an existing Gaussian posterior: EI(x) = (mu - y*) Phi(z) + sigma phi(z) with z = (mu - y*) / sigma, computed from the predictive mean and standard deviation the Anchor already produces for every one of its 160 pool members, with y* the session's own best accepted score. It introduces no model, no new dependency and no fitting step, and it prices the magnitude of the improvement a purchase could deliver instead of letting one sampled tail realization win a position.
sources.finding: Frazier (2018) states the expected-improvement criterion and its decision-theoretic derivation, and derives it as the expectation of the improvement over the best value observed so far, with the noisy generalization justified by the same argument rather than by an ad hoc correction. The tutorial presents expected improvement, entropy search and knowledge gradient as the three standard acquisition families.
sources.title: A Tutorial on Bayesian Optimization

sources.applicability: The Anchor selects ten candidates per announced batch, so a single-point criterion needs a batch rule. Kriging Believer is the one that keeps the inherited cross-candidate correlation live and load-bearing: the pool covariance and its Cholesky factor already exist in the Anchor, so conditioning the remaining pool on each pick's predictive mean reuses them exactly. It is adopted only as the batch-construction rule; the paper's Branin-Hoo experiments and its continuous design space transfer nothing to a molecular pool.
sources.finding: Ginsbourger, Le Riche and Carraro (2010, Computational Intelligence in Expensive Optimization Problems, pp. 131-162) show that the exact q-point expected improvement is analytic only for q = 2 and expensive beyond it, and propose two nearly optimal sequential heuristics for building a batch of q points: Kriging Believer, which imputes the model's own predictive value as a fictitious observation at each point already placed in the batch, and Constant Liar, which imputes a fixed value instead.
sources.title: Kriging is well-suited to parallelize optimization (q-EI, Kriging Believer and Constant Liar)

sources.applicability: Gives the principle for the one declared change in position 2: correct the dispersion of an existing predictive distribution from the model's own recorded prediction-outcome pairs instead of changing the model. The adaptation is severe and is pre-registered as such: there is no held-out calibration set at 300 chronological accepted observations, so the correction is a single bounded robust scale computed from the session's own accepted one-step-ahead standardized residuals, and no distributional guarantee is claimed.
sources.finding: Kuleshov, Fenner and Ermon (ICML 2018) recalibrate a probabilistic regressor post hoc, by a procedure inspired by Platt scaling, and report that it is guaranteed to produce calibrated uncertainty estimates given enough data while consistently producing well-calibrated credible intervals for Bayesian linear regression and for feedforward and recurrent networks.
sources.title: Accurate Uncertainties for Deep Learning Using Calibrated Regression

sources.applicability: Deferred, not scheduled. The Anchor's pool of 160 with an explicit cross-candidate covariance is exactly the finite correlated-belief setting this policy is defined on, so it is implementable here. It is deferred because the benchmark endpoint is the final Top-1 value of molecules actually evaluated, which makes improvement over the incumbent the matched criterion this round; a decision-value criterion is the right second construction only once an improvement-priced rule has been measured on this Parent.
sources.finding: Frazier, Powell and Dayanik (INFORMS Journal on Computing 21(4):599-613, 2009) give a value-of-information policy for a finite set of alternatives under a correlated multivariate normal prior, computable exactly for the correlated case, provably optimal in special cases and with bounded suboptimality otherwise; correlation lets one measurement inform many alternatives, which is what makes the policy efficient on large alternative sets.
sources.title: The Knowledge-Gradient Policy for Correlated Normal Beliefs

sources.applicability: Deferred. It is the principled version of position 2's correction and the named successor if a single session-level scale proves too coarse, but it needs a calibration split of the session archive and a per-candidate interval construction, which is a second construction on top of an untested one; the campaign's own rule is one declared change per position.
sources.finding: Stanton, Maddox and Wilson (AISTATS 2023) note that acquisition values are unreliable under model misspecification or covariate shift, and use conformal prediction, which retains coverage guarantees for a misspecified model, to steer queries toward regions where the predictions are reliably valid; they report improved query coverage without loss of sample efficiency on black-box optimization and tabular ranking tasks.
sources.title: Bayesian Optimization with Conformal Prediction Sets

sources.applicability: Context and boundary only. It establishes that a GP over fingerprints with a genetic acquisition optimizer is a competitive architecture class, which is the class this lineage already occupies, and that the published strong configuration uses an optimistic bound rather than a sampled draw or an improvement criterion. No reported number is campaign evidence: the budget is 10,000 against 300 here, the task sets differ and the scoring is AUC Top-10 rather than final Top-1.
sources.finding: Gao, Fu, Sun and Coley (NeurIPS 2022) benchmark 25 molecular design algorithms on 23 single-objective tasks under a 10,000-call oracle budget and report that most recent methods fail to beat their predecessors once sample efficiency is scored; their GP BO entry pairs a Tanimoto-kernel GP with a Graph GA acquisition optimizer and a UCB acquisition with a randomly drawn beta.
sources.title: Sample Efficiency Matters: A Benchmark for Practical Molecular Optimization

sources.applicability: Examined and declined for this round, which is itself a useful boundary: the risk RAHBO prices is aleatoric, the variance of repeated noisy outcomes at the same input. The five frozen objectives here are deterministic functions of the molecule - the Anchor records 0 invalid and 0 duplicate attempts and identical scores on repeated identities - so there is no outcome risk to price, and the downside this campaign measured (a widened interval winning a position with a low posterior mean) is epistemic. A mean-variance penalty on epistemic variance is posterior-mean-greedy allocation, which this lineage already measured at -0.116317.
sources.finding: Makarova, Usmanova, Bogunovic and Krause (NeurIPS 2021) optimize a mean-variance objective rather than the expectation alone, modelling both the mean and the input-dependent observation variance and proposing a risk-aware acquisition with sublinear regret guarantees and a robust reporting rule.
sources.title: Risk-averse Heteroscedastic Bayesian Optimization

sources.applicability: The Anchor already satisfies the fingerprint half (radius-two 2048-bin integer Morgan counts with the generalized dot-product Tanimoto kernel), which is why that element is adopted as a confirmation and not as a change. The prior-width diagnosis is the published statement of this lineage's own measured defect (standardized error 40.72 near the archive against 6.69 far on the Anchor's own picks), and the proposals-per-selection diagnosis maps onto the inherited pool_multiplier 16 (160 candidates per announced batch of ten, so sixteen per selection). Their marginal-likelihood fitting, batch size one and 10,000-evaluation budget are not transferable: the profile epoch freezes announced batches of ten and 300 observations per task, and this lineage fits no kernel hyperparameters at all.
sources.finding: Tripp and Hernandez-Lobato (ICML 2024 AI for Science workshop) diagnose three defects in the PMO GP-BO baseline and report that fixing them makes a basic GP BO the strongest entry they measure (sum of AUC Top-10 over 23 tasks 16.303 against Genetic GFN 16.213, MolGA 14.708, REINVENT 14.196): the prior signal variance fitted by marginal likelihood on poor starting data is too small and is replaced by a declared outputscale of 1.0 for objectives in [0,1]; binary Morgan fingerprints over-smooth the Tanimoto kernel and are replaced by count fingerprints; and the acquisition was maximized over only about six proposals per selection, raised to about one thousand with batch size one. Their acquisition stays UCB with beta drawn log-uniformly from [0.01, 1]. They describe it as a pilot without ablations, so the three fixes are not separated.
sources.title: Diagnosing and fixing common problems in Bayesian optimization for molecule design

sources.applicability: Supplies the exact closed form this position needs over an existing Gaussian posterior: EI(x) = (mu - y*) Phi(z) + sigma phi(z) with z = (mu - y*) / sigma, computed from the predictive mean and standard deviation the Anchor already produces for every one of its 160 pool members, with y* the session's own best accepted score. It introduces no model, no new dependency and no fitting step, and it prices the magnitude of the improvement a purchase could deliver instead of letting one sampled tail realization win a position.
sources.finding: Frazier (2018) states the expected-improvement criterion and its decision-theoretic derivation, and derives it as the expectation of the improvement over the best value observed so far, with the noisy generalization justified by the same argument rather than by an ad hoc correction. The tutorial presents expected improvement, entropy search and knowledge gradient as the three standard acquisition families.
sources.title: A Tutorial on Bayesian Optimization

sources.applicability: The Anchor selects ten candidates per announced batch, so a single-point criterion needs a batch rule. Kriging Believer is the one that keeps the inherited cross-candidate correlation live and load-bearing: the pool covariance and its Cholesky factor already exist in the Anchor, so conditioning the remaining pool on each pick's predictive mean reuses them exactly. It is adopted only as the batch-construction rule; the paper's Branin-Hoo experiments and its continuous design space transfer nothing to a molecular pool.
sources.finding: Ginsbourger, Le Riche and Carraro (2010, Computational Intelligence in Expensive Optimization Problems, pp. 131-162) show that the exact q-point expected improvement is analytic only for q = 2 and expensive beyond it, and propose two nearly optimal sequential heuristics for building a batch of q points: Kriging Believer, which imputes the model's own predictive value as a fictitious observation at each point already placed in the batch, and Constant Liar, which imputes a fixed value instead.
sources.title: Kriging is well-suited to parallelize optimization (q-EI, Kriging Believer and Constant Liar)

sources.applicability: Gives the principle for the one declared change in position 2: correct the dispersion of an existing predictive distribution from the model's own recorded prediction-outcome pairs instead of changing the model. The adaptation is severe and is pre-registered as such: there is no held-out calibration set at 300 chronological accepted observations, so the correction is a single bounded robust scale computed from the session's own accepted one-step-ahead standardized residuals, and no distributional guarantee is claimed.
sources.finding: Kuleshov, Fenner and Ermon (ICML 2018) recalibrate a probabilistic regressor post hoc, by a procedure inspired by Platt scaling, and report that it is guaranteed to produce calibrated uncertainty estimates given enough data while consistently producing well-calibrated credible intervals for Bayesian linear regression and for feedforward and recurrent networks.
sources.title: Accurate Uncertainties for Deep Learning Using Calibrated Regression

sources.applicability: Deferred, not scheduled. The Anchor's pool of 160 with an explicit cross-candidate covariance is exactly the finite correlated-belief setting this policy is defined on, so it is implementable here. It is deferred because the benchmark endpoint is the final Top-1 value of molecules actually evaluated, which makes improvement over the incumbent the matched criterion this round; a decision-value criterion is the right second construction only once an improvement-priced rule has been measured on this Parent.
sources.finding: Frazier, Powell and Dayanik (INFORMS Journal on Computing 21(4):599-613, 2009) give a value-of-information policy for a finite set of alternatives under a correlated multivariate normal prior, computable exactly for the correlated case, provably optimal in special cases and with bounded suboptimality otherwise; correlation lets one measurement inform many alternatives, which is what makes the policy efficient on large alternative sets.
sources.title: The Knowledge-Gradient Policy for Correlated Normal Beliefs

sources.applicability: Deferred. It is the principled version of position 2's correction and the named successor if a single session-level scale proves too coarse, but it needs a calibration split of the session archive and a per-candidate interval construction, which is a second construction on top of an untested one; the campaign's own rule is one declared change per position.
sources.finding: Stanton, Maddox and Wilson (AISTATS 2023) note that acquisition values are unreliable under model misspecification or covariate shift, and use conformal prediction, which retains coverage guarantees for a misspecified model, to steer queries toward regions where the predictions are reliably valid; they report improved query coverage without loss of sample efficiency on black-box optimization and tabular ranking tasks.
sources.title: Bayesian Optimization with Conformal Prediction Sets

sources.applicability: Context and boundary only. It establishes that a GP over fingerprints with a genetic acquisition optimizer is a competitive architecture class, which is the class this lineage already occupies, and that the published strong configuration uses an optimistic bound rather than a sampled draw or an improvement criterion. No reported number is campaign evidence: the budget is 10,000 against 300 here, the task sets differ and the scoring is AUC Top-10 rather than final Top-1.
sources.finding: Gao, Fu, Sun and Coley (NeurIPS 2022) benchmark 25 molecular design algorithms on 23 single-objective tasks under a 10,000-call oracle budget and report that most recent methods fail to beat their predecessors once sample efficiency is scored; their GP BO entry pairs a Tanimoto-kernel GP with a Graph GA acquisition optimizer and a UCB acquisition with a randomly drawn beta.
sources.title: Sample Efficiency Matters: A Benchmark for Practical Molecular Optimization

sources.applicability: Examined and declined for this round, which is itself a useful boundary: the risk RAHBO prices is aleatoric, the variance of repeated noisy outcomes at the same input. The five frozen objectives here are deterministic functions of the molecule - the Anchor records 0 invalid and 0 duplicate attempts and identical scores on repeated identities - so there is no outcome risk to price, and the downside this campaign measured (a widened interval winning a position with a low posterior mean) is epistemic. A mean-variance penalty on epistemic variance is posterior-mean-greedy allocation, which this lineage already measured at -0.116317.
sources.finding: Makarova, Usmanova, Bogunovic and Krause (NeurIPS 2021) optimize a mean-variance objective rather than the expectation alone, modelling both the mean and the input-dependent observation variance and proposing a risk-aware acquisition with sublinear regret guarantees and a robust reporting rule.
sources.title: Risk-averse Heteroscedastic Bayesian Optimization

Their marginal-likelihood fitting, batch size one and 10,000-evaluation budget are not transferable: the profile epoch freezes announced batches of ten and 300 observations per task, and this lineage fits no kernel hyperparameters at all.
sources.finding: Tripp and Hernandez-Lobato (ICML 2024 AI for Science workshop) diagnose three defects in the PMO GP-BO baseline and report that fixing them makes a basic GP BO the strongest entry they measure (sum of AUC Top-10 over 23 tasks 16.303 against Genetic GFN 16.213, MolGA 14.708, REINVENT 14.196): the prior signal variance fitted by marginal likelihood on poor starting data is too small and is replaced by a declared outputscale of 1.0 for objectives in [0,1]; binary Morgan fingerprints over-smooth the Tanimoto kernel and are replaced by count fingerprints; and the acquisition was maximized over only about six proposals per selection, raised to about one thousand with batch size one. Their acquisition stays UCB with beta drawn log-uniformly from [0.01, 1]. They describe it as a pilot without ablations, so the three fixes are not separated.
sources.title: Diagnosing and fixing common problems in Bayesian optimization for molecule design

sources.applicability: Supplies the exact closed form this position needs over an existing Gaussian posterior: EI(x) = (mu - y*) Phi(z) + sigma phi(z) with z = (mu - y*) / sigma, computed from the predictive mean and standard deviation the Anchor already produces for every one of its 160 pool members, with y* the session's own best accepted score. It introduces no model, no new dependency and no fitting step, and it prices the magnitude of the improvement a purchase could deliver instead of letting one sampled tail realization win a position.
sources.finding: Frazier (2018) states the expected-improvement criterion and its decision-theoretic derivation, and derives it as the expectation of the improvement over the best value observed so far, with the noisy generalization justified by the same argument rather than by an ad hoc correction. The tutorial presents expected improvement, entropy search and knowledge gradient as the three standard acquisition families.
sources.title: A Tutorial on Bayesian Optimization

sources.applicability: The Anchor selects ten candidates per announced batch, so a single-point criterion needs a batch rule. Kriging Believer is the one that keeps the inherited cross-candidate correlation live and load-bearing: the pool covariance and its Cholesky factor already exist in the Anchor, so conditioning the remaining pool on each pick's predictive mean reuses them exactly. It is adopted only as the batch-construction rule; the paper's Branin-Hoo experiments and its continuous design space transfer nothing to a molecular pool.
sources.finding: Ginsbourger, Le Riche and Carraro (2010, Computational Intelligence in Expensive Optimization Problems, pp. 131-162) show that the exact q-point expected improvement is analytic only for q = 2 and expensive beyond it, and propose two nearly optimal sequential heuristics for building a batch of q points: Kriging Believer, which imputes the model's own predictive value as a fictitious observation at each point already placed in the batch, and Constant Liar, which imputes a fixed value instead.
sources.title: Kriging is well-suited to parallelize optimization (q-EI, Kriging Believer and Constant Liar)

sources.applicability: Gives the principle for the one declared change in position 2: correct the dispersion of an existing predictive distribution from the model's own recorded prediction-outcome pairs instead of changing the model. The adaptation is severe and is pre-registered as such: there is no held-out calibration set at 300 chronological accepted observations, so the correction is a single bounded robust scale computed from the session's own accepted one-step-ahead standardized residuals, and no distributional guarantee is claimed.
sources.finding: Kuleshov, Fenner and Ermon (ICML 2018) recalibrate a probabilistic regressor post hoc, by a procedure inspired by Platt scaling, and report that it is guaranteed to produce calibrated uncertainty estimates given enough data while consistently producing well-calibrated credible intervals for Bayesian linear regression and for feedforward and recurrent networks.
sources.title: Accurate Uncertainties for Deep Learning Using Calibrated Regression

sources.applicability: Deferred, not scheduled. The Anchor's pool of 160 with an explicit cross-candidate covariance is exactly the finite correlated-belief setting this policy is defined on, so it is implementable here. It is deferred because the benchmark endpoint is the final Top-1 value of molecules actually evaluated, which makes improvement over the incumbent the matched criterion this round; a decision-value criterion is the right second construction only once an improvement-priced rule has been measured on this Parent.
sources.finding: Frazier, Powell and Dayanik (INFORMS Journal on Computing 21(4):599-613, 2009) give a value-of-information policy for a finite set of alternatives under a correlated multivariate normal prior, computable exactly for the correlated case, provably optimal in special cases and with bounded suboptimality otherwise; correlation lets one measurement inform many alternatives, which is what makes the policy efficient on large alternative sets.
sources.title: The Knowledge-Gradient Policy for Correlated Normal Beliefs

sources.applicability: Deferred. It is the principled version of position 2's correction and the named successor if a single session-level scale proves too coarse, but it needs a calibration split of the session archive and a per-candidate interval construction, which is a second construction on top of an untested one; the campaign's own rule is one declared change per position.
sources.finding: Stanton, Maddox and Wilson (AISTATS 2023) note that acquisition values are unreliable under model misspecification or covariate shift, and use conformal prediction, which retains coverage guarantees for a misspecified model, to steer queries toward regions where the predictions are reliably valid; they report improved query coverage without loss of sample efficiency on black-box optimization and tabular ranking tasks.
sources.title: Bayesian Optimization with Conformal Prediction Sets

sources.applicability: Context and boundary only. It establishes that a GP over fingerprints with a genetic acquisition optimizer is a competitive architecture class, which is the class this lineage already occupies, and that the published strong configuration uses an optimistic bound rather than a sampled draw or an improvement criterion. No reported number is campaign evidence: the budget is 10,000 against 300 here, the task sets differ and the scoring is AUC Top-10 rather than final Top-1.
sources.finding: Gao, Fu, Sun and Coley (NeurIPS 2022) benchmark 25 molecular design algorithms on 23 single-objective tasks under a 10,000-call oracle budget and report that most recent methods fail to beat their predecessors once sample efficiency is scored; their GP BO entry pairs a Tanimoto-kernel GP with a Graph GA acquisition optimizer and a UCB acquisition with a randomly drawn beta.
sources.title: Sample Efficiency Matters: A Benchmark for Practical Molecular Optimization

sources.applicability: Examined and declined for this round, which is itself a useful boundary: the risk RAHBO prices is aleatoric, the variance of repeated noisy outcomes at the same input. The five frozen objectives here are deterministic functions of the molecule - the Anchor records 0 invalid and 0 duplicate attempts and identical scores on repeated identities - so there is no outcome risk to price, and the downside this campaign measured (a widened interval winning a position with a low posterior mean) is epistemic. A mean-variance penalty on epistemic variance is posterior-mean-greedy allocation, which this lineage already measured at -0.116317.
sources.finding: Makarova, Usmanova, Bogunovic and Krause (NeurIPS 2021) optimize a mean-variance objective rather than the expectation alone, modelling both the mean and the input-dependent observation variance and proposing a risk-aware acquisition with sublinear regret guarantees and a robust reporting rule.
sources.title: Risk-averse Heteroscedastic Bayesian Optimization

Report the field receipts first: pool_size = pool_target = 320 and truncated_by_attempt_limit false in all 435 batches, generation attempts and admission rejections per batch against the Anchor's, zero posterior_fallback, the restricted-batch count and depth distribution against the Anchor's 88 batches and 29 episodes, the posterior-mean and SD percentiles of the picks, the heavy-atom distribution of admitted members against the Anchor's mean pooled 29.37 (the law-free re-draw alone reaches 31.73, so drift is read against that), and realized incumbent-increment mass against 5.978073 split by session third.

literature_basis.method: Acquisition-maximization breadth: more candidates ranked per selection

r0046-03-improve-L01.objective: Give the unchanged rule more to rank per selection: raise one inherited CONFIG constant, pool_multiplier 16 to 32, so each announced batch of ten ranks 320 freshly generated, inherited-admission-passing candidates instead of 160. The posterior, the correlated Thompson rule and its ten rows, the stall mask (M stays 40 of the now larger field), admission, the operator menu and weights, crossover, retention, breeding and every probability stay exactly as inherited; only the pool target changes.
r0046-03-improve-L01.parallel_rationale: The four positions are one designed set on one Parent, profile and panel, not four independent guesses at the same mechanism. Positions 1, 2 and 3 are a graded triple through the single stage three independent round-45 arms named as the recurring limitation: position 3 removes the sampled draw entirely and gives the greedy end of the pricing stack on this Anchor (previously measured only on another Parent at -0.116317), position 2 keeps the inherited draw and corrects only the dispersion it reads, and position 1 is the joint arm that needs both an honest scale and an incumbent-referenced criterion to be well posed at all. Run in the same batch they attribute each other: the joint arm's reading is bounded above by the greedy control and below by the calibration-only control, which no sequential order of two rounds would give at the same path realization. Position 4 is on a disjoint axis - how many candidates the unchanged rule ranks per selection - and shares no changed law with the other three, so it cannot confound them and it keeps a conservative evidence-backed attempt in the round while the pricing question is open.
r0046-03-improve-L01.question: Is this method's endpoint partly bounded by how few candidates the inherited rule ranks per selection, given that cutting the field from 160 to 120 on the previous Parent cost -0.055666 with increment mass falling 14.3 per cent?
r0046-03-improve-L01.rationale: This is the only conservative axis in the round with a measured gradient on this lineage and an independent external precedent. Internally, n-eaa24506506e changed exactly this constant in the other direction - 160 to 120 on n-1744a1494180 - and lost -0.055666, with realized increment mass 4.9844 against 5.8194 (-14.3 per cent), the deficit concentrated entirely in the first session third (2.3991 against 3.7484) and the largest single increment falling 0.4620 to 0.2690; the same arm bought more and smaller gains (751 of 4,350 parent-beating against 648), which is the signature of a thinner field. Externally, Tripp and Hernandez-Lobato name the number of proposals per selection as one of three defects whose repair made a basic GP BO the strongest method they measured on PMO, moving from about six proposals per selection to about a thousand; this Anchor sits at sixteen. The change adds no component and no dependency - it is the inherited pool target - which is why it carries no break-in reservation, and it is the arm in this round whose failure is also informative: if a doubled field changes neither the purchases nor the mass, then supply breadth is not what the inherited rule lacked and the pricing diagnosis stands alone.

candidate_methods.method: Improvement-priced batch allocation: expected improvement over the session incumbent with Kriging-Believer batch construction
required_elements: The closed-form criterion over an existing Gaussian posterior: EI = (mu - y*)Phi(z) + sigma phi(z) with z = (mu - y*)/sigma, referenced to the best value observed so far rather than to any absolute level
An incumbent reference that is the session's own best accepted score, which is what makes a wide interval with a low mean lose a position instead of winning it on a tail draw

Kriging-Believer sequential batch construction: impute each already placed pick's own predictive value as a fictitious observation and recondition the remaining candidates through the existing covariance, so one criterion fills a batch of ten without ten near-identical picks
A predictive dispersion the criterion can be read on at all, which the same review's prior-width source names as a measured defect of this architecture class

candidate_methods.method: Session-calibrated predictive scale: prior-width correction and post-hoc recalibration of the dispersion the acquisition reads
required_elements: The diagnosis that a GP prior scale inherited from poor early data is too small, with the fix stated as declaring the scale rather than fitting it on that data
Post-hoc correction of an existing probabilistic regressor's dispersion from its own prediction-outcome pairs, leaving the model and its mean untouched
A bounded, declared estimator with a clip so an early session cannot produce a degenerate scale, and a reported clipping rate
The confirmation half of the same source, already satisfied here: count rather than binary Morgan fingerprints under the Tanimoto kernel, which is why no fingerprint change is proposed
The identical construction is reused as the declared second half of position 1, where an improvement criterion is not well posed without it

candidate_methods.method: Acquisition-maximization breadth: more candidates ranked per selection
required_elements: The diagnosis that the baseline maximized its acquisition over about six proposals per selected molecule, and the fix of raising it to about one thousand
The requirement that the extra breadth comes from the same proposal distribution and the same admission path, so the rule ranks more of the same chemistry rather than different chemistry
A cost accounting that keeps the enlarged per-selection search inside the frozen budget, which here is the task and node timeout rather than the paper's batch-size-one schedule

candidate_methods.method: Knowledge-gradient pricing for correlated normal beliefs (value of information)
required_elements: Exact computation of the expected increase in the maximum posterior mean over a finite set of alternatives under a correlated normal prior, which the Anchor's 160-member pool and explicit cross-candidate covariance already provide
The correlated-belief structure that lets one measurement re-price many candidates, which is what distinguishes it from a candidate's own improvement
A decision-value objective, which is the element that does not match a final-Top-1 endpoint and is why this method is deferred rather than scheduled

candidate_methods.method: Conformal-corrected acquisition under a misspecified surrogate
required_elements: Conformal prediction sets that retain coverage under misspecification, used inside the acquisition so queries are steered to regions where the model's predictions are reliably valid
A calibration split of the observed data, which at 300 chronological accepted observations would have to come out of the same session archive the surrogate is trained on
A per-candidate interval construction rather than a single dispersion scale, which is the named successor if the scalar correction in position 2 proves too coarse

candidate_methods.method: Risk-averse heteroscedastic mean-variance acquisition (RAHBO)
required_elements: A mean-variance objective with the input-dependent observation variance modelled alongside the mean
An aleatoric risk to price, that is repeated noisy outcomes at the same input, which these five deterministic benchmark objectives do not have

A risk-aware acquisition whose variance penalty on purely epistemic variance would reduce to posterior-mean-greedy allocation, already measured on this lineage at -0.116317, which is why this method is declined rather than deferred

observed_bottleneck.summary: Candidate pricing and ranking, not proposal capability and not admission. On this Anchor, three independent round-45 arms built to test three different hypotheses each measured the same obstruction: the inherited correlated-Thompson rule over an accepted-only count-Morgan Tanimoto posterior converts neither coarse multi-atom products nor archive-far products into realized incumbent increments, and supplying more of either, or recalibrating the far-field uncertainty it reads, does not change that. Four disjoint stages (proposal supply, admission, survivor retention, predictor geometry) are now refuted on this Anchor with no positive result, and the one measured positive in the lineage's history is a crude special case of pricing by posterior mean: restricting eligibility to the top forty posterior means during stalls. No node of this lineage has ever run an acquisition that weighs expected improvement against risk, and the dispersion any such rule would read is itself measured wrong by more than an order of magnitude near the predictor's own archive.

sources.applicability: The Anchor already samples a jointly consistent residual across the whole 160-member pool once per announced batch; this source supplies the one element we take, that a bootstrap resample of the session own accepted records can play the role of the posterior draw, so the dispersion the rule reads stops being a kernel distance. sources.finding: Thompson-sampling exploration can be implemented without maintaining or sampling an explicit posterior: fit a model to a bootstrap resample of the observed data (optionally with artificially generated data that induces a prior) and act greedily on that one resampled model, which the authors argue is what makes the exploration coherent across a whole episode rather than independent per decision.
sources.title: Bootstrapped Thompson Sampling and Deep Exploration

sources.applicability: We adopt only the principle that disagreement among refits of the same model family on resampled data is a usable dispersion, and the practice of reading it per input. We adopt no neural architecture, no adversarial training, no proper-scoring-rule objective (the Anchor fits no hyperparameters) and none of their datasets or numbers.
sources.finding: An ensemble of independently trained predictors, scored by a proper scoring rule, yields predictive uncertainty that is competitive with or better than Bayesian alternatives such as MC dropout, and in particular expresses higher uncertainty on out-of-distribution inputs; the uncertainty is the ensemble disagreement rather than a closed-form function of the input.
sources.title: Simple and Scalable Predictive Uncertainty Estimation using Deep Ensembles

sources.applicability: This is the external statement of this lineage own measurement: the Anchor dispersion IS a Tanimoto-distance statistic, and round 46 showed that correcting its magnitude (n-707027cd2146) does not help because the ordering, not the scale, is what is wrong. It bounds our expectation too: an ensemble dispersion is not promised to be better calibrated, which is why this position registers a behavioural reading rather than a predicted gain.
sources.finding: In a systematic comparison on molecular regression the authors separate distance-based uncertainty estimates (Tanimoto distance in structure space, Euclidean distance in latent space) from ensemble, mean-variance and union-based estimates, and state explicitly that Tanimoto distance is a relative quantity and not a metric intended to match the magnitude of error, excluding the distance-based methods from their miscalibration and NLL analyses; no method is unequivocally superior, and ensembles tend to underestimate out-of-domain error.
sources.title: Uncertainty Quantification Using Neural Networks for Molecular Property Prediction

sources.applicability: Precedent that model-based optimization over structured spaces routinely replaces a stationary-kernel GP with a surrogate whose uncertainty is not a kernel distance. sources.finding: For conditional, high-dimensional and otherwise complex search spaces the package uses a random forest surrogate rather than a Gaussian process with a stationary kernel, and the authors attribute SMAC advantage in those spaces to that choice; the Gaussian-process facade is reserved for low-dimensional continuous problems.
sources.title: SMAC3: A Versatile Bayesian Optimization Package for Hyperparameter Optimization

sources.title: Batched Gaussian Process Bandit Optimization via Determinantal Point Processes

sources.finding: Choosing the alternative with the highest estimated value makes the chosen alternative tend to fall short of its own estimate even when every estimate is individually unbiased, because selection favours whichever estimate carries the largest positive error; the authors remedy is a Bayesian adjustment of the value estimates before ranking, which they describe as disciplined skepticism.

observed_bottleneck.summary: Every rule this lineage has tried for converting its posterior into purchases loses, and round 46 fixed both ends of the axis at one path realization on the Anchor itself: the inherited sampled correlated-Thompson rule at 0 by construction, a session-calibrated robust predictive scale alone at -0.035153, closed-form expected improvement with Kriging-Believer batch conditioning on that scale at -0.053288, and pure posterior-mean allocation at -0.126894. The campaign own diagnosis of why is representational rather than algorithmic: predictive SD under the accepted-only count-Morgan generalized-Tanimoto covariance is a monotone function of archive distance, and in this generator archive distance is a function of molecular degeneracy, so every rule that rewards uncertainty or dissimilarity is arbitraged by fragments and oversize duplicated-fragment products. The magnitude of that dispersion has now been corrected successfully and it did not help; the unresolved object is the statistic itself, and no node of this lineage has ever supplied the allocator a dispersion that is not computed from archive similarity.

sources.applicability: The Anchor already samples a jointly consistent residual across the whole 160-member pool once per announced batch; this source supplies the one element we take, that a bootstrap resample of the session own accepted records can play the role of the posterior draw, so the dispersion the rule reads stops being a kernel distance. We adopt neither their bandit or RL setting, their artificial-prior construction, nor any reported number.
sources.finding: Thompson-sampling exploration can be implemented without maintaining or sampling an explicit posterior: fit a model to a bootstrap resample of the observed data (optionally with artificially generated data that induces a prior) and act greedily on that one resampled model, which the authors argue is what makes the exploration coherent across a whole episode rather than independent per decision.
sources.title: Bootstrapped Thompson Sampling and Deep Exploration

sources.applicability: We adopt only the principle that disagreement among refits of the same model family on resampled data is a usable dispersion, and the practice of reading it per input. We adopt no neural architecture, no adversarial training, no proper-scoring-rule objective (the Anchor fits no hyperparameters) and none of their datasets or numbers.
sources.finding: An ensemble of independently trained predictors, scored by a proper scoring rule, yields predictive uncertainty that is competitive with or better than Bayesian alternatives such as MC dropout, and in particular expresses higher uncertainty on out-of-distribution inputs; the uncertainty is the ensemble disagreement rather than a closed-form function of the input.
sources.title: Simple and Scalable Predictive Uncertainty Estimation using Deep Ensembles

sources.applicability: This is the external statement of this lineage own measurement: the Anchor dispersion IS a Tanimoto-distance statistic, and round 46 showed that correcting its magnitude (n-707027cd2146) does not help because the ordering, not the scale, is what is wrong. It bounds our expectation too: an ensemble dispersion is not promised to be better calibrated, which is why this position registers a behavioural reading rather than a predicted gain.
sources.finding: In a systematic comparison on molecular regression the authors separate distance-based uncertainty estimates (Tanimoto distance in structure space, Euclidean distance in latent space) from ensemble, mean-variance and union-based estimates, and state explicitly that Tanimoto distance is a relative quantity and not a metric intended to match the magnitude of error, excluding the distance-based methods from their miscalibration and NLL analyses; no method is unequivocally superior, and ensembles tend to underestimate out-of-domain error.
sources.title: Uncertainty Quantification Using Neural Networks for Molecular Property Prediction

sources.applicability: Precedent that model-based optimization over structured spaces routinely replaces a stationary-kernel GP with a surrogate whose uncertainty is not a kernel distance. We take only the precedent and the direction, not a random forest, because keeping the inherited count-Morgan predictive mean is what makes this position one attributable change; the page we read does not state how its forest obtains variance and we claim nothing about that.
sources.finding: For conditional, high-dimensional and otherwise complex search spaces the package uses a random forest surrogate rather than a Gaussian process with a stationary kernel, and the authors attribute SMAC advantage in those spaces to that choice; the Gaussian-process facade is reserved for low-dimensional continuous problems.
sources.title: SMAC3: A Versatile Bayesian Optimization Package for Hyperparameter Optimization

sources.applicability: Deferred. It is the only remaining batch-construction element this campaign has not tried, but the kernel it would need here cannot be the count-Morgan kernel: n-698a02f85be1 closed within-batch decorrelation through that covariance, and h-ec64b8c24e9bd359 shows raw within-batch similarity on this panel is confounded by fragments. A DPP over a scaffold-level kernel with members below twelve heavy atoms excluded is a separate construction and needs its own position.
sources.finding: A batch of parallel evaluations can be chosen by sampling from a determinantal point process whose kernel encodes diversity, which the authors prove gives better regret bounds than greedy batch construction and which outperformed the batch methods they compared against.
sources.title: Batched Gaussian Process Bandit Optimization via Determinantal Point Processes

sources.applicability: Deferred. It names exactly the measured residual asymmetry in h-07f6b6867d828341: on sitagliptin_mpo about a third of this Anchor picks land more than three predictive SDs below their prediction, and the standardized residual mean square there is 136.73 before and 111.28 after a width correction. A location adjustment is a different mechanism from a width adjustment and needs its own forecast and falsifier.
sources.finding: Choosing the alternative with the highest estimated value makes the chosen alternative tend to fall short of its own estimate even when every estimate is individually unbiased, because selection favours whichever estimate carries the largest positive error; the authors remedy is a Bayesian adjustment of the value estimates before ranking, which they describe as disciplined skepticism.
sources.title: The Optimizer Curse: Skepticism and Postdecision Surprise in Decision Analysis

sources.applicability: Deferred, and only as the construction: here the two estimators would be two cross-fitted halves of the session own accepted records, one ranking the pool and the other valuing the ranked candidates. Nothing about reinforcement learning, bootstrapping of targets or their benchmark transfers; the campaign has no evidence yet that selection-induced optimism is what wastes its evaluations, which is why this is named and not scheduled.
sources.finding: Using the same value estimates both to select and to evaluate an action makes overestimation systematic; decoupling selection from evaluation with two independently fitted estimators reduces the overestimation and improved performance on the benchmark the authors studied.
sources.title: Deep Reinforcement Learning with Double Q-learning

plan_obstacle.explanation: The registered construction is implementable exactly as written, needs no asset or dependency, and the goal g-L01-predictive-location-bias is well posed. What blocks this position is that the frozen transformation's effect on n-61b9b3bfb40d is the opposite of the effect its own approach and question require, this is measurable before any oracle call, and condition 10 forbids repairing it inside this ticket. BASIS. Because the Anchor draws samples = m + score_scale * (normals @ L_transpose), replacing m_i by m_tilde_i displaces every already logged sampled value by exactly -(1 - alpha_i)(m_i - m_bar). Each of the 435 announcements in the Anchor's own receipts can therefore be re-decided from its logged means, stds and function_values with no re-run, holding the standard-normal array, the Cholesky factor, the dispersion, the eligibility mask and the sequential first-index rule exactly as inherited. The replay reproduces the ticket's own published strata exactly, 997 of 3,470 unrestricted purchases at posterior-mean rank 40 or worse and 0 of 880 restricted, confirming it reads the same receipts conditions 13 and 15 were computed from. NOT A DEGENERACY READING. The declared alpha is non-trivial: over 69,600 member-announcements its median is 0.759, 10.3 percent fall below 0.5, the per-announcement median ranges 0.308 to 0.958, and at least one purchase changes in 379 of 435 announcements at mean pick overlap 7.59 of 10. Condition 14's implementation-reading clause is cleared with margin, so what follows is about the class, not about a failed build. THE SIGN IS STRUCTURALLY WRONG. On this kernel sigma_i is strongly anti-correlated with m_i: the per-announcement Spearman correlation is -0.689 on average, median -0.732, and negative in 434 of 435 announcements. alpha_i = s2/(s2 + sigma_i^2) is therefore increasing in m_i, so m_bar + alpha_i (m_i - m_bar) lifts the low-predicted high-variance tail far more than it deflates the inflated top. Of the absolute location mass the transform moves, 823.4 units lift below-mean members at +0.0276 each against 357.7 units deflating above-mean members at -0.0090 each, a 2.30-to-1 split against the direction the optimizer's-curse remedy is adopted for; the top-ten-by-posterior-mean members, the ones that remedy concerns, move only -0.0141. BOTH DEGENERATE ENDS ARE SUBSIDIZED, NOT PRICED. The approach's premise is that sigma_i is maximal at both degenerate ends so a pull toward the pool mean prices them. The first half holds: mean alpha is 0.368 below six heavy atoms and 0.687 above fifty against 0.746 for the 12-to-50 bulk. The second half does not, because both ends are predicted below the pool mean, not above it: mean m_i - m_bar is -0.0959 below six heavy atoms and -0.0570 above fifty against +0.0083 for the bulk, so the pull toward m_bar is a lift of +0.0621 and +0.0186 for those ends against +0.0030 for the bulk. In the replay, purchases below six heavy atoms rise from 91 to 372 of 4,350 and below twelve from 124 to 492, while purchases above fifty fall only 44 to 38. In the exact batch-one counterfactual, the fifteen first batches where no trajectory divergence has yet occurred and the replay is a true counterfactual, fragment purchases rise from 3 to 18 of 150 and mean purchased size falls 29.63 to 24.71. The question's 'moves the purchases off both degenerate ends at once' is already answered no at the fragment end. IT ALSO CONTRADICTS THE CAMPAIGN'S OWN ORDERING EVIDENCE. Of 1,361 displaced purchases, 1,031 (75.8 percent) move to a member of lower posterior mean; mean selected posterior-mean rank rises 27.31 to 44.52; unrestricted purchases at rank 40 or worse rise 997 to 1,505 of 3,470, worsening the exact leakage statistic condition 13 asks to be reported. n-707858263b1e measured that purchases departing from the inherited order convert at 0.000482 of increment mass per evaluation against 0.001904 for agreed purchases, and n-707027cd2146 with n-698a02f85be1 established that this predictor's ordering rather than its magnitude is the defect. The registered form increases order departures by half, so it is predicted to lose for an ordering reason unrelated to the location-bias question it was registered to answer. ROBUST TO THE OTHER READING OF SIGMA. Reading sigma_i in standardized latent units instead of raw score units is worse, not better: alpha collapses to median 0.017 with 98.9 percent below 0.5, fragment purchases reach 901 of 4,350 and 3,276 of 3,470 unrestricted purchases land at rank 40 or worse. The conclusion does not depend on the unit choice because it follows from the scale-free anti-correlation of sigma with m. WHY THIS BLOCKS RATHER THAN MERELY FORECASTS A LOSS. Condition 10 states that a failed configuration authorizes no sweep of the shrinkage form, its reference point, its variance estimate or its floor. Spending this position on the frozen configuration would therefore close the entire shrinkage family, and with it the open question h-07f6b6867d828341, on a reference-point sign error rather than on the location-bias hypothesis. The campaign would record that location correction fails on this Anchor when what was tested is that subsidizing below-mean high-variance candidates fails. Honouring the goal requires amending the reference point before the position is spent, which is not inside what this ticket leaves open to the plan.
plan_obstacle.requested_change: Keep the code Parent n-61b9b3bfb40d, the goal g-L01-predictive-location-bias, the frozen question, the external introduction and the two reserved follow-up positions; amend the registered construction in conditions 10 and 11 of approach a-L01-selection-shrunk-predictive-location so that the affine shrinkage uses a reference point under which the transform is a discount rather than a subsidy, then re-issue this position. Every actual restart throws away predictive conditioning and starts with one root label. All 19 first-reset fields have constant raw mean equal to the root score. A fixed root-plus-nine-neighbor replay on the 186 actually bought first-reset labels reduces RMSE from 0.31751984699030944 to 0.25338367925576977 and MAE from 0.22077670112539952 to 0.15790520520149648; it improves SSE in all 19 episodes but measures only the selected stream. Highest-score unused identity is usually a near-neighbor of an existing region, so identity-level restart does not ensure structural relocation. The 19 actual roots have mean minimum distance to retiring/other center 0.09522585113201158. The fixed score-first separation rule changes all 19 historical root decisions and gives mean minimum distance 0.5408330388773716, while sacrificing mean known starting score 0.2403781890912353 (range -0.6100153217769878 to -0.012481276883127168). This is an explicit cost to test against subsequent fresh progress, not evidence that diversity improves Top1. Old forced-diversity and retention results do not establish transfer to restart-center selection.

Tree value averages all descendant returns even though the campaign ranks final Top1. On actual chronological states, 56368 repeated-support rows have a strict maximum/mean gap; replacing only the within-sibling statistic changes 3272 virtual-root and 1445 deeper choices out of 10104. This identifies an actionable selector distinction without estimating any alternative terminal score. Sparse maxima can also reinforce lucky historical branches, so reduced average dilution is not itself useful conversion.

B3: review solution-to-root feedback, forced observation and contrary loss-of-breadth conditions before choosing the next tests. Ordinary Anchor continuation needs host-matched attribution, not transfer from the tree.

Passive choices describe their actual states only and supply no unpurchased score or counterfactual adaptive trajectory. Preserve all cell heterogeneity and adaptive path changes; omitted products have no counterfactual scores. Reuse review with internal_evidence basis and empty adoptions. No new schedule, chemistry filter or tuned walk length is authorized. Preserve these registered applicability conditions through the intent and contribution evidence so that completion can assess the same criterion and scope.

required_elements: Use a genuinely observed improved solution as the next search origin; the triggering score must be accepted before root construction.

Declare the tree-boundary statistic rule. This adaptation discards the old active tree and initializes one cached incumbent root, separating its context receipt from new optimizer evaluations; it does not transfer ancestor visits.

candidate_methods.method: Minimal final-slot regional feedback coverage
required_elements: Separate a real observation-access condition from posterior optimism and from success/failure updates; no-purchase is never fabricated failure evidence.

With two nonempty regions and the frozen batch ten, keep first nine selections exactly as inherited, then constrain the final sample choice only if one region remains unpurchased. Use the same final normal row and identity exclusion.

A real accepted purchase enables the unchanged episode model and controller update. Report diverted slots, later adaptation and complete utility including opportunity cost. This is an explicit finite-budget adaptation, not the source age schedule or its regret guarantee.

candidate_methods.method: Randomized whole-tree meta-search restarts
required_elements: Independent restart searches retain the best complete solution while exploring alternative initial trajectories.

n-ded8f57a69ad restores field variance and changes purchased sets after all 18 natural resets, yet mean gain is only +0.0005827761218230032 and late mass declines. n-970847a1987c changes the global progress consumer at eight paid updates and gains +0.0015117398029903528, below +0.002, with twelve endpoints unchanged. Do not retune either refuted conjunction or claim blanket reset starvation.

Ordinary continuation has contrary condition-specific evidence: n-c070e95b09ef whole-run removal on n-1744a1494180 loses 0.03069975142490533; n-8b168a9969bb stall-only removal on that host gains 0.0038879442353230154 with cell fragility. The closest catalogue method is Mol GA itself, with Graph GA supplying its graph operators; these are one method family, not distinct lineages created by parameter changes. method_proposal.first_improvement_direction: If the root succeeds but its observed offspring gains show that most oracle evaluations do not improve their breeding parents, first test posterior-sampling guidance for the existing graph search. Fit a fingerprint surrogate only to accepted observations from the current task, run the existing graph operators against sampled surrogate functions, and evaluate the generated sample maximizers. This is an inferred molecular transfer of the optimization specialization of [PS-BAX](https://proceedings.neurips.cc/paper_files/paper/2024/file/f3c8bfcc9c2bc13a0f141cb58afc6e5a-Paper-Conference.pdf), where the target is the maximizer and posterior sampling reduces to Thompson sampling. Check chronological predictive usefulness and whether selected offspring produce more parent-beating scores; retain the change only if the protocol's final Top-1 evidence supports it. No campaign evidence currently establishes this bottleneck.
method_proposal.method_name: Mol GA: rank-selected de novo graph evolution
method_proposal.method_thesis: Anchor the root in Mol GA: maintain a population of oracle-evaluated molecular graphs, sample breeding parents across high-ranked quantiles, generate new offspring through graph crossover and atom/bond mutations, and update survivors greedily after each observation. These are the proposal and selection mechanisms described by [Tripp and Hernández-Lobato (2023)](https://arxiv.org/html/2310.09267v1). Start from the supplied initial observations and incorporate newly evaluated offspring immediately, following the evaluator's announced batching. Repeated graph edits and recombination create an evolving search space; no corpus ranking, stored molecule library, pretrained model, or fixed candidate enumeration is needed. The causal hypothesis is that direct selection on task-local scores concentrates successive structural changes around improving molecules quickly enough to raise the final best observed score. The published evidence concerns a larger-budget AUC-Top-10 setting, so its transfer to this benchmark's final Top-1 objective remains a hypothesis.

references.citation: Austin Tripp and José Miguel Hernández-Lobato. Genetic algorithms are strong baselines for molecule generation. arXiv:2310.09267, 2023. Sections 2–3 and Appendix A describe the anchor.

Chu Xin Cheng, Raul Astudillo, Thomas Desautels, and Yisong Yue. Practical Bayesian Algorithm Execution via Posterior Sampling. NeurIPS 2024. Section 3 describes posterior-sampled target sets and the maximization specialization motivating the conditional first improvement.

method_proposal.differentiation: The supplied context contains no bound methods and no mechanism clusters, so there is no existing lineage to name as the nearest comparator or campaign refutation to overcome. The nearest catalogue family is conventional latent BO, including InvBO: this proposal predicts scores in molecular structure space and generates by posterior-conditioned sampling, rather than optimizing a latent-space acquisition or repairing encoder-decoder inversion. Its proposal mechanism also differs from graph crossover and policy-gradient sequence generation. I fixed COWBOYS from the catalogue before opening its external paper. Published evidence is a nearby small-budget setting, not a replication of this benchmark's feedback schedule; learning an adequate prior within permitted preparation remains an empirical prerequisite.
method_proposal.first_improvement_direction: If the successful root shows batches with highly correlated GP predictions and few independent incumbent improvements, add one mechanism: covariance-aware selection among surplus molecules freshly generated by its existing MCMC sampler. Retain candidates with credible incumbent-improvement probability, then select subsequent batch members using posterior variance conditioned on already selected members. This imports the conditional-entropy batch selection idea from [PS-BAX, Appendix C](https://proceedings.neurips.cc/paper_files/paper/2024/file/f3c8bfcc9c2bc13a0f141cb58afc6e5a-Paper-Conference.pdf), without adopting its finite-library experiments. The proposed transfer keeps the VAE, GP and MCMC target fixed and uses only transient de novo candidates. Test whether selected-batch conditional information increases and whether that translates into a higher final Top-1 mean; reduced correlation alone is not success. No root evidence exists yet, so this direction is conditional rather than an asserted observed bottleneck.
method_proposal.method_name: COWBOYS: GP-conditioned de novo latent sampling
method_proposal.method_thesis: Train a compact SELFIES VAE from the permitted unlabeled corpus during preparation, then freeze its decoder. Within each independent objective session, fit a Tanimoto-kernel GP directly to the observed molecular fingerprints and scores. Generate new molecules through preconditioned Crank-Nicolson MCMC targeting the Gaussian latent prior multiplied by the GP probability that the deterministically decoded molecule exceeds the observed incumbent. The molecule assessed by the surrogate must be the molecule submitted. Fill the protocol-announced batch with distinct generated structures and update the GP after feedback. The corpus supplies a generative prior, never a ranked molecule library. This follows the decoupled mechanism in [COWBOYS](https://proceedings.mlr.press/v267/moss25a.html). Our hypothesis is that structure-level prediction and immediate Bayesian conditioning can direct scarce labels toward a higher final observed maximum without fitting a reward-dependent neural generator. Success is measured by the benchmark's mean of independent final Top-1 scores.

method_proposal.differentiation: The supplied context.bound_methods is empty, so there is no most-similar bound lineage to name; context.evidence_view.clusters is also empty, with no earlier refutation to revisit. The closest catalogue family is REINVENT and its replay variants. This proposal anchors that policy-learning family through Augmented Hill-Climb, whose root learns only from current-batch elites. Its defining proposal mechanism is autoregressive generation from reward-updated parameters, distinct from graph crossover or mutation and from acquisition optimization through a frozen latent decoder. A different recurrent backbone or reward multiplier would remain this same lineage. All objective adaptation uses only observations from the current session.
method_proposal.first_improvement_direction: After the root succeeds, probe reuse of scored elites through randomized-SMILES experience replay. If the root logs show that high-reward molecules lose policy likelihood after later batches or that updates affect only their original serialization, retain a bounded elite memory and train on fresh equivalent SMILES views using the existing scores. Hold the prior, AHC loss, and generation rule fixed. Measure replayed-view count, policy likelihood on held-out equivalent views, and the rewards of subsequently evaluated new molecules; improvement must ultimately appear in final Top-1, not merely duplicates or validity. [Guo and Schwaller](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11200228/) provide direct molecular evidence for combining replay with SMILES augmentation. Mining the cross-domain catalogue suggests the related principle of exploiting known objective invariances: [Bardou et al.](https://arxiv.org/abs/2509.25051) study this through max kernels. Transferring that principle to equivalent SMILES training views is an inference; their GP kernel and reported optimization gains are not part of this proposal.
method_proposal.method_name: Augmented Hill-Climb with a corpus-trained SMILES policy
method_proposal.method_thesis: Train a compact autoregressive SMILES prior solely on the supplied unlabeled corpus, then initialize a fresh policy from that prior for each objective. Use the initial observations and each subsequent scored batch to update only its highest-reward sequences with the Augmented Hill-Climb loss: fit policy log likelihood to frozen-prior log likelihood plus scaled observed reward. Sample complete molecules token by token from the updated policy, canonicalize them, and refill invalid or duplicate proposals by further generation. The corpus supplies language training, never a ranked molecular pool. Elite-conditioned policy updates should shift generation toward new high-scoring molecular combinations quickly enough to improve the benchmark's mean final Top-1. This is a small-budget transfer hypothesis, not a claim that published larger-budget gains carry over. The root uses the current scored batch; randomized historical replay is reserved for the first improvement. The anchor's elite augmented-likelihood mechanism is described by [Thomas et al.](https://link.springer.com/article/10.1186/s13321-022-00646-z).

It also differs from Mol GA: rank-selected de novo graph evolution, which breeds evaluated graph parents, and from COWBOYS: GP-conditioned de novo latent sampling, which conditions a VAE through GP-guided MCMC. method_proposal.method_name: ChemTS: UCT-guided SMILES prefix search with a frozen rollout prior
method_proposal.method_thesis: Anchor the root in [ChemTS](https://arxiv.org/html/1710.00616v1): train a compact autoregressive SMILES model solely on the supplied unlabeled corpus during preparation, then freeze it. method_proposal.method_name: Simulated annealing through de novo molecular graph walks
method_proposal.method_thesis: Anchor the method in simulated annealing: randomly perturb a current configuration, accept improvements, sometimes accept deterioration, and gradually cool the acceptance rule. [Kirkpatrick, Gelatt and Vecchi](https://hedibert.org/wp-content/uploads/2013/12/1983KirkpatrickGelattVecchi.pdf) describe this mechanism for combinatorial optimization. Our molecular transfer maintains independent graph walks initialized from the current objective's supplied scored molecules. Each walk generates a new neighbor through atom or bond edits. After real feedback, accept a higher-scoring neighbor as the next working state; accept a lower-scoring neighbor with probability exp((new_score-current_score)/T), otherwise retain the source state. Subsequent edits follow the accepted working state, while a separate archive preserves the best observed molecule. Cool as feedback accumulates and distribute the evaluator-announced batch across walks with explicit proposal-to-source provenance. Regenerate invalid or already evaluated structures through further edits. Every submitted molecule is generated de novo; no corpus pool, learned prior or labeled source task is required. The hypothesis is that temporary score losses permit useful structural transitions whose later gains increase the mean of the five independent final Top-1 scores. This finite-budget optimizer does not claim equilibrium sampling or asymptotic convergence under molecular validity and novelty filtering.
