The construction grammar, heuristic, evaporation and pheromone bounds remain fixed. This applies known objective invariance to reuse one accepted score across more relevant action contexts. [Bardou et al., Section 2.2](https://arxiv.org/html/2509.25051v1), found in the cross-domain catalogue, discusses observation reuse under known symmetries; its max-kernel algorithm is not imported, and the pheromone adaptation is an inference. Measure distinct equivalent traces, newly reinforced context-action entries, and actual subsequent incumbent gains. Retention requires improved final Top-1 evidence, not broader trace coverage alone. No supplied observation establishes this ant-colony-specific bottleneck yet.
method_proposal.method_name: MAX-MIN Ant System over a molecular construction grammar
method_proposal.method_thesis: Anchor the method in MAX-MIN Ant System: construct solutions probabilistically from components, evaporate their pheromone weights, reinforce the iteration-best solution, and bound every pheromone weight away from zero and excessive dominance. [Stutzle and Hoos, Sections 2 and 4](https://www.cs.ubc.ca/~hoos/Publ/fgcs00.pdf) describe this mechanism. Our molecular adaptation constructs a fresh graph from an empty state through valence-aware atom, bond, ring-closure and termination actions. Choice probabilities combine a fixed chemical heuristic with task-local pheromones keyed by the local attachment context and action, allowing a useful action to transfer between different partial graphs. Preparation uses the permitted unlabeled corpus only for aggregate construction frequencies and stopping statistics. Initialize pheromones broadly, reconstruct valid construction traces for the supplied scored molecules, and use their best trace for the initial reinforcement. Generate the announced batch through complete new construction trajectories; only accepted whole-molecule feedback drives evaporation and reinforcement of that batch's best trace. Resample failed or duplicate constructions locally. There is no stored complete-molecule library, corpus ranking or fixed product enumeration. The hypothesis is that reusing successful local construction choices across new molecular combinations raises the mean of independent final Top-1 scores. Whether coarse construction contexts carry useful reward information quickly enough is unproven; pheromone concentration or validity alone is not success.

references.citation: Thomas Stutzle and Holger H. Hoos. MAX-MIN Ant System. Future Generation Computer Systems 16(8), 889-914, 2000. Author-hosted near-final manuscript; Sections 2 and 4 describe probabilistic construction, best-ant reinforcement, evaporation and pheromone limits.

Anthony Bardou, Antoine Gonon, Aryan Ahadinia, and Patrick Thiran. Symmetry-Aware Bayesian Optimization via Max Kernels. arXiv:2509.25051, 2025. Section 2.2 supplies the objective-invariance and observation-augmentation principle motivating the conditional construction-trace improvement.

method_proposal.differentiation: The closest bound lineage is CMA-ES: covariance adaptation through a frozen molecular decoder. Both can share a frozen generative representation, but CMA-ES samples a common adaptive Gaussian while this method preserves particle-specific velocity and personal-best memory and combines cognitive and social displacement vectors. This changes the proposal dynamics, not the decoder or a covariance constant. COWBOYS: GP-conditioned de novo latent sampling uses posterior-tilted MCMC, and NF-BO: invertible sequence-flow search with token-adaptive latent proposals uses adaptive flow inversion and GP-selected token perturbations; this root fits no objective surrogate. Mol GA: rank-selected de novo graph evolution and Genetic GFN: reciprocal learning between a flow policy and graph search breed molecular graphs. Simulated annealing through de novo molecular graph walks changes graph states through temperature-dependent acceptance. Augmented Hill-Climb with a corpus-trained SMILES policy updates neural generation weights, ChemTS: UCT-guided SMILES prefix search with a frozen rollout prior updates an explicit prefix tree, GenMol fragment remasking with a corpus-trained discrete denoiser completes masked contexts, and DST: gradient-guided construction through relaxed scaffolding trees follows structural surrogate gradients. MAX-MIN Ant System over a molecular construction grammar reinforces construction-action pheromones; it has no persistent continuous particle trajectories. The supplied cluster history is empty. The refuted NF-BO observation n-77c41c9bc036 concerns loss of exact token reconstruction after flow adaptation. This proposal freezes its representation and requires scored position-to-molecule provenance without assuming an exact inverse; latent decoding plateaus nevertheless remain a relevant unresolved risk. I fixed the particle-swarm anchor after reviewing the catalogues and bound methods, before locating its external source.
method_proposal.first_improvement_direction: If the successful root shows large decoded structural jumps accompanied by repeated losses relative to particle personal bests and few later incumbent gains, first test posterior-guided step lengths along the existing velocity directions. Fit a molecular fingerprint GP using accepted observations from the current objective. For each proposed direction, sample fresh scalar positions along its line segment, decode them, and use a joint posterior function draw over those generated molecules to select a step for evaluation. Keep the decoder, velocity-direction rule and best-memory update fixed; record the actual selected displacement for subsequent inertia. No objective labels are assigned to unqueried decodes. This imports the one-dimensional posterior-sampling line-search principle from [BayeSQP, Section 4.3](https://proceedings.neurips.cc/paper_files/paper/2025/file/564ccf9de3a2a959d3d338889bad9d88-Paper-Conference.pdf), identified in the cross-domain catalogue. Replacing its SQP direction with a swarm velocity and modeling decoded structures is an inferred transfer, not its full algorithm. Log selected step lengths, chronological predictive calibration and personal-best improvement rates, and require improved final Top-1 evidence for retention. The supplied NF-BO observation reports optimistic predictive miscalibration, so useful guidance cannot be assumed merely because this added GP returns uncertainty. No supplied observation yet establishes a swarm-specific step-length bottleneck.
method_proposal.method_name: Molecule Swarm Optimization with persistent latent velocities
method_proposal.method_thesis: Anchor the method in Molecule Swarm Optimization: each particle keeps its latent position, velocity and best observed position, and moves through inertia plus independent stochastic attractions toward its personal best and the swarm's best. [Winter et al., Methods 2.2-2.4](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6836962/) describe this molecular use of particle swarm optimization. For our adaptation, train a compact SELFIES VAE solely on the permitted unlabeled corpus, freeze its encoder and deterministic decoder, and start each objective with clean swarm memories. Encodings of supplied molecules provide starting geometry; their scores initialize attractors only when decoding preserves canonical molecular identity. Otherwise establish scored attractors from actual generated evaluations, never from mislabeled reconstructions. Generate fresh latent positions through particle motion and decode new complete molecules. Locally retry stochastic motion for invalid or duplicate outcomes until the announced batch is filled. Match accepted feedback to the exact generating position before updating personal and shared bests; each batch uses only resolved memories. The corpus supplies a generator, never a molecule library for ranking or retrieval. The hypothesis is that persistent individual trajectories explore alternatives while shared successful locations redirect them quickly enough to improve the mean of independent final Top-1 scores. This uses the provided scalar objective directly, without additional desirability terms. Useful latent geometry and rapid transfer of discoveries between particles remain empirical prerequisites. The published model and evaluation scale do not establish those prerequisites under the permitted preparation and scarce feedback.

references.citation: Robin Winter, Floriane Montanari, Andreas Steffen, Hans Briem, Frank Noe, and Djork-Arne Clevert. Efficient multi-objective molecular optimization in a continuous latent space. Chemical Science 10, 8016-8024, 2019. Methods 2.2-2.4 describe particle memory, velocity updates and molecular decoding; the proposed root adapts this mechanism to independent scalar feedback.

Paul Brunzema and Sebastian Trimpe. BayeSQP: Bayesian Optimization through Sequential Quadratic Programming. NeurIPS 2025. Section 4.3 describes posterior-sampling line search, the mechanism motivating the conditional first improvement.

method_proposal.differentiation: The closest bound lineage is Simulated annealing through de novo molecular graph walks because both continue molecular edit trajectories. Annealing randomly proposes a neighbor and applies temperature-dependent acceptance after scoring. MolDQN selects the next edit through a learned continuation-value estimate and learns across transitions with Bellman backups; a worse accepted molecule can become a deliberate intermediate state. This changes action proposal and temporal credit assignment, not an acceptance constant. Mol GA: rank-selected de novo graph evolution and Genetic GFN: reciprocal learning between a flow policy and graph search use breeding populations; neither learns this finite-horizon action-value controller. Augmented Hill-Climb with a corpus-trained SMILES policy learns sequence likelihoods, ChemTS: UCT-guided SMILES prefix search with a frozen rollout prior traverses a prefix tree, GenMol fragment remasking with a corpus-trained discrete denoiser samples masked completions, and MAX-MIN Ant System over a molecular construction grammar reinforces construction components. DST: gradient-guided construction through relaxed scaffolding trees differentiates an immediate structural surrogate, rather than backing up future edit returns. COWBOYS: GP-conditioned de novo latent sampling, NF-BO: invertible sequence-flow search with token-adaptive latent proposals, CMA-ES: covariance adaptation through a frozen molecular decoder, and Molecule Swarm Optimization with persistent latent velocities move through learned continuous representations. This root acts directly on graphs. The supplied cluster history is empty, with no refuted MolDQN family to reconcile. Observation n-bd0cbfe35fa3 reports low reconstruction in the tested CMA-ES representation; avoiding a decoder removes that particular prerequisite, but does not establish a Q-learning advantage. MolDQN was fixed after reviewing the catalogues and bound methods, before its external source was located.
method_proposal.first_improvement_direction: If the successful root records delayed episode improvements but its exploration repeatedly changes direction through independent random actions, first add episode-consistent randomized value functions. Train independently initialized Q-heads with persistent bootstrap masks on accepted replay and head-specific target networks; select one head at episode start and keep its identity through that episode. Preserve graph operators, reward, horizon, replay records and the underlying double-Q update. [Osband et al., Sections 2-3](https://arxiv.org/html/1602.04621v2) supplies this temporally extended exploration mechanism. Mining the cross-domain catalogue also identifies the related principle in [PS-BAX, Algorithm 1](https://proceedings.neurips.cc/paper_files/paper/2024/file/f3c8bfcc9c2bc13a0f141cb58afc6e5a-Paper-Conference.pdf): run an algorithm under one sampled function. Applying that principle to a bootstrapped continuation-value controller is an inference; these heads are not exact GP posterior draws and the full PS-BAX acquisition is not imported. Measure actual head disagreement, persistent head use, realized delayed gains and final Top-1 evidence. More disagreement or longer trajectories alone cannot justify retention. No supplied observation currently establishes this MolDQN exploration bottleneck.
method_proposal.method_name: MolDQN: Bellman-guided de novo graph-edit episodes
method_proposal.method_thesis: Anchor the root in MolDQN's value-based control of molecular edits: learn future action returns from scored transitions and choose subsequent graph modifications with a deep Q-network. [Zhou et al., Sections 2.1, 2.2 and 2.5](https://arxiv.org/html/1810.08678v3) describe finite molecular edit episodes, fingerprint features and double Q-learning. Our adaptation starts short episodes from task-local scored molecules and samples fresh valence-aware atom and bond edits at each state. A compact Q-network takes current and successor fingerprints, remaining episode depth and the episode's best observed score. Use a single Q-function with epsilon-greedy action selection in the root. Evaluate only selected new whole molecules; values assigned to unselected successors are predictions. Advance each trajectory after its matched feedback, even when the new molecule scores worse. For Top-1 alignment, use reward max(previous_episode_best, new_score) minus previous_episode_best and undiscounted finite-horizon backups: accumulated reward equals improvement in that episode's best score. This reward adaptation is our inference, not the paper's original reward. Train immediately from accepted transition replay using double-Q target selection and a lagged target network, with zero continuation value at episode termination. Retain all accepted intermediate molecules in the task incumbent archive. Interleave episodes according to announced batches, and generate further edits to replace invalid or duplicate proposals. Each decision samples an evolving neighborhood; no corpus pool, complete-molecule retrieval or fixed candidate enumeration is involved. No pretrained generator or external labels are required, and every objective starts with clean learning state. The hypothesis is that learned lookahead identifies useful edit sequences, including temporary score losses, quickly enough to raise the mean of independent final Top-1 scores. Learning useful continuation values from scarce transitions is unproven; the paper's much larger training regime does not establish this transfer.

references.citation: Zhenpeng Zhou, Steven Kearnes, Li Li, Richard N. Zare, and Patrick Riley. Optimization of Molecules via Deep Reinforcement Learning. Scientific Reports 9, 10752, 2019; arXiv:1810.08678v3. Sections 2.1, 2.2 and 2.5 support the molecular edit and double-Q anchor.

Ian Osband, Charles Blundell, Alexander Pritzel, and Benjamin Van Roy. Deep Exploration via Bootstrapped DQN. NeurIPS 2016; arXiv:1602.04621v2. Sections 2-3 describe bootstrap heads, separate target networks and episode-consistent value-function selection.

Chu Xin Cheng, Raul Astudillo, Thomas Desautels, and Yisong Yue. Practical Bayesian Algorithm Execution via Posterior Sampling. NeurIPS 2024. Algorithm 1 motivates the related sampled-function execution principle considered for the conditional improvement.

method_proposal.differentiation: The closest bound lineage is DST: gradient-guided construction through relaxed scaffolding trees. Both optimize a structural predictor, but DST ascends continuous tree relaxations and samples their realization afterward. This method jointly chooses integer atom, bond and attachment variables while enforcing the descriptor equations inside the construction problem. It therefore changes the proposal mechanism, rather than the predictor's kernel or an ascent constant. Observation n-0e1f7686dea8 reports that positive relaxed gains can become negative assembled predicted gains; the proposed formulation directly tests that realization bottleneck, while leaving surrogate error as a separate risk. Mol GA: rank-selected de novo graph evolution and Genetic GFN: reciprocal learning between a flow policy and graph search use genetic offspring. Simulated annealing through de novo molecular graph walks uses temperature-dependent state transitions, and MolDQN: Bellman-guided de novo graph-edit episodes learns continuation values for edit actions. None solves the coupled graph-construction program. COWBOYS: GP-conditioned de novo latent sampling, NF-BO: invertible sequence-flow search with token-adaptive latent proposals, CMA-ES: covariance adaptation through a frozen molecular decoder, and Molecule Swarm Optimization with persistent latent velocities move through learned latent representations. Augmented Hill-Climb with a corpus-trained SMILES policy samples reward-adapted sequences; ChemTS: UCT-guided SMILES prefix search with a frozen rollout prior traverses a prefix tree; GenMol fragment remasking with a corpus-trained discrete denoiser samples inpainted fragments; MAX-MIN Ant System over a molecular construction grammar samples pheromone-guided actions. The supplied cluster history is empty, so there is no refuted mixed-integer construction family to revisit. I fixed mixed-integer inverse molecular design after reviewing the catalogues and bound methods, before locating its external source. The bounded local construction and online maximization loop are adaptations, not a claim to reproduce the paper's full workflow.
method_proposal.first_improvement_direction: If the successful root repeatedly favors similar descriptor combinations while coefficient estimates remain unstable and incumbent gains diminish, first replace its point-estimate construction objective with sampled linear objectives. Form a Gaussian coefficient posterior from accepted task-local observations with a posterior mean matching the root's ridge fit, draw one coefficient vector per construction, and optimize that sampled function with the existing graph program. Hold descriptors, context selection and chemical constraints fixed. This imports the optimization specialization of [PS-BAX, Section 3](https://proceedings.neurips.cc/paper_files/paper/2024/file/f3c8bfcc9c2bc13a0f141cb58afc6e5a-Paper-Conference.pdf), identified in the cross-domain catalogue: execute the target optimizer under a posterior function draw. Here the optimizer constructs fresh graphs, and a bounded solve gives approximate sampled-function optimization rather than a claimed exact global maximizer. Measure whether posterior draws change constructed descriptor combinations, whether chronological uncertainty predicts subsequent errors, and whether the accepted molecules improve incumbents. Retention requires improved final Top-1 evidence. The supplied DST observation establishes predictive error in another structural optimizer, but does not establish this root's coefficient-uncertainty bottleneck or show that posterior sampling fixes model misspecification.
method_proposal.method_name: Inverse-QSAR: mixed-integer de novo molecular construction
method_proposal.method_thesis: Anchor the method in inverse-QSAR through coupled linear regression and mixed-integer graph construction. [Zhu et al., Sections 1, 3 and 4](https://www.imrpress.com/journal/FBL/27/6/10.31083/j.fbl2706188) encode both a molecular descriptor function and a learned predictor in a program that constructs a graph satisfying structural specifications. Our benchmark adaptation fits a regularized linear score model only to the current objective's accepted observations, using atom-type, degree and typed-bond counts that can be represented exactly by integer constraints. For each proposal, take a scored molecule, choose a bounded editable peripheral region and retain its connected surrounding context. Represent replacement atom identities, bond orders and attachment choices as discrete variables, with connectivity, valence and descriptor-consistency constraints. Maximize the fitted scalar prediction over these variables instead of solving the paper's fixed target-interval problem. A feasible integer assignment supplies the new molecular graph directly. Validate the actual graph and recompute its descriptors before submission; exclude repeated assignments and retry construction when canonical identity is duplicate or invalid. Vary contexts and editable regions as feedback accumulates, and continue construction until the announced batch is filled. Use bounded subproblems and feasible solver incumbents rather than requiring a proof of global optimality for every proposal. The root needs no generative checkpoint or external labels. It constructs atom and bond combinations, without a corpus molecule pool, stored-fragment retrieval or the paper's subsequent isomer-enumeration stage. Each objective starts with clean scored and fitted state. The hypothesis is that jointly enforcing realizable structure while optimizing a task-local prediction concentrates evaluations on improving molecules and raises the mean of independent final Top-1 scores. Exact descriptor realization cannot compensate for an inaccurate predictor; both predictive usefulness and sufficient construction throughput remain unproven.

references.citation: Jianshen Zhu, Naveed Ahmed Azam, Kazuya Haraguchi, Liang Zhao, Hiroshi Nagamochi, and Tatsuya Akutsu. An Inverse QSAR Method Based on Linear Regression and Integer Programming. Frontiers in Bioscience-Landmark 27(6), 188, 2022. Sections 1, 3 and 4 describe coupled predictor, descriptor and chemical-graph constraints.

Chu Xin Cheng, Raul Astudillo, Thomas Desautels, and Yisong Yue. Practical Bayesian Algorithm Execution via Posterior Sampling. NeurIPS 2024. Section 3 describes sampled-function algorithm execution and its maximization specialization, motivating the conditional first improvement.

method_proposal.differentiation: Compared against all fourteen bound methods. 'Mol GA: rank-selected de novo graph evolution' uses evolutionary graph operators; this proposal makes its search region depend explicitly on negative examples. 'COWBOYS: GP-conditioned de novo latent sampling' uses posterior-conditioned latent sampling, whereas RACOS constructs categorical exclusion regions without a score-regression posterior. 'Augmented Hill-Climb with a corpus-trained SMILES policy' learns sequence likelihoods from elites; RACOS has no sequence-policy training. 'ChemTS: UCT-guided SMILES prefix search with a frozen rollout prior' maintains a prefix-search tree; this method samples complete frames from fresh classifiers. 'GenMol fragment remasking with a corpus-trained discrete denoiser' learns conditional fragment reconstruction; RACOS learns which coordinates must be fixed to exclude observed negatives and samples free coordinates directly. 'NF-BO: invertible sequence-flow search with token-adaptive latent proposals' requires a learned invertible latent mapping and Bayesian acquisition; neither mechanism is present here. 'Genetic GFN: reciprocal learning between a flow policy and graph search' couples trajectory-flow learning to evolutionary replay; RACOS has neither component. 'Simulated annealing through de novo molecular graph walks' advances chains through temperature-dependent acceptance; RACOS retains labeled examples and reconstructs a region for each proposal. 'DST: gradient-guided construction through relaxed scaffolding trees' differentiates a relaxed molecular objective; RACOS uses discrete classifications. 'CMA-ES: covariance adaptation through a frozen molecular decoder' learns a continuous Gaussian search distribution; RACOS has no learned latent geometry or covariance update. 'MAX-MIN Ant System over a molecular construction grammar' reinforces construction actions with pheromones; RACOS uses explicit negative-exclusion constraints. 'Molecule Swarm Optimization with persistent latent velocities' retains particle trajectories and personal/global attractors; RACOS has no particle motion. 'MolDQN: Bellman-guided de novo graph-edit episodes' learns multistep action values; RACOS directly classifies complete observed constructions. 'Inverse-QSAR: mixed-integer de novo molecular construction' optimizes a learned numerical objective through coupled integer constraints; RACOS samples categorical regions without a numerical predictor or combinatorial solver. The brief contains no Mechanism Clusters, so no cluster has already refuted this family. Evidence in n-9bd1200edbf6 and n-bd0cbfe35fa3 reports poor molecular reconstruction through their learned latent decoders; direct verified SELFIES encoding changes that dependency, without implying those lineages are refuted or that RACOS already works. The exact token-inversion failure in n-77c41c9bc036 is also avoided as an architectural dependency, rather than being treated as evidence against all latent methods.
method_proposal.first_improvement_direction: After a successful root, first investigate representation-order dependence: if coordinate restrictions vary while decoded neighborhoods repeatedly overlap and incumbent improvement stalls, rebuild RACOS classifiers using equivalent randomized molecular serialization views. Before each classifier construction, select one verified randomized-SMILES-to-SELFIES encoding per labeled molecule, retaining exactly one weighted record and its existing score. Require canonical identity before reusing a label. Keep molecular labels, ranking, region-shrinking rule, free-coordinate limit, and sampling mechanism fixed. This transfers the observation-equivalence principle discussed in Section 2.2 of [Bardou et al., Symmetry-Aware Bayesian Optimization via Max Kernels](https://arxiv.org/html/2509.25051v1); using equivalent coordinate views for RACOS is my proposed adaptation, not that paper's GP algorithm. Measure whether equivalent views change retained token positions and decoded proposal neighborhoods, then whether newly evaluated molecules more often beat their exemplars and improve task incumbents. Retain the change only if it improves the five-task final Top-1 mean; representation variety alone is insufficient. The existing latent-reconstruction observations motivate the root's direct representation, but do not yet establish this serialization-order bottleneck.

method_tags.acquisition_mechanism: stochastic region generation with a broader construction-space sampling component
method_tags.learning_mechanism: objective-rank positive/negative labeling followed by randomized coordinate shrinking
method_tags.proposal_mechanism: uniform de novo token sampling inside randomized positive-exemplar regions that exclude observed negatives

method_proposal.method_thesis: The anchor is RACOS, selected before locating the primary source. Its categorical form chooses a positively labeled exemplar, randomly fixes coordinates to that exemplar until negative examples are excluded, further restricts the number of free coordinates, and samples the resulting region; a broader uniform component preserves exploration. Each proposal can use a newly randomized classifier. These are the mechanisms described by Yu, Qian and Hu in [Derivative-Free Optimization via Classification](https://ojs.aaai.org/index.php/AAAI/article/view/10289/10148). My molecular adaptation applies this process directly to bounded categorical SELFIES frames, with removable padding that permits changes in molecular length. Preparation extracts only a construction-token alphabet from the permitted unlabeled corpus. There is no trained molecular encoder or decoder. Initial labeled molecules become exemplars only after encoding and decoding reproduce their canonical identity. For generated molecules, retain the actual sampled frame, its decoded canonical molecule, and the score actually returned for that molecule. Rank the current objective's observed molecules into a high-score positive group and a lower-score negative group; use these labels to construct exclusion regions. Free token positions are newly sampled and decoded into complete molecules, checked, canonicalized, and deduplicated. Rebuild a region or use the broad generation component when a region cannot provide a fresh molecule. These are online constructions from token primitives, not retrieval or enumeration of complete molecules. After each announced batch receives real feedback, refresh the labeled sets and incumbent; all pending proposals use only previously observed scores. Each objective starts with clean task-specific state and follows the protocol's supplied batch and resource limits. The hypothesis is that explicitly excluding observed poor token configurations will concentrate new molecular proposals around combinations that improve the incumbent with few labels. Success is the mean of the five independent final Top-1 scores. Region exclusion, validity, or classification accuracy alone cannot establish that hypothesis. Positional token restrictions may have weak structural meaning, and multiple frames can decode to the same molecule; exact representation checks address score provenance but do not establish useful search geometry.

references.citation: Yang Yu, Hong Qian and Yi-Qi Hu. Derivative-Free Optimization via Classification. AAAI 2016, pp. 2286–2292. Algorithms 1 and 2 describe classifier-guided sampling and randomized coordinate shrinking, including discrete domains.

Anthony Bardou, Antoine Gonon, Aryan Ahadinia and Patrick Thiran. Symmetry-Aware Bayesian Optimization via Max Kernels. arXiv:2509.25051, 2025. Section 2.2 describes reusing objective observations under verified invariant transformations; the RACOS serialization-view transfer is proposed here.

Node n-77c41c9bc036 reports failed exact token inversion after flow adaptation. These motivate checking direct molecular score provenance and do not establish RACOS performance.

method_proposal.differentiation: The closest bound method is 'Simulated annealing through de novo molecular graph walks'. Its trajectory uses temperature-dependent probabilistic acceptance; tabu search uses explicit history-dependent structural prohibitions and chooses the best observed admissible neighbor even when all sampled neighbors are worse. This changes the search paradigm, rather than a cooling constant or graph-edit parameter. 'Mol GA: rank-selected de novo graph evolution' maintains breeding and survivor populations; this root follows a current-state trajectory with expiring move restrictions. 'MolDQN: Bellman-guided de novo graph-edit episodes' learns action values and multistep returns; tabu memory records recent structural moves without a Bellman model. 'RACOS: negative-exclusion sampling of de novo SELFIES regions' learns categorical regions from positive and negative score classes; tabu restrictions depend on recency and move reversals, not negative-example classification. 'MAX-MIN Ant System over a molecular construction grammar' reinforces reusable construction actions with pheromones; this root temporarily prohibits reversal attributes while walking from a complete graph. 'COWBOYS: GP-conditioned de novo latent sampling' and 'NF-BO: invertible sequence-flow search with token-adaptive latent proposals' generate through latent probabilistic models and Bayesian guidance; neither mechanism defines this root. 'CMA-ES: covariance adaptation through a frozen molecular decoder' and 'Molecule Swarm Optimization with persistent latent velocities' adapt continuous population motion through a decoder; this root has direct graph transitions and no latent geometry. 'Augmented Hill-Climb with a corpus-trained SMILES policy' updates a neural sequence policy, while 'Genetic GFN: reciprocal learning between a flow policy and graph search' couples learned flow probabilities with genetic refinement; tabu search has neither neural reward learning nor population exchange. 'ChemTS: UCT-guided SMILES prefix search with a frozen rollout prior' directs prefix-tree exploration, and 'GenMol fragment remasking with a corpus-trained discrete denoiser' reconstructs masked fragments; this root uses explicit structural edits and walk memory. 'DST: gradient-guided construction through relaxed scaffolding trees' and 'Inverse-QSAR: mixed-integer de novo molecular construction' generate by optimizing numerical surrogates under continuous or integer representations; this root evaluates sampled admissible neighbors directly. The supplied cluster history is empty, so no Mechanism Cluster refutes this family. Node n-4fa9546e559e reports that most graph offspring failed to beat their generating parents, motivating measurement of useful walk transitions without establishing a tabu-specific bottleneck. Node n-3ab6a944e3dd shows that frequent reuse of reinforced construction components need not produce incumbent gains; this reinforces the need to distinguish memory activation from actual Top-1 benefit. Neither observation proves that structural reversals are currently limiting search.
method_proposal.first_improvement_direction: If the root succeeds and its restrictions affect novel moves, but most evaluated admissible neighbors still fail to improve the current state or incumbent, first add Bayesian selection among surplus neighbors freshly generated by the same tabu-constrained graph process. Transfer the fully Bayesian tree-kernel model and integrated upper-confidence acquisition from [Boyne et al., BARK](https://arxiv.org/html/2503.05574v2), fitting only accepted task-local scores on molecular fingerprints and structural counts. Average the acquisition over sampled tree kernels, then select the announced batch from these transient de novo neighbors. Keep the graph operators, move attributes, tenure rule and real-feedback state transition unchanged. This imports BARK's uncertainty over tree structure; its global mixed-integer acquisition solver and finite-compound experiments are not imported. The molecular neighborhood application is a proposed transfer, and fitting must remain within the supplied runtime. Record predictions before observations, posterior calibration and selection changes, then assess whether selected neighbors produce more current-state and incumbent improvements. Retain the addition only with improved final Top-1 evidence. The graph-offspring weakness in n-4fa9546e559e is a relevant precedent, but the root must first demonstrate the corresponding limitation itself.
method_proposal.method_name: Tabu search: de novo graph walks with expiring structural prohibitions

method_tags.acquisition_mechanism: direct evaluation of fresh admissible graph neighbors
method_tags.learning_mechanism: accepted-score best-neighbor state updates and short-term structural move memory

method_proposal.method_thesis: The anchor is the basic tabu-search procedure in Section 2 of [Glover, Tabu Search—Part I](https://leeds-faculty.colorado.edu/glover/TS%20-%20Part%20I-ORSA-aw.pdf), fixed before locating this external source. It chooses the best available admissible move, including a worsening move, while temporarily prohibiting reversals through short-term attribute memory. My molecular adaptation starts from the best supplied observation and maintains one current molecular graph, its true score, an independent best-observed archive, and expiring structural restrictions. At each feedback step, stochastically generate a new neighborhood through atom and bond edits, additions, deletions and chemically checked ring changes. Define move attributes from presence/absence changes of canonical local subgraphs around the edited region. After selecting a move, temporarily forbid a bounded record of its inverse attribute changes. These restrictions must apply to different canonical molecules sharing the affected local chemistry, so they can alter search beyond the protocol's mandatory whole-molecule duplicate rejection. Generate valid, canonical-unique, admissible neighbors until the announced batch is filled, then submit them directly without a learned score predictor. Only after real feedback choose the highest-scoring accepted neighbor as the next current graph, even when it scores below the current graph; retain the best score seen anywhere. Age restrictions by completed walk steps. If restrictions prevent sufficient fresh generation, release the oldest restrictions only as needed and record that release. This root uses the basic tabu form without an aspiration rule requiring unknown candidate scores. Preparation needs no learned model or corpus molecule store. Each objective restarts the same task-agnostic procedure with clean labeled and tabu state, and every proposed structure is generated online from the evolving current graph. The hypothesis is that an aggressive observed-neighbor choice combined with temporary structural reversal restrictions can move through useful intermediate structures and reach higher scoring molecular regions within the supplied feedback schedule. Activation requires restrictions to veto otherwise valid novel structural moves and thereby influence later current states. That diagnostic is insufficient by itself: success is the mean of the five independent final Top-1 scores. Overbroad attributes may suppress productive chemistry, while overly specific attributes may never affect novel proposals; the root must expose both possibilities.

references.citation: Fred Glover. Tabu Search—Part I. ORSA Journal on Computing 1(3), 190–206, 1989. Section 2 describes best admissible moves, inverse-move memory, partial attributes and releasing older restrictions.

Toby Boyne, Jose Pablo Folch, Robert Matthew Lee, Behrang Shafei and Ruth Misener. BARK: A Fully Bayesian Tree Kernel for Black-box Optimization. ICML 2025, PMLR 267:5291–5318. Sections 5 and 6 describe posterior tree-kernel inference and integrated acquisition; their molecular tabu-neighborhood use is proposed here.

Brief node n-4fa9546e559e reports weak average graph-offspring improvement despite activated evolution. Node n-3ab6a944e3dd reports extensive reinforced-component reuse with few later incumbent gains. These motivate score-linked activation checks, without establishing a structural-reversal failure or tabu-search advantage.

L01.method_thesis: The representative n-fc2c108a5253 is scored molecular-graph evolution with a task-local fingerprint Gaussian process that selects which freshly bred offspring receive oracle calls. Preparation writes deterministic operator and selector configuration only. Each objective process starts from its supplied scored molecules, keeps an all-accepted archive and a bounded score-ranked breeding population, fits the posterior to accepted labels, breeds a temporary surplus of connected novel graphs, computes their joint conditional distribution, and emits masked maximizers of independent correlated function draws. Accepted feedback both updates the archive and competes for survival, so admitted offspring can breed in the next batch. The implementation retains the root n-4fa9546e559e graph operators, parent quantiles and greedy survival; its added mechanism is learned selection before evaluation. The representative has complete seeds 0, 1 and 2 with macro mean 0.5443738005952443 and population SD 0.013310111166991866. Activation is confirmed, but only the original seed supplies a paired direct-parent comparison. Curate c-1e7b33da25 records replicated uncertainty-dependent choices without isolated evidence for uncertainty's marginal score contribution. Only 565 of 4350 selected offspring beat their generating best parent across the three runs. The blueprint therefore separates state, graph production, prediction and evaluation allocation, and closes by testing their interactions. The graph is a one-iteration data-dependency graph: accepted feedback from an emitted batch is an external input to the next iteration of feedback_memory, not a same-iteration cycle. Integration is a cross-cutting concern over that real closed loop. The frozen settings permit 24 Children in waves of four, hence six waves: one each for memory, posterior, allocation and integration, and two for graph production, whose coupled chemical edit and admissibility mechanisms have substantial documented headroom.

L03.method_thesis: Representative n-15499bde2e65 is an Augmented Hill-Climb molecular language policy with bounded historical elite replay. Preparation trains a recurrent next-token SMILES prior on the supplied unlabeled corpus, selects a checkpoint by a fixed unlabeled holdout and publishes only weights and metadata. Each objective clones an independent trainable policy from that verified frozen prior. Accepted observations retain their actual sampled serialization under a canonical molecular identity. Each nonempty batch contributes its highest-scoring half, joined by a uniform sample of earlier accepted elites from a score-ranked memory capped at 32. The policy fits each selected sequence toward frozen-prior log likelihood plus 60 times its accepted reward, using equal row weights and bounded clipped Adam updates. It then generates complete SMILES by ancestral token sampling; RDKit validation and canonical novelty checks refill a full announced batch directly from the policy. There is no surrogate, graph-edit generator, candidate-library ranking or randomized-SMILES training in this representative. The source comparison with current-only root n-4552e16d798a leaves preparation, model, sampler, ingestion and protocol functions unchanged; replay changes objective initialization and training membership/update accounting. The representative completes three seeds with macro mean 0.5075540530185733 and population SD 0.01151827890752029, but its paired root comparison remains seed 0 only. Curate c-a5a5c8a507 confirms replay gradient contributions in all 280 eligible new updates and reduced historical target error in 278; 328 of their 1400 historical exposures nevertheless have mathematically unattainable positive log-probability targets. The Layers therefore isolate prior learning, accepted-memory membership, reward-to-policy adaptation and direct generation/admission before integration. The dependency graph unrolls one learning-and-proposal iteration: evaluator feedback returns to accepted_elite_memory in the next iteration, not through a cyclic same-iteration edge. Memory commitment occurs after optimization in the implementation but depends on accepted elite records, not learned parameters. The frozen 24-Child cap and four-Child waves allow six waves: one each for prior, memory, generation and integration, with two for adaptation to address target attainability and productive current/history learning as separate possible mechanisms.

L07.method_thesis: The implemented method is a reciprocal neural/graph optimizer with posterior selection of graph offspring. Unlabeled SMILES train a recurrent prior; every objective starts a fresh adaptable copy and fresh accepted-only memory. After each feedback message, exact accepted molecular trajectories train the policy through trajectory balance, a learned log normalizer and categorical regularization toward the unchanged prior. The current cycle emits one ancestral policy batch directly, then two graph batches. Accepted policy molecules refresh the scored population; the first graph batch protects a real descendant of a fresh policy parent. Connected-fragment crossover and atom/bond edits produce a temporary novel offspring pool. A task-local Morgan/Tanimoto Gaussian posterior fits all earlier accepted labels, predicts the pool jointly, and an independent correlated function draw chooses each remaining evaluation slot. Only real accepted emissions enter survivors, replay and later posterior fits; unselected pool molecules remain unlabeled. Accepted graph descendants therefore influence subsequent policy sampling and later breeding. The current representative n-cc2d839e347b confirms both selection and reciprocal feedback across its complete replicas, while its supplied analysis leaves weak parent-beating yield, predictive calibration and chemically credible core coverage unresolved. Its direct-submission ancestor n-39550a3f15d7 supplies only the reported screening comparison; replicated component activation does not isolate a replicated score benefit. The six Layers below group preparation, neural learning, graph generation, conditional modeling, allocation and cross-component validation. Dependency edges describe the forward data dependencies within a feedback boundary and their development prerequisites. The runtime feedback loop is unrolled across boundaries: emitted molecules are scored outside the candidate, and the next accepted message becomes the next boundary input. Integration is a cross-cutting attribution Layer, not an extra molecular transformation.

L16.method_thesis: L16 is a task-local best-admissible-neighbor graph walk with short-term structural memory. The supplied representative n-9f7c7ec50039 prepares a fixed configuration without consuming a corpus or training a model, starts at the highest-scoring supplied molecular observation, and keeps separate current-state, best-observed, proposed-identity and pending-feedback records. From a Kekule representation of the current graph it samples atom substitutions, bond-order changes, path additions/deletions/insertions/contractions and ring opening/closure. Sanitization, connectivity, radical and atom-domain checks precede the repaired parse-and-reserialize identity normalization and canonical novelty check. For each valid fresh neighbor it computes signed occurrence changes of canonical rooted radius-one motifs. An active restriction vetoes the neighbor only when both inverse signs match restrictions carrying the same selected-transition provenance; one-sign and cross-transition-only matches remain admissible. The first complete announced batch of admissible neighbors is submitted directly, with no score predictor or acquisition model. Real accepted scores join the exact pending proposal. The highest-scoring accepted neighbor becomes the next current graph even on a worsening move; equal maxima currently use the canonical lexical tie rule. Every accepted observation also updates the independent best archive. A completed transition ages memory, expires entries and installs a bounded, sign-balanced selection of inverse attributes, with latest-transition overlap refresh. Documented generation obstruction can release the globally oldest live restriction; an empty accepted batch does not move or age the walk. The workflow graph below unrolls one proposal/feedback iteration. Its next current graph, seen set, archive and live-memory state return through the declared workflow boundary as inputs to the following iteration; these time-delayed feedback edges are not same-iteration dependency edges. Memory update operations belong to the memory component even when invoked after the feedback component emits its selected-transition event. The complete representative evidence and clusters c-c24599cabf and c-cfe57a29f0 establish real memory-dependent decisions and recovery of the recorded identity mismatch. They leave productive neighborhood chemistry, the score contribution of the surviving vetoes and plateau navigation unresolved. Reactive heteroatom bonds, unusual sulfur environments, dense closures and unspecified stereochemistry motivate chemistry-aware local research without supplying objective-specific answers. Passive alternative-batch traces are allocation diagnostics, not scored alternative trajectories. The identity repair remains a correctness invariant throughout Development.

applicability_summary: Evidence covers complete matched seeds 0, 1 and 2 against n-15499bde2e65 on five tasks with 300 evaluations per task and batches of ten; macro mean 0.498445, population SD 0.009303, paired seed changes [-0.017951, +0.000123, -0.009499]; supplied current eligibility is rejected and task_safe is false, which this report does not alter.

Exactly one uniformly selected eligible internal content embedding is zeroed per sequence while original tokens, targets and uniform loss remain intact; all 7,613,952 training-sequence exposures per prior and the three target/mask receipts are reproduced, with clean holdout selection and intact-input online computation preserved.

Across full 4,096-row holdouts, erased-downstream NLL falls from 1.00417 to 0.53006 and the erasure penalty from 0.53933 to 0.05658, while clean full-sequence NLL worsens from 0.56458 to 0.57213; the absolute probe improvement is not merely an artifact of degraded clean performance.

The probe retains all subsequent teacher-forced tokens, so it establishes missing-vector robustness rather than recovery from an incorrectly sampled token or invalid molecular graph; no online erasure or mistake-recovery mechanism is measured.

Raw validity falls from 90.43% to 89.27%, while fewer duplicates raise raw canonical novelty from 60.31% to 61.76%; zaleplon gains 0.03533 in task mean, but sitagliptin loses 0.08046 and declines in every seed.

Mostly conventional amide, amine and sulfonamide chemistry remains broadly plausible, yet extreme polar/lipophilic tails, missing favorable parental polar-ring/carbonyl families and absent configurations show that novelty and probe robustness do not ensure useful chemical coverage.

All actual alternate views pass canonical/isomeric identity, token-roundtrip and length checks, and a separate equivalent string stays outside training; fallback is unexercised and terminal exposures are excluded from subsequent-generation conclusions.

Frozen-prior sequence likelihood makes the same-identity augmented target spelling-dependent: alternate targets shift by about -47.86 on average, reducing positive unattainable targets from 461 to 64 on matched examples, so improved view fitting does not isolate representation-independent reward transfer.

Original-string error worsens from 144.14 to 152.33, raw validity falls from 90.43% to 87.24%, and duplicates fall from 30.11% to 14.07%; broader sampling and excluded-string transfer do not imply stronger endpoints or resolved chemical limitations.

The related c-cdeef82b5c definition explicitly concerns unlabeled prior preparation and original-string holdout selection; this online accepted-score replay experiment changes the supervision and intervention stage and is recorded separately without redefining that history.

summary.text: Round 8 confirms 2100 nonterminal accepted-identity-equivalent replay exposures and changed gradients in all 420 eligible updates, improving excluded-view target error from 202.59 to 169.07 in every session but weakening original-string support and lowering paired macro score by 0.014387, triggering the utility falsifier.

applicability_summary: Evidence covers complete matched seeds 0, 1 and 2 against n-9f7c7ec50039 on five tasks with 300 evaluations per task and batches of ten; macro mean 0.511159, population SD 0.026963, paired seed changes [+0.013487, +0.001052, -0.043817]; supplied current eligibility is rejected and task_safe is false, which this report does not alter.

The observed channel applies to the registered RDKit-perceived neutral, nonaromatic, single-bonded tetrahedral carbon centers; all 24 direct products assign a previously unspecified center, and relative CW/CCW tags are interpreted in current atom order rather than treated as fixed absolute R/S labels.

Both relative assignment orientations reach evaluation, but assigned-center inversion and opposite fully assigned pairs do not; unscored inversion menu opportunities cannot establish scored stereoisomer preference or universal score insensitivity.

Nine tied assignment neighbors become current states; the inherited motifs omit stereo, so these transitions age memory without installing inverse restrictions, providing a possible route to later trajectory changes rather than evidence of direct configurational score benefit.

Assignments persist through later edits and all identity joins remain correct, but the macro non-inferiority margin is missed; the 32 exact ties concern only actually evaluated partial-assignment comparisons, with complete multi-center stereo, sulfur chirality and E/Z geometry untested.

Partial labels leave reactive heteroatoms, unusual sulfur and dense bridged frameworks in place; unspecified remaining centers and unresolved geometric feasibility prevent interpreting this coverage as complete stereochemical or synthetic resolution.

summary.text: Round 7 confirms 24 evaluated carbon-configuration assignments preserving composition and connectivity and 488 emissions carrying assigned carbon centers, but every one of 32 evaluated same-graph partial-assignment pairs ties in score, no inversion is evaluated, and the paired macro change is -0.009759.

applicability_summary: The protected quantity is the first-order directional derivative of mean augmented-target loss for five fixed selected historical rows at the pre-step policy; it does not constrain finite loss, each historical row, all stored memory, prior-distribution likelihood or molecular reward.

Projection changes parameters while preserving proposed Adam moments and counters, with unchanged strings, rewards, targets, equal row weights, replay selection and frozen prior; all fifteen no-history initialization updates and first generated batches match the Parent exactly.

Nonterminal projections affect 381 of 420 history-bearing updates; 125 triggering corrections are below analytical resolution and are separate from 1,904 measurable corrections, while 99 terminal projections are excluded from subsequent-generation claims.

Historical MSE is lower than the proposed Adam state in 2,019 of 2,029 projected nonterminal steps, yet 1,807 still increase it relative to their own starting state; current MSE worsens against the proposal in 1,379 steps, demonstrating the finite-curvature and current-history tradeoffs left outside the first-order guarantee.

Historical group worsening falls to 118 of 420 updates versus Parent 131, but historical row worsening remains 837 of 2,100 versus 834 and positive historical targets remain in 607 exposures; group protection therefore does not demonstrate improved individual memory retention or useful generation.

All sessions finish, but macro deltas are -0.006076, -0.012316 and -0.041007 with supplied rejected eligibility; lower duplication and broader observed core coverage coexist with worse endpoints, and complete gradient vectors or parameter/RNG snapshots were not persisted for stronger reconstruction claims.
c-ea66577da3.stable_definition: First-order historical augmented-loss half-space projection of proposed molecular-policy Adam displacements while retaining optimizer moments and counters.

summary.text: Round 9 confirms that n-9297414147d2 projects 2,029 nonterminal Adam displacements, with all 1,904 analytically resolved corrections changing parameters and satisfying the historical-loss half-space, while improved historical fitting relative to the proposed step coexists with finite loss increases, current-fit tradeoffs and paired macro decline -0.019800 against n-06c043e9d303 in three negative seeds.

applicability_summary: Both variants learn only a scalar noise level from the contemporaneous ordered accepted archive under the inherited binary Morgan representation, Tanimoto kernel, unit amplitude, plug-in score normalization and correlated selector; this is distinct from changing fingerprint multiplicity or introducing posterior allocation.

The seven-level rule in n-9002c3d22369 tests fixed multipliers [0.25, 0.5, 1, 2, 4, 8, 16] around reference SD 0.05 and reuses the winning factor, while n-e6bce5cb59ec tests [1, 2, 4, 8, 16] and performs the final training factorization at the winner; their tie rules also differ, so their activation counts must not be treated as identical implementations.

The seven-level panel selects its smallest SD in 179 fits, its largest in 116 and the reference in one; the five-level panel retains the reference in 180 fits and selects the maximum in 116, establishing frequent boundary choices without evidence that extending either menu would improve search.

On the same actual emissions and earlier accepted archives, latent 1.96-SD coverage improves from 79.75% to 82.51% for the seven-level rule and from 79.68% to 82.44% for the five-level rule, with lower MSE but weaker within-batch rank association; noise-inclusive coverage reaches 89.91% and 89.84% through wider intervals and remains separate from latent uncertainty.

Likelihood selection models residual surrogate mismatch rather than demonstrated stochastic oracle noise, and better training likelihood or selected-stream coverage does not establish global calibration, improved discrimination among unscored alternatives or a whole-search score advantage.

In the five-level panel, a nearly flat early archive with scale 0.001 still yields an observed-score residual above 157 predicted SDs despite maximum standardized noise, identifying a score-unit scaling limitation that the tested bounded noise rule does not resolve.

Both variants have one improving and two declining seed macros and substantially greater endpoint dispersion than their Parent; the five-level rule preserves decoration and median trajectories exactly and gives 592 versus 593 best-parent beats, showing that posterior activation need not change every evaluated choice or improve useful offspring yield.

All likelihood trials and pool factorizations succeed at first jitter, leaving failure recovery and exact-tie behavior unexercised; passive same-data reconstructions do not isolate the value of individual changed decisions, the count-representation siblings are separate, and existing chemical liabilities remain.

summary.text: Round 10 confirms likelihood-selected noise in n-9002c3d22369 and n-e6bce5cb59ec, measurably changing 434 and 255 of their respective 435 fitted posteriors and improving matched selected-stream MSE and interval coverage, while within-batch ranking weakens and paired mean endpoint scores fall by 0.015961 and 0.017540 respectively.

applicability_summary: Evidence covers complete matched seeds 0, 1 and 2 against n-9f7c7ec50039 on five tasks with 300 evaluations per task and batches of ten; macro mean 0.517522, population SD 0.010113, paired seed changes [+0.004044, -0.024305, +0.010073]; supplied current eligibility is rejected and task_safe is true, which this report does not alter.

The gate uses one deterministic source shortest path and admits overlap with existing rings of zero atoms, one atom or exactly one old ring edge; it changes only the close_ring introduction channel and preserves other operators, source state, identity, memory and feedback.

Restricted closure emissions fall from 241 to zero; permitted evaluated closures include six ring-disjoint, three one-atom and 31 one-edge cases, with nine source beats and seven archive improvements, so selective suppression does not disable ring growth.

Molecules with an RDKit-perceived pair of rings sharing at least three atoms fall from 1,867/4,350 to 10/4,350 while mean ring-atom participation changes only from 62.89% to 61.70%; attempts per full batch rise from 12.15 to 12.83.

The removed Parent channel contained 37 source-improving and 19 selected closures, but rejected Child candidates have no labels; only single-bond allowed closures are evaluated, and alternative shortest-path or ring-basis invariance is not demonstrated.

DRD2 improves in mean while four other task means decline; reduced overlap neither removes inherited complexity nor establishes conformation or synthesis, and unusual sulfur, reactive halogen attachments and unspecified configurations persist.

nodes.hypothesis: Jointly fit the count-GP constant latent mean, positive signal variance and positive observation variance by exact accepted-archive marginal likelihood, then deliver that single fitted posterior coherently to the unchanged correlated Thompson selector.
nodes.finding:
All 435 joint fits moved the model and its predictive distribution, and 2,216 of 4,350 accepted choices strictly differed from the original GP under the same selection mask and random draw. Of these changed choices, 2,150 reached the next fit; 638 later produced 2,228 distinct accepted direct children. This was a fully exposed intervention, with all 15 sessions completing. On the same selected labels, MSE improved from 0.00810 to 0.00735 in aggregate and improved in every task/seed session. Ordering remained mixed: pair accuracy rose slightly from 0.67051 to 0.67247, while mean batch Spearman fell from 0.44131 to 0.44005; all three sitagliptin sessions worsened on both ranking measures. The fitted observation variance raised diagnostic noise-inclusive coverage from 76.60% to 89.95%, but latent coverage used to characterize allocation fell from 76.46% to 75.22%. More offspring beat their generating parents (763 versus 648), yet those parents and offspring had lower absolute scores. Positive gain mass fell from 17.2515 to 15.1509 and sequential incumbent gain from 5.8194 to 5.1026. Mean final score fell from 0.59645 to 0.54867, a matched difference of −0.04779 against the required +0.002. There were 4 endpoint wins and 11 losses; seed macro differences were −0.15366, +0.01987 and −0.00957, and population standard deviation rose from 0.03397 to 0.04206. The primary result includes the Parent’s late deco_hop breakthrough.

The experiment rules out lack of delivery as the explanation for this recipe’s failure: fitted models changed accepted molecules, later training and actual breeding. It also narrows the predictive bottleneck. Smaller same-label squared error and wider noise-inclusive intervals were insufficient for useful discovery; ordering did not improve consistently, and extra local wins came against weaker parents with smaller gains. The exact joint likelihood-fitting operation borrowed from the literature worked computationally, but its transfer to tiny, repeatedly fitted adaptive archives on the retained raw-count geometry did not improve endpoints. This does not test the source’s larger random-subset regression setting or identify a separate contribution from mean, signal or noise. Successful optimization also needs a limited reading: 97 fits stopped on function tolerance above the gradient tolerance, 11 reached the signal floor and 167 the noise floor. Seven early near-constant archives produced almost collapsed latent intervals covering none of their next 70 labels, even though noise-inclusive intervals covered 61; observation uncertainty is a different quantity from the latent uncertainty passed to selection. These are measured boundaries, not evidence for an automatic bounds or optimizer rescue. The molecular assessment likewise finds slightly more new cores without stronger typed-core descendant gains or independent leading families, alongside persistent stereochemical and local-geometry problems; fewer reactive attachments do not establish feasible chemistry or explain the score causally. The registered complete exposed miss ends this fixed joint-fit recipe. A future revision would require new evidence and planning; scalar attribution, mediation, broader molecular feasibility and the campaign’s reliable-gain goal remain open.

nodes.hypothesis: Remove all posterior-based influence on successful offspring allocation by selecting the first announced-batch-size valid unique candidates in inherited generation order from the fully generated pool, while retaining the complete accepted-only posterior computation and original draws passively.
nodes.finding:
All 435 successful batches evaluated the first ten members of a completed 160-member pool, with zero prefix-order violations or choices outside that prefix. The passive original sampler selected a different set in all 435 batches, and its sampled values strictly preferred another candidate on 4,317 of 4,350 generation-order masks. Thus the removal changed real evaluation choices under strong exposure. All 435 fits, full covariance factorizations and original normal arrays remained computed; the accepted-only feedback and identity-bound prediction joins passed. No natural numerical fallback or incomplete pool occurred.

Mean final Top-1 fell from 0.595670 to 0.471282, a paired change of -0.124388, well beyond the registered 0.002 loss scale. Seed macro changes were -0.134968, -0.105769 and -0.132426. All five task means declined. Thirteen of fifteen task-seed endpoints declined; zaleplon_mpo seeds zero and one improved by 0.019694 and 0.005802. Macro population deviation changed from 0.026593 to 0.014583. Correct removal and the predicted score loss support positive contribution from the composite selector in this exact full-pool search loop.

This closes a different question from the earlier count, residual and correlation controls: allocating evaluations using the complete predictive selector matters even when generation effort is held at the inherited full-pool boundary. The earlier selector addition also enlarged the pool and lacked a complete matched Parent panel, so it could not establish this conditional contrast. Local parent beats increased from 629 to 653, yet incumbent improvements fell from 258 to 163; adaptive local success is not a substitute for endpoint quality. The present loss does not apportion value among posterior means, counts, residual amplitude or correlation, and separate sibling losses cannot be added.

A plausible place to investigate the loss is how evaluation choices preserve useful chemical relationships across adaptive histories. The molecular report finds that generation-order output still reaches useful nitrile and aryl-amine alternatives, including both improved endpoints, while other streams move into densely connected heteroatom frameworks and miss strong Parent families. Reactive bonds, questionable ring geometry and unspecified stereochemistry persist. This concerns the evaluated distribution; it does not show that better alternatives were absent from the complete pools or identify a chemical mediator. Passive alternatives have no counterfactual scores.

Removing predictive influence is also different from removing computational cost: all surplus generation and model computations remain, and numerical failures would still use the inherited routes. No reduced-pool, compute-saving or optimizer-deletion conclusion follows. Actual recovery branches remain unexercised despite passing deterministic synthetic checks.

nodes.hypothesis: Weight breeding-parent draws within each inherited score quantile by a smoothed fraction of that parent's earlier accepted offspring that beat their generation batch's pre-feedback incumbent.
nodes.finding:
Historical credit changed parent selection on the recorded trajectories. Within-band probabilities differed from uniform in 101,614 of 109,053 draws (93.18%), and the selected parent differed from the passive uniform choice using the same random variate in 43,310 draws (39.71%). Selected parents had mean historical weight 0.3649, compared with 0.3037 under uniform selection over those same eligible lists. The accepted archive, score-ranked survival, offspring production and posterior selection retained their prescribed behavior. Among 4,350 scored offspring, strict improvements over the incumbent known before generation increased from 286 to 304, sequential incumbent improvements from 218 to 228, and strict best-parent beats from 565 to 578. These were smaller gains overall: cumulative incumbent improvement across the fifteen task/seed runs fell from 5.0382 to 4.7145. Mean generating-best-parent score fell from 0.4196 to 0.3840, and mean offspring score from 0.3192 to 0.2939. The three-seed final macro mean fell from 0.54437 to 0.52279, a paired mean change of -0.02158; the seed changes were -0.03001, -0.05149 and +0.01676. All five task means fell, with the largest loss on sitagliptin_mpo (-0.05863). The intended +0.002 mean improvement was not achieved.

The historical fraction enriched the intended weight without identifying stronger absolute proposal quality. Its fixed smoothing prior gave untested parents substantial opportunity: their share of actual parent draws rose from 36.91% to 50.50%, while the share with an earlier incumbent-beating offspring fell from 14.51% to 13.39%. Thus much of the observed effect was trying parents with no evaluated offspring history. More progress events against the evolving incumbent did not imply a better search trajectory; their mean size fell from 0.02311 to 0.02068, and the search finished lower. Correctly freezing the reference within a batch removes feedback-order leakage but cannot make different runs' incumbent thresholds equally difficult. These results narrow the useful claim to executable, feedback-sensitive allocation, with negative transfer under this seed panel and budget. Credit is conditional on the posterior selector having chosen an offspring for evaluation, and crossover assigns the same outcome to both parents, so the selected outcome groups cannot establish a causal parent effect. The molecular assessment also found that the modest increase in core coverage retained strained rings, reactive heteroatom variants and oversized repeated assemblies. Parent-outcome credit alone supplied no demonstrated control over those chemical liabilities.

nodes.hypothesis: Remove only the off-diagonal completed-count term from the exploration and zero-start-priority consumer when episode > 0 and parent_id == 0. For each currently eligible origin i, retain the inherited kernel records D_i=sum_j K_ij*N_j, P_i=sum_j K_ij*O_j, B_i=sum_j K_ij*N_j*M_j, and shared exploitation B_i/D_i (or its inherited neutral default). Replace started_i=D_i+P_i by started_i=N_i+P_i solely for active exploration and the started_i==0 priority. Keep beta=0.5, the parent N+O logarithmic numerator and earliest-occurrence ties. Because K_ii=1 and off-diagonal K_ij*N_j is nonnegative, removing it decreases started on exposed rows and weakly increases their bonus without changing shared value or shared pending support. Different bonuses can change which accepted origin supplies a direct frontier purchase. Only the complete paid panel can determine this consumer's conditional retained contribution; joint-density effects and own-value signs are not assumed to transfer.
nodes.finding:
All fifteen Search sessions completed. Exploration bonuses increased on all 7,528 exposed promoted-root rows, while shared peak values, shared pending counts and all 33,816 rows outside that gate stayed exact at the same state. There were 737 changed root choices among 3,764 promoted-root decisions: 699 reached paid molecules and 38 ended in failed routes. Changed routes covered 699 of 4,350 full purchases and 472 of 2,175 late purchases. Three task/seed cells had no changed paid choices, including the session with no root promotion; they remain in every denominator. Receipt, pending-count, widening, root-context and backup checks found no isolation mismatch.

Full incumbent-gain mass fell from 4.08717 to 3.89612, with 146 strict improvements versus 148. Late gain mass rose from 0.86560 to 1.03907, with 46 strict improvements on each side. Mean final Top-1 nevertheless fell from 0.480970 to 0.468234, a paired change of −0.012736. The three seed changes were +0.014003, −0.072016 and +0.019804; eight endpoints improved, four declined and three tied. The largest endpoint loss was 0.448131 on the second docking seed. The complete mean loss exceeds the registered descriptive 0.002 scale, triggering the score-preserving-removal falsifier. The result remains 0.138797 below the formal Anchor, whose unchanged improvement target was not reached.

Execution and changed allocation are established; the prediction that this removal would preserve scores is refuted. Under the retained shared-value/shared-pending composition, the completed-count consumer has positive conditional retained contribution. The three-seed variation makes that a descriptive result for this frozen panel, not a significance claim or a universal advantage. The late improvement does not rescue the endpoint claim, and it is not evidence that changed-choice descendants mediated that improvement: only two of the 699 changed-route purchases improved the incumbent, and none of the 472 late changed-route purchases did. Those adaptive strata have no measured alternative rewards. The membership intervention remains refuted, and this result neither assigns separate identities to the count consumers nor determines their interactions or the fate of the broader tree approach. No RAVE estimator or blending method was introduced or tested.

The method still reaches both incumbent origins but tends toward local refinement: fragment-excluded within-session similarity rises from 0.40124 across the full window to 0.46373 late, while pooled typed/generic scaffold counts fall to 1,755/1,240 from the Parent’s 1,837/1,284. This is not total scaffold collapse. Both size tails persist and enlarge: 341 molecules below six heavy atoms and 250 above fifty, versus 319 and 244; late counts are 184/152 versus 170/141. Molecular assessment associates the weak docking seed with a different nitrogen environment and shows that useful aromatic, amine and carbonyl arrangements are reachable but inconsistently preserved, alongside questionable heteroatom bonds and unspecified stereochemistry. That supports a limitation in the graph proposal operator’s preservation of useful local chemistry, without establishing the cause of a particular score loss. A proposal operator that makes coherent fragment or scaffold changes while preserving attachment context is the kind of method that could address this limitation; its benefit remains untested. The current evidence does not diagnose surrogate ranking error because this direct-frontier method has no learned surrogate ranking stage.

nodes.hypothesis: Within score-greedy live-population retention, order records by descending raw accepted score, then descending origin_batch only at exact score equality, then ascending serial within each batch, retaining the original population cap and score-quantile parent sampler.
nodes.finding:
The new tie priority changes 3,504 of 4,350 local retained orders and 207 survivor sets while preserving every same-contest retained score vector and all 15 initial populations. At the 435 states actually used for generation, 136 first-parent probability maps and 46 support sets differ. Parents whose probability increases are used in 2,813 draws and participate in 126 evaluated products: 16 beat the best generating parent, nine tie and 101 lose. Seven raise the incumbent. All 145 records newly kept at the population cutoff remain outside later breeding support and never breed after that protection.

The mechanism activates, including real probability shifts and evaluated descendants, but the complete endpoint prediction fails. Mean final Top-1 falls from 0.595670 to 0.574891, a paired change of -0.020779 against the required +0.002. Seed changes are -0.041461, +0.001143 and -0.022017. Seven of fifteen endpoints improve and eight decline; four task means decline. Every supplied run completes and every proposal pool fills. Lower seed dispersion accompanies the lower mean.

Most first changes in the search come from deterministic reordering rather than stronger sampling pressure: 14 of 15 first differing parent draws occur in states with unchanged first-parent probability maps. A fixed random index can select a different tied molecule even when its marginal probability is unchanged. Later band shifts do reach real breeders, so the result is not explained by absent exposure. However, the population-cutoff route remains unused, and the two evaluated products of newly supported parents both lose to their best parents. Local descendant wins and widespread later ancestry do not identify which part of the key change causes the endpoint loss.

Immediate score equality protects a local decision, not the usefulness of future neighborhoods. The molecular assessment finds chemically distinct exact ties, reactive bond environments, questionable ring geometry and unresolved stereochemistry alongside useful conventional amines and carbonyl frameworks. A newer record supplies no chemical-quality guarantee. The large loss in one decoration-hopping seed coexists with gains in its other two seeds; the very small first docking loss coexists with larger docking losses in the other seeds. These exceptions remain part of the complete result.

The single registered gain test ends with this negative conditional result. Earlier structural-retention and walk-tie failures remain separate counterexamples, and the two identical compactness panels count as one history. This experiment does not assign separate membership and ordering effects, establish chemical mediation, resolve the whole evolutionary foundation or combine with the other shared-Parent interventions.
