nodes.hypothesis: Ablate enforcement of the retained same-transition bidirectional inverse-motif tabu gate: every graph-valid canonically fresh neighbor reaches the inherited first-full-batch admission path, while the unchanged Parent predicate and selected-transition memory lifecycle run only as passive diagnostics.
nodes.finding:
Removal was exercised throughout the panel. All 435 batches contained the first ten valid fresh neighbors, with zero active tabu rejections, compared with 195 rejections in the Parent. The unchanged predicate identified 170 evaluated neighbors it would have vetoed on the actual Child history, spread over 135 batches and all 15 task sessions. Of these, 23 beat their source, 12 tied and 135 lost; nine strictly improved the archive and 29 became the next state. Across all proposals, source wins rose from 468 to 496 and strict archive updates from 238 to 269. Nevertheless, final macro mean fell from 0.521759 to 0.519484, a decrease of 0.002275 that narrowly meets the registered 0.002 prediction. Seed deltas were +0.021475, -0.037773 and +0.009471; their population deviation was 0.025574. Task mean changes were +0.006636 for zaleplon_mpo, -0.008325 for deco_hop, +0.039404 for drd2_docking, +0.007223 for median_2 and -0.056314 for sitagliptin_mpo. All runs completed with full validity. Raw generation attempts fell from 5303 to 5123, while recorded task runtime rose from 82.59 to 100.20 seconds.

The active gate provides a small net endpoint benefit in this panel despite excluding some immediate improvements and even one molecule that becomes a Child task maximum. The result therefore rules out judging the gate solely by the quality of its excluded neighbors or by counts of local gains. Its effect develops through changed batch membership, random-stream consumption and later sources: every paired session first diverged at a common recorded neighbor vetoed by Parent and admitted by Child, but the next state sometimes stayed identical for several more batches. The effect is strongly seed- and task-dependent; the average loss is dominated by the second seed, especially sitagliptin_mpo, while two seeds improve. This is evidence for the entire gate in the tested panel, not universal necessity or an individual motif contribution. Removing restrictions also did not guarantee greater access to the retained nitrogen exchange: eligible source batches fell from 97 to 49 and accepted exchanges from ten to four; none of the four beat its source or was selected. Chemistry remained mixed. Similar typical size and ring counts conceal more peroxide and sulfur-triple-bond products alongside fewer nitrogen- and oxygen-halogen bonds; 80 of the 170 bypass admissions carry at least one defined concern marker. High labels do not establish stability or feasible geometry. Finally, all 135 affected Child batches stop with only six to nine observed retained-gate alternatives, so their unobserved replacements and alternative winners remain unknown.

nodes.hypothesis: Remove candidate-dependent original count-GP predictive location only at successful fresh-pool allocation by setting every active sample row to original_archive_score_mean + original_score_scale*(original_normals @ original_count_pool_factor.T), while retaining the exact original correlated residuals, complete passive count-GP computations and all generation, admission, breeding and accepted-feedback rules.
nodes.finding:
The removal operated in every session: all 435 pools retained nonconstant original GP predictions but used one constant active location, with the original correlated residuals preserved. It changed 3,733 of 4,350 strict masked choices and placed 3,631 accepted molecules outside the passive original selected sets. Changed choices entered later fits and produced actual accepted descendants in all 15 sessions. Mean endpoint score fell from 0.596453 to 0.413485, a paired loss of 0.182968; every task–seed endpoint and all three seed averages declined. Seed-average population spread increased from 0.033970 to 0.072847. Useful progress weakened: strict parent-beating offspring fell from 648 to 414, their positive gain total from 17.251535 to 11.477453, and sequential incumbent gain from 5.819415 to 3.074901. Local gain totals nevertheless rose in all three zaleplon sessions, deco_hop seed 1 and docking seed 2; those exceptions did not produce an endpoint gain.

Candidate-dependent GP location has positive conditional value when the original correlated residuals, count representation, sulfur gate and breeder policy are retained. This is a complete answer to the registered location-presence contrast, not proof of total selector value or of how location and residuals mediate the effect. The original passive GP still ordered the same selected labels substantially better than the active constants: pair accuracy was 0.799 versus 0.500, while constant within-batch Spearman was undefined. That rules out missing or constant original predictions as an explanation for the loss. Broader structural output did not translate into productive exploration: first-arriving typed cores increased from 1,820 to 2,537 across sessions, yet parent-beating gain and incumbent progress fell. Chemistry helps describe the change in output: molecules with at most five heavy atoms increased from 105 to 612, aromatic-containing observations decreased, and oversized recombinations and reactive groups remained. These associations do not establish a chemical mediator or justify a universal fragment or functional-group ban. The retained GP location appears to supply useful adaptive direction beyond correlated residual exploration under this fixed panel. The pathway test should end with this answer; its registration supports no blend, scale or model rescue. Broader mechanism contribution, transfer to other conditions, physical feasibility and independent replication remain open.

nodes.hypothesis: Remove only m-00000000000a on code Parent n-cf8d309c06de: change CONFIG.crossover_probability from 0.45 to exactly 0.0. Every breeding attempt still selects the same first-parent law and consumes the existing single pre-branch Python RNG draw in its original position. The original member_attempts > 40 attenuation still multiplies the active probability by 0.5, leaving it zero. The existing two-parent branch, partner exclusion, connected-fragment constructor and conditional finishing code remain in source but cannot execute. Every attempt therefore enters the existing ordinary route: sample one/two/three mutate calls with probabilities 0.82/0.15/0.03 and stop at the first failed call. Causal path: exposed crossover routing is removed, fresh pool ancestry and purchased identities change, then accepted population and GP training histories change; if the retained route contributes useful discoveries, complete full/late gain and endpoint mean should fall. This is the total adaptive route-removal effect, including absence of conditional finishing access and naturally changed graph RNG consumption. It does not separately identify fragment construction, finishing, RNG or chemistry mediation.
nodes.finding:
All fifteen Search sessions completed. Across 73,861 breeding attempts, 33,506 retained random draws would have entered the old crossover route, yet there were zero partner draws, crossover constructions or finishing calls. Recombinant purchases fell from 1,480 to zero; all 4,350 Child purchases had one generating parent and complete provenance joins. Every paid stream diverged at its first proposal. Full incumbent-gain mass fell from 5.978073 to 5.205729 over 4,350 purchases, and late mass fell from 1.022408 to 0.990278 over 2,175 purchases. The complete mean fell from 0.607030 to 0.555541, a paired change of -0.051490; the three seed changes were -0.106268, -0.027952 and -0.020249. Ten task/seed endpoints declined and five improved. Task-average changes were -0.168953 for sitagliptin, -0.091639 for scaffold hopping, -0.011228 for median similarity, +0.002993 for docking and +0.011379 for zaleplon. No registered falsifier triggered. This supports positive conditional contribution of the retained crossover route at the registered 0.002 descriptive scale, despite the Child scoring worse.

Frequent small improvements did not replace the larger gains supplied by the complete Parent search. The Child produced 305 strict incumbent improvements versus 253, but their mean size fell from 0.023629 to 0.017068; late improvements likewise increased from 76 to 101 while their total gain fell. Stall-restricted batches fell from 88 to 53, so fewer stalls also failed to predict stronger endpoints. Higher parent-beating frequency is not independent support because a single-parent hurdle is easier than the Parent’s better-of-two hurdle. The molecular report narrows the structural explanation: generic scaffold coverage fell from 951 to 878 even though typed scaffold count rose from 1,667 to 1,762. Both size tails disappeared—the Child stayed at 22–47 heavy atoms—but that narrower size range did not preserve endpoint quality. Fragment-excluded similarity changed only from 0.311054 to 0.316818, which does not establish global scaffold collapse. Together these observations support a loss of access to larger improvements through the proposal scheme, rather than a shortage of valid molecules or enough evidence to diagnose surrogate failure. A topology-changing graph proposal operator or a search scheme that preserves access to distinct ring/linker arrangements is the kind of method that could address that limitation; its benefit remains untested. Reactive oxygen/nitrogen decorations and unspecified stereochemistry persist, so removing crossover did not establish chemically reliable generation. The measured contribution belongs to the total adaptive route, including its finishing access and changed random histories. Fragment construction, finishing and chemical mediation remain inseparable here; the sign is not a significance claim and does not transfer automatically to a different score model or end the broader approach.

nodes.hypothesis: Replace only the final successful posterior-selection position by the smallest-index maximizer of the original latent posterior variance conditional on earlier selected locations with the inherited observation noise, while preserving every preceding masked correlated Thompson choice and learning only from real accepted feedback.
nodes.finding:
All 435 batches preserved the nine preceding Thompson choices on the same decision state. The final choice changed in 433 batches, always with a strict increase in remaining model variance; the other two choices coincided. Every final molecule was accepted. All 418 changed labels with a later fit opportunity altered next-batch predictions when compared with a passive fit omitting that row. Their next-query mean squared error fell slightly, from 0.0094934 with the row omitted to 0.0094283 with it included, although 89 of 418 next-batch comparisons worsened. None of the 435 final molecules beat its generating parent, improved the incumbent or was subsequently used for breeding. The Parent’s final positions produced 46 parent-beating molecules and 232 later-used breeders. Across the complete matched panel, mean final score fell from 0.595670 to 0.572880, a paired change of −0.022790 against the required +0.002. Seed changes were −0.045797, +0.011083 and −0.033656; 11 of 15 task/seed endpoints declined. Selection and later learning are confirmed; useful reserved-identity breeding and the performance prediction are not.

The missing benefit cannot be explained by a failure to select different molecules, accept their labels or update the predictor. This rule repeatedly spent its final evaluation on small, weak-scoring structures: 340 of 435 final choices had at most five heavy atoms, versus 18 in the Parent’s final positions. This accounts for most of the molecular assessment’s increase from 123 to 382 tiny accepted proposals overall. The winner’s mean variance fell only from 0.8596 before location conditioning to 0.8581 afterward, and conditioning changed the marginal-variance winner in just five batches. Thus the experiment mostly exposed uncertain molecules far from the selected prefix, rather than demonstrating a benefit from correcting within-batch redundancy. Their labels did provide measurable predictive information in the limited sense of fixed-history sensitivity and slightly lower observed next-query error; the omission contrast also changes normalization, and it does not establish calibrated uncertainty, information gain or endpoint mediation. Those modest predictive effects did not offset the unsuccessful final evaluations under this budget. The broader output still contains useful aromatic and heterocyclic families alongside reactive bonds, difficult ring geometry and unspecified stereochemistry; these chemical observations do not identify the cause of the endpoint loss. The negative contribution finding is conditional on this one-position rule, Parent composition and Search panel. It neither refutes ordinary accepted-label learning nor isolates the value of the covariance-conditioning term, and the registered complete exposed failure ends this rule without tuning its reserved count or schedule.

nodes.hypothesis: Replace uniform historical-elite replay membership with the highest accepted-score eligible records, ordered by descending score and canonical identity, while preserving the inherited replay count, original accepted sequence and reward provenance, memory admission/retention and equal-per-sequence online learning.
nodes.finding:
The selection mechanism ran on the intended records. All 405 nonterminal updates with surplus eligible history changed replay membership and increased accepted replay reward relative to the passive uniform draw on that same memory. Across all 420 nonterminal historical updates, replay reward rose from the uniform comparator's 0.301506 to 0.376503; the fifteen no-surplus updates had no reward difference. Selected history exceeded the current elite mean in 370 updates, compared with 185 for the uniform comparator. All 405 changed selections also produced measurable changes in the actual training gradient at the registered tolerance. Original accepted strings, scores, chronological admission, top-32 retention, equal row weights and frozen priors were preserved.

The stronger replay was more concentrated: summing distinct replayed identities within the fifteen objective sessions gave 540 actual identities versus 1,103 under the passive comparator, and 335 versus 751 distinct Murcko cores. Actual replay was younger on average, at 4.47 batches versus 5.52, rather than simply older. In subsequent generation, raw validity increased from Parent 90.43% to 92.58%, while duplicate draws rose from 30.11% to 40.78% and novel yield fell from 60.31% to 51.81%. Forty-one batches needed additional sampling, versus five in the Parent. All fifteen tasks still completed the same 300-call budgets.

Mean final Top-1 increased from 0.507554 to 0.513272, a paired mean gain of 0.005718. The three paired changes were -0.012216, +0.009216 and +0.020155, so the benefit was uneven across replicas. Four task means increased; sitagliptin decreased. The final fifteen updates are excluded from the selection-to-proposal conclusions because no later proposals follow them.

The experiment separates using replay from choosing its members. Historical replay already supplied measurable gradients in the Parent; selecting the strongest available history demonstrably changed both the reward distribution and the gradient of the loss actually optimized. The comparison uses the child's own memory and policy state, so it establishes the selection effect without inventing an alternative scored trajectory. Stronger reward did not mean a larger gradient: on changed updates, the mean actual combined-gradient norm was about 363 versus 493 for the passive uniform group. Repeatedly selected records were often already closer to their targets, and historical mean squared error moved only from 105.05 to 102.64 across the real updates; 834 of 2,100 historical row exposures nevertheless worsened.

The tradeoff is a narrower stream of accepted evidence and more repeated proposals. That concentration is visible in chemistry as well: the deco-hop proposal set fell from 529 to 392 distinct cores and the strongest neighborhoods repeatedly decorate related aromatic, amide, urea, amine or hydrazone families. Conventional connectivity remains dominant, but score ordering alone does not improve attachment chemistry, control oversized outliers or add missing stereochemical configurations. Positive augmented targets also persist in 595 of 2,100 historical exposures, despite being above the log-probability ceiling. The campaign now has evidence that reward enrichment can improve some endpoints while reducing novelty and producing inconsistent gains; preserving a broader supply of useful accepted evidence is an open question separate from whether this selector activates.

nodes.hypothesis: Replace generation-order submission with distinct maximizers of independent joint posterior function draws from an accepted-only, task-local Tanimoto fingerprint Gaussian process over the Parent's existing fresh surplus SAFE fragment completions.
nodes.finding:
Both new replicas executed accepted-only GP conditioning and full-covariance posterior selection. Across their ten task runs, all 280 nonterminal feedback probes changed the posterior mean and variance on the same previously submitted molecules. Every one of 2,900 choices replayed as the maximum of its logged joint draw over the remaining pool. Selection changed the submitted generation-order set in 284 of 285 batches with surplus completions, replacing 1,304 prefix entries. Uncertainty changed 1,939 of 2,850 eligible choices (68.04%) relative to the posterior-mean maximizer of the identical remaining pool. The five batches without surplus were excluded from that uncertainty denominator; there were no numerical fallbacks, fingerprint collisions or exact choice ties. The same mechanism was already active in the supplied seed-0 baseline, where uncertainty changed 1,019 of 1,450 choices (70.28%). These are replications of activation, not new algorithm changes. The new macro scores were 0.50778 and 0.47068, alongside the original 0.50903. The three-seed mean was 0.49583 with population standard deviation 0.01779. Task means were 0.41036 for zaleplon, 0.59284 for scaffold hopping, 0.96337 for DRD2 docking, 0.20040 for median similarity and 0.31218 for sitagliptin. All tasks completed 300 oracle evaluations. The supplied comparison runs are the same selector on different seeds, so they do not establish a replicated score improvement over generation-order submission.

The experiment now rules out activation being peculiar to the first seed: accepted-only posterior updates, use of cross-candidate covariance, and uncertainty-driven changes to actual submissions all persisted across different prepared denoisers and search trajectories. The natural surplus was sufficient for selection in 285 of 290 new batches without increasing the inherited generation width or generating beyond the first sufficient call. Correct activation still leaves efficacy unresolved. Chronological GP prediction error beat the archive-mean predictor in nine of ten new task runs, but lost on seed-2 sitagliptin (RMSE 0.06228 versus 0.05839). The lower-scoring second replica had lower pooled prediction error and more completions beating their contexts than the first; neither diagnostic alone establishes better final best scores. Unsubmitted alternatives have no oracle labels, and there are no matched generation-order or greedy-mean control runs here. The molecular assessment further limits what the selector can accomplish: it reallocates calls among mostly related aromatic analogue families and inherits gaps in scaffold coverage, stereochemical specification and chemical plausibility. High scores and score ties across chemically different products do not by themselves show that reactive or questionable structures have been avoided. A matched selector ablation with the same prepared prior, together with inspection of the high-scoring chemistry, would separate the value of correlated uncertainty from prior quality and score permissiveness.

nodes.hypothesis: Redirect halogen append mutations from heteroatom anchors to uniformly sampled eligible carbon anchors, preserving the selected halogen and single-atom growth.
nodes.finding:
The intended attachment change reached both pools and evaluation. All 489 halogen draws with a heteroatom anchor and available carbon support were redirected, sanitized and reconstructed as the same selected halogen attached by one new C-halogen bond. Every old heavy atom and bond was preserved, and all 489 direct products retained the source ring core. One further opportunity had no carbon site and correctly continued the bounded retry. The successful edits supplied 482 distinct pool descendants and 22 evaluated descendants; 19 of those ended with the append, while three underwent later edits.

The direct channel produced no new heteroatom-halogen bonds. The Parent’s single-append pool products had added 160 N-halogen, 55 O-halogen and 25 other heteroatom-halogen bonds; its emitted single-append products added 16 N-halogen and three other heteroatom-halogen bonds. Across all evaluated proposals, molecules containing N-halogen decreased from 572 to 535 and O-halogen from 441 to 173, but both remained common. Ring-core identities across the full emitted stream increased from 2,266 to 2,409; no explicit tetrahedral stereochemistry appeared.

All fifteen tasks completed the same 300-call budgets. Novel pool yield rose from 92.05% to 92.55%, and accepted molecules beating their best generating parent increased from 565 to 605. Among the 22 redirected descendants, two beat their best parent, one improved the incumbent and none was a final task/seed best. Mean final Top-1 nevertheless fell from 0.544374 to 0.539209, a paired change of -0.005165; seed changes were -0.011685, -0.020367 and +0.016558. The mechanism is confirmed, with negative and uneven endpoint utility.

The experiment establishes that an attachment rule can remove a specific reactive-bond introduction while preserving the surrounding graph, without solving the broader chemistry problem. The rule changed a small evaluated channel: 22 of 4,350 proposals carried its redirected edit in their immediate breeding history. Meanwhile, 56 emitted N-halogen-containing molecules and 31 O-halogen-containing molecules had no such motif in either original generating parent, demonstrating introductions through the unchanged operators. Other products already had that motif available in their parents; their exact bond ancestry cannot be inferred from motif presence alone.

Carbon attachment itself remains chemically permissive. Four redirected pool products acquired a carbonyl-halide connection and three an imine-carbon-halide connection; none of those seven was evaluated. The full selected stream also contained more carbonyl/imine halides, while the molecular assessment still found strained small rings, reactive decorations, oversized repeated assemblies and unspecified stereochemistry. These observations narrow the next chemistry question to attachment environment and other introduction routes, rather than treating all carbon-bound halogens as robust alternatives. The simultaneous increase in core coverage and parent-beating events with a lower final best score also shows that these intermediate gains do not establish endpoint benefit. The altered stochastic search paths and posterior selection do not identify a causal score penalty for the removed, unscored attachment alternatives.

nodes.hypothesis: Replace the original dot-product count Tanimoto covariance TDP by the fixed exponential warp K(x,y)=exp(TDP(x,y)-1), lambda=1, on the unchanged folded Morgan integer occurrence vectors, preserving the inherited TDP zero conventions and exact TDP=1 aliases.
nodes.finding:
All 15 task/seed evaluations completed. Selected sets changed in 417 of 435 batches, with 1230 active selections outside the passive original set. On the actual Child emissions, MSE fell from 0.007744 with passive original predictions to 0.007064, pair-order accuracy rose from 66.48% to 67.19%, and mean within-batch Spearman rose from 0.4279 to 0.4417. These averages retain the losses: pair ordering worsened on every deco-hop seed and on one sitagliptin seed. Strict best-parent wins increased from 629 to 697 of 4350 offspring, and sequential incumbent advances from 258 to 273, but mean best-generating-parent score fell from 0.47046 to 0.44229; mean offspring score also fell slightly, from 0.38526 to 0.38235. Total incumbent gain fell from 5.80766 to 5.32350. Final macro score decreased from 0.59566965 to 0.56339196, a mean loss of 0.03227769 against the required gain of 0.002. Paired seed changes were −0.06839278, +0.00744768, −0.03588798; Child population SD was 0.00472367 versus 0.02659287. Median-2 improved in every seed, while deco-hop and docking lost in every seed. There were six task/seed wins and nine losses.

The fixed law clearly executed; missing exposure, broken Gaussian arithmetic, passive fit failure or altered random draws do not explain the endpoint loss. Better prediction on the actively selected stream and more wins against weaker parents did not translate into higher absolute search quality. Productive new typed cores rose only from 280 to 288 and generic cores from 190 to 191; more later breeding also failed to recover the lost endpoints. All 150 terminal offspring in each panel remain censored, and 73 Child versus 50 Parent offspring had later breeding support but were never drawn. The molecular assessment associates the lower results with extended and geometrically uncertain families alongside conventional high-scoring alternatives; fewer unusual local bonds do not establish chemical stability or explain covariance contribution. The experiment narrows the case against this exact lambda-one warp under the tested composition and budget. It cannot tell us whether covariance-floor smoothing, omitted candidate rewards or subsequent feedback caused the loss, and selected-stream diagnostics do not establish pool-wide ranking or calibration. The registered complete gain test ends this exact law; a materially different future law needs a sourced distinguishing experiment.

nodes.hypothesis: Replace each selected row’s squared augmented-likelihood residual with the Huber penalty rho(r)=r^2 for abs(r)<=1 and rho(r)=2*abs(r)-1 otherwise, preserving the Parent exposure coefficients, fixed augmented targets and training membership, so the scalar likelihood-gradient factor becomes -2*q_i*clamp(r_i,-1,1) instead of -2*q_i*r_i.
nodes.finding:
The Huber rule changed the learning direction after clipping at all 429 nonterminal starts with tail residuals. On those comparisons, its mean gradient cosine with the original squared-error objective was 0.888. Across the child's 435 nonterminal starting tensors, the original objective's two largest scalar factors held 52.66% of absolute influence on average; those same rows held 33.20% under Huber. All 53,100 actual-step row derivatives obeyed the registered bound and all 450 first backward passes matched the direct Huber gradient. In the 420 history-bearing nonterminal updates, mean weighted Huber loss fell from 13.588 to 9.621. Historical row errors worsened in 863 of 2,100 appearances, compared with 906 for the parent.

All 15 task runs completed their 300-evaluation budgets. Mean endpoint score fell from 0.517655 to 0.500773; the paired mean change was -0.016882, with seed changes -0.023903, +0.004450 and -0.031193. The largest task loss was sitagliptin_mpo (-0.088317), followed by deco_hop (-0.009741); zaleplon_mpo improved by 0.012418, drd2_docking by 0.001297, and median_2 was nearly unchanged (-0.000067). Recorded mean AUC rose from 0.406769 to 0.448820, chiefly through earlier drd2_docking progress. Raw duplicate draws rose from 36.22% to 38.41%, and distinct chemical-core counts fell in four of five tasks. The predicted endpoint gain of at least 0.002 was therefore not achieved.

Residual bounding survives global gradient clipping as a directional change; the result rules out the explanation that clipping simply erases it as a common rescaling. Yet reducing scalar concentration and slightly reducing historical row regressions did not produce broader useful search. Faster discovery on a task already near its score ceiling can improve average AUC while substantial losses elsewhere lower final quality. The chemistry assessment is consistent with this split: strong amine-rich families coexist with repeated analogue families, scattered winners on the weakest task, uneven attachment chemistry and unresolved stereochemistry. Those observations do not identify which chemical limitation caused the score loss.

The bound also leaves the target problem intact: positive, individually unattainable targets occur in 1,243 nonterminal selected-row appearances, versus 988 for the parent. Their scalar influence is reduced, but their feasibility is unchanged. Whether useful large residuals were damped too strongly remains open; these runs do not isolate initialization, upward versus downward pressure, or individual chemical families as the cause. Six updates began entirely in the quadratic region and matched the original gradient exactly, then entered the Huber tail during later Adam steps. Starting-state equality is therefore a narrower control than whole-update equality. Recorded sequence likelihoods support these conclusions, but token-level probability changes and forgetting between unobserved appearances remain unmeasured.

nodes.hypothesis: Augment the Parent's exact molecular count representation with bond-order-resolved counts of the unordered pair of endpoint heavy-atom degrees, and fit and optimize the existing accepted-only ridge predictor over this enlarged descriptor vector through exact MILP equations.
nodes.finding:
The added counts separated 556 of 705 molecular pairs that the parent represented identically, including 507 of 625 pairs with unequal recorded scores. The learned distinctions affected construction: 145 feasible comparisons with the same-data legacy predictor produced 107 strict preference reversals and 11 legacy ties broken in favor of the molecule actually emitted. All 1,450 emitted molecules exactly matched all 468 optimized counts, and every batch completed.

On the single screening seed, mean final Top-1 rose from 0.286518 to 0.296789. Docking increased from 0.189601 to 0.284516, decoration hopping from 0.583606 to 0.589489, and median_2 from 0.175888 to 0.183910. Zaleplon slipped from 0.395373 to 0.394288, while sitagliptin fell from 0.088123 to 0.031740. Mean trajectory AUC decreased slightly, from 0.252148 to 0.250435. Of 1,389 predicted source improvements, 604 became observed improvements, compared with 578 of 1,400 in the parent. Average actual source-relative gain remained negative, at -0.006834 versus -0.006591. Total evaluation time increased from 435 to 714 seconds, including about 43 seconds for diagnostic comparisons.

This closes a specific representational gap: adjacency of branching and substituted sites can supply learned information that changes exact graph construction. The eleven choices between molecules with identical old descriptors are particularly clear evidence, because the added counts alone break those predictor ties. Exact descriptor agreement and correct attachment corrections rule out optimized-to-submitted mismatch as the explanation for the remaining prediction errors.

Predictive usefulness is still uneven. On the same emitted molecules and the same accepted training data, the augmented predictor reduced pooled prediction RMSE from the shadow legacy model's 0.055579 to 0.053050, but increased mean absolute error from 0.024969 to 0.025680. Its advantage in final best score therefore does not establish generally better predictions or search trajectories, especially with only one replica and unscored diagnostic alternatives. The molecular assessment finds that familiar inherited rings still carry many unusual heteroatom-halogen and heteroatom-chain appendages, alongside conventional high-scoring chemistry. These richer degree counts do not enforce functional-group compatibility or expand the ring-construction domain. Further evidence should separate reliability across replicas, remaining representation limits, and chemical compatibility; the observed gain does not settle any of them.

nodes.hypothesis: Make the ordinary floor-one requested mutation-call probability vector a session-local quantity driven by realized payoff: each accepted ordinary floor-one product contributes max(0, its score minus the best score among its own scored generating parents) as credit to the arm that requested its walk; the most recent 96 such accepted products form one sliding window; and the vector used by the next ordinary attempts is 0.05 on each of the arms {1, 2, 3} plus the remaining 0.85 split in proportion to the per-arm windowed credit sums, reverting to the inherited [0.82, 0.15, 0.03] whenever the window is missing an arm or holds no positive credit.
nodes.finding:
The law ran exactly as built in all fifteen sessions. Each session was the Anchor's own run, molecule for molecule, up to the batch in which its vector first left the inherited 0.82/0.15/0.03, and diverged inside that batch. The two sessions the preregistered replay said would never collect a three-call product (zaleplon_mpo and sitagliptin_mpo, seed 1) never left the fallback and reproduced the Anchor's 300 evaluations exactly. Every ordinary attempt drew exactly one walk length, the escalation never rose above one (at most six consecutive attempts without a pool admission, against the eighty it needs), the vector never changed inside a batch, and every one of 2,793 credited products was credited exactly its clipped gain over its own scored parent; 1,557 crossover-derived or finished products were correctly left out.

Thirteen sessions left the fallback: nine within the first five batches (after 5 to 26 credited products) and four late (batches 11 to 22, after 68 to 129). Over the panel 61% of ordinary attempts (25,529 of 41,802) were drawn under credit. Three sessions later fell back when an arm dropped out of the window; sitagliptin_mpo seed 0 stayed on the fallback for its last twelve batches. The realized multi-call share moved from the Anchor's 0.17-0.195 to anywhere between 0.10 and 0.55, and the requested mean from 1.21 to 1.33. Three sessions went long: deco_hop seeds 1 and 2 (0.52 and 0.55, on three-call walks) and median_2 seed 1 (0.55, on two-call walks). Seven shortened to 0.10-0.16 and three stayed near 0.18. What set the vector was the first one to three parent-beating products, not a sustained payoff difference. In median_2 seed 1, two two-call products that beat their parents by 0.0055 and 0.0049 in batch 2 put 0.66 on the two-call arm, which stayed at or above 0.50 until batch 20. In deco_hop seed 1, one three-call product that beat its parent by 0.047 in batch 1 held the three-call arm at 0.54-0.58 for eighteen batches. In deco_hop seed 2, a single +0.006 three-call hit sent 0.80 of the mass to three-call walks from batch 2. Positive credit is sparse (one credited product in seven beats its parent). In 128 of the 266 credit-driven batches only one arm held any credit, which pins the vector to a corner: 0.90/0.05/0.05 whenever that arm is the one-call arm.

By task, the pooled multi-call share became deco_hop 0.39, median_2 0.28, drd2_docking 0.17, zaleplon_mpo 0.16 and sitagliptin_mpo 0.155, against 0.175-0.183 for the Anchor. Both tasks with a measured preference moved the wrong way, as the replay of the Anchor's streams had predicted. median_2, which gains from shorter walks, went longer (0.18 to 0.28, all of it from seed 1). sitagliptin_mpo, which gains from longer walks, went shorter (0.18 to 0.155; both active sessions sat at the 0.10 floor while credit-driven). But the seed-to-seed spread within median_2 and deco_hop (0.10 to 0.55) is as wide as the whole panel, so the separation is by session, not by task. The replay had capped median_2 at 0.29; the realized 0.55 shows that once the law steers, it feeds itself.

The longest arm was no longer starved in aggregate: accepted three-call products rose from 42 to 177 (2.8 to 11.8 per session). But 122 of them came from the two long deco_hop sessions, and five sessions still accepted at most one. The extra multi-call products were low-yield. Summed over all fifteen sessions, the mean clipped gain per accepted product was 0.0039 for one-call, 0.0022 for two-call and 0.0008 for three-call walks, against 0.0042, 0.0025 and 0.0016 in the Anchor. deco_hop is the only task where three-call products paid more per product than one-call ones, in both runs. Realized incumbent increments from ordinary products fell from 3.47 to 3.19 (the multi-call part rose from 0.17 to 0.21), crossover-derived increments fell from 2.35 to 2.14, and the overall parent-beat rate fell from 0.149 to 0.143. No proxy improved.

The complete matched panel fell from 0.5965 to 0.5635, a paired delta of -0.0330. The seed macros moved -0.0850, +0.0020 and -0.0161, and with any one cell left out the delta stays between -0.0358 and -0.0189. median_2 did not move: its three-seed mean is 0.22267 against the Anchor's 0.22273 (-0.00007), with cells 0.2083, 0.2281 and 0.2317 against 0.2145, 0.2214 and 0.2323. That is far from the +0.010 target. Among the protected tasks, drd2_docking (+0.0011, margin 0.03) and zaleplon_mpo (-0.0140, margin 0.02) held. deco_hop (-0.0876) and sitagliptin_mpo (-0.0644) broke their 0.02 margins. deco_hop seed 0 is the known departure cell: like every whole-run child, it lost the inherited 0.856 (0.626 here), which is worth -0.0153 of the panel. sitagliptin_mpo seed 0 lost 0.168 after being held at 0.10 multi-call from batch 3. Six of the seven sessions the law shortened lost ground (the seven together sum to -0.469 of cell score), while the three lengthened sessions sum to -0.026. The same-batch law-free reference that should calibrate pure path departure had not finished. The registered non-inferiority bar is therefore read against the Anchor alone, and at -0.033 it fails.

The open question was whether a session's own payoff can choose the walk length each task prefers, without knowing the task. With this credit form the answer is no, and the run shows why. The law is highly steerable: it moved the realized multi-call share across a fivefold range. What steers it, though, is not information about which length pays. Only about one credited product in seven beats its parent, so a 96-product window holds a handful of non-zero credits, and whichever arm lands the first one or two hits takes the vector. Because credit is summed rather than averaged, the arm that is sampled more then collects more credit by volume. In the median_2 session that locked onto two-call walks, two-call and one-call products paid almost the same per product (0.00031 against 0.00033), yet the two-call arm kept most of the mass for seventeen batches. At 300 evaluations per task, this rule is a lottery seeded in the first few batches, not an estimator of arm value.

Where the drift did line up with tasks, it pointed the wrong way, exactly as the preregistered replay predicted: median_2 went longer and sitagliptin_mpo shorter. Per accepted product, multi-call walks pay less than one-call walks everywhere except deco_hop. The local signal (how far an accepted child beats its parent, under the surrogate's selection) and the endpoint dose-response (which walk length leads to the best final molecule) measure different things. The endpoints fit that reading without proving it. In most sessions the law mainly shortened walks, and those sessions carried almost the whole loss, including both sitagliptin_mpo cells and both zaleplon_mpo cells. That resembles the earlier finding that removing multi-edit walks costs this Anchor about 0.03. But these are single realizations after divergence, and they identify no mediator.

By its preregistered stop conditions, this ends the credit-driven walk-length route on this Anchor: no window, floor, reward-definition or arm-count sweep follows. A sweep would not touch the cause, which is the sparsity of the payoff signal and the volume coupling of the summed form. The reserved radius-memory repair targets a different failure (collapsing back to the fallback after improvements) and is not justified by what happened here. A count-normalized or confidence-bound rule, the parts of the source method this node left out, would remove the volume coupling but not the sparsity, so it is not a clean next test either. Fixed shortening remains the one replicated median_2 gain on this walk-length axis, but it costs sitagliptin_mpo, and this run shows that a payoff signal cannot pick it per session. The walk-length lever therefore cannot serve the brief's target without hurting a protected task unless some other, non-payoff session signal is found.

Two things stay open. First, how much of the -0.033 is pure path departure: the ungated law-free reference running in the same batch answers that, and the one known departure cell alone accounts for -0.015. Second, whether median_2 is limited by walk length at all. The molecular review finds median_2's best molecules already spread over 20 scaffolds, its late edits (alkyl against ethoxy, N-methyl against N-ethyl) moving the score by under 0.01, and generator-wide gaps that no walk length reaches: no multi-atom substituent can be inserted in one move, and ring-system replacement is not a move of its own. That points to the move vocabulary, not the number of moves, as the next distinguishing test for median_2.

nodes.hypothesis: Allocate the batch by greedy marginal expected-maximum gain over a shared antithetic panel of the inherited joint posterior draws, so each selection accounts for the score peaks already covered by earlier selections.
nodes.finding:
The rule changes 431 of 435 submitted batch sets versus independent posterior draws on the same pools. All 3,596 later choices with positive marginal value follow the registered maximizer; 3,256 differ from the original draw's choice on the identical available mask. Another 319 positions use the registered mean completion after sampled gains reach exactly zero. Average maximum over the shared scenario panel rises by 0.00617, with 396 pools improving and 0 declining. This is internal sampled utility.

Evaluated three-seed mean final score falls from 0.57434 to 0.55824, a change of -0.01610 against the registered +0.002 target. Seed changes are −0.03008, +0.01124 and −0.02948; 8 of 15 task/seed endpoints decline, and every task's mean declines. The largest mean loss is sitagliptin at 0.05362. Strict improvements over the best generating parent are 621/4,350 versus 624/4,350, and incumbent improvements are 250 versus 241. Mean evaluated batch maximum falls from 0.48731 to 0.45721, while prediction MSE on each run's selected stream falls from 0.01127 to 0.00924. Nominal 95% latent intervals cover 77.86% of selected scores versus 76.92% for the Parent. All evaluations complete; no numerical fallback occurs.

This establishes a real effect from later marginal allocation, beyond the first mean-ranked choice or antithetic arithmetic alone. It also shows that correctly increasing the model's sampled batch maximum is insufficient to improve the final best evaluated score on this panel. The original predictive model and random draws remain intact on identical inputs, narrowing the explanation to the changed allocation and its subsequent feedback trajectory. Unavailable alternative molecules have no oracle labels, so same-pool utility comparisons cannot identify which individual replacements caused the score losses.

The objective rewards a batch's maximum without requiring it to beat the incumbent, and twenty dependent antithetic scenarios approximate the model's tails. Together with the selected-stream uncertainty undercoverage, these leave a concrete mismatch between acquisition utility and useful search progress. More incumbent updates and lower selected-stream prediction error also failed to produce a higher endpoint: improvement frequency and average prediction accuracy do not measure how far the search advances. Because the later selected molecules differ, the MSE comparison does not establish better prediction or calibration on common molecules. An incumbent-relative utility or a separately tested correction to predictive uncertainty is worth distinguishing next; neither is established as the cause here. On the Child's fixed pools, mean count-fingerprint similarity falls from 0.6860 to 0.6810, yet distinct nonempty cores per batch also fall from 6.846 to 6.641 and acyclic selections rise from 104 to 145. Similarity instead increases when the same rule is applied to the Parent's pools. This separates lower pairwise similarity from broader core coverage and shows that the secondary effects depend on the pool.

The molecular assessment finds useful polar motifs within ring-rich families alongside reactive heteroatom bonds, constrained ring systems and unspecified stereochemistry. Smaller molecules do not consistently give better endpoints. Allocation preserves those chemical limitations, so the internal utility increase supplies no evidence of improved feasibility or broadly useful chemistry.

nodes.hypothesis: Freeze a corpus-trained masked-substructure graph encoder, fit a regularized linear readout to current-task accepted scores, ascend that fixed surrogate through relaxed leaf identities and leaf/expansion existence variables of observed molecules' scaffolding trees, and stochastically sample and assemble new structures from the optimized variables while preserving their internal scaffold context.
nodes.finding:
Macro mean 0.361872161920233 on the single screening seed, placing this root in the middle of the thirteen-root field. Per objective: 0.5890616392238477, 0.42602011617052177, 0.380138751942517, 0.23408968632790841 and 0.18005061593636776. Every observable activated and the falsifier did not trigger. Masked-substructure pretraining cut held-out loss from 5.444202465850716 to 0.9686623942998355 over 30000 steps, publishing the checkpoint at step 27000. All 150 readout fits used only prior same-objective observations, growing from 10 to 300 records. All 175 structural optimizations ended with a surrogate prediction strictly above their own starting relaxation, with all four gradient families active at every one of the 3850 steps. From 6268 sampled trees, 1450 valid novel context-preserving molecules were assembled; the remainder were 3712 duplicates and 1106 failed assemblies, of which 732 had no compatible attachment point and 374 failed kekulization. The result the run turns on is the transfer gap: 380 of 1450 proposals beat their generating source, but the mean actual score change relative to that source was negative on all five objectives, ranging from -0.00180775181701 to -0.108386772041, while the surrogate's relaxed gain was positive throughout. Predicted improvements were realised only 26 to 46 percent of the time, and chronological prediction error reached 0.135969779 on the worst objective against an in-sample residual of 0.0515970171356 on the same one.

The campaign now knows that this style of surrogate-gradient construction executes faithfully at this budget, and that the surrogate is systematically optimistic. It is fitted in sample to a few hundred points, it is ascended to a strictly higher prediction every single time, and the molecules assembled from that ascent still average worse than the molecules they were built from. The failure is not in the gradient step, which is verified, but in the two lossy translations after it: from relaxed probabilities to a sampled tree, and from a tree to an assembled molecule, where roughly a quarter of attempts fail outright. At 0.3619 against a field spanning 0.2331 to 0.5103, this sits well clear of the undirected search methods and well short of the leader, which suggests that a learned model of structure is worth having but that a point estimate with no uncertainty is the wrong thing to ascend, since ascent drives proposals precisely into the region where the fit extrapolates worst. What stays open is whether calibrating the readout, with a posterior rather than a point prediction or an explicit penalty for distance from the fitted data, would close the optimism gap, and whether the fixed-interior constraint that keeps the chemistry clean is also what caps the score.

nodes.hypothesis: Extend the Parent's existing uniformly sampled leaf-deletion menu with whole multi-atom acyclic branches attached by one non-ring single bond directly to a ring atom, so the same deletion-operator allocation can emit a compact neighbor in one edit while retaining the complete ring framework.
nodes.finding:
The expanded menu was available in 391 of 435 actual batch-start states. It selected 83 whole-branch edits, all graph-valid; after seven duplicate exclusions and seven tabu vetoes, 69 prunings reached evaluation. Each removed 2-14 heavy atoms in one step, averaging 3.75 atoms and 2.10 rotatable bonds, while retaining every ring atom and bond. The recorded menus, uniform selection, graph edits and identity joins passed the audit, including exact original behavior in all 55 deletion draws where no added branch was available.

Eight of the 69 evaluated prunings beat their source, and four became the next current state. All four later grew again. Typical emitted size remained essentially unchanged at 33.21 heavy atoms, compared with 33.20 for Parent. All three seeds completed their five 300-evaluation tasks; sampling cost was also similar at 12.14 versus 12.15 attempts per ten-member batch.

Mean macro final Top-1 fell from 0.520918 to 0.456635, a paired mean change of -0.064283. The three seed changes were -0.020009, -0.101316 and -0.071524. Every task mean declined, with the largest losses in DRD2 and sitagliptin. The intended neighborhood expansion and immediate size reduction occurred, while the score-retention hypothesis failed on the supplied panel.

A lack of eligible branches was not the bottleneck: the Parent already had branch opportunities in 399 of 435 states, and the extension successfully turned such opportunities into new evaluated neighbors. The added prunings usually lost source score, rarely won their batch and were followed by regrowth whenever selected. Those observations help explain why immediate reductions of several atoms did not produce a lasting shift toward smaller sampled molecules under the unchanged accepted-score walk.

The experiment separates direct access to compact analogues from retaining useful score. Its complete method loses score in every seed, although that loss cannot be assigned solely to the pruned candidates because the changed menu also changes later sampling and trajectories. The molecular assessment remains dominated by sulfur-rich polycycles, reactive heteroatom bonds and unresolved ring geometry and stereochemistry. Ring-preserving removal alone does not resolve those chemical limitations.

nodes.hypothesis: Remove only the consumption of the stall-conditioned top-forty eligibility mask by fixed-field qPO. For every successful allocation, let E be every admitted current-pool index and recompute all 10000 row winners over E using the original stable first-index maximum. Count one winner per row, then select the announced batch by (-winner_count,-original_mean,pool_index). Keep the original K=3 stall state and its mean-ranked top-forty mask E_parent as passive diagnostics. The hypothesized path is full-domain winner redistribution -> actual outside-E_parent purchases on naturally stalled states -> accepted feedback that can yield direct or later productive progress. The intervention makes no claim that wider access or higher model probability must improve real scores.
nodes.finding:
All 435 allocations preserved the intended 10,000-draw law, and independent replay reproduced their original posteriors, random states, active counts and passive restricted counts exactly. The 57 naturally stalled announcements changed 142,158 of 570,000 row winners and produced 75 outside-screen purchases across 12 of 15 sessions. The 378 unrestricted announcements matched the inherited law exactly. Outside-screen purchases supplied one direct incumbent improvement worth 0.001547, and three outside origins had later paid descendants. This was real exposure, but it did not improve overall progress: full-run incumbent-gain mass fell from 5.24320 to 5.11213 and late gain from 1.33524 to 1.26997. Mean final Top-1 fell from 0.558039 to 0.549301, a paired loss of 0.008738, with all three seed macros negative. The separate formal Anchor deficit was 0.057729. Zaleplon and sitagliptin also breached the Parent task-regression margins. The allocation/access mechanism is confirmed; the registered useful-progress and score-benefit prediction is refuted.

The stall screen has a positive conditional endpoint contribution on this qPO composition at the registered 0.002 descriptive scale. Its removal was neither dormant nor technically unsuccessful, and missing outside feedback no longer explains the result. Yet the effect cannot be attributed solely to outside purchases: recounting over the full field also changes rankings within the old screen, and one session changed its paid decisions without buying an outside molecule. Later feedback and breeding histories then diverge. The selected outside group exposes a useful limitation: its average prediction overstatement was 0.0820 versus 0.0187 for stalled inside-screen purchases, its prediction MSE was 0.0201 versus 0.0060, and 33 of its 75 purchases were fragments below twelve heavy atoms, none with direct gain. Only 25 survived their batch and eight bred later. Broad access therefore reached structures that the current surrogate and graph proposals converted poorly into useful outcomes. A better ranking or calibration model, or graph operators that preserve coherent molecular frameworks, could address that limitation; these observations do not establish which would work, justify a size gate, or imply missing biological features. Overall typed/generic scaffold counts also fell from 1,982/1,203 to 1,938/1,170 while both size tails grew, so broader eligibility did not create broader realized scaffold coverage. The Molecular assessment further shows unresolved heteroatom-halogen chemistry and unspecified stereochemistry, descriptive limitations shared with the generator rather than proven causes of this loss. Three outside origins had 206 paid descendant memberships and 0.05114 gain summed over origins, but those chains overlap and end at the fixed horizon; they cannot be treated as causal recovery or added to direct gain. This result settles this consumer contrast under the retained posterior and sampling law. It leaves alternative proposal/ranking methods and other qPO compositions open, and supplies no reliable-generalization claim or decision to end the approach.

nodes.hypothesis: On each successful allocation from actual code Parent n-cf8d309c06de, hold the inherited pool order, original raw-score mean mu, score scale s, standardized latent covariance C, actual successful jitter j and full Cholesky factor L fixed. Keep the original eligible set E: all pool indices, or the exact inherited top-forty mean mask when its existing stall predicate is active. Generate exactly R=10,000 joint latent rows F[r,i]=mu[i]+s*(Z@L.T)[r,i]. Draw Z first at the inherited (announced_batch_size,len(pool)) shape and then at (10000-announced_batch_size,len(pool)) from the same existing generator, in that order. For each row assign one winner w[r]=min argmax over original indices in E, and let c[i]=sum_r 1[w[r]=i]. Choose the announced batch by sorting E once by (-c[i],-mu[i],i). The domain E remains fixed for every winner count; selecting a member does not remove it from later winner events and does not condition covariance or introduce a fantasy label. An exact zero count is a valid finite-panel result: it is filled by the same original-mean then index rule, never an adaptive sample-budget change or a fallback. For selected set S, M(S)=sum_{i in S} c[i]/10000 is the empirical probability that a single row winner lies in S. The active top-count set must weakly maximize M among all feasible batches. Compared with the complete passive original Thompson batch on the first rows and its own availability masks, predict at least one changed paid set and strictly positive aggregate captured-mass gain. That is a finite-panel allocation prediction, not a calibrated chemical-optimality or global-optimum claim. Higher full/late useful paid gain is a separate downstream prediction. The extra allocation RNG advance is intrinsic to this registered construction; there is no assertion of matching later Parent/Child random states or adaptive histories.
nodes.finding:
The allocation mechanism is confirmed. All 435 batches exactly reproduce the registered 10,000-draw counts and ordering, with no fallback. Average captured winner probability rises from 0.44950 for the passive original rule to 0.56646; 432 batch sets change, and 2,311 changed-to molecules receive real feedback. This is a finite-panel result on the Child’s actual states, not a score for the unpurchased alternatives. Mean final Top-1 falls from 0.60703 to 0.55804, a paired change of -0.04899; all three seed macros decline and the 0.60903 target is missed. On all 4,350 purchases, parent-beating offspring increase from 634 to 723 and incumbent updates from 253 to 300, but total incumbent-gain mass falls from 5.97807 to 5.24320. The late half improves: 96 versus 76 updates and gain mass 1.33524 versus 1.02241 on 2,175 purchases. Prospective mean-squared error on the purchased stream falls from 0.01160 to 0.00671. Thus more frequent small gains, better selected-stream error and stronger late progress do not compensate for the lost full-run progress.

The borrowed winner-frequency and top-probability batch construction both operated faithfully. Their transfer is limited to the inherited latent posterior and each freshly generated eligible field; this does not test the paper’s observation posterior, fixed-library setting or global-optimum guarantee. The loss cannot be explained by wholesale failure to sample or by mean/index completion dominating allocation: the median field has 118 positive-count candidates, only 11 of 4,350 selections have zero counts, and the two 5,000-draw halves share an average 9.06 of ten selected members. Some estimator uncertainty remains—283 of 435 half-panel sets differ—but this experiment does not identify its causal cost. The deeper limitation is useful conversion. Within purchased batches, winner probability has mean rank correlation 0.178 with realized scores, compared with 0.429 for the original predictive mean; these are selected-stream diagnostics, not measurements of unpurchased winners. Probability concentration also coexists with more similar purchases: fragment-excluded within-batch similarity rises from 0.483 to 0.524 even while typed/generic scaffold counts grow from 1,667/951 to 1,982/1,203. This supports a diagnosis of continued local refinement and motif growth within the current search, rather than global scaffold collapse. The size tails remain costly: all 143 purchases below twelve heavy atoms contribute zero incumbent gain, and the above-fifty tail grows from 44 to 194 purchases while contributing only 0.04996 gain. Changed-to molecules do survive and breed, so a missing feedback path is ruled out; their lineage does not reveal the scores of displaced alternatives. A different ranking model aligned with realized gain, or a proposal/search method that sustains useful distinct molecular frameworks, could address these limitations; neither is established as a remedy here. The result settles activation of this frozen configuration and rejects its full-run benefit prediction on this panel. It leaves the broader approach open and does not authorize an automatic sample-count or mask retune.

nodes.hypothesis: Sample accepted trajectory-balance replay from an equal mixture of inherited score-rank probabilities and uniform scaffold-group mass with the inherited conditional rank probabilities preserved within each group.
nodes.finding:
The declared replay mixture ran in all 449 executed feedback states. Actual distinct scaffold groups per 32-member update rose from 17.87 to 23.26, with broader exposure in all fifteen task sessions. Graph-origin replay received less probability, but its average sampled trajectory log-probability increase rose slightly from 0.169 to 0.176 nats and more later policy emissions occupied previously trained graph families. Mean accepted policy-origin score increased from 0.205 to 0.238. This did not improve every output measure: raw valid-novel yield fell from 66.59% to 64.74%, duplicates increased, and emitted scaffold coverage narrowed slightly. Both formally successful seed endpoints fell, by 0.02618 and 0.06224. The third seed completed its oracle calls but failed on the final canonical-identity feedback join, leaving its formal macro score unavailable.

Extra archive coverage did reach neural learning and subsequent sampling, so the result rules out a purely cosmetic entropy increase. It also exposes the allocation tradeoff: on the same accepted histories the mixture cuts expected graph-origin mass from 72.53% to 59.12% and reduces high-score rank emphasis, while giving much more replay to lower-ranked policy and initial records. Some transfer measures and average policy scores improve, yet those changes coexist with fewer novel raw candidates and weaker completed-seed best results. Broad replay therefore does not establish better endpoint search. The chemical assessment reinforces the distinction: plausible cyclic amines coexist with peroxide, N-halogen and constrained unsaturated-ring families, so family breadth does not certify useful functional context. The terminal failure is a separate inherited canonicalization weakness exposed by one emitted molecule; it explains the missing third formal score and does not explain the losses in the two successful seeds. A complete three-seed score-benefit conclusion remains unavailable.

nodes.hypothesis: Select historical replay members by oldest last-training-membership batch, breaking ties by the inherited descending accepted-score/canonical order, while preserving the original accepted records, replay count, top-score memory retention and equal-row online learning.
nodes.finding:
The scheduling and learning effects both occurred across all three seeds and five tasks. In the 390 nonterminal updates with surplus memory and unequal waiting ages, selected examples had waited 4.425 updates on average, versus 2.568 for the passive uniform choice on the identical memory and timestamp state: an increase of 1.856 updates. The increase was strict in 389 cases; in the remaining case both choices already selected five examples at the maximum waiting age. Refreshing the actual selection never left a larger pending maximum wait and reduced it in 286 of 420 comparisons. Replay memberships differed from uniform in 405 updates, and all 405 produced gradient changes above the registered numerical tolerance. Historical mean squared target error fell from 163.326 to 113.039, decreasing in 416 of 420 updates. These intermediate gains did not deliver the intended score gain. The three-seed mean final-best score was 0.495438, versus 0.507554 for the parent, a paired mean change of -0.012116. Population standard deviations were 0.022530 and 0.011518. Paired macro changes by seed were -0.029843, -0.035944 and +0.029439. Sitagliptin accounted for the main loss: its task mean fell from 0.297258 to 0.205390, with a decline in every seed. Zaleplon and median similarity gained 0.015642 and 0.015419 in task mean; scaffold hopping changed by -0.000575 and DRD2 by +0.000804. All 4,350 submitted policy proposals were valid and canonically novel within their sessions, and every task completed its 300 evaluations. Raw duplicate draws declined from 30.11% to 26.93%; all 435 child batches completed in one sampling call, whereas five parent batches needed another call.

More even access to retained records is now established, but it did not ensure that more of the available records were revisited before they disappeared. Across the actual trajectories, the mean largest waiting age in eligible memory fell from 9.898 to 4.486 updates and its observed maximum fell from 25 to 7. First historical reuse had a shorter tail, with its maximum falling from 23 to 6 updates, while its mean became later: 3.385 to 3.967. Of 1,602 identities with a usable replay opportunity, 556 never received one, compared with 540 of 1,562 in the parent. Among those 556 child identities, 401 had been evicted and 155 were still retained when the last useful replay opportunity ended. Scheduling the oldest records therefore improved waiting-time balance without resolving loss of access through retention turnover and the finite horizon. The actual selection had slightly higher reward than passive uniform on the same memory, by 0.003784 on average. Its poorer endpoint is therefore not explained by a general same-memory preference for weaker accepted scores. The adapted trajectories nevertheless supplied lower average rewards in both their historical and current elite groups. The fixed parent-stream schedule also shortened waits, but cannot predict which new molecules a changed policy would generate. Waiting time does not measure forgetting, and a larger learning gradient does not demonstrate useful transfer. The 480 positive log-probability targets among 2,100 nonterminal historical exposures remain mathematically unattainable. The supplied chemistry assessment describes broad, mostly conventional aryl amide and basic-amine chemistry, with incomplete local attachment and substitution comparisons, occasional uncontrolled growth and no explicit tetrahedral stereochemistry. Its scattered sitagliptin leaders do not establish a consistent productive local series. These findings, together with lower duplicate concentration and lower score, show that fitting retained strings more evenly is insufficient to preserve useful chemical relationships during exploration. Future tests need to connect refresh opportunities to retention lifetime, measured target error and the quality of subsequent novel molecules.

nodes.hypothesis: Replace the Parent's single acting Q-function with five independently initialized Q-functions trained on persistent Bernoulli bootstrap masks of accepted replay, each with its own lagged double-Q target, and select one head uniformly at episode start to control all exploitation decisions in that episode while retaining the Parent's epsilon branch.
nodes.finding:
The heads learned from different persistent transition subsets and kept their assigned identities through all 250 molecular editing episodes. Of 1070 exploitation decisions after learning, 710 strictly preferred an edit outside head zero’s maximizing choices; every episode offered multiple exploitation decisions under its persistent head. All 7250 head updates had nonzero parameter changes, and paired average learning residuals decreased for every task and head. Mean molecular fingerprint distance from episode starts rose from 0.443448 to 0.489426, and distance between contemporaneous lane states rose from 0.681615 to 0.733227. Later episode-best gains following losses increased from 123 to 145 events, although their mean positive increment fell from 0.015693 to 0.010788. The single-seed evaluator macro Top-1 score fell from 0.406693 to 0.350704, a change of -0.055989. Task Top-1 scores changed as follows: zaleplon_mpo 0.332184 to 0.438122 (+0.105938); deco_hop 0.614535 to 0.621204 (+0.006669); drd2_docking 0.753647 to 0.301684 (-0.451962); median_2 0.195125 to 0.184354 (-0.010772); sitagliptin_mpo 0.137973 to 0.208154 (+0.070181). All five tasks completed their 300-evaluation budgets with no invalid or duplicate proposals.

Scarce feedback was sufficient to produce distinct learned head policies that changed real multistep search. The receipts rule out unused network copies, numerical value offsets alone, mask regeneration and broken feedback handling as explanations for this run. The exploration effect also appeared in average fingerprint distances, yet the large docking-score loss outweighed gains on three tasks. Greater policy and state diversity therefore did not deliver a higher aggregate score in this test. The molecular assessment still finds concentrated high-scoring families, reactive heteroatom motifs and demanding short bridges. The docking decline accompanies a different nitrogen, bridge and sulfur arrangement, which is an observed association rather than an identified causal structural defect. Broader fingerprint movement has not yet established broader coverage of useful, practical scaffold families. Further evidence is needed to separate the contributions of independent initialization, masked learning and persistent head identity, and to estimate score reliability across seeds. These results come from one paired screening seed; they do not establish a general score penalty or calibrated uncertainty.

nodes.hypothesis: Within m-eca1b7eb5895, remove only off-diagonal pending-density consumption at selections satisfying episode > 0 and parent_id == 0 on code Parent n-fc3b91c9623a. With K the inherited eligible-sibling count-Tanimoto kernel, leave D_i=sum_j K_ij*N_j and P_i=sum_j K_ij*O_j computed and recorded unchanged. The active root started quantity becomes D_i+O_i rather than D_i+P_i, so only sum_{j!=i} K_ij*O_j is omitted from the exploration denominator and zero-start priority. Active exploitation remains M_i if N_i>0, else inherited neutral 0.5; active bonus is 0.5*sqrt(2*log(max(2,N_parent+O_parent))/(D_i+O_i)) when started>0 and the existing None/priority convention when zero. Earliest occurrence wins ties. Actual own pending O_i and the parent pending numerator are retained. The causal activation claim is that naturally nonzero cross-origin pending support ceases to suppress these bonuses, producing different root choices that reach actual paid descendants; any score consequence is a separate measured hypothesis.
nodes.finding:
The intended removal executed faithfully. It increased 6,068 exploration bonuses and indices and changed 1,269 of 3,830 promoted-root choices. Those changes reached 1,201 of 4,350 paid optimizer molecules, including 722 of 2,175 late purchases; 68 changed routes were abandoned. Fourteen task/seed cells were exposed. The never-promoted median task at seed 0 remained unexposed and unchanged. No selector, backup, pending-accounting or preserved-law violation was found. Mean score fell from 0.5001487124432433 to 0.46001796961200997, a paired loss of 0.04013074283123336: seven cells improved, seven worsened and one tied. Full incumbent-improvement mass fell from 4.37484902101401 to 3.772887878545513 over all 4,350 purchases; late mass fell from 0.8438973049856529 to 0.4888364972281913, with 30 strict improvements instead of 38. The registered score-preservation prediction is refuted. The separate formal Anchor mean remains 0.607030316211131, and its required improvement of 0.002 is not reached.

Shared pending density has a positive conditional contribution when promoted roots already use their own accepted-return peaks and retain shared completed density. Removing it almost always redirects a changed choice from the current origin toward the preceding origin; realized preceding-origin purchases rise from 785 to 1,481, while current-origin purchases fall from 2,795 to 2,099. The result rules out score preservation for this frozen intervention, while leaving the broader tree approach and interactions with completed density open. It does not overturn the earlier benefit of removing shared root values: the two consumers have different conditional roles. The loss is concentrated unevenly across seeds, especially the first docking run, so neither generalization nor per-choice mediation is established. Methodologically, broader graph variety still fails to ensure useful chemical conversion. Typed scaffold unions increase from 1,684 to 1,744, yet the paid stream still contains 314 molecules below six heavy atoms and 287 above fifty, with both tails also present in the Parent. Molecular assessment finds useful intact aromatic/amine and aromatic/carbonyl combinations mixed with core-deleted fragments, repeated large cores and difficult bond or ring contexts. This supports a limitation in the proposal operator’s ability to change topology while preserving useful connected chemical environments, rather than literal scaffold collapse. A proposal operator with coherent functional-substructure edits and bond/ring-context awareness is the relevant missing kind of capability; this panel does not establish its score benefit. Candidate-exclusive timing, precise late timing, measured RNG invariance and independently trusted task-safety evidence remain unavailable.

nodes.hypothesis: Project each representable fresh decoded canonical molecule through the current sequence-flow encoder before applying the unchanged latent-GP joint Thompson acquisition, so acquisition uses the molecular representation on which accepted-score training is defined.
nodes.finding:
Both added replicas used canonical projected coordinates for all 2,900 evaluated proposals, with exact token and molecular-identity reconstruction. Every evaluated proposal moved from its raw continuous coordinate; the mean distance in normalized GP features was 0.95846. Holding the eligible molecules, fitted GP and random draw fixed, projection changed the selected identity set in 218 of 272 groups with more eligible molecules than available positions, replacing 469 selections. Every objective completed 300 evaluations in full batches of ten valid, novel molecules.

On the same accepted outcomes, projected predictions reduced mean absolute error from 0.07795 to 0.04938. Nominal 95% coverage increased from 1,656/2,900 (57.1%) to 2,653/2,900 (91.5%), and mean signed standardized residual moved from -1.83106 to +0.03189. Mean interval width increased from 0.16169 to 0.21524. Lower error and higher coverage occurred in every objective in both added replicas; the original screening replica showed the same direction of change.

The added replicas scored 0.4858806 and 0.2958706 in macro final Top-1, compared with 0.4804828 in the screening replica. The complete three-seed mean is 0.4207447, with population standard deviation 0.0883268. DRD2 accounts for most of this variation: final scores were 0.9043966, 0.9089320 and 0.0688042. The original unprojected Parent has only its screening result at 0.4197516, so a paired three-seed score benefit remains unresolved.

The coordinate correction has a reproducible local effect: it changes allocation beyond duplicate and representability filtering, and improves predictions for the molecules actually evaluated. The low-scoring DRD2 replica makes the remaining limitation concrete. It still changed the selected molecules in 23 of 28 groups with surplus candidates and achieved projected prediction error of 0.00416 with 95.2% coverage, yet never reached the high-scoring family found in the other two runs. Accurate predictions within a weak region can coexist with poor discovery. The molecular assessment supports this distinction: the successful DRD2 run finds a recognizable aromatic saturated-amine core, while the weak run stays among less useful arrangements. Which aspect of preparation or subsequent search determines access to that family remains open; the replicas use different pretrained checkpoints and vocabularies as well as different search seeds.

Proposal support remains narrow. Of 184,080 raw decodes in the added replicas, 174,820 returned their generating center; filling the batches required 477 refill groups. The representability gates excluded 675 candidates for unknown tokens, 46 for excessive length and 18 for failed lossless encoding. The shared-pool diagnostic separates the immediate projection effect from those gates, but their separate effects on a complete search have not been measured. Coverage also remains uneven, falling to 83.4% and 78.6% on sitagliptin despite wider intervals. The assessed chemistry retains radical, unusual-charge and chain-growth liabilities around recurring cores. Projection therefore establishes representation agreement and a more useful local predictive model; reliable access to useful scaffolds, uncertainty calibration and chemically plausible alternatives remain distinct problems.
