nodes.hypothesis: Stall-conditioned contraction of the Thompson residual amplitude: while this session's counter of consecutive non-improving announced batches is at or above three, multiply only the sampled residual of the correlated fresh-pool allocation, score_scale * (standard_normals @ Cholesky_factor.T), by the fixed constant 0.6666666666666666 (the float64 nearest to 1/1.5, so sampled residual variance is four ninths of the inherited variance around unchanged count-GP posterior means), so the ten sequentially masked argmax choices of a stalled batch move toward higher fitted posterior mean and out of the high-posterior-SD tail. The factor is exactly 1.0 before the counter first reaches three and again from the batch after the first strictly improving batch. The fitted posterior mean, the count-Tanimoto kernel, normalization, noise, the covariance and its Cholesky factorization with the original jitter retries, the single standard-normal draw with its shape, order and consumption count, the sequential availability masks and the first-index tie rule are unchanged.
nodes.finding:
The change ran exactly as registered. Every session was identical to the Parent until its first stalled batch, the two deco_hop sessions that never stall reproduced the Parent record for record, the sampled deviation was exactly two thirds of the Parent's in stalled batches and untouched everywhere else, and the logged stall counter matched an independent recount in all 435 batches. Inside stalled batches the allocator did what the contraction was meant to do. On the 13 identical first-stall pools it changed 54 of 130 picks and swapped in 38 molecules, moving the average pick from the 78th to the 88th percentile of predicted score and cutting tiny fragment picks from 6 to 3, exactly the preregistered numbers. Across all of its own stalled batches, picks sat at the 91st percentile of predicted score (Parent 84th), with fewer picks from the model's uncertain tail (15 against 43) and fewer fragments (12 against 22). The swapped-in molecules were better bets: on identical pools they averaged 0.473 against 0.350 for the molecules the Parent evaluated instead, higher in 12 of 13 sessions, which is the mirror image of the earlier widening arm (0.18 against 0.36). Stalls ended sooner: a third of stalled batches broke the stall (27.5% for the Parent) and resolved stalls lasted 2.1 batches instead of 3.2, so the Child spent 79 batches stalled instead of 91. Within those batches offspring beat their parents more often (10.9% against 8.6%), positive parent-relative gain rose from 1.64 to 1.89 and summed incumbent improvement from 0.477 to 0.519, but the number of incumbent improvements stayed at 28 and the mean offspring score stayed at 0.405. The gain was not broad: stalled-batch improvement was higher in only 5 of 13 sessions, and much of the first-stall advantage came from one sitagliptin session. None of this reached the endpoint. After the first stall the Child's ordinary batches realized less than the Parent's (0.470 against 0.563 summed incumbent gain, lower in 8 of 13 sessions), so total gain after the trigger was 0.989 against 1.039. The complete 15-cell mean fell 0.0033 (0.5931 against 0.5965), short of the +0.002 bar, with seeds at -0.029, +0.020 and -0.001. Two sitagliptin cells swung -0.103 and +0.129, and dropping any single cell moves the mean anywhere from -0.013 to +0.004. The loss is inside the -0.014 to +0.008 spread of the earlier same-trigger arms.

The stalled-regime allocation question now has a clear local answer. The two directions of the same knob behave as mirror images on identical pools: widening swapped in worse molecules and contraction swapped in better ones, so during stalls the model's predicted mean is a better guide than its uncertainty and, judged by the molecules it picks, the inherited amplitude over-explores there. What this arm also shows is that this local improvement is too small to steer the endpoint. Stalled batches are only about a fifth of the budget, and the extra stalled-batch gain (about +0.04 summed over 13 sessions) is far smaller than the variation between runs that diverge after the first stall: single cells move by 0.10 to 0.13 depending on whether a session breaks out of a stall early or stays stuck. Raw stalled-batch totals do not discriminate between the two directions, since both widening and contraction raised them while both lost on the panel. Per-pick quality does discriminate: mean offspring score, parent-beating rate and same-pool swap quality. Future arms on stall-time allocation should be judged on those, not on totals that grow or shrink with exposure. Two leads remain open, and neither can be settled from one realization. First, the Child's ordinary batches after a stall realized less gain than the Parent's. That may be path noise, or it may mean contraction narrows what the population later breeds from: the molecular review found the Child's top zaleplon molecules collapsed onto 8 skeletons against the Parent's 16, sitting on a flat plateau of halogen swaps. Second, a constant contraction neither escalates nor lets go without an improvement. One sitagliptin session stayed contracted for its last 14 batches and finished 0.10 below the Parent, which is the case TuRBO handles with a restart this arm did not adopt. The route on this knob should stop here. Both directions are measured at the bound trigger, removal is already known to cost about 0.12, and any further dose would be a sweep. If stall-time behaviour is pursued further, the lever is what happens once a stall ends, or the plateau-forming edits of the generator, not the amplitude of the stalled-batch draw. Placing this delta against this round's neutral path-divergence reference is left to Curate.

Thirty evaluated products are single-call edits of scored parents; three follow crossover and two receive later edits. Formula preservation does not fix those liabilities. Earlier results from other optimizers, their partial composition records and shared-Parent sibling experiments remain separate; they do not identify an interaction with counts, additivity or universal benefit.

nodes.hypothesis: Add a task-local, score-ranked memory of at most 32 previously selected elites and uniformly replay up to one historical elite per current elite, using each molecule's original accepted SMILES serialization and score in the unchanged Augmented Hill-Climb loss alongside the current batch elites.

Across the two new replicas, previously accepted elites entered training 1,400 times in 280 feedback updates that could affect later proposals. Every eligible update had a measurable historical gradient contribution. Historical mean squared target error fell from 152.985 before an update to 119.449 afterward, a mean paired decrease of 33.536; the mean decreased in all ten task runs. Current-elite error also fell on average. All memories respected the 32-elite cap, the prior stayed frozen, and all 2,900 submitted proposals were valid, canonically unique direct policy samples. Duplicate draws were 29.04% and 28.48% in the new replicas, versus 32.82% in seed 0; only three of their 290 batches needed an additional sampling call. The new macro final-best scores were 0.50517 and 0.49479, compared with 0.52270 in seed 0. The three-seed mean was 0.50755 with population standard deviation 0.01152. The largest loss of the screening result was on zaleplon: its final-best score was 0.52806 in seed 0 and 0.40677 and 0.39007 in the new replicas. Each task completed all 300 oracle evaluations.

The repeated result establishes that accepted historical information changes learning and is fitted again across seeds; the original activation was not peculiar to the screening run. It does not establish forgetting in the current-only algorithm or a reliable score advantage over it, because the supplied baseline is the same replay implementation on seed 0 and each replica used a separately prepared prior. Historical reward was stronger than current-elite reward in 150 of 280 new updates, including 42 of 56 median-similarity updates and 35 of 56 sitagliptin updates. Its pooled reward mean was nevertheless lower than that of current elites. Older elites therefore add stronger reward information in particular sessions, rather than being uniformly better training examples. Fitting these targets requires both likelihood directions: the historical sequence log likelihood rose by 2.530 on average when its target was above the starting value, and fell by 1.253 when the target was below it. Of the 1,400 exposures, 328 had positive log-probability targets, which cannot be attained. This inherited limitation remains even when replay works. Lower duplicate concentration did not recover the strongest zaleplon result. The molecular assessment points to different amide connectivity and substituent arrangements there, while finding continued narrow productive families, uncontrolled growth and unspecified stereochemistry elsewhere. Replay preserves accepted reward information but does not by itself preserve favorable chemical relationships during exploration. Matched current-only replicas would be needed to assess score benefit separately from prior and search variation.

The removal operated with shared exploration density and virtual-root choices preserved on every audited state. It resolves the value-consumer question on this Parent and finite Search panel; it does not separately price density, root sharing, maximum memory or their interactions, and it does not decompose the earlier joint-removal effect. The change ran exactly as registered. Every session was identical to the Parent until its first stalled batch: same candidate pools, same random draws, same picks. The two deco_hop sessions that never stalled reproduced the Parent's runs record for record. Inside stalled batches the sampled noise was exactly 1.5 times the Parent's, and outside them it was exactly unchanged. The Child spent 107 of 435 batches in the stalled regime over 36 episodes in 13 of 15 sessions, against 91 batches and 29 episodes for the Parent. In those batches the widened sampling changed the chosen set in 105 of 107 batches and swapped 356 of 1,070 picks, about the one third the pre-run replay predicted. Choices moved as intended. The median pick fell from the 92nd to the 78th percentile of predicted score, and rose from the 32nd to the 49th percentile of model uncertainty. Outside stalls no pick changed.

The extra exploration did not produce more gain. The cleanest test is the first stalled batch of each session, where Child and Parent faced the identical pool and the Parent actually scored the molecules the Child dropped. There the best new score was identical in all 13 sessions. The 43 molecules the wider sampling swapped in averaged 0.182, while the 43 they displaced averaged 0.363, and the swapped-in set was worse in 12 of 13 sessions. Across all stalled batches, a stalled batch raised the session best 27.1% of the time, against 27.5% for the Parent. Swapped-in picks beat their best parent 3.4% of the time, against 10.6% for the picks both rules agreed on. Summed gain inside stalls did rise, from 0.477 to 0.603, and resolved stalls ended slightly sooner (2.93 batches against 3.20). But that sum grew because the Child was stalled longer: gain per stalled batch was essentially flat, and more stalls ran out of budget unresolved (7 against 4). From the first trigger onward, over the same 2,340 evaluations, the Child realized less best-score gain than the Parent (0.894 against 1.039) and fewer parent-beating offspring (230 against 261).

The complete matched panel mean fell from 0.5965 to 0.5867, a paired change of -0.0097 against the required +0.002, and all three seed macros were lower. Five cells rose, seven fell and three tied: the two never-stalled deco_hop sessions, plus one sitagliptin session that ended level. Most of the loss sits in zaleplon_mpo, the task that stalls most: it fell in all three seeds (-0.065, -0.034, -0.034) after 41 stalled batches against the Parent's 33, and its gain inside stalls fell from 0.152 to 0.052. The other ten exposed cells average about -0.001; that is a sensitivity note, not a substitute for the panel.

Widening the Thompson draws while the search is stuck does what it says. It reliably moves picks toward molecules the model is unsure about. But on this Anchor those molecules are worse bets, not hidden opportunities. At this dose, the exact same-pool comparison at the first stall contradicts the hope behind this experiment: the uncertain tail did not hold untapped value that a stall-time boost could convert into gain. In the Parent, incumbent improvements during stalls came mostly from high-mean, low-uncertainty picks (21 of 34 incumbent beats came from the top 3% of predicted score and none from the most uncertain tenth), and those are the picks the wider sampling gave up. The inherited amplitude is therefore at least as good as 1.5 even under measured stagnation, and a larger factor or a lower threshold would swap in more of the same kind of pick. The registered recipe ends here, and no factor or threshold sweep is justified.

The chemistry offers a concrete reason. The molecular review found Child and Parent output nearly indistinguishable except for more 1-4 heavy-atom fragments (139 against 97 of 4,350). That entire excess sits in stalled batches: 69 of 1,070 stalled evaluations against 22 of 910 for the Parent, and 44 of the 356 swapped-in picks. Fragments score at the floor and are what the model is least sure about, so uncertainty-boosting allocation spends budget on them unless emission screens them out. The result also narrows the stagnation question to its other side. TuRBO-style contraction, meaning sharper sampling during stalls, is untested here, and this node does not show that it would help, although the evidence that top-mean picks carry stalled-regime gains is consistent with it. Still open: why zaleplon_mpo absorbs most of the loss, and whether the higher in-stall gain on sitagliptin and median_2 was added gain or merely gain moved from unstalled batches into stalled ones. nodes.hypothesis: Two objective-blind structural predicates are added to the shared generated-pool admission path of the Anchor, applied to every candidate from every origin in every batch, after the inherited checked-graph and identity admission and before the novelty and sulfur checks that stay exactly as inherited. Rule one, the size floor: a candidate whose heavy-atom count is below seven is refused, so no molecule of six or fewer heavy atoms can enter a fresh field, be priced by the posterior, or receive an oracle call. Rule two, the transannular aromatic closure refusal: a candidate is refused when it contains a non-aromatic bond whose two atoms both lie in one connected system of aromatic bonds, are joined by that aromatic system, and are separated in it by a shortest aromatic path of two or three bonds, that is when the new bond closes a three- or four-membered ring through the interior of an aromatic ring or fused aromatic system. Both are pure functions of the proposed molecular graph: no accepted score, no score level, no task identity, no model quantity and no corpus lookup enters either decision. Refused candidates consume a generation attempt exactly as an inherited rejection does and are absorbed by the inherited bounded retry path, so the field target, the batch size, the posterior fit, the correlated draw and its consumption, the stall counter, the stall mask and the fallback routing are untouched; the mechanism's only effect is on the composition of the field the allocator is allowed to price.
nodes.finding:
Both rules executed on every generated candidate in all fifteen sessions and the two target channels are gone. Of 78,031 valid candidates examined, 3,144 were refused (4.03 per cent, inside the forecast two-to-five band): 2,767 by the heavy-atom floor (3.55 per cent, per-session 1.76-5.56 per cent, non-zero in 430 of 435 batches) and 377 by the transannular closure refusal (0.48 per cent, ring size four in 369 cases and three in eight). Both rules fired in 15 of 15 sessions, so neither is dormant. No admitted pool member of the 69,600 and no accepted molecule of the 4,350 violates either rule, confirmed by re-deriving both predicates from the molecules themselves; the Anchor's own stream carries 2,286 sub-floor pool members, 1,974 closure members, 98 sub-floor picks and 140 closure picks.

The field's composition changed as predicted at the bottom and not as predicted above it. The 0-6 heavy-atom band emptied (2,286 to 0), but its mass did not reappear just above the floor: the 7-15 bands are essentially unchanged (2,032 to 1,987) while the 26-30 band collapsed from 23,351 to 13,479 and the 36-plus band doubled from 11,401 to 24,540, lifting the mean admitted size from 29.4 to 34.8 heavy atoms. This is the wholesale upward shift the observable was written to be able to show, and it starts immediately: at batch one, with identical populations, the admitted field is already 1.0 heavy atoms larger, growing to about 6 by batch ten. Every batch still filled to exactly 160 with no truncation. The uncertainty reading moved exactly as forecast: the median of the field's maximum posterior standard deviation over the fitted score scale, over all 435 announced batches, fell from 0.9823 to 0.8909 (quartiles 0.8297 and 0.9417 against 0.9576 and 0.9987), and the number of batches whose single most uncertain member is a sub-floor fragment fell from 421 of 435 to zero; the most uncertain member is now a 10-heavy-atom molecule at the median instead of a 2-atom one. The extra rejections were absorbed: breeding attempts rose from 76,057 to 78,155 (mean 174.8 to 179.7 per batch, maximum 199 to 203 against the limit of 50,000) with zero truncated batches, zero exhaustion errors and zero posterior fallbacks.

The budget freed from the two channels bought nothing. The 98 fragment picks and 140 closure picks fell to zero. The exploration-end picks they had occupied were re-spent above the floor and did slightly better in a weak sense - 246 of 900 mask-free picks ranked fortieth or worse landed above their session median, against 221 of 997 for the Anchor - but they bought exactly the same 32 incumbent improvements. Whole-run realized increment mass fell from 5.978073 over 253 improvements to 5.330399 over 289 improvements, down 0.647674 and lower in 11 of 15 sessions. Both registered session groups fell: the thirteen closure-dormant sessions went 5.264193 to 4.689375 (-0.574817) and the two closure-heavy sessions, seed-2 deco_hop and seed-2 sitagliptin_mpo, went 0.713880 to 0.641024 (-0.072857). The registered "rules need separation" branch, which requires a rise confined to the thirteen while the two fall, therefore does not apply; the main scientific falsifier does, because the rules fired at forecast rates and the fragment band emptied while increments and the panel both failed to rise.

The panel fell on every seed: paired delta -0.043178 over matched seeds 0/1/2 (-0.063587, -0.043393, -0.022554), macro mean 0.563852 against 0.607030, four of fifteen cells up and eleven down, against a registered minimum effect of +0.002. Read against this round's law-free reference on this same Anchor, whose own luck band is -0.055482 to +0.014579 at a realized -0.020452, the delta lies inside the band, so its magnitude is not separable from path luck. The cell-by-cell reading is sharper than the mean. The largest single loss, deco_hop seed 0 at 0.856148 to 0.610130, is reproduced by that pure re-draw, which lost the same cell to 0.607697; this node is in fact 0.002433 above it there. The second fragile high cell, sitagliptin_mpo seed 0, went 0.765861 to 0.650421 against the re-draw's 0.670248. Exactly one cell is not explained by path luck: drd2_docking seed 1, where the Anchor reached 0.999992 and the re-draw 0.991320 but this node stopped at 0.795923, which alone is about -0.013 of the macro mean. In that cell the Anchor's decisive move was a size contraction to a 23-heavy-atom compact molecule at evaluation 34, and this node's field barely contained that region - 9.7 per cent of pooled members at or below 25 heavy atoms against 39.9 per cent, five accepted picks against 111 - while the session's own 115 refusals were all 1-5 atom fragments plus six large closures, so no refusal removed a molecule near the Anchor's winning chain. Increment mass tells the same mixed story: the single available law-free realization on this Anchor sits at 5.671299, so roughly half of the 0.648 drop is reproduced by changing nothing but the path, and this node is a further 0.341 below that one realization.

The admission half of the open admission-versus-operator question now has a measured answer on this Anchor, and it is negative: the two degenerate output channels the chemistry audits kept naming can be removed completely, at full enforcement and negligible cost, and the search does not get better. Removing measurable waste is not the same as creating gain. The fragment channel was real waste by every intermediate measure - 2,286 of 69,600 admitted members, the single most uncertain member of the field in 421 of 435 batches, 98 oracle calls every one of which scored below its session median and improved nothing - and refusing it bought the same 32 tail improvements and a lower realized increment mass. The honest conclusion is the one the intent registered in advance: on this scoring surface the budget spent on the degenerate channels was not the binding constraint, so no floor sweep, no closure-size variant and no valence-context extension follows from this node, and the named successor needs its own forecast and its own test rather than this node's authority.

Two things the campaign believed about this experiment turned out to be path properties rather than rule properties. First, the closure channel's concentration does not transfer: in the Anchor's stream two of fifteen sessions carried 1,596 of 1,974 closure pool members, but in this node's own stream those sessions refuse 0.46 and 0.16 per cent of examined candidates while the heaviest closure load moves to seed-0 deco_hop and the zaleplon cells. A session partition defined on the Parent's realization cannot be used to separate two rules in a Child that diverges from the Parent at its first refusal - here batch one, attempt seventy, on a two-atom candidate. Any future attempt to separate the floor from the closure rule has to do it by running them separately, not by splitting sessions. Second, this round's law-free reference is now the right lens for the whole panel: it already showed that both of the Anchor's high seed-0 cells belong to its particular path, and this node loses them in almost exactly the same way. Reading the two together, the campaign should stop treating deco_hop seed 0 as evidence about any intervention on this Anchor.

What the evidence does add about the method is a size asymmetry. The floor is a lower bound with no upper counterpart, and the operator repertoire has no contraction move of comparable strength to its growth moves: nothing in any trajectory trims an overgrown molecule back to a ring system. With the only downward pressure at admission now one-sided, the admitted field shifted up by about 6 heavy atoms and this node bought 428 molecules above 50 heavy atoms against the Anchor's 44, including 181 and 207 in two deco_hop cells whose scores never left the 0.605-0.614 plateau, and 102 candidates rejected by the inherited 120-atom cap. That runaway is not new and is not this node's invention - the law-free re-draw, which changed no rule, produced 288 such picks in a deco_hop cell of its own - but the mirror image is what cost the one unexplained cell: in drd2 seed 1 the Anchor's win came from contracting 38 heavy atoms down to 23, and a field whose compact region had shrunk to a tenth of its former share never found it. The method class that would address this is not a different floor value but a size-symmetric proposal or admission scheme: a contraction or whole-ring-system replacement operator weighted comparably to the growth moves, or an admission window defined relative to the breeding parents a product came from rather than an absolute bound.

Two further diagnoses from this node's own trajectories bear on where the remaining headroom is. Late budget buys almost nothing: the median session took only 15.2 per cent of its total gain after evaluation 150 (the Anchor 18.1 per cent), and the molecular report shows the tail spent on score-identical isosteres, two molecules sharing 0.46092619586 and differing only by N-F against N-Br, with scaffolds inherited from the starting pool and decorated rather than replaced. And the surrogate's ranking is fine while its uncertainty scale is wrong in a task-dependent way that this intervention did not touch: improvers sit at a median posterior-mean rank of 6 of 160 on both sides, yet only 17.4 per cent of sitagliptin picks land within one posterior standard deviation of their predicted mean and 40.3 per cent land more than three below it, against 94.5 per cent within one standard deviation on median_2 - essentially identical in the Anchor (19.2, 42.3, 95.6). Because the error runs in opposite directions across tasks, no single noise or amplitude constant fixes it; an online-calibrated or heavy-tailed heteroscedastic surrogate would be the class of change that could. Taken with this result, the evidence now points away from the product-admission predicate and toward the proposal repertoire and the surrogate's uncertainty as the places where this lineage is actually bound - a reading that should be finished against the operator-granularity position running in parallel on this same Parent and profile.

nodes.hypothesis: Among exact accepted-score batch maxima, select the neighbor with the smallest capped inverse motif-occurrence overlap with the immediately previous selected transition, then use canonical lexical order for any remaining tie.
nodes.finding:
The rule changed five of 26 tied maximum decisions across two of fifteen task/seed sessions. Each change kept the same accepted score and reduced overlap with the previous move to zero; the corresponding lexical choices would have reversed eight motif occurrences in total. All five choices had later evaluations. Across the complete walks, inverse overlap during score plateaus fell from 26 to 14 occurrences, yet plateau transitions increased from 49 to 52. The three-seed macro mean was 0.52169764, compared with 0.52175912 for the parent: a paired change of -0.00006147, below the predeclared +0.002 improvement. The changed deco_hop continuation finished at 0.61072664 versus 0.60921826, while median_2 finished at 0.18849201 versus 0.19092251. The other thirteen full molecule/score trajectories were identical. The local mechanism is confirmed; the predicted score benefit is refuted.

This rules out failure to execute the tie rule as the explanation for the absent score gain. Reducing immediate motif-count reversal can change the search without shortening its plateaus or improving its aggregate endpoint. The five choices overlap within only two task/seed continuations, so the later deco_hop improvement cannot be credited independently to each of its four changed ties. The count statistic also has a narrower chemical meaning than preserving the last physical edit: it can penalize extending an ethyl group to propyl, or match a motif lost on one ring to a motif introduced on another. One changed choice preserves a C#S-O group by extending an unrelated N-alkyl chain, while another replaces a carbonyl carbon with sulfur. The molecular assessment finds that the altered paths retain or add questionable sulfur, oxygen-oxygen and sulfur-halogen connections, with no change to the pooled highest-scoring molecule on any task. Lower overlap therefore supplies no evidence of improved feasibility or more useful chemistry. Whether a comparison tied to actual edited sites or chemically useful arrangements would improve these choices remains open.

nodes.hypothesis: Regime-split predictive uncertainty inside the accepted-only posterior. The single global fixed-kernel Gaussian process is replaced by a Dirichlet-process mixture of the same fixed-kernel Gaussian processes over this session's accepted archive: assignments are resampled at every announced batch by collapsed Gibbs sweeps that marginalize the latent functions, using a CRP prior whose concentration follows alpha_t = 0.2*sqrt(t)/log(t+e) at announced batch t, an existing-component likelihood equal to that component's leave-one-out GP predictive density of the record's raw score, and a new-component likelihood equal to the exact prior predictive density; each component carries its own location and scale estimated from its own members and shrunk toward the inherited archive-wide values with a fixed five-record pseudocount. Every fresh-pool candidate then receives spatial component weights w_k(x) proportional to (n_k/(n+alpha_t)) / sigma_k(x), plus a fresh-component weight proportional to alpha_t/(n+alpha_t) priced at the prior location and the full prior amplitude; its predictive mean is the weighted mixture mean mu_mix(x) and its predictive variance is the moment-matched mixture variance decomposed into an intra-regime part sum_k w_k(x) sigma_k(x)^2 and an inter-regime part sum_k w_k(x) (mu_k(x) - mu_mix(x))^2. The inherited correlated Thompson allocation consumes a joint 160x160 covariance built as sum_k sqrt(w_k(x) w_k(y)) * [ Sigma_k(x,y) + (mu_k(x) - mu_mix(x)) (mu_k(y) - mu_mix(y)) ], whose diagonal is exactly that decomposition and which is positive semidefinite by construction, with the same single standard-normal array per batch consumed in the same order and count, the same jitter ladder, the same sequential masked argmax, the same per-pick mask update, the same first-index tie rule, the same stall-time top-forty eligibility now ordered by mu_mix, and the same bounded generation-order fallback. No quota, reserved pick, availability override or post-hoc variance rescaling is introduced anywhere, and at one occupied component the whole construction reduces identically to the Parent's own posterior, which is the registered degenerate control.
nodes.finding:
The replacement executed in all fifteen cells and routed every selection: 300 oracle calls and 290 accepted proposals per cell, all 435 pools full at 160 members, zero posterior fallbacks, zero invalid or duplicate proposals, and the twenty Gibbs sweeps per announced batch completed in every batch with no time-budget hit. Cost was never the issue: regime inference took 1.8 to 5.1 seconds per session and the audit under 3 seconds, the slowest cell ran 193.6 wall seconds against the registered 1200-second bound and the 7200-second task timeout.

The partition was real but uneven. Two or more components with at least two members each appeared in 230 of 435 announced batches (52.9 per cent, a bare majority, so the registered degeneracy falsifier did not trigger), and up to nine components occurred, but the session-median occupied count reached two or more in only 8 of 15 sessions against the registered 12. The two flat-label objectives behaved exactly as the degenerate control: all three median_2 sessions never produced a second multi-member component, and across the 158 one-component batches the mixture posterior differed from the inherited single Gaussian process by at most 5.8e-4 in the mean and 1.2e-3 in the SD. The posterior was emphatically not inert where it did split: only 15 of 69,600 pool members agreed with the passive single-GP value to 1e-9, the ten picks differed from the passive inherited replay in 292 of 435 batches (67.1 per cent), and 1,606 of 4,350 accepted evaluations (36.9 per cent) were priced by a component other than the incumbent's, with no quota, mask override or reserved pick anywhere.

The registered uncertainty geometry came out backwards. The archive-far to archive-near predictive SD ratio was supposed to rise above the inherited model's roughly 1.7; instead it fell in 435 of 435 batches and 15 of 15 sessions (for example 0.98 against 1.72 on sitagliptin_mpo seed 0 and 1.01 against 1.56 on zaleplon_mpo seed 2), because the only new variance source, the inter-regime disagreement term, supplied a larger share of total variance in the archive-near half than in the archive-far half in every session (0.89 against 0.80 on sitagliptin_mpo seed 0). Overall predictive SD inflated by 1.0x to 2.0x, and fewer than a fifth of pool members were priced more confidently in 14 of 15 sessions against the registered 20 per cent floor. The pre-endpoint ablated-cluster audit, read before any score, produced 808 comparable held-out-component splits: the mixture's cluster-over-random standardized-error ratio fell below the single GP's on the same splits in only 3 of 15 sessions (12 measurable; median_2 unmeasurable because a single component cannot be ablated) and in 414 of 808 individual splits, against the registered 12 of 15. That is the registered calibration-direction falsifier, and it triggered. The one calibration reading that did improve is interval coverage: held-out-component 95 per cent coverage moved closer to nominal under the mixture in 11 of 12 measurable sessions and was never worse (0.76 against 0.50 on zaleplon_mpo seed 1). The fourth observable also moved as predicted wherever the partition split: the late-session near-minus-far price gap was lower under the mixture in 14 of 15 sessions (0.008 against 0.073 on sitagliptin_mpo seed 0), and its first-to-last-third widening was smaller in 10 of 15, the five exceptions being degenerate cells where the two models differ by under 3.3e-4.

Conversion failed. Realized sequential incumbent-increment mass was 3.928 over 221 improvements, against 5.978 over 253 recomputed on the Parent's own panel by the identical convention and the registered 5.819415 and 255; 74.9 per cent of the Child's mass and 67 of its 221 improvements were carried by picks whose dominant component was not the incumbent's, so the cross-regime channel was wide open and still delivered less. The matched fifteen-cell panel fell to 0.470387 from 0.607030, a paired mean delta of -0.136643 on all three seed macros (-0.125 / -0.247 / -0.039), far below the registered ungated law-free lower bar of -0.050871, and still -0.079 with the worst cell removed and -0.068 with the two worst removed. Per task: zaleplon_mpo +0.006 (inside its 0.02 margin), median_2 -0.009 (just outside its [-0.0078, +0.0067] band), deco_hop -0.075, sitagliptin_mpo -0.258 on all three seeds, drd2_docking -0.347. The reported drd2_docking seed-1 collapse to 0.0617 against the Parent's 1.0 is an instance of the mechanism acting, not a separable failure: at batch 1, with ten records and essentially flat labels, the sampler carved the archive into a nine-member component and a singleton that happened to hold the best record, every pool member was then dominated by the nine-member component, and the candidates the single GP priced at the top (0.0176 to 0.0183, ranks 8 to 26) were repriced down to 0.008 to 0.010 while mid-and-bottom-ranked candidates (single-GP ranks 50 to 143) were bought. The passive replay on that same pool reproduced the Parent's own ten picks exactly, so eight of ten purchases were displaced by the mixture alone; the Parent's line reached 0.55 by batch 3 and 1.0 later, while this cell spent its remaining 280 calls growing the sugar-ketal conjugate it bought at batch 1. The same de-pricing is systematic, not local: in every non-degenerate cell the mixture lowered the single GP's top-ten candidates by 0.048 to 0.236 in score units while moving the whole-pool mean by only -0.075 to +0.020, and the incumbent's component held 8 to 63 per cent of the archive, under 38 per cent in seven of the eight sessions where the partition split, while 82 to 100 per cent of pool members were dominated by the largest component.

The regime split is inferable at this budget and its purchases are real, so the open question of this route is now answered in the negative at the layer that matters. What the campaign did not know is why: the failure is in the weighting principle, not in the split. The component weight is proportional to membership mass over the component's own predictive SD, exactly as the source method specifies, which makes the predictive mean a popularity-weighted average. On a maximization problem the best-known chemistry is almost always the smallest regime, so the rule systematically discounts precisely the candidates nearest the incumbent: the incumbent's component held 8 to 63 per cent of the archive in the active cells and under 38 per cent in seven of the eight, 82 to 100 per cent of pool members were dominated by the largest component, and in all three sitagliptin_mpo cells the incumbent's own component was the largest in just 1 of 29 batches, and the single GP's top-ten candidates were marked down by 0.05 to 0.24 while the pool mean barely moved. For the same reason the predicted far-field uncertainty growth never appeared: with the kernel fixed and only location and scale allowed to differ per component - the deliberate deviation from the source method, which fits per-regime amplitude and lengthscale - the only new variance term is disagreement between component means, and that is largest near the archive where the components actually overlap, not out where knowledge stops. So the far/near SD ratio fell in every single batch. This rules out a specific and previously plausible hypothesis: giving the predictor more locations and scales, with the covariance shape held fixed, does not produce comparable cross-chemotype uncertainty, and the archive-distance calibration defect this lineage has documented for three windows cannot be repaired by partitioning labels alone.

Two things are narrowed rather than closed. First, the premise that recalibration would not convert was never tested here, because calibration did not improve in the registered sense; the one part that did improve, held-out-component interval coverage closer to nominal in 11 of 12 sessions, coexisted with worse standardized error, which says the mixture widened intervals without putting the width where the error is. A predictor that makes uncertainty grow with archive distance has to change the covariance - per-regime amplitude or lengthscale, or an explicit distance-dependent prior variance - not the number of means. Second, the price-gap observable did move as predicted wherever the partition split, so the mechanism can be made to compress the near-versus-far price gap; it simply bought worse chemistry while doing it.

On method, two limitations are now measured on this node's own trajectories. The surrogate's ranking agreed less with realized scores than the Parent's did: pooled chronological batch rank correlation between predicted and realized offspring scores fell to 0.42 from 0.52, and the number of batches where the surrogate beat the archive-mean baseline fell to 364 of 435 from 415, with the collapse concentrated in sitagliptin_mpo (3 to 8 of 29 batches against the Parent's 17 to 28) - the same objective where the mechanism was most active and the score loss most consistent across all three seeds. These are each node's own purchases on diverged archives, so the comparison is descriptive, but it points at the ranking model rather than at the proposal supply, and the remedy is a different ranking rule - one whose component weight reflects the probability that a component contains the maximizer, or a single model whose variance grows with distance - not a different concentration or component count. The second limitation is the search scheme, and it is inherited: the Molecular report finds that within a cell the search enumerates one substituent of one scaffold (twelve proposals at an identical 0.6559 differing only in an alkoxy or thioether arm; ten of another cell's top ten the same enaminone), that diversity lives across seeds rather than inside a session, and that there is no size regulator - the drd2_docking seed-1 cell grew mean SMILES length from 87 to 154 while its best sat at 0.0289 from evaluation 24 to 249 and ended on an MW-991 polyketal cage with 226 of 290 proposals carrying a ketal inherited from one starting-pool sugar. That combination is what turned one mispriced first batch into a 0.94 cell loss: the operator set has no deletion move and the archive rule prices no structural novelty, so a committed line cannot be abandoned. The methods that would remove this are a proposal operator with substructure deletion and intact-ring substitution, and a retention or acceptance rule that prices scaffold-level novelty against the accepted set - not a tuning of the surrogate.

Finally, a measurement lesson with teeth for this panel. In the 158 batches where the partition stayed at one component, the posterior differed from the Parent's by at most 5.8e-4, and that was still enough to flip at least one of the ten correlated Thompson picks in 34 of them (21.5 per cent); in multi-component batches picks moved in 258 of 277 (93.1 per cent). The deco_hop seed-0 departure cell lost 0.231 with an essentially Parent-identical posterior throughout. Single-cell deltas on this benchmark are therefore not attributable to a predictor change of this size, which is why the panel-level reading, robust to removing the two worst cells, is the only usable one here.

nodes.hypothesis: Law-free breeding-stream path divergence. At the start of every announced batch, before that batch's GP fit and its first breeding decision, draw exactly one value with random() from the Evolution's own seeded random.Random generator and discard it. GraphOperators shares this generator, so it drives quantile parent and rank sampling, the crossover-versus-mutation coin, the post-crossover finishing coin, the ordinary walk-length draw and every operator, site and element draw. The discard changes which pseudo-random words all later breeding decisions consume, from the first announced batch of every session. Offspring pools, emitted molecules, the accepted archive and survivors therefore diverge from the Anchor's realization. Every law is unchanged: probabilities, thresholds, operator menu, escalation, sulfur gate, identity admission and both duplicate scopes, pool target, accepted-only count-GP fit, and correlated Thompson allocation. The allocator's separately seeded torch generator still draws one (10, 160) block per batch, so its standard-normal rows stay bitwise equal to the Anchor's. The claim is about a measurement, not a gain. This one change moves the realized breeding path in all fifteen sessions, including deco_hop seeds 0 and 2. Its complete matched panel delta is what path departure alone costs on this Anchor, and it is the reference band for ungated whole-run contrasts.
nodes.finding:
The control ran as registered. In all 15 sessions the run drew and threw away one breeding random number at the start of each of its 29 rounds (435 in total). Each discard came before that round's model fit and first breeding step, and the round-1 values were exactly the predicted ones for each seed. No other rule moved. The selector's own random numbers matched the Parent's bit for bit in all 4,350 picks. Every pool held 160 candidates and no round used the backup route. The model's training sets and normalization matched the inherited rule, and its predictions recomputed to within 5e-14. Operator frequencies, the crossover rate (45.1%) and the finishing rate (35.6%) sat within their nominal bands. The selected candidates also sat at the same places in the predicted-score and uncertainty rankings as the Parent's: shift statistics +0.03 and +0.24, far inside the 3.26 bound.

The path departed in every session, but in ten of them later than registered. On seed 1 all five sessions changed their very first breeding decision, and their round-1 pools shared only 137 to 159 of 160 candidates with the Parent's. On seeds 0 and 2 the two runs made identical decisions within that first parent draw. Python draws random integers by rejecting and redrawing some random words. The Parent's run happened to spend extra words on rejections at exactly that point, which absorbed the two words the discard had used. Round 1 therefore came out identical molecule for molecule. Those ten sessions departed at a later discard instead: round 2 in nine of them and round 3 in drd2_docking seed 0. Their first differing scored molecule came at evaluation 21 to 32, not 11. After the split the runs were as far apart as any rule change. Only 2.3% of the molecules scored after the split also appear in the Parent's same session; the round-38 rule changes ranged from 2.3% to 6.1%.

Scores: the panel mean was 0.586565 against the Parent's 0.596453, a reference delta of -0.009888. Seed macros moved -0.0671, +0.0314 and +0.0060. Six cells rose and nine fell, with a wide spread (cell SD 0.079). Two cells dominate. Deco_hop seed 0 fell from 0.856 to 0.611 (-0.245), and sitagliptin seed 1 rose from 0.500 to 0.657 (+0.157). Without deco_hop seed 0, the other fourteen cells average +0.0069. The Parent's 0.856148 deco_hop seed-0 endpoint was not reproduced. This run's best-so-far there was 0.6073 at evaluation 200 and 0.6112 from evaluation 265 onward, including evaluations 280, 281 and 300. The Parent was at 0.6096 at evaluation 280 and jumped to 0.8561 at evaluation 281. That one cell costs -0.0163 of the panel mean, inside the predicted -0.014 to -0.018. Sitagliptin seed 0 also fell, from 0.694 to 0.599.

For the Research Brief, the median_2 three-seed mean went from 0.222732 to 0.222196 (-0.0005), with cells -0.0024, +0.0058 and -0.0051. On the protected tasks, drd2_docking (+0.0057), sitagliptin_mpo (+0.0335) and zaleplon_mpo (-0.0083) stay within their margins. Deco_hop falls by 0.0798, far beyond its 0.02 margin, and all of that loss comes from the seed-0 cell (seeds 1 and 2 moved +0.0105 and -0.0050). Against the two earlier luck-only controls, which perturbed only the selector and only after a stall, this panel is 0.0082 and 0.0176 lower.

Pure path luck, with no rule changed, produces the same signature as all 28 earlier whole-run rule changes on this Parent. It loses the 0.856 deco_hop seed-0 endpoint, landing at 0.611, inside the 0.581-0.635 range of those 28. It also loses the 0.694 sitagliptin seed-0 endpoint, which all 28 fall below as well. Both cells are favourable draws of the Parent's own run, not damage done by the rule changes. The deco_hop must-preserve margin is therefore breached by departure alone. Any change that leaves the Parent's path early should be expected to lose about 0.08 on the deco_hop task mean, whatever it does. That is a property of the frozen panel for the human to weigh; it does not relax the margin or exclude the cell. The chemistry fits this reading. The re-drawn deco_hop seed-0 session ran away into roughly 1,100-Da peroxide-linked polyaromatics, and 269 of its crossover attempts produced no molecule, consistent with the 120-atom cap on two parents of that size. The two sessions that stayed small reached higher endpoints. Which path a run happens to take decides this cell.

The cell spread makes the pre-registered reading band wide: R3 = -0.0099 with half-width 0.0410. An ungated panel now stands above the law-free reference only above +0.0311 and below it only under -0.0509. Of the 28 earlier ungated changes, 13 fall below (-0.183 to -0.052) and 15 cannot be told apart from luck (-0.051 to -0.013, including the two mildest); none stands above. So 'all 28 negative' is roughly half harm beyond path luck and half the ordinary cost of leaving the Parent's path. The median_2 band is narrower: R3 = -0.0005 with half-width 0.0072, so above +0.0067 or below -0.0078. Five earlier ungated changes clear its upper edge by 0.002 to 0.005 (largest +0.0120), 10 fall below and 13 sit inside. Those five are leads, not achievements. This is one dependent draw, the median_2 floor width was borrowed from the stall-gated controls, and luck alone has moved single median_2 cells by up to 0.006 here and 0.029 in an earlier control. Median_2 also showed its plateau again: this run's seed-2 best and the first selector control's seed-2 best are different molecules with exactly the same score, 0.227237.

The design assumed that one discarded number would shift every later breeding draw. At the level of raw random words that is false. Python's rejection sampling can re-synchronize two streams within a draw, and on all three seeds it did so inside the very first parent draw. On seed 1 the one decision made before re-synchronization still differed, and that was enough. On seeds 0 and 2 nothing in round 1 changed. The reference is still ungated, and every session left the Parent's path by evaluation 32, long before the evaluation-281 jump. Its whole-run calibration therefore stands. A design that needs a guaranteed round-one departure would have to re-seed the breeding generator rather than discard a value. The route's review condition rules out a second ungated draw, so this is recorded only as design knowledge.

Still open: this is one realization. It is coupled to the Parent through the identical selector stream and the re-synchronized breeding stream, so it bounds the size of path noise without estimating it, and no significance statement follows. The round's own ungated position was still running when this brief was written, so applying the band to it is left to Curate.

nodes.hypothesis: On the shared-amplitude episode-owned regional Parent, constrain only the final purchase's eligibility when a feasible region is still absent from the selected prefix. For announced batch size B and candidate ordering O inherited from the Parent, retain the original sample rows and available canonical identities. At positions k < B-1 choose the original global maximum. At k=B-1, form M from regions with zero selected-prefix members and at least one remaining valid novel candidate. If M is nonempty, choose the maximum of that same final sample row among remaining candidates owned by regions in M; otherwise choose the original unrestricted maximum. Preserve first-in-existing-order tie resolution and global identity exclusion. In the frozen two-region batch-ten profile at most one region can be missing after the first nine, and at most the final purchased identity can change. A real accepted final-slot purchase enters the existing episode fit and local-center success/failure law; no missing purchase creates an observation, success or failure. The hypothesized chain is elimination of feasible no-feedback boundaries, more actual local learning/control updates, useful later descendants and improved full/late global conversion. More exposure alone does not establish useful conversion.
nodes.finding:
Every region received a real purchase in every batch: paid regional update boundaries rose from 523 of 870 to 870 of 870, and the longest feedback drought fell from 29 batches to zero. All 435 auctions preserved the first nine choices. The final coverage rule applied 197 times, genuinely diverting 191 purchases and leaving six final choices unchanged. All were accepted. The unchanged controller then made 94 contractions and 62 natural restarts, versus 50 and 19 in the Parent. Of the 191 diverted observations, 165 entered a subsequent owned model fit; 21 ended a retired episode and five arrived at the final boundary. They produced 41 local improvements but only three immediate global improvements. Sixty-two had later accepted descendants; those descendants supplied four further chronological global improvements.

Late global gain per evaluation increased from 0.000382624 to 0.000486230, but full-run gain per evaluation decreased from 0.001296971 to 0.001280512. Complete mean endpoint score fell from 0.5846137565 to 0.5798405659, a paired loss of 0.0047731906 instead of the required gain of 0.002. Seven of fifteen task/seed endpoints improved and eight declined; the seed-macro differences were -0.0273125, -0.0018620 and +0.0148549. The Child also remained 0.0271897503 below the formal Anchor. All fifteen sessions completed without evaluator rejection or numerical fallback. Thus execution and real feedback coverage are established, while the registered conjunction of better full and late conversion and endpoint gain is refuted.

This experiment separates access to observations from productive use of them. The regions can now learn and advance their counters throughout the run, so continued feedback starvation is no longer an explanation for this variant’s weak endpoints. The borrowed forced-access element operated, and the retained separation between selection and paid-data updates operated too. Its finite final-slot adaptation supplies no evidence for the source literature’s age schedule, continuous trust-region geometry or regret guarantees. More paid updates and more restarts did not provide the required finite-budget benefit. Improved late conversion is real, but it did not recover the earlier loss; full increment mass and endpoint score express the same final-minus-initial quantity.

The measured limitation is conversion of the newly purchased regional information into globally useful refinement. Only three of 191 diversions immediately beat the global incumbent, and the union of 478 later accepted descendants contains just four strict global gains totaling 0.008703. Another 129 diversions have no accepted descendant, including five terminal observations for which later use is censored. This does not prove that their labels had no indirect model effect, and the displaced candidates were never evaluated, so the audit cannot assign an actual opportunity cost or identify causal mediation. It narrows the unresolved method question to the quality of regional proposals and their ranking for useful improvement. A proposal operator that can reach distinct complete scaffold/linker arrangements, or a ranking model that estimates their useful improvement, could address that limitation; this node does not establish either remedy.

Molecular evidence explains why broader exploration is insufficient: typed/generic scaffolds increased from 1,880/1,234 to 2,064/1,382, yet one high-score subset of 87 still occupied only 14 typed and eight generic scaffolds and included tied peripheral variants. Both the fragment tail and the oversized tail grew, from 134/245 to 162/262 molecules, while reactive bond environments and unresolved stereochemistry remained. These associations locate proposal-quality limitations, not a proven cause of the score loss or a mandate to remove every unusual group. The finding settles this specific final-slot utility prediction under two feasible regions and batch ten; the wider local-model approach and the isolated contributions of its retained components remain open.

nodes.hypothesis: Reallocate unlabeled prior-training rows within each inherited length bucket using an equal mixture of uniform sampling and capped inverse-document-frequency context-rarity weighting, while retaining original strings and the ordinary holdout checkpoint rule.
nodes.finding:
Training consumed the intended redistribution in every seed: all 89,226 minibatches changed row membership, and mean capped rarity rose from 2.25875 under the paired uniform reference to 2.38357, a 5.53% increase. Rarity rose in all seven length buckets in every seed. Exposures to contexts below the training-frequency median increased about 1.86-fold. Independent evaluation of the selected checkpoints on identical holdout rows found lower rare-context token loss in all three seeds: pooled Parent loss 2.25659 fell to 1.85778. Common-context loss increased from 0.56370 to 0.56435; the recorded ordinary mean holdout loss increased slightly from 0.56458 to 0.56501. All preparations completed 29,742 steps, with mean preparation time rising from 259.5 to 368.4 seconds. Original strings, ordinary checkpoint selection and online search interfaces remained intact.

The generation outcome was less favorable. Across matched complete tasks, raw policy validity fell from 70.04% to 62.77%, although candidate-side duplicate rejection also fell. First-batch validity was 91.17% in the Parent and 89.67% in the child; later batches were substantially less valid and already reflected task feedback. The two fully completed replicas increased mean final Top-1 from 0.522200 to 0.576765, with paired gains of 0.035148 and 0.073981. Gains centered on sitagliptin and one deco-hop replica, while other task comparisons were mixed. The third zaleplon task stopped after 120 of 300 evaluations when repeated canonicalization of a ring-closure offspring alternated aromatic representations and tripped the inherited trajectory-identity check. Fourteen of fifteen tasks completed, so no complete three-seed child macro result is available.

This establishes that extra exposure to existing rare token contexts can improve their heldout likelihood without improving average likelihood or adapted generation validity. The conditional result concerns only 306 rare-context targets across the three holdouts, about 0.052% of all heldout targets; there are no heldout contexts absent from training. It therefore supports learning of underrepresented existing syntax, while broad chemical support and unseen-context generalization remain open. Common contexts slightly deteriorated in every seed, and all update caps were reached, ruling out fewer training updates as the explanation for that tradeoff.

The molecular evidence further limits what the higher completed-replica scores mean. Conventional aromatic/amine and carbonyl families coexist with high-scoring peroxide/O–halogen variants, hydroxyallenes and strained closures; favorable scores do not show that those liabilities are necessary, since more conventional alternatives also score highly. The changed training distribution did not supply missing stereochemical examples. The early termination exposes a separate fragility in inherited graph canonicalization, whose source was unchanged; it does not invalidate the verified training allocation, but it prevents a complete reliability claim. A useful next question is how to retain the observed rare-context learning while preserving common-context performance and chemically credible generation, with the identity failure addressed as a separate online mechanism.

nodes.hypothesis: Add an optional single-source two-single-bond rewiring mode inside change_bond that replaces two vertex-disjoint nonaromatic single bonds by an alternative perfect matching of their four endpoints, conserving atom attributes, per-atom heavy degree, bond-order sum and molecular formula under the fixed selected-first-bond sampling law.
nodes.finding:
The route executed throughout the panel: 3,141 switches were sampled, 74 failed the sanitation conservation gate, and 3,067 passed, including 2,861 immediate identity changes. It supplied 178 evaluated offspring. Of 124 clean rewrites of a scored source, 26 beat that source and 24 of those winners later bred; one unused winner still had a later opportunity, while one was born in the final batch. Across all route offspring there were 38 wins, 32 ties and 108 losses, and 126 were actually reused. Nevertheless, mean final Top-1 fell from 0.595670 to 0.556135, a complete paired loss of 0.039534 against the required gain of 0.002. All three seed averages declined; four of fifteen endpoints improved and eleven declined. The standard deviation of seed averages fell from 0.026593 to 0.020758, which does not offset the lower score.

Lack of valid products, failed delivery and complete absence of productive reuse are ruled out as explanations for this route’s loss. Local improvements were real, but they were insufficient: over the whole search, parent wins rose from 629 to 709 while mean offspring score fell from 0.38526 to 0.35259 and the mean best-parent reference fell from 0.47046 to 0.42528. There were more incumbent improvements, but their summed magnitudes fell from 5.80766 to 5.21465. Thus easier parent comparisons and more reuse can coexist with worse endpoints. The chemical review likewise shows that alternative ring arrangements can retain reactive bonds and unresolved geometry or stereochemistry; conservation does not establish feasible or useful chemistry. Four unevaluated pool products also changed aromatic representation after passing the registered conservation witness, so exact attribute preservation cannot be extended across every canonical reparse. The complete result supports an adverse effect of adding this fixed route in this composition, including its displaced legacy opportunities and changed adaptive history. It does not identify a chemical mediator or the value of the whole graph-search foundation.

nodes.hypothesis: Remove only the active qPO winner-frequency consumer from n-0eae06e8d311. E, mu, scale, covariance, actual jittered L, both normal arrays and all numerical guards remain inherited. Continue computing all 10000 fixed-E winners and (-count,-original_mean,pool_index) qPO top-b as a passive reference. The active batch must exactly equal the already implemented sequential first-row rule; its total same-panel winner mass is no larger than the passive qPO optimum, with strict decrease on positive-mass departures. Changed purchases and feedback can alter later search and endpoints; their benefit is unknown. This is the registered obstacle intervention and component removal, not an RNG reset, a full posterior-selector removal or a repeat of the refuted whole-replacement benefit prediction.
nodes.finding:
All 329 observed allocation states reproduced the registered sequential rule, unchanged posterior and the same two normal draws totaling 10,000 rows. Relative to passive qPO on those same states, 328 batch sets changed and one changed only in order. Mean captured winner mass fell from 0.621196 to 0.492151; 326 batches lost mass and three tied. These changes reached 1,650 of 3,280 observed paid molecules. One further ten-molecule batch was selected before interruption but has no observed scores. Seeds 0 and 2 completed: their mean endpoint was 0.547781, versus 0.559914 for the code Parent on those seeds, a difference of -0.012133. The seed differences were -0.032094 and +0.007828. Against the formal Anchor on the same two seeds the mean difference was -0.070147. On this matched subset, full incumbent-gain mass fell from 3.514219 to 3.392891, while late gain rose from 0.694548 to 1.125092. Seed 1 completed the first task and only 90 paid proposals of the second before the allocation ended. Thus 1,070 of the required 4,350 paid observations and 580 of the required 2,175 late observations are missing; the registered complete-panel non-inferiority and contribution tests cannot be decided.

This result separates verified consumer removal from an execution failure: selection, posterior fitting, random-number consumption and real paid-path exposure all check out wherever the mechanism ran. It also separates late recovery from endpoint success. The two complete seeds have fewer incumbent updates (179 versus 200), larger purchased-stream prediction MSE (0.008048 versus 0.006986), and lower full gain despite greater late gain. The observed loss is adverse descriptive evidence for abandoning the count consumer on this host, but the missing seed prevents assigning its registered positive or negative contribution. The study does not restore the Anchor random stream or test removal of posterior selection itself, and it does not settle the wider qPO approach. Chemically, the search still refines close analogues: fragment-excluded similarity to the prior archive rises from 0.8898 overall to 0.9044 late despite 1,423 typed and 901 generic scaffold identities. All 94 observed purchases below 12 heavy atoms yield no incumbent gain; larger molecules sometimes help, so these data do not justify a universal size ban. Reactive nitrogen/oxygen-halogen motifs and unspecified stereochemistry remain inherited limitations. A proposal operator that changes connectivity while preserving useful functional-group arrangements and molecular scale could address the observed local refinement and fragmentation; the evidence does not establish that a different ranking model alone would remove them. Changed-to purchases produce 0.962080 of the 3.611243 observed gain, versus 2.649162 from agreed purchases, but those route groups are selected on different states and have no unpurchased counterfactual scores. Their difference is not causal credit.

nodes.hypothesis: Remove m-00000000000b only: in every ordinary single-parent construction attempt of Evolution.suggest, retain exactly the existing rng.choices([1,2,3],[0.82,0.15,0.03]) draw at its current location but execute exactly one GraphOperators.mutate call, regardless of that draw. Preserve the call's twelve-attempt internal retry law and its failure handling. The direct mechanism is eliminating unscored ordinary continuation transitions, making any successful first-call product the sole ordinary final product offered to the inherited admission gates and posterior selector. This changes which ordinary graphs can enter the pool, be purchased and seed descendants. The working score expectation is loss of some useful multi-edit lineage access and therefore a removal loss, informed by the earlier whole-run control but explicitly unsettled on this mask-bearing Parent. A gain or an interior-band effect is an equally reportable answer to the frozen three-sided contribution question. Crossover construction, finishing and all other consumers are outside the intervention.
nodes.finding:
All 15 Search sessions completed. Every one of 41,559 ordinary attempts executed exactly one mutation call; 7,462 requests still drew two or three calls, representing 8,713 omitted requested slots. The Parent executed 34,210 one-call, 6,245 two-call and 1,233 three-call attempts. Shortened requests remained usable: 527 reached accepted evaluations, 460 were admitted to the survivor population, and 182 later generated an accepted child. The Parent had accepted 289 multi-call products, of which 64 later generated an accepted child; those classes describe separate realized paths, not paired replacement molecules.

Mean final Top-1 fell from 0.607030 to 0.572105, a loss of 0.034925 against both the code Parent and formal Anchor. Seed-average changes were -0.065123, -0.033205 and -0.006448; nine task/seed cells lost and six gained. Task-average changes were +0.024940 for zaleplon, -0.093439 for decoration hopping, +0.007175 for docking, +0.001727 for median similarity and -0.115029 for sitagliptin. Population SD across the three seed averages fell from 0.030175 to 0.014335. The retained continuation therefore has positive conditional contribution by the registered -0.002 removal-loss rule. The protocol task-safety comparison flags the sitagliptin regression.

Local hits moved in the opposite direction to endpoints: parent-beating evaluations increased from 634 to 686 and incumbent improvements from 253 to 273. Full incumbent-gain mass fell from 5.978073 to 5.454194 over 4,350 evaluations, whereas late gain increased from 1.022408 to 1.090617 over 2,175 evaluations. No posterior fallback or incomplete pool occurred. First-call complete failure was never exposed on either panel; its retained handling was checked in source rather than inferred from a runtime event.

This closes the registered whole-session contribution question on this stall-masked Parent: removing occasional longer ordinary walks reduced endpoint search even though single-call products were admitted, bought, reused and often beat their immediate parents. Local hit frequency and slightly higher late gain did not recover progress lost earlier. The loss is concentrated—decoration-hopping seed 0 and sitagliptin seeds 0/1 account for 87.9% of gross negative endpoint differences—but the mean remains below -0.002 after removing any one cell or any one task. This is stronger than a sign that depends on one cell, while still being one finite, adaptive contrast. It does not identify the omitted molecule that would have helped, separate path divergence from a molecular mediator, or establish a preferred continuation schedule. Older mask-free and stall-only findings retain their original, qualified scopes.

The method limitation is uneven structural exploration, not a demonstrated universal scaffold collapse. Fragment-excluded within-batch similarity increased from 0.432 to 0.461 overall, yet the number of distinct scaffold types increased in several tasks. The largest decoration-hopping loss coincides with substantial molecular growth: 271 of 870 purchased products exceeded fifty heavy atoms, versus 18 in the Parent, and its within-batch similarity rose from 0.430 to 0.521. The molecular assessment also associates the sitagliptin losses with fewer ordinary aliphatic-amine alternatives and more N-halogenated/imino variants. These are observed associations, not proof that size or a functional group caused the loss. A proposal operator that can rearrange rings and linkers while preserving useful functional-group relationships and controlling molecular growth could address the structural limitation; a walk-length retune alone does not provide that capability. No evidence here settles the broader graph-search approach, the tree suffix, or the independent value of the retained posterior and stall-mask components. Full gain mass merely restates endpoint progress. Runtime also illustrates why costs must be separated: summed task wall time rose from 578.5 to 1,237.5 seconds, while oracle time rose from 162.9 to 828.8 seconds; the record does not establish a slower candidate implementation.

nodes.hypothesis: Remove two-parent connected-fragment crossover from fresh-pool production, routing every proposal through the inherited single-parent local-mutation walk while retaining the count-based posterior and correlated batch allocation.
nodes.finding:
Crossover is absent from all 73,389 eligible breeding attempts, all 69,600 pooled candidates and all 4,350 evaluated offspring. All 15 task-and-seed evaluations complete, and the inherited mutation operators, nitrogen-position exchange, accepted-score archive and correlated posterior selector remain active. The three-seed mean final score falls from 0.57434 to 0.54548, a loss of 0.02886 against the registered 0.002 non-inferiority threshold. Every seed mean declines: by 0.06136, 0.00445 and 0.02078. Mean task scores fall by 0.11996 for sitagliptin, 0.01804 for DRD2 and 0.01126 for decoration hopping; they rise by 0.00327 for median similarity and 0.00167 for zaleplon. Seed dispersion increases for every task.

Mutation-only search makes more strict improvements over its generating parent: 713 versus 624 among 4,350 offspring. It also records 286 versus 241 incumbent improvements and reuses 2,606 versus 2,455 nonterminal offspring as later parents. Yet mean absolute offspring score falls from 0.38664 to 0.34884. Generic scaffold coverage contracts from 13,420 to 9,655 in the pools and from 1,059 to 984 among evaluated molecules. Pools need fewer attempts, and internal invalid graphs fall from 536 to two, but there is no isolated generation-speed measurement: the large total runtime reduction comes mainly from recorded oracle time.

The complete-loop ablation supplies evidence that crossover still contributes to this integrated method on the supplied panel. Its lower observed parent-beating rate was an inadequate argument for removal. That rate compared crossover products with the better of two parents, and both route cohorts had already been shaped by population history and posterior selection. The simpler route makes many small local advances on lower-scoring search paths; more improvements and more survivor reuse do not guarantee stronger endpoints. Removing crossover also changes the opportunities seen by the retained nitrogen move: valid exchange steps increase from 435 to 658, while accepted walks containing an exchange fall from 46 to 27. Local availability therefore does not establish useful allocation after the search distribution changes.

The coverage evidence narrows, but does not settle, the explanation. Evaluated scaffolds distinguished by atom and bond types increase from 1,806 to 1,898, while generic topologies decrease. This is consistent with more chemical variation within a narrower set of shapes. Even the number of generic cores producing incumbent gains rises, so broad exploration loss alone is insufficient to explain the lower endpoint quality. The molecular assessment shows a tighter size range, 21–44 heavy atoms instead of 1–120, alongside an increased median, 33 instead of 29. N–halogen structures and unspecified stereochemistry become more frequent, and bridged or strained heterocyclic families remain. Compactness has not supplied chemical control. Which recombination opportunities preserve productive scaffold relationships, and how their changed populations interact with posterior allocation, remain open. The result does not show that crossover is useful in every generator or that any individual omitted recombinant would have scored well.

nodes.hypothesis: Remove only live accepted-population capacity truncation, retaining every usable canonical unique finite-scored accepted record in inherited descending score and ascending serial order for the unchanged score-quantile breeder.
nodes.finding:
The removal ran as intended in all fifteen task/seed sessions. Every accepted molecule stayed live, and 1,632 records that the old cap would discard were actually used in 5,005 parent draws. They produced 120 accepted direct offspring; 56 of those later bred and 20 produced another 47 accepted descendants. Eligibility did not guarantee delivery: 289 supported records were never drawn while beyond the old cap, and many batches drew them without accepting an offspring. Probability changes among records already inside the capped population also had substantial exposure, so this is the total capacity effect under the inherited sampler.

Mean final Top-1 fell from 0.595670 to 0.572175, a paired change of -0.023495, beyond the registered 0.002 descriptive scale. All three seed macros declined; twelve of fifteen task/seed endpoints declined and three improved. Seed population SD fell from 0.026593 to 0.011713, which does not itself establish reliability. Across accepted proposals, mean absolute score fell from 0.385256 to 0.370365 and the mean best-parent reference fell from 0.470456 to 0.449157. Strict parent wins rose from 629 to 773, while incumbent improvements fell from 258 to 229. All formal sessions completed their full oracle budget.

This answers the narrow capacity question: bounded live membership adds conditional endpoint value when the original weighted score bands, recursive breeding and full-archive predictor remain active. Retained lower-ranked molecules really reached breeding and accepted reuse, so their failure to improve the aggregate cannot be explained by storage without access. The higher parent-win count is not evidence of better search: it accompanies weaker parent references, lower absolute offspring scores and fewer incumbent gains. Evictee-derived products were not uniformly useless—one became its session’s final leader and three improved an incumbent—but those local successes did not offset the total loss.

The audit also identifies the access boundary: merely exceeding 64 live records was insufficient; the original upper-half sampler first exposed discarded ranks when the archive reached 130. This separates the evictee route from earlier probability shifts among shared records. Their individual causal contributions remain unresolved. The frozen molecular assessment found mixed chemistry, with fewer direct nitrogen-halogen bonds but more oxygen-halogen and peroxide bonds, and persistent ring-geometry and stereochemical gaps. Broader breeding therefore did not demonstrate consistently more credible chemistry, nor does that association explain the endpoint loss causally. Whole-loop contribution, chemical mediation, transfer beyond this three-seed profile and any additive relationship to earlier controls remain open; the exact capacity control is answered without a cap sweep.

nodes.hypothesis: Admit generated pool candidates only under a parse-and-serialize-stable canonical identity, normalizing stable aliases and rejecting representations that remain inconsistent on confirmation.
nodes.finding:
Both known stable aliases were normalized, reducing disagreements between stored pool identities and their molecules from two to zero. Across 75,484 otherwise valid checked attempts, 75,482 identities stayed unchanged and two received confirmed spellings of the same graphs. Independent checks found no admitted identity instability, graph modification, new identity collision or feedback mismatch. Neither corrected pool member was selected. All 435 pools reached 160 candidates, and all 4,350 generated evaluations retained the parent’s exact molecule and score order. Mean final-best score across three seeds remained 0.544374, with population standard deviation 0.013310; every paired task and seed score difference was zero, within the supplied 0.002 non-inferiority allowance. The offspring parent-beating rate also stayed at 565 of 4,350, or 12.99%. Identity checks consumed 7.28 seconds in aggregate, and the added receipts increased diagnostic log size from 98.24 MB to 147.13 MB. Recorded total wall time was lower, but these historical runs do not isolate the incremental runtime cost.

This establishes a correction at the pool interface that preserves the represented graphs and the search trajectory under the installed parser. Its demonstrated benefit is stable bookkeeping: the only corrected entries were unselected, and their fingerprints were unchanged. A separate read-only replay rejected all 59 unstable representations recorded in the sibling with carbonyl preservation, including one that sibling had emitted. Five of those unstable representations retained the same fingerprint after another parse, showing why fingerprint equality cannot substitute for the registered identity test. The child itself produced no unstable candidate and never evaluated a renamed identity, so empirical failure prevention and accepted feedback under a changed key remain open. Its unchanged emitted chemistry still contains reactive heteroatom-halogen and peroxide bonds, concentrated aromatic ring families and unspecified stereochemistry. Identity consistency does not resolve those chemical limitations.
