nodes.hypothesis: Quality-ranked structurally separated restart centers: In n-7d1e6230ecce, change only restart-center ranking at an existing natural restart. Preserve exclusions of retiring and other center and preference for never-used roots; if all eligible roots were used, first restrict to the least-recent-use tier. Within that tier, retain accepted candidates whose count-Morgan generalized Tanimoto similarity is at most 0.5 to BOTH retiring and other center; choose the highest observed score, tie earliest serial. If this subset is empty, choose the original highest-score/serial root within the same tier and log infeasibility. Threshold 0.5 is frozen once as a geometric separation rule, not fitted to objective labels. Keep all initial roots, model ownership, singleton restart fit, shared amplitude, graph operators, radius/success/failure logic and auction unchanged. No forced distant purchases, new candidates, predictor context borrowing or continuous recentering. The causal claim is that deterministic geometric eligibility makes an actually triggered reset leave both current neighborhoods, altering subsequent de novo graph support and paid exposure; useful escape requires larger GLOBAL incumbent increment mass per real post-reset evaluation despite lower root quality. Root reuse itself spends no evaluation and supplies no fresh label.
nodes.finding:
The restart rule operated correctly in all 14 observed resets: 13 chose a different root and one kept the original choice. All satisfied the fixed separation condition, all received immediate feedback, and the inherited trigger and singleton model initialization were preserved. Mean distance from the nearer old center rose from 0.204 for the same-state original choices to 0.532, at a mean known starting-score cost of 0.176. The new episodes produced 6,140 identities absent from earlier fields and bought 627 evaluations, but only three evaluations improved the global best. Their total fresh global gain was 0.0012921, or 0.000002061 per paid evaluation, versus the Parent’s 0.000123063. Local recovery was much larger, totaling 0.64113, which does not establish useful escape.

Seeds 0 and 2 completed: their mean score was 0.571827 with population SD 0.021043, a paired difference of -0.005351 from the Parent and -0.046102 from the formal Anchor. Neither complete seed improved its macro score; among all 11 completed task endpoints, five fell and six tied the Parent. Seed 1 completed its first task, stopped during the second with exit143, and has no observations for the remaining three. These partial receipts remain evidence, but the full fifteen-endpoint macro and the registered joint benefit falsifier cannot be evaluated. The result therefore establishes activation and adverse observed benefit movement, while the overall registered intervention remains inconclusive.

This result rules out failure to move the reset roots or blanket denial of first feedback as explanations for the observed lack of useful progress. Structural displacement, new proposals and recovery from a weak local root can all occur without beating the session incumbent. The narrow literature borrowing—score ranking after a separation feasibility test—operated; the result does not evaluate the source method’s global surrogate or diverse-output objective. The surviving controller still starts each reset with one label and a constant predicted mean. A restart model that conditions on accepted evidence beyond that single label, or a search scheme that evaluates restart opportunity in terms of global improvement, is a different kind of intervention that could address that information gap; this experiment does not establish either as beneficial.

The molecular assessment also narrows the diagnosis: the generator already produces many ring systems and frameworks, so a universal shortage of scaffold diversity is unsupported. Yet 112 of 3,410 paid proposals were tiny fragments, 228 exceeded fifty heavy atoms, and unusual N-halogen connections remained frequent. Broad graph novelty often failed to preserve the useful connected group arrangements present in stronger molecules. Proposal operators that preserve those arrangements while changing scaffold or linker structure could address this distinct limitation; increasing geometric distance alone did not do so here. The missing seed-1 panel leaves the complete benefit test open, and this node does not overturn earlier findings or decide the future of the broader approach.

nodes.hypothesis: Veto a valid novel neighbor only when its signed motif changes match every currently live inverse restriction of at least one selected-transition provenance group and that complete group contains both inverse signs, replacing the Parent's one-match-per-sign criterion without changing memory credit or lifecycle.
nodes.finding:
On the Child's actual source states and live memory tables, the inherited rule would veto 178 fresh draws; the complete-signature rule vetoed 65 and admitted the other 113. Every new admission was evaluated, affecting 96 batches across all fifteen task sessions, and twenty became next states. Fifteen improved on their source, five tied and 93 worsened it; five produced immediate archive gains. Complete signatures still vetoed 63 distinct fresh molecular identities, including a two-attribute group left after overlap replacement. Memory credit, four-step tenure and overlap handling were preserved. All budgets and batches completed, using 5209 generation attempts versus the Parent's 5303. The three-seed macro mean fell from 0.521759 to 0.482572, a paired change of -0.039187 against the required +0.002. All three seed means declined. Four task means fell; median_2 rose by 0.002696. The largest task-mean losses were sitagliptin (-0.104268) and DRD2 (-0.075446). Across all accepted proposals, source improvements fell from 468 to 436, and strict archive improvements changed from 238 to 237 while their total magnitude fell from 4.699005 to 4.111202.

Incomplete motif matches do exclude some useful variations: newly admitted methyl addition, ring opening and aryl substitution produced real archive gains. A newly admitted phenol-oxygen deletion was selected despite a score loss, then a newly admitted hydroxymethyl addition in the next batch produced the strongest observed DRD2 molecule. Those concrete successes did not rescue the overall score claim. The checks rule out an unexercised predicate, missing feedback, loss of unconditional memory credit, altered expiry or restored historical signatures as explanations for the negative panel result. Requiring full motif coverage reduces exclusions as intended, but this panel shows that greater matching specificity is not sufficient to identify restrictions that can be removed beneficially. Whether the partial-signature vetoes help diversification remains open: once batch membership changes, later source graphs and random-stream consumption change, and ancestry alone cannot assign the final score difference to one admitted edit. The chemistry assessment also finds persistent reactive heteroatom bonds, unusual sulfur environments, difficult ring geometry and absent stereochemical assignments alongside recognizable aromatic/carbonyl and amine families. The stronger individual molecules therefore do not establish improved chemical feasibility or broader useful scaffold coverage.

nodes.hypothesis: Replace episode-owned raw response amplitude by a shared current-session accepted-label amplitude. At every announcement, let A_b contain exactly the finite records already accepted into this Objective Session's unique global archive before the batch, including initial records and retired-episode records once per accepted identity/receipt. Set s_shared=max(sqrt(mean_{i in A_b}((y_i-mean(A_b))^2)),0.001), with population rather than sample variance. Keep local fitting and raw conditional mean mu_r intact, as well as normalized covariance C_r, its existing jittered Cholesky factor L_r, and original normal block Z_r. Replace s_region by s_shared only in sample_r=mu_r+s_shared*(Z_r@L_r.T), and report active predictive SD s_shared*sqrt(clamp(diag(C_r),0)). This pools amplitude evidence without pooling conditional labels or means. It changes raw observation-noise amplitude as well as raw predictive residual amplitude; standardized kernel/noise/jitter remain fixed. The hypothesized path is removal of singleton amplitude collapse, changed non-quota competition, real additional small-cohort feedback, then improved complete-panel useful gain per evaluation. No calibrated-posterior or latent-only-variance claim is made.
nodes.finding:
The shared amplitude ran faithfully in all 435 batches, with both local conditional models preserved. On the same actual search states it changed 168 purchase sets, added 305 evaluated identities, and increased mixed-region batches from 55 to 88. Singleton-region purchases increased from 156 under the local-amplitude replay to 186 actual accepted labels. All 19 real restarted regions received feedback immediately; the Parent had two restarted regions that received none over 19 and 23 subsequent batches. The whole-panel global improvement per evaluation rose from 0.00125135 to 0.00129697, so the registered exposure and useful-conversion predictions are supported. Mean endpoint score rose from 0.571384 to 0.584614, a paired gain of 0.013230 across three seeds, although one seed lost. The formal Anchor mean is 0.607030: the Child remains 0.022417 below it and fails the separate +0.002 performance target. Task-safety margins were not supplied, so no new task-safety classification is made.

The experiment establishes that a singleton local model need not stay starved when amplitude information is shared: on three real restart states, 26 accepted labels came from regions that would have received zero purchases under the local-amplitude rule. Both literature-derived separations—shared amplitude from local conditioning, and amplitude aggregation from conditional solves—operated; the particular archive-moment estimator is not the sources’ estimator and these results do not establish calibrated uncertainty. The complete-panel benefit does not prove that rescued restarts caused the score gain. Across all restarted episodes, improvement per evaluation fell from 0.00017542 to 0.00012306; active-only purchases produced just 10 global improvements totaling 0.02410, while most improvement came from purchases the two rules agreed on. Late-half improvement also fell, from 1.15447 to 0.83221. Thus amplitude sharing removes a demonstrated feedback obstacle without establishing efficient later exploration. The molecular evidence supports that limitation: evaluated batches remain highly local (mean within-batch count-Tanimoto 0.7315 versus 0.4945 in generated fields), and median_2 gains more typed and generic scaffolds yet loses all three paired endpoints. Frequent unusual N-halogen chemistry and unresolved stereochemistry further separate scalar score from practical molecule quality; their contribution to score is not isolated here. A proposal or search scheme that reaches alternative coherent frameworks while preserving useful functional arrangements is the kind of method change that could address the remaining conversion limitation. This panel does not establish which such method would work, durable expected benefit, or that this approach should end.

nodes.hypothesis: On code Parent n-cf8d309c06de, remove only m-000000000006 sampled residual influence from the successful allocation consumer when restrict_top_mean is None at announcement. Keep the original fitted mean mu, score scale s, full covariance, actual successful Cholesky factor L, standard-normal array Z and original P=mu[None,:]+s*(Z@L.T), including the original finite guard and failure routing. At every position of an unrestricted successful announcement choose the lowest original pool index attaining the largest original mu among currently available indices. Remove the chosen index from the active availability mask exactly once. Every restricted successful announcement continues choosing the maximum original P row on the original top-mean eligible set and original sequential masks. The direct causal path is residual-consumer removal -> changed unrestricted molecular identities with weakly higher original mean at a shared available set, and weakly higher batch summed original mean -> accepted feedback and its downstream population/fit. At least one changed paid set and a strictly positive aggregate original-mean gain versus the separately masked passive original sequence are predicted. Higher original means need not produce higher realized scores; the conservative utility prediction is that removing useful residual exploration decreases the complete endpoint mean. This changes neither cross-candidate correlation alone nor residual amplitude, fitted covariance, mean location, eligibility, or the state predicate.
nodes.finding:
The removal executed cleanly. Across all fifteen sessions, 343 unrestricted announcements made 3,430 paid choices by the original predicted mean, while all 920 choices in the 92 restricted announcements retained their original sampled rule. Relative to an independently masked replay of the original rule at those same states, 341 purchased sets changed, 2,115 paid identities were different and the summed original predicted means rose by 80.584. Every paid identity joined real feedback. The complete endpoint mean nevertheless fell from 0.607030 to 0.512644, a difference of -0.094386; the three paired seed differences were -0.172229, -0.047378 and -0.063552. Thirteen task/seed endpoints fell, one rose and one tied. The loss exceeds the registered descriptive 0.002 scale. Full incumbent-gain mass fell from 5.978073 to 4.562278 over 4,350 purchases, although positive improvement events increased from 253 to 271. Late gain mass moved in the opposite direction to its conservative prediction, rising from 1.022408 to 1.401443 over all 2,175 late purchases. This late increase is real, but it does not recover the complete endpoint loss.

On this retained host, sampled residual influence outside the stall restriction contributes useful exploration beyond greedily maximizing the fitted mean. The result prices that consumer conditionally; it does not show that every sampled component is useful, identify correlation separately, or establish a transferable benefit on another host. More local wins and smaller selected-stream prediction error were not reliable substitutes for final progress: full mean-squared prediction error fell from 0.011599 to 0.004092 while endpoints worsened. Paid search concentrated on related structures: nonempty typed/generic scaffold identities fell from 1,667/951 to 948/452, and nearest-prior-archive similarity after excluding molecules below twelve heavy atoms rose from 0.7322 to 0.8110. This is consistent with a loss of exploratory breadth, but does not prove that scaffold contraction mediates the score loss. Chemistry also remained uneven. Tiny fragments became rarer, yet above-fifty-heavy-atom purchases increased from 44 to 260, including 229 late purchases; peroxide-containing output increased from 118 to 516. Ring-rich generation is already available, while attachment context, controlled growth and explicit stereochemistry remain weak. A search scheme that preserves multiple chemically plausible families, together with context-preserving scaffold or linker moves, could address that observed limitation; this experiment neither implements nor validates such a method. The full panel, both size tails, adaptive gate-zero cells, unchanged sets and terminally censored purchases remain included. Passive alternatives have no measured outcomes, and the restricted and unrestricted interventions cannot be added together. Ending or replacing the approach remains a later planning decision.

nodes.hypothesis: Freeze the active count-Tanimoto GP training dataset to immutable copies of the original usable initial accepted archive in its original order for every inherited fit, jointly freezing its empirical label normalization while retaining full real-archive feedback for live graph breeding and the original correlated posterior allocation on fresh pools.
nodes.finding:
All 435 GP fits keep the same ten initial accepted molecules, raw labels and normalization within each task/seed. Across 420 later fits, 4,200 generated observations remain in the real archive but never enter training; the 150 final observations have no later fit opportunity. Predictions for the same previously emitted molecule stay fixed to numerical precision. The selector remains active on every fresh 160-member pool, with nonzero correlated draws. Recursive breeding also remains active: 1,751 accepted offspring later serve as parents in 102,673 draws.

Every first batch matches the Parent. In batch two, the same pool and normal draws produce different evaluated sets after the first excluded feedback; parent and pool histories diverge in batch three. All three replicas complete. Mean final Top-1 falls from 0.595670 to 0.443813, a paired change of -0.151856 against the predicted loss scale of 0.002. Seed changes are -0.181637, -0.118363 and -0.155569. All fifteen endpoints and all five task means decline. The zaleplon result in seed zero nearly matches its Parent, losing only 0.000484, while the largest loss is 0.430456 in docking seed two. Seed dispersion also falls, around the lower mean.

Ongoing conditioning on generated accepted observations adds value beyond an initially fitted predictor in this optimizer, even when real-label survival, recursive breeding and posterior selection remain active. The experiment therefore answers a narrower question than removing the whole selector or freezing the breeding cohort. Training membership, later label information and empirical normalization were held together: their individual effects, and their interaction with survival, remain unassigned. All sitagliptin fits retain the initial scale floor, but this exposure alone does not establish that the floor causes its endpoint losses.

Useful local search persists under the frozen predictor. It produces 580 best-parent wins and 125 incumbent advances, and every endpoint exceeds its initial best. The molecular assessment finds recognizable amide and aromatic-carbonyl families, useful available amines, changed linkers and ring closures. Some lower-scoring Child leaders have more conventional local chemistry than their Parent counterparts; other outputs retain reactive bonds, doubtful ring geometry and unresolved stereochemistry. The loss does not establish absent chemical novelty, require reactive motifs or identify a chemical mediator. Three leaders arrive in the final batch and cannot show later feedback effects.

The lower selected-stream prediction error is measured on different molecules and cannot establish better calibration or replace the endpoint contrast. Likewise, passive full-archive calculations change all 420 later selected sets on the actual Child pools, but do not supply alternative rewards or future histories. This complete exposed result ends the registered initial-cohort control. Shared-Parent sibling experiments and historical repeated trajectories are dependent evidence, so their effects cannot be added or treated as independent replications.

nodes.hypothesis: Trigger-matched law-free path divergence on the stall-masked Anchor. No law, probability, threshold, rule or constant changes anywhere. In Evolution.suggest, after the inherited stall-state block has computed this batch's regime from the inherited K=3 counter of consecutive non-improving announced batches and logged stall_regime_state, and before the GP fit, the probe update and the batch's first breeding draw, draw exactly one value with random() from the Evolution's own seeded random.Random(seed) generator - the generator GraphOperators shares - and discard it, if and only if that same batch's inherited restrict_top_mean is not None, which is exactly the condition under which the top-forty eligibility restriction is passed to the allocator for that batch. Outside the restricted regime nothing extra is consumed. That generator drives quantile parent and rank sampling, the crossover-versus-mutation and finishing coins, walk length and every operator, site and element draw, so from the discard onward every breeding decision consumes different pseudo-random words and the realized path departs from the Anchor inside the restricted regime only. Everything that decides anything stays exactly as inherited: the eligibility rule itself with K=3, M=40 of the unchanged 160-member pool, the (-posterior mean, pool index) ordering, the per-pick mask update and restoration on the first improving batch; the accepted-only chronological count-Morgan generalized-Tanimoto posterior with its 0.05 noise SD, adaptive mean and population-SD normalization, full covariance and float64 Cholesky jitter ladder; the single (10, 160) standard-normal array drawn from the separately seeded torch generator, its consumption order and the sequentially masked argmax pricing with its tie rule and numerical fallback; the sulfur gate, canonical identity admission, both duplicate scopes, greedy-64 retention, quantile breeding, the continuation law, the seven operator families at unchanged weights and connected-fragment crossover at 0.45 with its finishing edit. No decision reads the discarded value. The claim is a measurement, not a gain: the complete matched fifteen-cell panel delta against the Anchor is what law-free path departure costs when it is confined to the batches the mask governs, with 347 of the Anchor's 435 announced batches and both of its never-stalling deco_hop sessions untouched by construction.
nodes.finding:
The placebo did exactly what it was built to do and nothing else. In all 15 runs it logged one discard record per round (435 in total) and threw away one breeding random number in exactly the 84 rounds in which that run's own stall reflex was active, and in none of the other 351. Each discard came after the round's stall check and before the model fit and the first breeding draw. The two deco_hop runs that never stall drew nothing and reproduced the Anchor's runs molecule for molecule and log record for log record, ending at exactly 0.856148 (seed 0) and 0.644234 (seed 2). In the other 13 runs, every scored molecule and every logged breeding, pool, selection and stall record before the first stalled round matched the Anchor's exactly: 2,160 of 4,500 scored molecules, including the 150 starting molecules, and 75,841 log records. The first stalled round fell where it did in the Anchor in all 13 runs, and each run left the Anchor's path right there, at the first breeding attempt of that round; the first different scored molecule came one to seven evaluations into that round. No rule moved. The selector's own random numbers matched the Anchor's bit for bit in all 4,350 picks, every round bred a full pool of 160, there were no fallbacks, and the stall counter, the top-forty restriction, the model fits, the sulfur gate, the duplicate checks and the operator, crossover and finishing rates all conformed to the inherited rules on the run's own records. Where both runs were unrestricted (317 rounds), the picks sat at the same places in the predicted-score and uncertainty rankings as the Anchor's (shift statistics -1.55 and +0.34 against a bound of 3.26).

After leaving, the runs went their own way: only 146 of the 2,329 molecules scored after the departure point (6.3%) also appear anywhere in the Anchor's same run. The stall reflex's own exposure drifted with the new paths, as the design allowed: 84 restricted rounds in 35 episodes against the Anchor's 88 in 29, with 13 rounds at restricted depth six or more against 19. Inside the restricted rounds no pick ever fell outside the top forty by predicted mean (840 picks, mean rank 11.2 against the Anchor's 11.7). Those rounds broke the stall 29 times in 84 (34.5%; Anchor 25 of 88) but added less best-score gain (0.445 against 0.547).

Scores: the panel mean was 0.585797 against the Anchor's 0.607030, a reference delta of -0.021233, with all three seed macros lower (-0.0291, -0.0294, -0.0052). Two cells rose, nine fell and four were identical: the two never-stalling deco_hop runs, plus drd2 and sitagliptin on seed 2, which re-reached the Anchor's exact scores with halogen-swapped analogues of its best molecules. In task order (zaleplon, deco_hop, drd2, median_2, sitagliptin) the cells moved: seed 0 -0.0383, 0, +0.0126, -0.0175, -0.1025; seed 1 +0.0132, -0.0016, -0.000005, -0.0011, -0.1575; seed 2 -0.0027, 0, 0, -0.0232, 0. Two sitagliptin cells carry most of the loss. Seed 0 ended at 0.6634 instead of 0.7659 and seed 1 at 0.4869 instead of 0.6444, together -0.0173 of the panel; the other 13 cells average -0.0045. Every exposed run still finished above its inherited pre-departure best.

The registered reading rule: the fifteen cell deltas have a spread of 0.045603, so the half-width is max(0.009482, 2 x 0.045603 / sqrt(15)) = 0.023549 and the gated band is -0.021233 plus or minus 0.023549, i.e. -0.044783 to +0.002316. The Anchor's +0.010577 over its mask-free Parent lies 0.008261 above the band's upper edge, so by the position clause it stands above this gated law-free scale. By the same rule's width clause, a half-width at or above about 0.010 leaves the element uncalibrated, and 0.023549 is well above that. For median_2 the band is -0.013938 plus or minus 0.010807 (-0.024745 to -0.003131), from cells -0.0175, -0.0011 and -0.0232. Protected task means: deco_hop 0.706851 against 0.707370 (-0.0005, inside its 0.02 margin), drd2_docking 0.988766 against 0.984572 (+0.0042, inside 0.03), zaleplon 0.428349 against 0.437595 (-0.0092, inside 0.02), and sitagliptin 0.590128 against 0.676784 (-0.0867, beyond its 0.02 margin); median_2 0.214892 against 0.228830.

The trigger-matched luck scale this Anchor lacked now exists, and it does not establish the stall restriction. By the registered position clause the Anchor's +0.0106 lies above the gated band, but only because the band is centred on this draw's own loss of -0.021. Its half-width, 0.0235, is more than twice the gain, which under the rule's width clause leaves the element uncalibrated rather than supported. So this is not the first supported reading of the stall restriction, and one dependent realization supports no significance statement either way.

The sharper finding is where the luck lives. The Anchor's entire +0.0106 over its mask-free Parent comes from two sitagliptin cells, seed 0 (+0.0716) and seed 1 (+0.1445); the other 13 cells net -0.0038. A perturbation that changes no rule and touches only the stalled rounds, about one round in five, moved those same two cells by -0.1025 and -0.1575, more than the gain they carry. On the one task that carries the Anchor's gain, the endpoint swings by 0.10 to 0.16 depending on which random words the breeding draws consume inside the stall regime. The molecular report shows how. The Anchor's seed-0 run left an N-aryl anisole branch for a polyfluorinated non-aromatic ring and climbed to 0.766, while this run stayed on the anisole branch and plateaued at 0.663 after three improvements. Whether the restriction contributes anything on this host therefore turns on two cells that regime-confined luck alone moves by more than the claimed gain. Attributing it is left to Curate, with a revised interpretation of the Anchor.

Confining the perturbation to stalled rounds did not shrink the average cost of leaving the Anchor's path. The gated loss (-0.0212) is almost the ungated one (-0.0205), though the cell spread fell (0.046 against 0.068) and the deco_hop seed-0 jackpot was preserved by construction. The loss simply moved from deco_hop to sitagliptin. The Anchor's panel holds several luck-sensitive high cells, and which of them a departure loses depends on where it departs. Arms on this Anchor that act inside stalled rounds now have their own gated scale, which must not be pooled with the ungated band or with the two mask-free gated references.

Method diagnosis, from this node's trajectories and the molecular report, in three parts. First, late search re-prices a few skeletons. Distinct scaffolds per run are 116.4 (Anchor 117.5) but only 52.0 in the second half and 36.5 in the last 100 evaluations. After evaluation 150, 19% of accepted proposals (13.5% overall; Anchor 17.2% and 12.3%) scored exactly a value already seen in the same run. The tied endpoints show what these are: halogen-placement and halogen-identity variants of one skeleton that the objective cannot tell apart, for example three distinct drd2 molecules at exactly 0.973518, all halogen variants of the Anchor's best. A batch acquisition rule that penalizes redundancy against already-scored molecules, or proposal operators that edit skeletons rather than substituent identity, would stop spending a fifth of late oracle calls on such relabellings. Second, the surrogate ranks worst exactly where the stall restriction leans on it. Among a round's ten picks, the rank correlation between predicted mean and realized score averages 0.56 in unrestricted rounds but 0.43 in restricted ones (Anchor 0.55 and 0.39). Part of that drop is simply the narrower spread of predicted means among top-forty picks, but restricted rounds also add far less best-score gain per round (0.0053 against 0.0149 here; 0.0062 against 0.0157 on the Anchor). A stall response that trusts the posterior mean more just when it is least informative is weak by construction. A response that changes where proposals come from, such as a trust-region shift or restart scheme, or a surrogate refitted locally around the current basin, would target the actual problem. Third, the endpoint is a lottery: one discarded draw in a fifth of the rounds moved two sitagliptin cells by 0.10 and 0.16, because each run commits to a single basin early. A search scheme that keeps several independent sub-populations alive would reduce that variance.

By the route's own conditions no second draw and no sweep of the discard count, trigger or bar follows, so this measurement route stops here. Still open is whether the stall restriction contributes on this host at all. A handoff named two measurements able to price it; this trigger-matched reference has now returned a band too wide to calibrate it, which leaves a mask-confined variant on the Anchor's own path, together with Curate's revised interpretation of the Anchor.

nodes.hypothesis: Change the unit of one proposal step from a single atom or bond to a whole corpus-frequent substructure: a motif-granularity operation that, with one declared probability, either attaches a drawn ring system or functional group to a scored parent at an explicitly resolved attachment point, or excises one complete ring system or side chain of that parent and installs a drawn one in its place, with the inherited seven atom- and bond-local operators and the connected-fragment crossover retained as the fallback for every attempt the motif path does not take or cannot complete.
nodes.finding:
Every structural forecast held, and the endpoint did not. The motif draw fired on 21,969 of 73,510 breeding attempts (0.2989 against the declared 0.30), split 0.4991/0.5009 between attaching a drawn unit and exchanging one of the host's own, and completed a molecule in 96.1 per cent of the attempts it fired on; the 848 failures were all exchange attempts and each one handed the attempt back to the inherited operators. The products were not destroyed at admission - the opposite: 98.8 per cent of them reached the candidate pool against 93.0 per cent for the inherited path, giving a motif-origin pool share of 0.2997 and at least one motif candidate in all 435 announced batches, against the Anchor's exact zero. Whole units really did arrive in one step: in all 343 accepted attach products the heavy-atom change equals the drawn unit's size exactly, 86 per cent of accepted motif products changed size by two or more atoms against the inherited mutation route's 2 per cent, 157 of them installed a complete new ring system (non-zero in all fifteen sessions, and in every case the system installed is the unit drawn) where the inherited mutation route installed none, and the generator produced trifluoromethyl groups (150 accepted molecules) and five-membered four-nitrogen rings (210) for the first time, against zero in all 4,500 of the Anchor's records. The pricing bought them at the pre-registered rate: 746 of 4,350 evaluations were motif-origin, a purchase ratio of 0.572 against the floor of 0.5, with a median accepted score of 0.2468 against the floor of 0.22, and only 97 of 435 batches bought none - not the round-42 declined-supply pattern. Every inherited law held: one configuration identical to the Anchor's apart from the added block, the stall restriction correct in 435 of 435 batches, the sulfur gate and identity admission on every pooled candidate, and the non-motif operator mix within sampling noise of the Anchor's. What did not happen is the gain. Whole-run realized incumbent-increment mass fell to 5.177434 over 235 improvements from the Anchor's 5.978073 over 253, a shortfall of 0.80 against a pre-registered threshold of exceeding it, so the registered falsifier's case (d) - bought and still no gain - applies. The motif route returned 0.117 of that mass from 0.172 of the evaluations; the panel mean came out 0.553654 against 0.607030, a paired delta of -0.053376 with every seed down (-0.0698, -0.0311, -0.0592). The panel figure sits just inside the lower edge of this Anchor's own luck band [-0.055482, +0.014579], so the panel mean alone cannot separate the arm from path luck; the task level can. Against the law-free re-draw on the same Anchor, zaleplon_mpo rose on all three seeds (task mean 0.4781 against 0.4314) and sitagliptin_mpo fell on all three by 0.12, 0.17 and 0.29 (task mean 0.4704 against 0.6620). Sitagliptin is where the operator was most expensive and least useful: it bought 88 of that task's 870 evaluations, none of which beat its generating parent or improved an incumbent, and the surrogate had priced them a median 5.2 standard deviations above what they scored. In the two cells named for tracing, the sitagliptin seed-2 cell that ended at 0.3695 reached its best molecule through a 22-step line of atom-level edits and crossovers with no motif product anywhere in its ancestry, while the median_2 seed-2 cell that ended at 0.2497 does carry four motif products in its ancestry, one of them a small-group exchange in the direct line at evaluation 45 - but every step after it is atom-level work on a fixed tricycle. Cost was never an issue: mining the vocabulary took 735 seconds of a 3,600-second allowance and produced 245 units rather than the planned 216, and the move itself cost 1.3 milliseconds per attempt.

The capability gap this lineage has been documenting for three rounds is now closed at the construction and admission layers and proven not to be the binding limit. A move whose unit is a whole ring system can be built, admitted, priced and bought inside this Anchor without breaking a single inherited law - and the search still got worse. That removes move granularity from the list of candidate explanations for this lineage's stalled endpoint gains, in the same way round 44 removed the selection rule and the breeding population, and it does so with the strongest possible version of the supply argument: 30 per cent of attempts, a 245-unit vocabulary containing the exact chemistry the generator could never build, and products admitted at a higher rate than the inherited path's own. The reason the supply did not convert is measurable and it is not about granularity, it is about pricing. The surrogate ranks coarse products systematically below the incumbent's one-atom neighbours (pool mean-rank percentile 0.56 against 0.36) and gives them no uncertainty premium at all (posterior-SD ratio 1.005), so the correlated Thompson draw has no route by which a large structural jump can win a pick on uncertainty. Size is what gets declined: units of nine or more heavy atoms were a third of the supply and a tenth of the purchases, a within-route purchase ratio of 0.32 against 1.33 for small units, which is exactly the shelf the molecular report describes - the bought unit is usually a small group hung on an unchanged skeleton, median five heavy atoms, with only 74 purchases in the whole run exchanging a whole ring system. Where the pricing did buy coarse products in quantity it was badly wrong about them on one objective: 86 per cent of sitagliptin's motif picks landed more than three standard deviations below their predicted mean, and those 88 wasted evaluations plus the declared dilution of crossover exposure from 0.45 to 0.32 of attempts are a sufficient account of that task's 0.19 loss against the law-free reference. A count-fingerprint Tanimoto kernel fitted on 10 to 290 accepted molecules cannot price a one-step multi-atom substitution, and no setting of the motif probability changes that. Two further things the campaign did not know. First, the added operator did move the degeneracy quantity that a richer breeding population failed to move: accepted scores exactly repeating an earlier accepted score fell from 565 to 365, and products scoring exactly their best parent from 205 to 111 - so coarse moves do break the exact-repeat channel, they just do not convert that into mass. Second, the operator is the lineage's first move that can delete a whole ring system, which is the contraction capability the admission-floor arm found missing, but its realized use is still net-growing (median exchange +2 heavy atoms) and the sibling arms' one-sided size diagnosis therefore stands. The method diagnosis from the trajectories is that proposal breadth is no longer the limit; ranking is, and so is the search regime. Mass in the first third of each session rose to 74 per cent from 62 per cent, each cell still converges on a single decorated series, and only 25 of 235 incumbent improvements came from the new route. What this result makes worth trying is a different ranking or surrogate model class - one whose features or kernel can price a fragment-level substitution, or a selection scheme that allocates part of each batch by proposal class rather than by a single posterior ordering - and, separately, a size-matched exchange that swaps a whole fused system for one of comparable size instead of hanging a small group on an intact skeleton. What it does not authorize is any sweep of this vocabulary, its threshold, the 0.30 share, the mode split or the attachment heuristic; the intent said so in advance and the evidence gives no reason to reopen it. One real gap remains in the audit: the registered nitro reading was unreachable because that unit has no free-hydrogen attachment atom under the declared site rule, so the claim that corpus-mined units are the only route to that group is untested here, and the oxidised-sulfur units are effectively unreachable too - the retained sulfur gate rejected 230 of the 236 motif products it refused, all from five such entries.

nodes.hypothesis: Reserved-evaluation allocation by archive distance inside the Anchor's unchanged posterior selector: in every announced batch of ten, each of the 160 pooled candidates is labelled with its maximum count-Morgan generalized-Tanimoto similarity to the session's accepted archive, read from the candidate-archive cross-covariance the selector already computes for its posterior mean; the pool is split at its own median of that statistic into a near half and a far half with ties to near; positions one to eight keep the inherited sequential correlated Thompson rule exactly, and positions nine and ten are taken by the same joint posterior draw with the availability mask restricted to unpicked members of the far half, so a fixed fifth of every batch is purchased where the archive-anchored posterior prices candidates worst.
nodes.finding:
The quota ran exactly as registered on all three seeds and all five objectives. Both of the last two evaluations in every one of the 435 announced batches were bought from the half of the pool farthest from the session's accepted archive: 870 of 870 reserved picks, none in the near half, no exhaustion fallback (the far half always held 78-80 of 160 members) and no numerical fallback. The restriction moved the pick at 610 of those 870 positions (70.1%), inside the 60-80% range predicted from the Anchor's own counterfactual, and the remaining 260 were picks the inherited rule would have made anyway. The far half's overall purchase share rose from the Anchor's 28.2% to 44.5%, higher in every one of the fifteen sessions, and the reserved picks paid exactly the predicted price: in-pool predicted-score percentile 0.58 against 0.81 for the free picks, uncertainty percentile 0.71 against 0.40, archive similarity 0.75 against 0.87. The inherited machinery is demonstrably untouched: all 3,480 free picks are still the unrestricted argmax of their own sampled row, the first announced batch of every session reproduces the Anchor's pool, fit, random draw and first eight picks bit for bit, and replaying all 435 of the Anchor's batches through this node's selector with the Anchor's own random numbers returns all 3,480 of its free picks identically. The mechanism's two payoff predictions both failed. The late-session price the far half must overcome did not shrink: the near-minus-far predicted-score gap in batches 21-29 was 0.1493 against the Anchor's 0.1443, above rather than below the predicted 0.10-0.14, with the far half's uncertainty still about 1.7 times the near half's; the only movement in the predicted direction was the free picks' own late far-half share, 23.0% against 18.6%. And the registered conversion test failed on both clauses. Total realized incumbent-increment mass fell to 5.3448 over 213 improvements, below the Anchor's 5.8194 over 255. The reserved stratum spent a fifth of the entire panel's evaluations and returned 8.2% of the realized gain: 0.000503 of incumbent increment per evaluation against the near half's 0.001243, a ratio of 0.40, well below the Anchor's far/near ratio of 0.85 and far worse than the -2.3% of mass the static-association null predicted. Reserved purchases also scored lower on average (0.318 against 0.425), beat their breeding parent less often (10.0% against 15.0%), survived the greedy-64 population less often (59.9% against 84.8%) and supplied only 11.3% of later breeding-parent draws for 20% of the purchases, so the spend also drained the population the free picks breed from. The endpoint panel moved -0.031639 against the Anchor on complete matched seeds (0.564814 against 0.596453; per seed -0.058007, -0.006352, -0.030558), inside the ungated reference band's lower half but below it on the four protected tasks as a group: deco_hop -0.0889, drd2_docking -0.0285, sitagliptin_mpo -0.0309 and zaleplon_mpo -0.0087 against margins of 0.02, 0.03, 0.02 and 0.02, so deco_hop, drd2_docking and sitagliptin_mpo are breached, while median_2 moved -0.0012 and stayed inside its band. The deco_hop loss carries the known one-cell departure penalty - the Anchor's seed-0 0.856148 endpoint, which no ungated child has reproduced; excluding that single cell descriptively leaves -0.0168, still a loss.

This closes the cheapest member of the round-42 lesson's prescribed class on the Anchor itself, with receipts, and the answer is the opposite of the lesson's expectation: the selector's preference for archive-like candidates is paying here, and the half it skips is skipped for a reason. The Anchor's own receipts had made the skipped half look nearly as productive per evaluation (0.85 of the near half's rate) and that number turns out to be a selection artefact, not a price. The far-half purchases the inherited rule chooses for itself are the ones whose sampled residual overcame the mean gap, and they do convert well here - the freely chosen far picks returned 0.00179 per evaluation, the best of any stratum. The ones the quota forces are the rest of that half, and they converted at 0.000503, two and a half times worse than the near half. Reserving evaluations by distance therefore does not buy the under-bought good candidates; it buys the ones the posterior was right about. That distinguishes 'the allocator under-buys valuable distant chemistry' from 'the allocator's distance-conditional ranking is informative', and the evidence now supports the second on this Parent. Read with the parallel arm on a different Parent at median similarity 0.61, this also separates the two explanations the round set out to separate: forcing distant purchases failed here inside the Anchor's own mildly-distant graph-edit chemistry (median similarity 0.87, reserved picks at 0.75), so the failure is not specific to an exotic prior's chemistry. What it does not close: the lesson's two other prescriptions, an explicitly novelty-adjusted acquisition and a surrogate whose uncertainty is comparable across chemotypes, are untouched, and this result makes the second more attractive rather than less - the near-minus-far mean gap still tripled within a session (0.051 to 0.149) while the far half's uncertainty stayed pinned at about 1.7x the near half's, so the surrogate still cannot express 'I do not know' strongly enough to let a distant candidate win on merit, and this experiment shows that overriding its ranking by fiat is not the way to fix that. A further allocation-quota arm on this Anchor is not justified: r=2 was the smallest reservation that moves the share, and a failure at this strength authorizes no sweep of r, of the split, or of a similarity threshold. The method diagnosis from the trajectories points the same way and adds a second, independent limitation. The surrogate's within-batch ranking of its own purchases is actually mildly informative and unchanged by this intervention (rank correlation between predicted and realized score about 0.52 on free picks in both this node and the Anchor), so the ranking model is not the proximate bottleneck; realized gain is concentrated almost entirely in the first ten batches (4.78 of this node's 5.34 mass, 0.11 in batches 21-29) and the search then stops producing distinct outcomes. The molecular report shows why: every seed locks onto one analogue series within the first 60-150 evaluations and then enumerates substituent swaps the objectives cannot distinguish - 530 proposals repeat a score an earlier proposal in the same run already had, six analogues differing only in which halogen sits on an amide nitrogen all score identically, and on one objective this node's series never rebuilt the compact fused bicyclic core the Anchor's lucky seed-0 run carried (10 proposals against the Anchor's 129), stacking 40-heavy-atom polycyclics to a 0.62 plateau instead. The proposal operator set, not the allocator, is what the budget is being spent inside: there is no move that changes ring topology or scaffold identity, so no allocation rule over that pool can supply chemistry the generator never proposes. A scaffold-level proposal operator (ring expansion or contraction, heteroatom walk, replacement of one ring system by another) triggered when successive edits stop producing distinct scores, or a chemotype-calibrated surrogate that can rank across scaffolds rather than within one, are the kinds of method that could remove this limitation; a different quota over the same pool cannot. Two further observations the quota made visible and cheap to fix: the forced far-half spend bought 75 fragment-sized molecules of twelve or fewer heavy atoms that sit at the objective floor by construction (against 0 in the near half), and removing them does not rescue the stratum's conversion, so a minimum-heavy-atom admission rule would recover part of a reserved budget if any future arm spends one. The attribution that remains open is the split between the direct cost of displacing 610 purchases and the indirect cost of the weaker population the reserved picks left behind (11.3% of later breeding-parent draws for 20% of purchases): unselected candidates carry no scores, so the within-run reserved-versus-free contrast is an association inside one realization and identifies no mediator, and the panel loss cannot be decomposed into those two channels from this node alone.

nodes.hypothesis: When forming a crossover's first-parent fragment, sample only pendant single-bond cuts and retain the side containing every source ring atom and its connecting linkers.
nodes.finding:
Across 34,564 informative first-parent fragment calls, the inherited rule would retain the complete source ring/linker core with mean probability 55.968%; the applied pendant-cut rule made that probability one. All 33,626 sanitized protected crossovers preserved the original core atoms and bonds before canonicalization. Protected crossovers reached 28,875 novel pool descendants and 1,714 actual evaluated descendants; 1,587 of those emissions followed an immediate crossover that changed the first parent’s identity. Of 600 evaluated crossover descendants with a later mutation, 224 no longer contained the original typed ring/linker core. One additional unselected immediate-only pool product changed aromatic representation during the inherited canonicalization step. Mean emitted size rose from 33.39 to 40.90 heavy atoms, and 938 attempted products exceeded the unchanged 120-atom limit. The protected crossover cohort had 210/1,714 strict best-parent beats and mean child-minus-best-parent score -0.112347, compared with 172/1,679 and -0.156871 in the Parent’s crossover cohort. All fifteen Child task/seed runs completed. Mean final score fell from 0.544374 to 0.529067, a paired change of -0.015307; all three paired seeds declined (-0.014873, -0.022309, -0.008738). The mean DRD2 change was -0.090254, despite gains on three other tasks.

Physical inheritance of the first parent’s complete ring system worked and reached evaluation, but the full-core restriction did not improve the complete method. The crossover cohort produced more parent-beating descendants while the complete search ended at lower scores, so that local diagnostic is insufficient to establish improved optimization. It rules out failed cutting or lack of exposure to the selector as the explanation for the negative utility result. Keeping every ring can also keep a large or unproductive framework, while the donor adds more structure and useful peripheral functional relationships can still be removed. Optional mutation can then undo the protected structure. The supplied chemistry is consistent with this limit: conventional arylamide and sulfinamide leaders coexist with duplicated frameworks, dense bridges, reactive substituents and unspecified stereochemistry. The next useful distinction is which core and attachment relationships deserve preservation, and when replacement or simplification is beneficial; this result does not establish that all rings should always survive. The observed crossover subgroups differ in parents and later edits, and the changed random-call schedule alters subsequent search history. Neither the subgroup score difference nor molecular size identifies an individual protected cut’s causal value, and unused candidates have no oracle counterfactual labels.

nodes.hypothesis: Neutral path-divergence control at the held stall regime. Track the session's own consecutive non-improving announced-batch counter exactly as the K=3 siblings do: after the ten initial records, a batch is improving when the session best-so-far after it exceeds the value held when it was announced. Enter the held regime when a batch is announced with the counter at three or more. Keep it active for that batch and every following announced batch until two consecutive announced batches have each been improving. Then leave it, resetting both the non-improving counter and the in-regime improving counter to zero. In each announced batch allocated while the held regime is active, draw one standard-normal array of the inherited allocation shape (announced batch size by pool size, float64) from the posterior selector's own seeded generator. Discard it immediately before the inherited correlated Thompson draw, so that batch and every later allocation consume the next unused blocks of the same i.i.d. stream. No law, probability, scale, threshold, pool size, operator, mask, tie rule or admission rule changes. Only the realized allocator path departs: from the Anchor at the same batch as the K=3 reference, and from the K=3 reference at the first held-only batch (held regime active while the counter is below three). Because no law changes, every discard after the first only changes which i.i.d. block a later allocation consumes, not the distribution of the continuation. The arm therefore supplies a second draw of the law-free continuation from the identical first-trigger state, partly shared with the first.
nodes.finding:
The control behaved exactly as registered, so its score is a valid second reference. Thirteen of fifteen sessions entered the held stall period, the same thirteen as the Anchor and the first control. The deco_hop sessions on seeds 0 and 2 never stalled and reproduced the Anchor record for record, including its 0.856 seed-0 endpoint. Over all 435 announced batches the logged stall state matched a recomputation from the run's own scores. The extra random block was drawn and thrown away in exactly the 184 held batches (21 held periods) and in no other batch. Every held period that ended did so after exactly two improving batches in a row; ten ran to the end of the session. 55 of the 184 held batches raised the session best.

Each session matched the Anchor molecule for molecule up to its first held batch. It matched the first control, whose stall period ended at the first improving batch, up to the first batch the longer period added. At both points the candidate pool and its predicted means and uncertainties were identical. The thrown-away block was bit-for-bit the block the other run had used, and replaying the rule on it reproduced that run's ten picks. The two controls shared 340 of 2,340 post-trigger evaluations, as predicted, and then went separate ways. 93 of the 184 held batches (51%) were batches the first control never touched, and every exposed session had some. Every held batch picked differently from its same-state replay, on average 6.2 of 10 molecules. Only 3.0% of molecules scored after divergence also appear in the Anchor's session, and 6.1% in the first control's. The selection rule itself did not move: the shift in where picks fell on the predicted-score and uncertainty rankings gave test statistics of -1.39 and +1.35, far inside the 3.26 bound. Every pool held 160 candidates and no batch fell back to the backup route.

On the score panel the matched mean went from 0.596453 to 0.604200, a reference delta of +0.007747. Seed macros moved by -0.0055, +0.0260 and +0.0027. Seven cells rose, five fell and three were exactly unchanged. One cell carries almost all of it: sitagliptin seed 1 rose from 0.500 to 0.620 (+0.120), and without it the reference is -0.0003. The other large swings were zaleplon seed 0 -0.045, median_2 seed 0 +0.029, zaleplon seed 2 +0.024, sitagliptin seed 0 -0.015 and median_2 seed 2 -0.011. The SD of the fifteen cell deltas was 0.034, more than twice the first control's 0.015. Measured directly against the first control, this run is +0.0095 higher, with cells from -0.041 to +0.138.

For the Research Brief: the median_2 three-seed mean went from 0.222732 to 0.227889 (+0.0052), with cells +0.029, -0.003 and -0.011. On the protected tasks, deco_hop moved +0.0013, drd2_docking +0.0013, sitagliptin_mpo +0.0351 and zaleplon_mpo -0.0041. None fell below its margin (0.02, 0.03, 0.02, 0.02).

The two luck-only controls are two draws of the same continuation from the same starting state, and they landed 0.0095 apart, at -0.0017 and +0.0077. Their crude two-draw width, 0.0067, is about 78% of the 0.0086 spread among the seven stall-time rule changes tested so far. That is still under the threshold, fixed before the run, at which the spread would be declared indistinguishable from luck, but not by much. Because the two draws share their first stretch and the entire breeding random stream, the width is an underestimate.

Under the interpretation rule fixed before the run, a stall-time change now needs a panel delta above +0.0172 to stand above both controls, or below -0.0112 to stand below both. None of the seven earlier changes clears the upper bar. The top-40 stall shortlist (+0.0106) drops from 'above the single reference' to partial calibration. The longer mutation walks (+0.0076) and the fourfold stall pool (+0.0047) stood above the first control alone, but now sit inside the two-point luck band. They are unidentified, not refuted. Only stall-time crossover removal (-0.0142) stands below both. The held-regime versions of the shortlist and the fourfold pool, run in this same round, should be read against these thresholds.

For the median_2 objective, a gain must now exceed +0.0124 in the three-seed mean to stand above both controls. That is stricter than the campaign's own +0.010 median_2 criterion, because luck alone just moved median_2 seed 0 by +0.029 and the mean by +0.005. The chemistry explains why. On that objective the best molecules all sit on one propylquinoline/bis-lactam framework, within about 0.01 of each other, and late progress consists of single-atom changes to it. So which variant a re-drawn path happens to reach can move a cell by a few hundredths. Sitagliptin is worse: its scoring surface is bimodal, and one re-draw moved one cell by 0.12. Single-cell gains of that size on these objectives cannot be read as mechanism. A real median_2 improvement has to clear that band, and showing it on all three seeds rather than in one cell is the more convincing sign.

Pure luck cost the protected tasks nothing beyond margin. Zaleplon seed 0 fell again (-0.045), so all nine stall-gated Children of this Anchor measured so far, both controls included, give up that cell. That confirms it as a favourable Anchor realization rather than something a change destroys.

Still open: two dependent draws only bracket the width of path noise; they do not measure it. A breeding-stream control or more protocol seeds is the way to an actual estimate. This reference recipe is complete under its review conditions, and a third discarded-draw arm would add another dependent draw rather than new information.

nodes.hypothesis: Select each successful batch by stable descending posterior mean on the existing fresh pool, removing sampled uncertainty from the identity-allocation rule while retaining the learned count-based posterior.
nodes.finding:
All 4,350 successful choices followed the stable highest-mean order, with zero violations. On the same 435 Child pools, the inherited sampled rule would have selected a different set in every batch. Mean-only selection raised average predicted quality from 0.357917 to 0.390251 and reduced original prediction SD from 0.038134 to 0.020556. Mean absolute within-batch posterior correlation rose from 0.054704 to 0.064071, count-fingerprint similarity rose from 0.5810 to 0.8211, and distinct nonempty chemical cores fell from 6.503 to 4.437 per ten molecules. These are comparisons on identical pools and model distributions.

The completed search scored worse. Three-seed final macro mean fell from 0.574344 to 0.533937, a paired change of -0.040407 against the required +0.002. All three macro replicas declined. Task mean changes were -0.104061 for sitagliptin_mpo, -0.043769 for drd2_docking, -0.036782 for zaleplon_mpo, -0.018368 for deco_hop, and +0.000944 for median_2. This occurred despite strict parent-beating offspring increasing from 624 to 707 out of 4,350 and batches improving the incumbent increasing from 182 to 197. Mean accepted batch-best fell from 0.487313 to 0.437676. Selected-stream prediction MSE fell from 0.011269 to 0.004397, while within-batch rank correlation fell from 0.550 to 0.316. Nominal 95% latent intervals covered only 77.24% of Child scores, versus 76.92% for the Parent. All batches were complete and accepted, with no numerical fallback.

This removal experiment supplies negative utility evidence for treating the sampled excursions as wasted evaluations. The learned mean remains informative against its own archive-mean baseline, but concentrating on its highest predictions produced more local improvements along a search that ended lower. Parent-beating yield and lower selected-stream prediction error therefore remain poor substitutes for final search quality. The model itself was frozen: lower SD exposure and lower error describe the selected molecules and their subsequent feedback, not improved uncertainty calibration.

Lost breadth is a plausible explanation to investigate. The chemistry assessment found fewer distinct cores in 14 of 15 paired streams, consistent with the matched-pool coverage loss. It also found persistent unusual bonds, burdensome decorations and unspecified stereochemistry, so more selective allocation did not establish better chemical feasibility. The result narrows the next question to which exploratory choices or independent molecular families help preserve useful search paths. It does not identify a particular discarded molecule as the missing winner: alternate choices have no counterfactual oracle outcomes, and the downstream histories differ. Transfer beyond this Parent and supplied panel remains open.

nodes.hypothesis: Remove the mandatory unscored rollout suffix on code Parent n-5cc901d1a9e3 by the one frozen parameter_adjustment rollout_successful_transitions_after_expansion: 2 -> 0. _normal_route still performs ordinary _expand; _rollout returns that same occurrence; the existing _terminal_on_route and canonical/pending/fallback laws decide whether it can be emitted. The actual oracle scores that existing valid frontier rather than a fabricated intermediate value. Directly scored occurrence-local frontier credit can then affect actual later-announcement choices and receive accepted descendant returns. Keep count-weighted best-return exploitation at both root and deeper levels, all-return and maximum backup, N+O widening and every graph-operator law fixed. Loss of rollout-only finishing calls follows solely from the zero horizon. The frozen contribution question is whether the two-transition suffix helps or harms useful first-frontier feedback under this best-return tree; no separate operator or selector contribution is inferred.
nodes.finding:
All 15 Search sessions completed. Every eligible first frontier was scored: 4,350 versus 21 in the Parent, with no rollout transition or unexplained bypass. New nonroot occurrences per paid evaluation fell from 3.0002 to 1.0317. Of those scored frontiers, 1,359 later received descendant feedback, versus nine in the Parent; 3,191 purchased descendants had an earlier-scored frontier ancestor and an actual later decision on that route. The 571 descendants with same-batch frontier support were counted separately. Full incumbent gain per evaluation rose 18.0%, from 0.00040791 to 0.00048141; late gain rose 2.36%, from 0.00049374 to 0.00050541. Mean final Top1 increased from 0.326785 to 0.348101, a paired gain of 0.021316 that passes the registered 0.002 target. The three seed changes were -0.071791, +0.119137 and +0.016603. The formal Anchor still scored 0.607030, leaving a gap of 0.258929. Thus the registered activation and useful-conversion prediction passed on this complete panel, while the separate Anchor performance goal did not.

The result rules out lack of direct frontier exposure as an unavoidable property of this tree controller: real frontier scores were available to later decisions, and the removal improved both endpoint mean and the registered gain rates. It supports a conditional negative contribution of the mandatory suffix on this panel. It does not show that the frontier feedback itself caused the improvement: the same removal also eliminates rollout-only finishing opportunities and changes subsequent random draws. Gain mass restates endpoint progress rather than independently corroborating it.

Useful search remains concentrated. By stop, 2,991 of 4,350 scored frontiers had no later decision use, and 2,822 of 4,488 nonroot occurrences had only one return. Fragment-excluded within-batch similarity rose from 0.250 to 0.333 while the sum of session-unique typed scaffolds fell from 2,722 to 1,946. The molecular assessment describes narrower size extremes but repeated inherited aromatic and heteroatom frameworks, with reactive linkages still present among high scorers. A strong polyaryl/amine family in one docking seed accounts for 57.9% of positive task-seed endpoint differences, whereas another docking seed loses 0.379209; the late-rate advantage is correspondingly fragile as a descriptive panel result. A graph proposal scheme that rearranges ring topology and linkers while retaining useful functional-group relationships could address this structural concentration; another rollout-horizon value does not supply that capability. Whether such a generator improves search, whether the suffix effect repeats, and how much of the gain is mediated by frontier feedback remain open. The literature-derived separation of termination from selection operated as registered, but its game heuristics and performance claims were not transferred, and this experiment does not settle the wider tree-search approach.

nodes.hypothesis: Introduce exactly one session-wide prequential direct-provenance decision-location offset. Let D_t contain all unique earlier accepted optimizer products in the current Objective Session whose recorded path.cross_origin.direct_noncopy_terminal is true and whose original uncorrected emission-time GP mean m_i is finite. Before announcing batch t, set b_t = sum_{i in D_t}(y_i-m_i)/|D_t|, or exactly 0 when D_t is empty. Freeze b_t for the entire batch. For every direct-class candidate j, use corrected mean m_j+b_t and active sampled score s_kj+b_t; non-direct candidates retain m_j and s_kj exactly. The coefficient is one, with no floor, clipping, decay, window choice, warmup threshold or coefficient fitting. The estimator uses base residuals only, pools qualifying accepted receipts from both regions and survives regional retirement, but resets at the next Objective Session. Local GP conditioning membership, covariance, amplitude, normal draws, graph construction and controller are unchanged. This is a source-conditioned decision-location heuristic, not a coherent new GP posterior, population-bias estimator, uncertainty correction or multivalid algorithm.
nodes.finding:
All fifteen sessions completed. Nonzero offsets reached 8,638 direct recombinant candidate occurrences and changed the purchased set in 56 of 435 batches, replacing 99 paid identities. On the 144 direct products actually purchased, mean squared prediction error fell from 0.0246044 to 0.0230033; all 40 cold-start products stayed in that comparison. The improvement was heterogeneous: six task/seed cells improved, five worsened and four stayed unchanged. The local-model and sampling laws stayed intact, and independent reconstruction matched all 870 Child fit and draw blocks. Full incumbent improvement mass rose from 5.22074 to 5.35395, and late mass rose from 0.63777 to 0.84245, each measured over the complete paid denominator. Mean final score rose from 0.556542 to 0.565422, a paired gain of 0.008880; two seed macros fell slightly and the third rose by 0.033875. The formal Anchor remained higher at 0.607030, so its +0.002 performance target was not reached. There was no technical failure.

The registered intervention settles a limited but useful question: earlier errors from an existing provenance class can change real decisions and reduce prospective error on the resulting paid stream without changing the local Gaussian processes. This is a substantive new error consumer, not another donor expansion or numerical retune, and it adopts none of the deferred literature algorithms. It leaves the Parent donor-support result intact. The complete matched panel supports a positive mean total effect of this particular consumer on its code Parent, but does not identify error reduction as the cause of the score gain or establish transferable calibration. Direct purchases fell from 261 to 144, and their own incumbent-improvement mass fell from 0.17186 to 0.14211 even as total progress rose; most realized gain therefore came through the rest of the evolving search, not more useful direct products. Late corrected direct-product MSE remained 0.07619 versus 0.01765 for nondirect purchases, so a single provenance offset did not resolve the conditional prediction problem. A candidate-dependent ranking or predictive model is the relevant kind of method for that remaining distinction; this result supplies no justification for tuning the scalar estimator.

The trajectories also show that better local prediction did not fix molecular routing. Fragment-excluded within-batch similarity increased from 0.7250 to 0.7418, reaching 0.7627 late, while the count above fifty heavy atoms rose from 153 to 448. The Molecular assessment found broad overall scaffold diversity but only 7-26 generic scaffolds in each task upper-score cohort, plus repeated enlargement, unusual heteroatom bonds and absent stereochemical assignments. This supports a limitation in finding coherent alternative whole frameworks, rather than a lack of graph novelty. Scaffold-preserving reconnection proposals and chemically credible attachment choices are the kind of capability that could address it; their benefit is untested here. The remaining Anchor gap, variable cell effects, missing trusted safety verdict and unmeasured alternative histories keep broader performance and mediation questions open. This node does not decide the fate of the regional approach.

nodes.hypothesis: Extend the inherited two-parent crossover with an equally weighted two-cut ring-segment mode only when both actual scored parents have eligible isolated nonaromatic-ring descriptors, joining one complete retained component from each parent by two single bonds while preserving the ordinary single-cut route and its no-support random law.
nodes.finding:
Ring mode was selected on 5,498 of 10,982 jointly eligible opportunities. All 5,496 products constructed below the atom limit conserved the selected source components and made the intended two attachments; two selected choices exceeded the inherited atom limit before construction. There were 4,957 immediate products distinct from both parents and 539 parent copies. The route delivered 179 evaluated descendants of nonidentical constructions: 124 pure crossovers and 55 with finishing mutation. Another 11 evaluations gained novelty only by mutating a parent copy. All 174 nonidentical descendants with a later opportunity entered the next model fit, 96 later bred, 35 beat their best generating parent and 15 improved the incumbent. Exposure was uneven: none of the six zaleplon and decoration-hop runs evaluated a ring-mode descendant.

All fifteen Child task runs completed. Mean final Top-1 score fell from 0.595670 to 0.550623, a paired change of -0.045046 against the required +0.002. Seed macro changes were -0.014404, -0.020055 and -0.100680; ten task-seed endpoints declined, two improved and three were unchanged. Seed population SD increased from 0.026593 to 0.045826. The largest losses were docking seed 2 (-0.309828) and sitagliptin seeds 0 and 2 (-0.113615 and -0.189390). Across the entire search, local parent beats nevertheless rose from 629 to 652 and incumbent increases from 258 to 266.

Failed construction and a globally blocked evaluation route do not explain this result: the new two-attachment products were built correctly, evaluated and reused. The complete exposed loss therefore supports a negative total contribution from this particular extension under the tested search composition, while leaving the separate evidence for ordinary crossover intact. Greater local win frequency is misleading here because the generating-parent references also became weaker. One positive endpoint even occurred in a run that never selected ring mode; its eligible mode draw changed the subsequent random stream, so that gain cannot be assigned to a new ring product.

The chemistry narrows the remaining limitation. The search now reaches medium and large nitrogen/carbonyl rings, including 72 accepted proposals with rings of at least twelve atoms, yet access to those graphs does not establish useful arrangements or feasible geometry. Finishing mutation also matters: the new typed ring pattern survives in all 124 pure evaluated recombinants but only 43 of the 55 finished ones. Aromatic, amine and carbonyl families remain well represented, alongside reactive bonds, difficult sulfur and small-ring structures, and unspecified stereochemistry. More scaffold identities and fewer molecules in a limited bond-alert screen coexist with lower scores. The unresolved question is which altered ancestors, pool competition and accepted feedback paths produced the endpoint loss; the observed cohorts do not supply scores for unselected alternatives or isolate an individual ring segment’s causal value. This complete failure closes the registered test without a ring-size, mode-weight or donor-preference sweep.

nodes.hypothesis: Modify optional ordinary second/third mutation continuation at saturation floor one by drawing exactly two fresh arms from the same current intermediate and continuing with the valid arm of greatest raw-score posterior mean from the existing suggestion-entry accepted-label count GP, with first-arm exact ties and bounded inherited fallbacks, while retaining the full final-product pool and correlated final selector.
nodes.finding:
The continuation rule executed 8,640 two-arm decisions. Independently reconstructed predictions confirm 4,266 strict choices of a different second-arm identity; 44 exact ties chose the first arm. Those changed paths delivered 237 distinct evaluated finals. All 230 with another suggestion remaining entered the next model fit, and 120 later served as breeding parents. The audit also retains 110 nonterminal finals with no later use and seven terminal births; one task/seed had six affected accepted finals and no later breeding. Final proposal capacity stayed at 160 products per suggestion. Nevertheless, mean final Top-1 fell from 0.595670 to 0.547587, a paired change of -0.048083 against the required +0.002. All three seed macros and all five task means decreased; four of the 15 individual task/seed cells improved. Macro population SD declined from 0.026593 to 0.017941, but the gain criterion failed.

This result rules out lack of execution, absent evaluated delivery, lost feedback, zero cohort-level recursion and reduced final-pool capacity as explanations for the failure of this fixed rule. The model successfully imposed its preferences without producing better search. Across all accepted offspring, mean raw score fell from 0.385256 to 0.326704 while mean best-generating-parent score fell from 0.470456 to 0.395280. Parent-beating counts rose from 629 to 690 and incumbent-update counts from 258 to 261, yet total incumbent increments fell from 5.807663 to 5.086425. More local wins therefore coexist with weaker sources and less endpoint progress. Selected-stream prediction MSE fell from 0.012718 to 0.007832, but the labels being predicted changed and recorded 1.96-standard-deviation coverage fell from 76.28% to 74.60%; this does not establish better transferable calibration. Chemistry inspection likewise finds both recognizable aromatic amides and amines and persistent questionable bond environments, ring geometries and unresolved stereochemistry. The largest deficits include failure to reproduce a compact high-scoring heterocyclic combination, but neither missing rings/amines nor a specific chemical mediator is established. Most unchosen arms remain unscored, and no alternate continuation future was executed. The evidence supports a negative total contribution of this exact fixed guidance rule under these conditions; it leaves the separate roles of local prediction preferences, extra random draws and later adaptive history unresolved, and does not reverse the value of ordinary continuation itself.
