nodes.hypothesis: Replace successful independent-row posterior allocation with greedy incumbent-referenced expected batch improvement over one fixed 128-or-announced-batch-size shared joint posterior panel, using only the best previously accepted raw score and exact smallest-index ties.
nodes.finding:
The allocation mechanism executed and changed real decisions. All 435 frozen incumbents, 128-row posterior panels and 4,350 exact greedy choices passed independent reconstruction. There were 3,681 positive-gain choices and 669 exact-zero choices; 23 complete batches had zero sampled improvement from their first position. Every zero choice followed the registered smallest-index tie rule without a fallback. All 435 selected sets differed from the Parent rule on the same panels. Mean sampled batch-improvement utility rose by 0.005726: 371 batches improved, 64 tied and none declined. Against the unthresholded shared-panel rule, 343 sets changed and mean utility rose by 0.000256, with fifteen contrary losses.

Real progress moved the other way. Average realized batch improvement fell from 0.013351 to 0.011410. Advancing batches rose from 202 to 204 and sequential incumbent updates from 258 to 270, but mean positive batch gain fell from 0.028751 to 0.024331. Mean accepted offspring score also fell, from 0.385256 to 0.351177. All evaluations completed, yet final mean score fell from 0.595670 to 0.539394, a paired change of -0.056276 against the required +0.002. Seed changes were -0.092867, -0.016706 and -0.059254. Nine task-seed endpoints declined and six improved, including all three median-similarity endpoints.

The experiment exposes a failure of the complete incumbent-referenced allocation rule under this Parent: correct positive-improvement targeting and higher sampled utility did not deliver larger real advances. More update events again accompanied smaller increments. The mean realized batch-improvement contrast telescopes to the final-score contrast on these equal-length streams, so those two failures should not be counted as independent endpoint evidence. The result supports a negative contribution from this whole rule under the tested composition. A threshold-only endpoint effect remains unresolved because the current unthresholded comparison has no separately evaluated future trajectory.

Finite-panel zero gain also failed to identify unproductive molecules. Fourteen zero-gain choices beat their frozen real incumbent, eleven made sequential incumbent updates, 205 were later bred and 119 survived to the final populations. Two became session leaders. Every one of those fourteen real wins had no sampled scenario above the incumbent. The chemical report includes a ring-free urea/enamide/thiocarbonyl leader and a distinct aza-dicarbonyl leader in this group. These are concrete limits of the sampled improvement support; they do not establish whether model error, finite tail sampling, myopic selection or later breeding caused the overall loss.

Selected-stream MSE and interval coverage improved while within-batch ordering weakened, but the selected molecules and histories changed. Those diagnostics do not establish repaired uncertainty or improved chemistry. Familiar amines and lactams still coexist with reactive bonds, difficult rings, large assemblies and unspecified stereochemistry. The older unthresholded and antithetic failures retain their exchange-containing Parent conditions, and shared-Parent siblings supply no isolated threshold, additive or joint-component effect. The complete exposed endpoint failure supplies the registered approach-review evidence without authorizing acquisition tuning.

nodes.hypothesis: Insert one bounded, oracle-free refinement stage between admission and pooling, for prior-origin slots only. When a decoded prior continuation has passed the inherited admission path (checked_molecule, pool_identity_admission, the emitted/initial and temporary-pool duplicate scopes, and the sulfur introduction audit against its single conditioning parent), exactly k=4 single-call variants of that admitted molecule are generated with the inherited GraphOperators.mutate at its unchanged operator names and probabilities and its unchanged internal retry behaviour, and each variant is passed through exactly the same inherited admission path against the same conditioning parent. The admitted continuation and its admissible variants - at most five molecules - are then scored in one query of the posterior already fitted for this announced batch, through the selector's existing features/distribution interface, and the member with the greatest posterior mean fills the slot; a tie or no improvement keeps the raw continuation, so the occupant is never worse-predicted than the decoded product. No oracle call, no additional posterior fit, no new covariance factorization, no new asset and no new dependency is added, the selector's own random generator is never consumed, and the refinement draws its operator randomness from a dedicated stream seeded from the session seed so the inherited generator's stream is not spent on it. Everything else is the inherited node: the frozen corpus prior and its per-seed checkpoint, prefix rule, temperature and twelve attempts per slot; the slot rule index mod 4 == 3 with the inherited graph fallback, so the realized prior-origin share stays at its registered quarter; the three-quarter graph-edit path with its crossover, floor-one continuation law and rejection-conditioned escalation; the pool target of 160; the accepted-only count-Morgan Gaussian process with its kernel, normalization, noise, jitter ladder and finite guards; and the correlated Thompson allocation with its availability masks and tie rules. One k=4 and one screening statistic are bound; no sweep of k, of the operator mixture or of the statistic follows this arm.
nodes.finding:
The stage executed exactly as pre-registered and the audit is complete. All 17,358 admitted prior-origin pool slots across the fifteen sessions were refined (the Parent refined none of its 17,302), four variants requested every time, 68,288 of 69,432 variants admitted with every rejection carrying an inherited reason, one single slot left unrefined because all four of its variants hit the sulfur gate, and zero refinement events on graph-edit slots. It cost nothing it was not allowed to cost: no oracle call, no extra model fit, no extra covariance factorization, 435 posterior fits and 870 factorizations exactly as in the Parent, 300 oracle calls and 290 accepted proposals with zero invalid and zero duplicate proposals in every cell, full 160-member pools in all 435 batches, and the prior itself byte-identical (same three per-seed parameter hashes, frozen, no gradient update, no oracle label). Wall time rose to 1.05-2.90 times the Parent's per cell, at most 296 seconds against a two-hour task limit.

The variant chosen by the posterior replaced the raw continuation in 12,181 of 17,358 slots (70.2%, inside the registered 55-95% range), always with a non-negative posterior gain, but the gain was small: median +0.0030 in score units against a pre-registered floor of +0.005, with an upper quartile of +0.0149. The refined products kept their distance, which was the mechanism's stated risk: occupants sit at median count-Morgan Tanimoto 0.6129 to their conditioning parent (Parent 0.6092; the graph-edit arm of the same sessions 0.8306), 71.3% still change three or more heavy atoms (Parent 70.3%; graph arm 30.6%), 96.4% still change the Murcko core, and the median per-slot distance change from raw to occupant is zero. Nothing collapsed into ordinary graph editing.

What the refinement bought downstream is much smaller than registered. The surrogate's pricing of the group barely moved: the prior group's median predicted score reached the graph group's in 7 of 435 batches against a pre-registered 25%, its maximum reached the graph maximum in 2 of 435 against 20%, the median in-pool predicted-score percentile of the picks it did make rose from 0.415 to 0.465 against a target of 0.50, and the uncertainty percentile stayed at 0.780 to four decimals. Purchases rose from 5.31% to 7.75% of the 4,350 evaluations, short of the registered 8% floor; 253 of 435 batches still bought no prior-origin candidate (target below 50%), though every one of the fifteen sessions now buys at least one, where the Parent had a session that bought none at all. Landing split in two directions. The quantity the question was built on moved the wrong way: the accepted median score of prior-origin products fell from 0.1853 to 0.1757, against a target of at least 0.22 and the same sessions' graph arm at 0.3112, with mean child-minus-best-parent worsening from -0.0682 to -0.0932 and the survivor rate easing from 0.675 to 0.653. Realized conversion nevertheless improved: the parent-beating rate rose from 0.108 to 0.151, prior-origin incumbent improvements from 13 to 20, sessions with at least one from 7 to 10 of 15, and the prior path's share of realized incumbent-increment mass from 2.8% to 9.1%. Because both quantities did not stay at or below the Parent's, neither registered falsifier branch fired, and neither did the distance-collapse branch or the timeout branch.

The panel rose. Paired on matched seeds against the round-42 corpus-prior arm the fifteen-cell mean is +0.0456 (seeds -0.0010 / +0.0592 / +0.0787), with ten cells up, four down and one tied, and all five task means above both the Parent and the round-43 no-prior breadth control. Against the formal Anchor the panel is -0.0063, inside the law-free ungated reference band, where the Parent sat at -0.0519; median_2 is +0.0310 above the Anchor, clear of its reference band; and of the Parent's three breached must-preserve margins only sitagliptin_mpo remains breached, at -0.0636. The deco_hop margin is held at -0.0053, the first time an ungated law-changing child of this Anchor has not paid the familiar -0.085 to -0.116 departure cost on that task - and it is held for a single reason, the seed-2 cell at 0.8713.

That cell is traceable to one event. At batch 18 of deco_hop seed 2 a prior continuation entered pool slot 111, four variants were generated, and the posterior preferred one that appended a fluorine onto a ring nitrogen already carrying a chlorine, worth +0.0035 of posterior mean. The allocator then bought that slot at the 0.396 in-pool predicted-score percentile with the 0.874 uncertainty percentile - a below-median-priced, high-uncertainty exploration draw, not a candidate the refinement had made attractive - and it scored 0.853304, beating the incumbent by +0.2552. Every one of the 103 molecules the session subsequently scored at or above 0.80 is a descendant of it, and the 0.871279 endpoint is its best descendant. Recomputed in the same pool, the unrefined continuation would have sat at percentile 0.333 instead of 0.396: the refinement moved that slot eleven ranks out of 160 and left it below the pool median. That cell alone is 37.7% of the fifteen-cell gain; with sitagliptin_mpo seed 1 and drd2_docking seed 1 it is 79%, and the other twelve cells average +0.0119.

The round-42 question is now answered in its two halves, and they separate cleanly. A bounded, oracle-free local refinement can be made to run at full coverage on this Parent at negligible cost and without surrendering the distance that made the prior interesting - that was the real risk and it did not happen, so "polishing destroys the distance" is ruled out for this operator family at k=4. But the refinement does not move prior-origin chemistry onto the incumbent scoring ridge: the accepted median score of its products went down, not up, and the surrogate still prices the group near the 0.46 percentile with unchanged uncertainty. The off-ridge explanation of the round-42 failure survives as an explanation and is not removed by this remedy, and pricing is not what admits these candidates: the one cell that carries the gain was bought on uncertainty, at a below-median predicted percentile, which is the allocator exploring and not the screen persuading.

The reason the screen cannot do more is measurable and it is a property of the statistic, not of k. Across the 201 selected variant-occupied picks, the larger the posterior-mean gain the refinement claimed, the further realized score fell below prediction (correlation -0.39), and the variant-occupied picks' predictive RMSE on this group rose from 0.0843 to 0.1102 while within-batch rank quality stayed where it was (Spearman about 0.52-0.60, unchanged from the Parent). Choosing the best of five by the mean of an accepted-only similarity-kernel posterior is a winner's curse: it selects the member whose optimism is largest, which is the member most similar to what has already scored, so a screen meant to finish a distant proposal instead domesticates it by a few thousandths. The molecular review independently reaches the same place from the chemistry: the winning edit was a single-atom move in 9,830 of the 12,181 replacements against 1,998 ring moves and 353 bond-order changes, so refinement re-decorates a molecule and never repairs or rebuilds a ring system or installs a whole functional group - and the one breakthrough edit installed an N-F bond onto an N-Cl nitrogen, a motif a chemist would reject, on a benchmark that does not price it out.

What this makes worth trying is therefore a change of statistic and of granularity, not a change of k or of the operator mix. The screening statistic needs to be something other than the same posterior mean the selector is about to maximize - predicted improvement, an uncertainty-aware or novelty-adjusted criterion, or a chemistry-side acceptance rule independent of the surrogate - and the variants need moves at fragment or ring-system granularity so one accepted refinement step can complete a structure. A valence-and-stability filter in the shared admission path would also change what both origins can reach the top with. The trajectories add a method-level diagnosis that no parameter will fix: late search collapses onto one decorated framework (9-58% of proposals in the last hundred evaluations within Tanimoto 0.6 of the running best, per-session top-thirty spanning as few as 2-5 generic frameworks on three objectives, up to 45% of late proposals repeating a score already seen to six decimals), and a stage that optimises every slot toward the already-fitted posterior mean reinforces that collapse by construction. Breadth has to be admitted on its own terms - diversity-aware pool admission, an explicit scaffold-level jump operator, or a ranking model whose uncertainty is comparable across chemotypes - and the 102 degenerate micro-molecules that still consume evaluations all come from the crossover path this stage does not touch, so a refinement attached to one origin leaves the other origin's failure mode intact.

What stays open is attribution, and the honest reading is that it is not settled by this node. The panel gain is real and it is concentrated: three of fifteen cells carry 79% of it, half of the prior path's increment mass is one session, and the largest contributor is one rare realization - only 2 of 189 previously recorded deco_hop seed-2 cells exceeded 0.70, and one of them was in this same lineage, so the basin is reachable without this mechanism. Within the field-reduced regime the ordering is consistent (no-prior control -0.0557 against the Anchor, raw-prior Parent -0.0519, this arm -0.0063) and every task mean is above both references, which is the strongest evidence the route has produced; but that ordering mixes three differences at once and the unselected raw continuations carry no counterfactual score, so it supports the joint recipe rather than the refinement stage as a component. A replication of this arm on the same code at new Confirmation-style realizations is what would separate a reproducible recovery from a lucky cell, and it is the one remaining iteration this route justifies before any change of statistic is tested; the complementary same-round arm that forces the allocator to buy raw distant chemistry answers the other half, and between them the campaign will know whether the allocator refused a good candidate or the candidate arrived off the ridge.

nodes.hypothesis: Suppress optional ordinary single-parent mutation continuation during measured stagnation only. In every breeding attempt of a batch announced while the session's own counter of consecutive non-improving announced batches stands at or above K=3, an ordinary single-parent proposal at the inherited saturation floor of one makes exactly one mutate call instead of the sampled one, two or three; the original base-length draw is still made at its original stream position, the escalation schedule above floor one is untouched, and the inherited optional second and third calls are restored exactly in every batch announced outside the regime and before the first activation. The unchanged round-38/39 entry rule and its original exit on the first improving announced batch are reused, so stalled search takes strictly shorter graph walks while improving search is unchanged.
nodes.finding:
The switch behaved exactly as registered. Thirteen of the fifteen task sessions stalled long enough to trigger it: 84 of 435 announced batches in 29 stall episodes, against 91 batches in 29 episodes on the Anchor's own path. The two decoration-hopping sessions that never stall (seeds 0 and 2) reproduced the Anchor molecule for molecule, including its 0.856 seed-0 endpoint. Every other session matched the Anchor exactly until its first stalled batch. The logged stall state matched an independent recount from the run's own scores in all 435 batches.

Inside stalled batches, all 8,036 single-parent mutation attempts made exactly one edit. 1,461 of them (18%) had drawn a two- or three-edit walk and were cut short, suppressing 1,686 edits. No multi-edit product entered a pool, where the Anchor had pooled 1,593 in its stalled batches. Outside stalls the walk-length mix stayed at the inherited 82/15/3 percent. The shortened walks did reach the oracle. Their first products filled 1,365 pool slots and the allocator picked 96 of them, about twice the rate at which it picked the Anchor's multi-edit products (7.0% versus 3.5%). Of those 96, 9 beat their parent and 5 briefly raised the session best, but none became a final endpoint. Inside stalls, the overall parent-beating rate (8.8% versus 8.6%) and the number of new bests (25 versus 28) were essentially the Anchor's.

On scores, the fifteen-cell mean rose by 0.0039 (0.6003 versus 0.5965). That lands in the pre-registered 'harmful presence' band (at least +0.002), the opposite of the decrease the plan expected, but it is fragile. The seed macros moved +0.0002, -0.0060 and +0.0174. Six cells rose, six fell and three were unchanged. The gain comes from zaleplon_mpo (+0.037 mean; cells +0.054, -0.035 and +0.094). Dropping the single zaleplon seed-2 cell turns the panel to -0.0025, and the other twelve cells average -0.0045.

median_2, the brief's target, did not move: 0.2221 versus the Anchor's 0.2227 (-0.0006; cells +0.014, +0.003 and -0.019). That is far short of the +0.010 goal, and the seed-2 cell is below the Anchor. Three of the four protected tasks held their margins: deco_hop (+0.0038), drd2_docking (+0.0001) and zaleplon_mpo (+0.0373). sitagliptin_mpo fell 0.0211 (0.5837 versus 0.6048), just past its 0.02 margin, almost entirely from seed 0 (-0.054).

Where continuation earns its keep. On this Anchor, removing optional multi-edit walks for the whole run cost 0.031 of panel mean. Removing them only while the search is stalled cost nothing (+0.0039). These are dependent single realizations and cannot be added together. Side by side, though, they suggest the channel's value sits in the improving phase, not in stalls. By the registered rule this node classifies stall-phase continuation as harmful presence. Because one cell carries that classification, it is a weak negative and not a case for removing continuation anywhere.

The median_2 lead does not run through stalls. The whole-run removal's +0.012 on median_2 did not reappear. median_2 rarely stalls at K=3 (8 stalled batches over three seeds here, 12 on the Anchor) because it keeps creeping upward in steps of about 0.003. The switch therefore cut only 16 to 73 walks per median_2 session (19 to 88 suppressed edits), and median_2 cell swings of about 0.02 are the size of path noise. A stall-gated change is structurally weak on median_2. If shorter walks really help median_2, they would have to act in the improving phase, where the whole-run removal showed that shortening costs deco_hop and sitagliptin. The molecular assessment explains why walk length is the wrong lever there. The median_2 sessions stay on inherited quinoline-plus-cyclic-imide cores whose leading decorations all score within 0.007 of each other, and the leader moved only from 0.222 to 0.229 over the whole run. Crossing that plateau needs a scaffold-changing move such as building a new ring, not a shorter or longer walk. Two things remain worth testing: a trigger that counts tiny gains as stagnation, computed only from the session's own score scale, and the molecular role's ring-construction gap.

A task-dependent sign. On this Anchor, sitagliptin_mpo and zaleplon_mpo respond in opposite directions to stall-time walk length, and they do so consistently across the two opposite doses. The stall-gated longer-walk sibling gained +0.053 on sitagliptin (all three seeds) and lost 0.010 on zaleplon. This shorter-walk node lost 0.021 on sitagliptin and gained 0.037 on zaleplon. Each is one dependent realization, and single cells can move by about 0.04 from path noise alone. Still, the mirror pattern suggests that no fixed stall-time walk length suits every task. The candidate never knows its task, so the next useful experiment is not another fixed dose. It is a rule that reads this session's own evidence on whether multi-edit products are paying off.

Still open: zaleplon seed 0, the cell that all eight earlier same-trigger siblings lost, rose here from 0.459 to 0.513, and one realization cannot say whether that was the shorter walks or luck. Path noise remains the binding uncertainty. This node's cell spread (standard deviation 0.033) is more than twice that of the single law-free reference (0.015), so a second realization would be needed before the harmful-presence reading is trusted. As a median_2 route, stall-gated continuation removal should stop.

nodes.hypothesis: Joint removal of off-diagonal completed and pending exploration density only at episode>0 and parent_id==0 on n-b13ef5ae4ba8. For eligible root i retain D_i=sum_j K_ij N_j, P_i=sum_j K_ij O_j and B_i=sum_{j:N_j>0} K_ij N_j M_j as exact inherited shared rows, and retain exploitation V_i=B_i/D_i if D_i>0 else the inherited 0.5 default. Replace only exploration started_i=D_i+P_i by N_i+O_i, including the zero-start priority. The active index for positive started is V_i+0.5*sqrt(2*log(max(2,N_parent+O_parent))/(N_i+O_i)); resolve exact ties by earliest occurrence ID. D remains the value normalizer and is not overwritten by N. With nonnegative similarity and diagonal one, removing borrowed density weakly increases bonuses at fixed state, strictly when off-diagonal density is positive, and can change root choices and purchased descendants. This is an obstacle intervention on a different statistical consumer of the refuted membership Parent, not another membership-benefit prediction. The Child’s adaptive paid feedback determines its conditional endpoint sign.
nodes.finding:
The mechanism operated: all 7,510 exposed root rows received smaller exploration denominators and larger bonuses while retaining their shared peak values. It changed 785 root choices; 743 reached accepted paid purchases, including 468 late purchases. No isolation violation was detected. Across all three Search seeds, mean final score rose from 0.48097006 to 0.48305964, a gain of 0.00208958 against the registered 0.002 scale. Seed differences were +0.04744, -0.05589 and +0.01472. Full incumbent progress rose from 4.08717 to 4.11851 and late progress from 0.86560 to 1.29429, while full strict improvements fell from 148 to 139. The formal Anchor remains ahead by 0.12397068; its performance target is unmet.

This completes the previously unobserved treatment cell without turning the small finite-panel gain into a reliability claim. Under the frozen shared-value composition, removing joint exploration density has a narrowly positive measured effect, so the retained joint consumer has a conditional negative contribution at the registered descriptive scale. Removing the same joint consumer under own values gains 0.01491352; the four-cell difference is +0.01282394, with seed differences spanning -0.04551 to +0.05727. That variation leaves generalization and separate completed-versus-pending attribution open. It does not repair the earlier pending-condition correspondence gap, reverse the membership finding or settle the route as a whole.

More switches did not mean consistently useful switched purchases: only 3 of the 743 changed-route purchases improved the incumbent. Preceding origins received 1,784 purchases versus 1,686 in the Parent, but their progress mass fell from 1.99807 to 0.69556 while current-origin progress increased. These are adaptive, selected strata and cannot establish mediation. The molecular evidence also shows a persistent proposal limitation: small-fragment purchases increased from 319 to 367, including 170 to 218 late, while the large-molecule tail stayed near 245. More than a thousand generic scaffolds remain represented, so wholesale scaffold collapse is unsupported. Useful ring, amine and polar arrangements are reachable, but graph edits do not preserve them reliably. A proposal operator that preserves useful local arrangements during scaffold and size changes, or a search scheme that ranks those alternatives using current-session feedback, could address that limitation; this experiment did not test either. No goal or approach completion is asserted.

nodes.hypothesis: Refine only the Parent's attachment and ring-closure pheromone keys with fixed, permutation-invariant one-bond neighborhood descriptors so accepted winner reinforcement transfers between matching local neighborhoods instead of all sites sharing the Parent's coarser endpoint description.
nodes.finding:
The intended credit localization happened. Across the five task-specific tables, 3,027 attachment keys and 6,522 ring-closure keys separated previously shared neighborhoods. All 145 online winner updates withheld deposits from other neighborhoods when opportunities existed, totaling 75,964 alternative/update pairs. Every one of 10,719 mixed-neighborhood update probes increased the winner neighborhoods' conditional probability mass. Later construction contained 18,485 selected moves whose conditional probabilities changed and whose exact neighborhoods traced to earlier accepted online winners. The optimization gain was much smaller than the amount of activity. Among accepted ants that reused online credit, 7 of 1,396 beat their pre-batch incumbent, compared with 3 of 1,399 for the Parent; reuse still reached about 96% of accepted ants. All strict incumbent beaters increased from 8 to 12, but three of the new online-reusing docking beaters were steps of at most 0.00000044 along a low score plateau. The single screening seed's mean final Top-1 rose from 0.2523 to 0.2579. The sitagliptin multi-property score rose from 0.0980 to 0.2392, while dopamine-receptor docking fell from 0.1371 to 0.0289 and decoration hopping fell from 0.5534 to 0.5484. The zaleplon and median-molecule scores stayed at 0.3051 and 0.1678. No generated molecule beat the supplied starting incumbent on three of the five objectives. All 1,450 submitted molecules were accepted; one additional local construction repeated a molecule and was replaced before submission.

This experiment separates local credit discrimination from productive molecular search. Different neighborhoods really were being collapsed by the old keys, and the new keys distinguish them without changing the legal chemistry or fixed heuristic weights. Matching neighborhoods also recur often enough to transfer credit across different partial molecules, so the refinement did not eliminate transfer through excessive sparsity. Yet most ants still inherit some online credit, and only 5.84% of the observed split-menu groups carried unequal refined pheromones. More precise keys therefore changed specific decisions without making successful whole molecules common. The chemistry explains why the modest mean gain should not be read as a broadly improved generator. The molecular assessment found a compact acyclic urea behind the strongest score increase, but long unsaturated chains and unconventional ring assemblies still dominate. Mean atom count fell slightly, while ring-closure actions fell sharply and terminations at the 64-atom ceiling became more frequent. In every task the late molecules were larger than the early molecules. Local credit refinement alone did not produce sustained access to compact, organized, functionalized chemistry. The result supports the implementation and shows a descriptive gain on this seed; it does not establish a reliable oracle-score benefit of selective credit. Larger changes in different objectives nearly cancel, some counted gains are near numerical ties, and the same-menu probability comparisons do not score unsubmitted alternatives. Whether broader molecular constraints or a better size and termination prior can make the now-demonstrated local discrimination useful remains open, as does its reliability across seeds.

nodes.hypothesis: Remove only original cross-candidate dependence from allocation residual draws by multiplying each original standard normal by the corresponding full Cholesky row norm, preserving the Parent’s actual jittered marginal variances, nonzero residual influence and fitted full count-based joint posterior.
nodes.finding:
The change did exactly what it was meant to do and nothing else. In every one of the 435 batch decisions (five tasks, three seeds, 29 batches each) the fitted model still treated the candidates as related: 99.9% of candidate pairs had nonzero model covariance. Even so, the random draws that pick each batch were, exactly as specified, independent across candidates, each with that candidate's full posterior variance, and the model's means, uncertainties and factorization matched the Parent's code on identical inputs. The random numbers themselves were identical to the Parent's in every batch. The change mattered at almost every decision. Replaying the original correlated draws on the Child's own pools would have picked a different set of ten molecules in 422 of 435 batches, with an average overlap of 6.8 of 10. On the 15 first batches, where Child and Parent saw identical inputs, the replay reproduced the Parent's actual choices exactly. Sampled noise still steered 3,713 of 4,350 picks away from the highest predicted mean. Molecule generation, the sulfur gate, identity checks, the survivor population and the feedback loop were re-audited with no failures.

The final score fell from 0.5965 to 0.5459, a paired loss of 0.0505, far past the 0.002 decision scale. All three seeds lost (-0.087, -0.030, -0.035), and 10 of 15 task-seed endpoints fell. The largest drops were on drd2_docking seed 1 (-0.269) and deco_hop seed 0 (-0.253). Five rose: sitagliptin_mpo seed 1 by +0.153, and four by less than 0.01 (median_2 seeds 0 and 1, sitagliptin_mpo seed 2, deco_hop seed 1). By task, drd2_docking (-0.131), deco_hop (-0.100) and zaleplon_mpo (-0.037) fell, while median_2 (+0.002) and sitagliptin_mpo (+0.014) edged up. The three Child seed scores sit close together (standard deviation 0.010 against the Parent's 0.034): the Child is consistently lower, not just noisier.

Search behaviour changed in a mixed way. The Child logged more local wins: 680 offspring beat their best parent (Parent 648), 289 raised the running best (255), and 319 of the parent-beating offspring carried new scaffolds (262). But the material it worked from was weaker. Offspring averaged 0.299 against 0.372, their parents 0.367 against 0.455, and the total of all running-best improvements fell from 5.82 to 5.06. On deco_hop and drd2_docking, four of six Child runs drifted to much larger molecules: 47 to 83 heavy atoms on average, against 27 to 35 for the Parent. In those four runs 819 crossover attempts produced no molecule, each pairing two parents that together exceeded the 120-atom limit (the whole Parent panel had 2 such failures), and in one deco_hop run scoring took 92 minutes, inside the time limit. Ranking quality on the selected molecules was essentially unchanged: pair-ordering accuracy 0.70 against 0.71, rank correlation 0.81 against 0.81.

This answers the open component question for the current Parent. On the sulfur-gated composition, letting similar candidates share their sampled noise is worth about 0.05 of mean final score. Under the registered rule, that is a positive conditional contribution of cross-candidate residual correlation. The same removal on the earlier, ungated Parent cost 0.018 and had one gaining seed; here every seed loses. These two results come from different Parents and are not an interaction estimate. The result is descriptive, from three seeds, and not uniform: sitagliptin_mpo and median_2 gained in two seeds each.

The replays on identical pools show what correlation does at a single decision. Without it, the chosen batch of ten looks more alike to the model: average absolute model correlation within the batch rises from 0.051 to 0.055, and the reverse replay on Parent pools shows the same shift. The batch also sits slightly farther from already-scored molecules, while molecule size and the crossover share barely change. Correlated noise therefore spreads each batch across regions the model treats as distinct. These per-decision differences are small, but they compound. Histories diverge from the first batch, and on two tasks they drift toward large, sprawling molecules. On those two tasks, the Molecular review finds that the Child's higher-scoring molecules are the smaller ones. This is the third allocation change in this lineage to show the same pattern: more local wins but less total progress (the earlier ungated removal and the exponential-residual substitution showed it too). Parent-beat counts and new-scaffold counts should not be read as evidence of useful exploration here.

Open questions remain. The size drift accompanies the biggest losses, but it is an association, not a demonstrated cause. In five of fifteen Child runs the sulfur gate never fired, and their scored trajectories are byte-identical to the earlier ungated removal. Two whole task-seed comparisons repeat the earlier experiment exactly, although the remaining 13 still average -0.040. So this is not an independent replication, and it says nothing about whether the gate and correlation interact. Whether a stronger batch-diversity rule would beat correlated draws is untested. The result argues for keeping correlated allocation and, if anything, strengthening batch-level diversity. It also makes molecule-size control a candidate lever: unchecked growth accompanies the largest losses on two tasks and pushes scoring time toward the per-task limit.

nodes.hypothesis: Train the reusable unlabeled recurrent prior on a half-original, half identity-checked alternative-SMILES serialization mixture for the same selected training rows, preserving the original holdout checkpoint rule and all online components.
nodes.finding:
The intended preparation mechanism activated in every seed. About 3.786 million changed-alternative exposures entered gradient minibatches per completed preparation, and more than 99.5% of the distinct consumed alternative rows added adjacent-token contexts absent from their own original strings. The original molecular row schedule and holdout split were preserved, with identity and encoding checks backed by independently reconstructed logged pairs and the full holdout. Learned support broadened: on the same held-out alternative traversals, token NLL falls from the Parent’s 1.76–1.78 to about 0.765, and the alternative-versus-original gap shrinks from about 1.19–1.22 to 0.157–0.159. Original-string fit worsens, from about 0.563–0.566 to 0.607, despite both nodes completing the same 29,742 training steps. Preparation takes about 1,056–1,071 seconds versus 218–281 seconds for the Parent. All online code and prior-freezing checks remain intact. All required evaluations finish, and all three seed macro scores improve: the mean rises from 0.520669 to 0.546307, a paired gain of 0.025638, with individual gains of 0.010517, 0.025244 and 0.041153. The benefit is uneven across tasks: the sitagliptin mean rises by 0.163551, while three other task means decline. Raw neural validity also falls from 70.34% to 61.88%; invalid and unterminated strings rise even though every announced batch is filled.

This establishes broader support for equivalent molecular traversals, with a measurable cost in fitting the original strings. That support does not automatically make adapted neural generation more chemically valid or improve every task. The higher overall score coexists with more invalid draws and with chemically questionable high-scoring structures: the Molecular assessment identifies an unusual hydrogen-bearing sulfur family in the largest-gain task, selenium-containing aromatic amines elsewhere, poor size control and absent stereochemical specification. The gain therefore cannot be interpreted as a general chemical-quality improvement, nor as evidence that selenium or the atypical sulfur connectivity is necessary. The experiment isolates the changed preparation mechanism in source, but its downstream effects pass through the inherited reciprocal graph search and posterior selection; the logged first neural batches already follow initial-observation adaptation and are not a pure-prior test. The useful new distinction is between learning more traversal syntax, sampling valid molecules, and obtaining favorable scalar scores. All three must remain visible.

nodes.hypothesis: Remove candidate-dependent predictive allocation location only when the inherited stall predicate requests the top-forty restriction and the original posterior allocation succeeds. Write R = original_score_scale * (original_normals @ original_pool_factor.T). On those restricted announcements active_sample_values = original_archive_score_mean + R; on every unrestricted announcement active_sample_values remains original_predictive_mean[None, :] + R exactly. The original GP mean remains active for constructing the identical top-forty mask. Original fitting, covariance, Cholesky jitter, residual scale, normal draw and consumption, availability updates and ascending-index first-maximum ties are retained. The causal claim is that removing this second mean consumer eliminates relative location within the eligible set and changes paid identities toward lower original predictive means; if the removed fine preference is useful beyond eligibility, full/late realized progress and the complete endpoint mean will fall. This is a partial-pathway contribution probe within m-000000000005, conditional on the mask and residual staying active, not removal of the fitted predictor or of all predictive-location influence.
nodes.finding:
The scoped removal executed in 93 of 435 batches and changed every restricted purchase set. It displaced 476 purchased molecules and changed 625 strict per-position choices; all reached accepted feedback. The original-mean eligibility mask, correlated residual and unrestricted rule were preserved. Summed original predictive mean fell from 367.52 for the same-state original choices to 328.83 for the actual purchases; 92 of 93 batches decreased, with one small increase. Across all fifteen matched Search sessions, mean final Top-1 fell from 0.607030 to 0.583938, a paired change of -0.023092. All three seed averages fell; ten task/seed endpoints fell, two improved and three tied. Full and late incumbent-gain amounts fell from 5.97807 to 5.63169 and from 1.02241 to 0.85718. Improvement counts instead rose slightly, from 253 to 258 overall and 76 to 77 late, so the loss reflects smaller gains rather than fewer gains. Complete prediction joins and zero numerical fallbacks rule out a technical failure. The decrease crosses the registered 0.002 descriptive boundary for positive contribution of the retained within-set mean preference; it is not a performance improvement by the removal.

Mean-based eligibility does not exhaust the useful information in the fitted mean: its finer ordering inside an already screened set still adds value on this Parent. The surviving original GP predictions also had lower squared error than the constant allocation location on the same restricted purchases (0.01332 versus 0.02867), but these selected outcomes cannot establish calibration or rankings for unpurchased molecules. Removing that guidance produced broader scaffold coverage and lower similarity, including after small fragments were excluded, while yielding less total progress and fewer survivors and reused offspring. The method can reach varied molecular graphs; the evidence narrows the limitation to converting that variety into larger useful gains, rather than universal scaffold collapse. Late search still concentrates, and the Molecular assessment finds narrow high-scoring chemical families, tied peripheral analogues, reactive heteroatom-halogen motifs and missing specified stereochemistry. A proposal operator that distinguishes attachment environments, or a ranking/search model that better values useful structural changes, could address those limitations; neither was tested here. Chemistry is not an established mediator of this score loss. The result settles the conditional contribution of fine location guidance on this composition. It leaves the separate eligibility mask, total selector, alternative ranking models and transfer to other compositions unresolved; it does not end the broader approach.

nodes.hypothesis: Replace only nonincumbent score-greedy survivor membership with the newest accepted serials from the current live retention contest, protecting the single inherited incumbent and restoring inherited score/serial order before unchanged breeding.
nodes.finding:
The rule executed exactly in all 4,365 retention calls. It changed 3,483 of 3,540 capacity-limited survivor sets and 3,451 retained score vectors while preserving the incumbent. Stored alternatives did not become new breeders: none of the 135 recency-only records ever gained later sampling support or bred. Shared survivors did change ranks and probabilities, producing 3,865 altered-rank parent draws and 713 altered-probability draws. Their accepted products numbered 126 and 18 respectively, with the latter inside the former; three of the 126 raised the incumbent and 58 later bred. Two task/seed sessions had affected draws but no immediately accepted product in this locally tagged cohort.

All three replicas completed. Mean final Top -1 fell from 0.595670 to 0.583863, a paired change of -0.011807 beyond the registered 0.002 scale. Seed changes were -0.044786, +0.024951 and -0.015585. Nine task/seed endpoints declined and six improved; decoration hopping, docking and median-task means declined, while zaleplon and sitagliptin means improved. Seed-macro population deviation fell from 0.026593 to 0.002305. All 4,350 accepted products survived their immediate batch and 2,746 later bred, versus 3,415 and 2,401 under the Parent, yet this greater survival and reuse did not produce a higher endpoint mean.

The result supplies positive conditional evidence for inherited nonincumbent greedy survival while the incumbent, score-quantile sampling, recursive feedback and learned allocation stay active. Its observed route is changed access to shared survivors, rather than reuse of the extra weak records kept at the local cutoff. The latter route is explicitly refuted here. Most changed memberships leave the immediate sampling probabilities unchanged; preserving a molecule is therefore not the same as exploring its neighborhood. Earlier protected-but-never-bred retention failures remain relevant counterexamples.

The shared-survivor route can still produce useful chemistry: a crossover involving a parent newly inside sampling support creates a halogen-free aromatic/carbonyl leader and then breeds 243 times. Another such crossover loses to its parents and never breeds again. The molecular assessment finds many tiny recency-only records and 16 tiny final survivors, alongside useful amines and carbonyl frameworks and persistent reactive bonds, unusual rings and unspecified stereochemistry. These observations explain what was retained and used; they do not establish a chemical cause of the aggregate loss, graph-equivalence guarantees, or practical chemical feasibility.

This answers the specified retention-component contrast on the complete three-seed panel. It leaves membership quality, age, rank changes and later learning bundled together, and does not measure the whole evolutionary foundation or combine additively with the separate rank-preference and recursive-breeding controls. The six endpoint gains and the zero-use pathways limit transfer beyond the registered conditions. No age-window or retention retuning is justified by this completed control.

nodes.hypothesis: Select the Gaussian process observation-noise scale at each fit by accepted-archive marginal likelihood over a fixed ladder around the inherited scale, so task-local label agreement controls posterior regularization.
nodes.finding:
Noise selection changed the implemented posterior in 434 of 435 fits, and every likelihood winner and recorded evaluation choice reconstructed correctly. The smallest available noise won 179 fits and the largest won 116; the chosen scale changed after feedback at 41 of 420 opportunities. On the same earlier archives and the same 4350 subsequently scored molecules, prediction MSE fell from 0.0121771 with fixed noise to 0.0116233 with learned noise. Latent 95% interval coverage rose from 79.75% to 82.51%, while mean within-batch rank correlation fell from 0.41596 to 0.39609. Noise-inclusive coverage reached 89.91% with wider intervals, reported separately from latent uncertainty. The same random draws applied to the two distributions changed the selected molecule set in 255 of 435 batches. Despite those prediction gains, mean final-best score fell from 0.551771 to 0.535810, a paired change of -0.015961 against the registered +0.002 target; seed variability increased from 0.008223 to 0.023346. One seed macro improved and two declined. Task means rose for median and sitagliptin and slightly for decoration, but fell for DRD2 and zaleplon. All tasks completed their budgets, and every factorization succeeded at the first jitter.

The experiment separates a real regularization benefit from a search benefit. The strongest controlled prediction improvement occurs in sitagliptin: latent coverage rises from 466 to 558 of 870 scored molecules, with lower MSE in all three seeds. DRD2 instead loses three covered molecules on the same scored identities, and ranking deteriorates in the pooled comparison. Thus reducing average prediction error and winning training likelihood do not establish better discrimination among the next candidates to evaluate. The frequent upper and lower boundary choices show that different accepted molecular/score relationships call for very different regularization; they leave the adequacy of the finite ladder unresolved. Substantial undercoverage remains even with learned noise, particularly in the harder streams. Scalar noise cannot distinguish molecules with identical binary fingerprints or correct every mismatch in the representation and mean model. The chemical assessment also finds recurring ring-rich families with more reactive N/O-halogen and peroxide motifs, oversized assemblies and unresolved stereochemistry, so these predictive gains supply no evidence that chemical liabilities were repaired. The measured same-data comparison supports a modest, heterogeneous prediction benefit. It cannot assign counterfactual scores to unselected molecules or identify which changed choices caused the loss in whole-search endpoints. The mechanism executed; the expected score improvement did not occur.

nodes.hypothesis: Archive-distance-dependent prior variance (non-stationary input-dependent signal amplitude) inside the inherited accepted-only predictor. The latent function is modelled as f(x) = h1(x) + s(x) h2(x) with h1 and h2 independent zero-mean Gaussian processes under the identical inherited count-Morgan generalized-Tanimoto covariance k, and with the gate s(x) = sqrt(beta) * d(x), where d(x) = 1 - max over the session's accepted archive of k(x, archive member) is the candidate's nearest-neighbour archive distance under that same kernel and beta = 2.25 is the one declared scale. The resulting prior covariance is k(x, x') + s(x) s(x') k(x, x'), so the prior variance of a candidate is k(x, x) (1 + beta d(x)^2): it rises monotonically with archive distance and is exactly the inherited prior at distance zero. Because every accepted record has d = 0 by construction (its nearest neighbour is itself at similarity one), the gated component is identically zero on the whole training set: the training covariance, its Cholesky factor, its jitter ladder, the fitted coefficients, the adaptive mean and population-SD normalization with its 0.001 floor, the 0.05 noise SD and the train-to-pool cross-covariance are all arithmetically unchanged, and therefore so is every pool posterior mean, the (-posterior mean, pool index) ordering and the retained stall-time top-forty eligible set. The single change reaching behaviour is the pool's joint predictive covariance consumed by the inherited correlated Thompson draw, which gains the positive semidefinite term s s^T elementwise-multiplied by the pool kernel: the extra uncertainty keeps the inherited similarity as its correlation structure, so cross-candidate correlation (m-000000000007) and sampled residual influence (m-000000000006) stay the channels through which it acts, rather than being replaced by independent per-candidate noise. One (10, 160) standard-normal array per batch in the same generator, order and consumption count, the same sequential masked argmax, the same per-pick mask update, the same first-index tie rule, the same bounded generation-order fallback, and no quota, reserved pick, availability override or post-hoc variance rescaling anywhere. At beta = 0 the construction is bit-identical to the Parent, which is its degenerate control.
nodes.finding:
Construction: in all 435 announced batches of all 15 sessions the gate was computed and consumed, and nothing else moved. Every pool posterior mean matched the ungated recomputation to exactly 0.0 (float64 identity, not a tolerance), the posterior-mean ordering was identical in 435 of 435 batches, the retained stall-time top-forty eligible set was identical in all 90 restricted batches, all 4,200 probed accepted records received gate exactly 0.0, the gate was monotone in logged archive distance in 435 of 435 pools, and the fitted normalization, the 0.05 noise SD and the 1e-8 training jitter equalled the Anchor's. Batch one is byte-comparable: identical pools, identical posterior means, identical standard-normal rows, and the passive ungated replay reproduced the Anchor's own ten picks in 15 of 15 cells. Cost and stability held: 870 factorizations with zero failures and no jitter escalation above 1e-8, zero posterior fallbacks, no pool truncation, and about 0.3 added seconds per session against per-cell wall times of 29 to 201 seconds inside a 7,200-second timeout.

The uncertainty geometry moved as predicted, and more cleanly than the refuted round-44 mixture did. The archive-far to archive-near predictive SD ratio rose above the ungated model's on identical pools in 435 of 435 batches and in all 15 session means (gated mean 1.974 against base 1.697), clearing the inherited 1.7477 reference in 409 of 435 batches against the base's 138. The inflation was ordered, not global: the archive-far half inflated 1.231 against the near half's 1.080 in 435 of 435 batches, with no batch in which the near half inflated at least as much, and the per-decile prior-variance inflation rose monotonically with distance in 435 of 435 batches. Oracle-free held-out-chemotype calibration over 390 cluster splits improved on both registered clauses: pooled 95 per cent coverage of held-out chemotype clusters rose from 0.830 to 0.882, all nine sessions that under-covered under the inherited model moved toward nominal (the worst from 0.376 to 0.463, another from 0.662 to 0.844), the six sessions already at or above nominal only over-covered further and are not counted, and the cluster-to-random standardized error ratio fell below the inherited model's in 11 of 15 sessions.

Allocation moved without any quota: the ten picks differed from the passive ungated replay in 402 of 435 batches, 1,284 of 4,350 picks changed, the archive-far share of accepted evaluations rose from the Anchor's 1,142 of 4,350 (26.25 per cent) to 1,767 of 4,350 (40.62 per cent), and the mean posterior-mean rank of purchases moved from 29.2 to 40.8 on the same pools. In the 90 restricted batches the eligible set was identical and the gate only reordered picks inside it (1.99 changed picks per restricted batch at mean rank 13.4 against 13.1).

The conversion clause failed. Realized best-so-far increment mass fell from the Anchor's 5.978073 over 253 improvements to 4.752540 over 250, a 20.5 per cent loss, and the archive-far share of that mass fell from 25.1 to 13.6 per cent. Per evaluation, archive-far purchases converted at 0.000366 against the Anchor's own far-half rate of 0.001312, while near purchases rose slightly (0.001590 against 0.001397). Splitting purchases by whether the ungated replay would also have made them: the 690 archive-far picks that only the gate bought returned 0.000232 of mass per evaluation and 19 incumbent improvements, against 0.001752 per evaluation for the 2,333 near picks both rules agreed on. The fifteen-cell panel fell on all three seeds: seed macros 0.580392 / 0.540161 / 0.455431 against 0.649701 / 0.585234 / 0.586156, paired mean -0.081702 against a registered minimum effect of +0.002. That is outside this round's law-free band measured on the same Anchor, [-0.055482, +0.014579], but the excess is carried by one cell: with the weakest cell removed the remaining fourteen average -0.047322, inside the band. Both fragile high cells lost as the intent anticipated (-0.247 and -0.093). The increment-mass loss does not depend on the two weak cells: removing both still leaves 3.930 against 4.381, a 10.3 per cent fall.

The covariance-shape question that round 44 left open is now answered in the affirmative at the model layer and in the negative at the conversion layer. An input-dependent prior amplitude, gated to exactly zero on the accepted archive, does make this predictor's uncertainty grow where its knowledge stops: it raised the far-to-near SD ratio in every batch, ordered the inflation by distance, and improved held-out chemotype coverage toward nominal in every session that under-covered - precisely the geometry the regime mixture inverted. So the recorded defect was real and is now fixable at this layer, and the mixture's failure is confirmed as a property of its construction rather than of the goal. What does not follow is benefit. Better-calibrated far-field uncertainty, delivered through the inherited correlated Thompson draw, bought 625 more archive-far evaluations that returned less mass than the evaluations they displaced. This is the third independent demonstration on this lineage that extra distant purchases convert worse than the inherited rule's own far-half choices, and the first in which the extra purchases were produced by the model's own pricing rather than by a quota or a reservation - which closes the remaining explanation that the earlier failures were artefacts of overriding the ranking. The registered stop condition applies exactly as written, and it forbids a sweep of the warp's form, its scale or the distance statistic: this recipe is finished.

What the trajectories show about the method is more useful than the score. The failure is not in the surrogate's ranking quality, which if anything improved (batch prediction-score rank correlation 0.544 against 0.515); it is in what the distance statistic means. Nearest-neighbour count-fingerprint dissimilarity is maximized as readily by degenerate proposals as by genuinely new scaffolds, so a monotone warp in it reprices both: 28 per cent of the archive-far picks that only the gate bought carry five or fewer heavy atoms, near-empty proposals rose from 91 to 236 of 4,350 evaluations and duplicated-fragment products above 50 heavy atoms from 44 to 344. That mechanism is visible in the two cells that collapsed. In the weakest cell the pool's mean size inflated from about 40 to 74-81 heavy atoms by the third to eighth batch while its incumbent stayed at 0.029 through batch 16 - the Anchor's same-seed cell was past 0.96 by batch 15 - because distance-driven purchases entered the archive, which moved the distance statistic again, a self-reinforcing drift that only broke when the session fell back onto a compact scaffold around batch 17 and ended at 0.4105. In the other weak cell the gate displaced the Anchor's best batch-one pick, the incumbent line lost its aromatic core by batch 10 and spent the remaining nineteen batches refining a non-aromatic caged core to 0.4335 while the same-objective sibling cells, which kept an aromatic core, reached 0.56-0.67; the molecular report reads the same cells the same way, with no aromatic ring in that cell's top band. Because the gate acts in every batch rather than in the 88 restricted ones, it displaced the Anchor's best batch-one pick in 7 of 15 cells, so cell-level dispersion is part of the cost, not noise around it.

What this narrows for the campaign: calibrating the covariance is not the binding constraint, and neither is the ranking - the binding constraint is that widening a Thompson draw converts uncertainty into purchases without pricing the downside of the candidate it buys, and that the archive-distance statistic this lineage uses conflates novelty with degeneracy. Two kinds of method, not parameters, follow from that. First, a value rule rather than a wider draw: an acquisition that scores a candidate's expected gain against its risk (an improvement-based or risk-averse ranking over the same calibrated posterior) would let the better-calibrated far field inform the choice without automatically buying it. Second, a proposal or admission class that makes distance mean scaffold novelty - a size-and-composition envelope on candidates, or group-level rather than single-atom proposal moves - so that the far half of a pool is populated by coherent alternative chemistry instead of fragments and duplication products; the molecular report's independent reading of this node's output asks for the same thing, and the two sibling tickets running this round touch exactly those two layers. Also still open: this arm raises only the far-field ceiling, so the inherited posterior's much larger near-archive overconfidence is untouched and remains a separate, unmeasured object.

nodes.hypothesis: Project each proposed online Adam parameter displacement onto the half-space that does not increase the fixed selected-historical augmented-target loss to first order, using that loss's gradient at the pre-step policy, while retaining the inherited equal-row objective, Adam moments and step counter.
nodes.finding:
The projection executed on 2,029 of 5,040 history-bearing Adam steps followed by further proposals. All 1,904 corrections above the registered numerical resolution measurably changed the parameters and satisfied the intended historical-loss half-space. The remaining 125 triggering corrections were below analytical resolution. Projection affected 381 of the 420 nonterminal historical updates; 99 additional terminal projections have no later molecules to influence. Original accepted strings, scores, targets, replay selection, equal row weights, Adam moments and counters, and frozen priors were preserved. All fifteen current-only initialization updates and first generated batches matched the Parent exactly.

On the same training tensor, the applied projection reduced historical MSE relative to the proposed Adam state in 2,019 of 2,029 nonterminal projected steps, by 1.320902 on average. Current MSE increased relative to that proposal by 0.885112 on average, with worse current fitting in 1,379 steps. Despite satisfying the local slope constraint, 1,807 projected steps still increased historical MSE relative to their own starting state. Across complete updates, historical group error worsened 118 times out of 420, compared with 131 for the Parent. Individual historical rows showed almost no improvement in worsening frequency: 837 of 2,100 exposures worsened, versus 834.

All fifteen tasks completed their 300-call budgets. In subsequent generation, raw validity was 92.56% versus the Parent's 92.67%, novel yield rose from 50.59% to 51.59%, and duplicate draws fell from 42.08% to 40.98%. Sampling nevertheless had a worse tail: 49 batches needed additional sampling, versus 41.

Mean final Top-1 fell from 0.513272 to 0.493473, a paired mean change of -0.019800. All three seed changes were negative: -0.006076, -0.012316 and -0.041007. The child population standard deviation was 0.013845, versus 0.001984 for the Parent. Sitagliptin accounted for the main loss, falling from mean 0.288538 to 0.172377. Zaleplon improved by 0.023783 and DRD2 by 0.001335, while deco-hop and median-2 decreased by 0.005779 and 0.002176. The expected score improvement was not observed.

The experiment establishes that adverse directions in the actual Adam displacement can be removed while preserving the optimizer's accumulated state and the original learning problem. Exact initialization controls, unchanged targets and verified state preservation rule out those confounds. The practical limit is visible within the same step: a first-order constraint usually softens historical error growth, but curvature often leaves a finite increase. Protecting the historical group also leaves individual historical rows unprotected and can sacrifice progress on the current batch.

The targets continue to ask for impossible positive log probabilities in 607 of 2,100 nonterminal historical exposures, compared with 595 in the Parent. Better protection of such fitting pressure has no demonstrated link to more useful molecules. Total chemical diversity also fails to explain the score loss: after historical updates, sitagliptin proposals covered 767 distinct molecular cores versus 714 in the Parent, yet only 142 proposals exceeded the common initial best score, versus 189. The molecular assessment describes abundant rings and aromatic fragments with uneven placement of useful polar groups and linkers. The open problem is consistently producing productive arrangements within that broad chemistry. These observations narrow the question to the connection between selected-history fitting, finite update tradeoffs and useful future proposals; the projection's execution is established.

nodes.hypothesis: Reject an otherwise valid canonically novel graph neighbor before tabu testing exactly when it introduces or increases the multiplicity of a sulfur local-environment signature outside a fixed neutral sulfur-valence envelope relative to the same scored source graph, then continue the inherited graph-edit sampling loop from that unchanged source.
nodes.finding:
The gate rejected 766 of 5,307 otherwise valid novel neighbors across all fifteen task sessions. Of those rejections, 760 would have passed the unchanged tabu rule, and every rejection was followed by a different permitted neighbor from the same scored source. None of the 4,350 emitted molecules contains sulfur outside the declared envelope, compared with 2,398 of 4,350 Parent emissions. Sulfur remains in 2,821 emitted molecules, including thiols, sulfides, aromatic sulfur, thiones, sulfoxides and sulfones.

All three seeds complete all five 300-evaluation tasks and all 435 ten-member batches. The sampling cost rises from 5,285 to 6,234 raw attempts, or 12.15 to 14.33 attempts per batch. Emission yield falls from 82.31% to 69.78% of raw attempts. Recorded edits, normalized identities, accepted-score joins and downstream memory/winner rules pass the independent audit.

Mean macro final Top-1 rises from 0.520918 to 0.526783, a paired mean change of +0.005865. The seed changes are +0.015565, -0.061423 and +0.063454, and the macro population standard deviation rises from 0.004890 to 0.046774. Zaleplon and median_2 improve in every matched seed; decoration hopping declines in every seed, while DRD2 and sitagliptin have mixed outcomes. The gate therefore achieves its intended chemical and allocation changes with an uneven score response.

The targeted sulfur channel was largely independent of the existing tabu veto: 760 of 766 rejected draws would otherwise have reached allocation. Ordinary sulfur alternatives remain abundant enough to fill every batch and retain the panel's average score, despite the extra sampling work. All selected initial sources were already clean under the envelope, so the experiment demonstrates prevention of new violations; it does not exercise recovery from an inherited violating source. Most rejected opportunities come from atom replacement, which accounts for 734 of the 766 rejections.

The small favorable mean score is accompanied by a substantial loss in one seed and lower mean scores on two tasks. It supports the stated mean non-inferiority direction on this panel without establishing a consistent improvement. The molecular assessment also shows where the chemical benefit stops: more ordinary sulfur and recognizable aromatic polyamines coexist with nitrogen/oxygen-halogen bonds, constrained unsaturation, dense cages and unspecified stereochemistry. Sulfur valence is one separable source of implausible chemistry; whole-molecule stability, accessible ring geometry and stereochemistry remain unresolved.

nodes.hypothesis: At each history-bearing adaptation update, set fixed current and historical loss shares inversely to the norms of their respective starting mean-loss gradients, with the historical gradient retaining the Parent's normalized inverse-exposure weights, so the two groups have equal starting contribution magnitudes; preserve selected members, augmented targets and the inherited optimizer.
nodes.finding:
The fixed-share mechanism reached the real optimizer. In all 420 history updates followed by proposals, the measured starting contribution imbalance fell from 0.7012 on average to at most 4.59e-8. History received 84.54% of the loss mass on average. Every update changed the direct gradient direction even after clipping, and all 450 real first backward passes matched the direct actual objective exactly. Original accepted targets, selected-member rules, within-history exposure ratios and the fifteen history-free first-proposal controls remained intact.

One registered numerical check failed systematically: the direct balanced gradient did not reconstruct from the separately measured group gradients within the stated tolerance in any of the 435 history updates. Relative discrepancies reached 0.283% in nonterminal updates and 0.413% in terminal updates, compared with the approximately 0.001% registered tolerance. This limits the claim of exact vector reconstruction; it does not erase the observed scalar balance, changed direct gradient or real optimizer execution.

After history fitting, raw duplicate draws increased from 37.38% to 57.67%, canonical-novel yield fell from 54.80% to 37.62%, and batches needing further sampling increased from 29 to 90. All fifteen evaluations nevertheless completed their 300-call budgets. Mean final Top-1 fell from 0.517655 to 0.493672, a paired change of -0.023983. Seed changes were -0.004895, -0.009276 and -0.057779. The largest task loss was sitagliptin, whose mean endpoint fell from 0.287161 to 0.169219. Mean recorded AUC rose from 0.406769 to 0.423980, mainly alongside faster docking progress, so better average early discovery did not deliver the predicted final-score gain.

The first historical intervention isolates a useful tradeoff before the sampled trajectories diverge. On identical starting examples and likelihoods, average final current-group error was 41.85 with balancing versus 29.32 with the Parent, while historical error was 18.88 versus 23.33. Current fitting was worse in thirteen of fifteen matched sessions. More historical influence can therefore buy better average historical fitting while weakening learning from the fresh batch; it is not a general protection guarantee. Across the later child stream, historical group error still rose in 71 updates and 817 individual historical exposures worsened. History received more than 99% of the loss in 21 nonterminal updates, and the effective selected batch shrank from 9.19 to 5.82 rows on the same selected inputs.

The score loss is not explained by a universal absence of chemical variety. Accepted core counts fell for three objectives but rose slightly for median-2 and sitagliptin. The molecular assessment finds that sitagliptin remains broadly diverse while failing to reproduce useful compact polar arrangements consistently; its largest score loss occurs despite 783 distinct cores versus 775 before. Docking already reaches coherent cyclic-amine chemistry near the numerical ceiling. Familiar rings, higher validity and improved replay fitting do not by themselves produce useful new molecular combinations. The same recurrent representation still generates oversized tails, questionable linkages and unspecified stereochemistry. Positive, unattainable historical targets also remain common: 627 exposures versus 489 in the Parent, on their different sampled streams.

This rules out failure to change coefficients or gradient direction as the explanation for lost utility. It also shows that scalar balance is an insufficient success criterion. Exact group-vector reconstruction remains open: real backward agreement establishes which objective executed, but cannot explain the systematic disagreement with the separately summed gradients. The saved evidence cannot determine whether that numerical discrepancy contributed to the score loss. Any interpretation that stronger historical influence is beneficial must now account for both the observed loss of fresh-batch fitting and increased repetition, as well as this unresolved numerical behavior.

nodes.hypothesis: On code Parent n-7d1e6230ecce, replace only the success reference of the existing purchased-progress controller. Freeze G=max(score of every unique already accepted current-session archive record) before each announcement. For each region r with at least one actual accepted owned purchase in that batch, success_r is exactly max(new owned scores_r) > G + tolerance_relative*max(abs(G),tolerance_score_floor). The regional center still advances to the best owned episode record even when such a local gain is classified as global failure. nodes.finding:
The global-reference controller executed correctly in all 15 task/seed runs. Across 535 paid regional updates, eight updates that would have counted as local successes became global failures; all eight changed counter state, and two immediately changed contraction or retirement. All 335 updates without a purchase preserved their state. Actual restarts rose from 19 to 24 and every restart immediately received feedback. The experiment rules out a wiring or feedback-exposure explanation for this adjustment: the shared reference, exact arithmetic, ownership and unchanged local-center updates all check out, and all new episodes receive purchases. Its influence is narrow: only four complete molecule-and-score trajectories differ, all in two tasks, while the other eleven remain identical. Global gain-bearing receipts actually fall from 260 to 255, and the ten largest increments are identical, so the benefit comes from a limited redistribution of later progress rather than broad improvement throughout search. Molecular evidence shows continued refinement of related aromatic/carbonyl or fluorinated heterocyclic families, fewer typed/generic scaffolds (1,858/1,215 versus 1,880/1,234), and slightly larger fragment and oversized tails. Ring diversity alone therefore has not delivered consistently useful alternative frameworks. A proposal operator that preserves functional architecture while changing ring/linker frameworks, or a restart search scheme that reaches different useful basins, addresses that method limitation more directly than this progress-reference change. Those are method diagnoses, not tested improvements; these records do not establish a surrogate-ranking fault or show that removing unusual bonds improves scores. The borrowed global-utility rule worked in its scalar, frozen-batch adaptation, but this result does not validate the other MORBO components. What is settled is the registered adjustment’s subthreshold finite-panel benefit; useful regional search under a different substantive intervention remains open.

nodes.hypothesis: Preserve local-environment multiplicity in the inherited Gaussian-process posterior by replacing binary Morgan features with radius-two 2048-bin Morgan occurrence counts and their dot-product Tanimoto covariance.
nodes.finding:
Occurrence weighting changed every one of the 435 fitted pool distributions across all five tasks and three seeds. On identical accepted data, 69,570 of 69,600 pool means and marginal standard deviations differed from the binary comparator. The logged count predictions, feedback updates and correlated selections reconstructed without mismatch. Reusing the same normal draws with the binary comparator changed 2,768 of 4,350 choice positions in 434 pools; those alternative choices were not scored.

On the 4,350 molecules actually evaluated, count-posterior MSE was 0.011269 versus 0.011797 for the matched binary posterior and 0.042504 for the archive-mean baseline. Mean within-batch rank correlation rose from 0.4694 to 0.5498. Coverage deteriorated: 60.90% versus 71.36% within one latent standard deviation, and 76.92% versus 85.63% within 1.96. All 4,200 eligible next-fit probes changed; standardized uncertainty fell on every probe, while score-unit uncertainty rose on 20 because the archive scale changed. All training and pool factorizations succeeded at the first jitter in both panels.

Recorded final-best macro score rose from 0.551771 to 0.574344, a paired mean gain of 0.022573 against the declared 0.002 criterion. Child and Parent population standard deviations across seeds were 0.012317 and 0.008223; paired-delta standard deviation was 0.020520. Seed gains were +0.044871, -0.004661 and +0.027509. Mean task changes were +0.062135 for sitagliptin_mpo, +0.023333 for median_2, +0.020559 for drd2_docking, +0.009115 for deco_hop and -0.002276 for zaleplon_mpo. Ten of fifteen task-seed endpoints improved. Strict improvements over each offspring’s best generating parent rose from 593 to 624 out of 4,350. These search outcomes include the ensuing changes in generation and feedback.

Multiplicity carries useful information for this accepted-data regime, but stronger similarity also produces narrower uncertainty. On the Child’s fixed pools, mean off-diagonal similarity rose from 0.3267 to 0.5873, and marginal standard deviation fell for 67,687 of 69,600 candidates. Exact feature ties remained inseparable: the Child’s single tied pair and all ten historical Parent ties survive count encoding. This locates the observed effect in changed weighting among distinct fingerprints.

Predictive utility and endpoint utility diverge most clearly on sitagliptin_mpo: it supplies the largest mean score gain, yet count MSE worsened in all three seeds and pooled 1.96-standard-deviation coverage fell from 54.48% to 33.33%. Together with the one regressing seed, this supports investigating uncertainty and task-local transfer separately from the useful covariance change. The matched comparisons establish effects on the actual selected stream; they do not establish an alternative whole-search score or outcomes for unselected molecules.

The supplied chemical assessment still finds repeat-rich ring systems, unconventional heteroatom bonds, unassigned stereochemistry and uneven molecular growth. Count weighting has therefore not demonstrated a remedy for chemical realism, exact fingerprint equivalence or stereochemical coverage. The numerical failure branches also remain untested because no eligible failure occurred.
