nodes.hypothesis: For each regional RACOS classifier, uniformly select one identity-verified equivalent SELFIES serialization view per scored molecular record from a bounded task-local view bank, and apply the inherited negative-exclusion, uncertainty-shrinking and uniform-sampling rules to those selected views while preserving one observation weight and the immutable original sampled-frame score receipt per molecule.
nodes.finding:
The equivalent views produced a measurable molecular effect. Verified alternatives were available for 1,175 of 1,500 scored records, and an alternative exemplar was selected in 808 of 1,341 regional constructions. Holding the molecular observations and sampling randomness fixed, 797 paired proposals decoded to different molecules; 782 of those changes survived filtering and received real evaluator scores. All identity, one-observation, score-attachment and batch checks passed.

Regional novelty acceptance rose from 96.24% to 97.61%, and decoded overlaps across regions fell from 48 of 1,355 raw draws to 31 of 1,341. The fraction of accepted regional children beating their exemplar rose slightly, from 67/1,304 (5.14%) to 78/1,309 (5.96%). The five-task final Top-1 mean nevertheless fell from 0.315539 to 0.289335. Parent-to-current maxima were 0.345581 to 0.366339 for zaleplon_mpo, 0.579123 to 0.571504 for deco_hop, 0.120104 to 0.028849 for drd2_docking, 0.167839 to 0.168550 for median_2, and 0.365051 to 0.311434 for sitagliptin_mpo. Both runs completed all five tasks with 300 evaluations each. This is one screening seed.

Equivalent construction representatives can change the molecules reached by a local token sampler. The effect comes from different fixed token values: all 1,341 paired regions fixed the same 75 coordinate locations and left four free. Alternative negative views changed when exclusion finished in 652 regions, but never added a final restriction beyond the uncertainty limit. This narrows the demonstrated contribution to the selected exemplar representation under the observed masks. Eleven alternative-view pairs still decoded to the same molecule, so token differences alone would have overstated the effect.

More novel support did not establish better search. Only 36 of 792 accepted children from alternative exemplar views beat their source, compared with 42 of 517 from original views; these conditional groups have different molecule and task support and do not isolate a score effect. The alternatives for generated records also remove an average of 17.58 non-PAD tokens, so this experiment combines atom traversal with normalization of redundant construction tokens. Coverage is uneven: 325 generated records have no admitted alternative, including 137/290 in drd2_docking and 119/290 in sitagliptin_mpo. The paired shadows have no scores, leaving both the contribution to later optimization and reliability across seeds open.

The supplied molecular assessment still finds frequent radicals, unusual charges and reactive or strained connectivity among generated molecules, including high scorers. Exact identity verification protects the already scored bank entries; it does not make their sampled offspring chemically credible or preserve useful scaffold relationships. Useful, chemically ordinary molecular neighborhoods remain unresolved despite the demonstrated representation effect.

nodes.hypothesis: Reweight the Parent's fixed graph-operator mixture at each suggestion boundary by each operator's smoothed accepted source-improvement fraction, using one generating operator per accepted neighbor and retaining positive probability for every unchanged operator.
nodes.finding:
The allocation change reached the evaluated search: 2,250 operator draws differed from the fixed mixture on the same random state, producing 1,594 accepted neighbors and 181 selected next states. All 435 batch allocations and 4,200 consumed feedback records matched the prescribed credit rule; first batches and all original graph, identity, winner and tabu rules were preserved. On each actual credit state, weighting raised the expected smoothed historical success fraction from an average 0.193425 to 0.231490. Accepted strict source improvements increased from 462 to 471 out of 4,350 neighbors, but their mean size fell from 0.024939 to 0.021552. Archive-improvement events fell from 238 to 230, and generation needed 5,537 attempts instead of 5,285. All sessions completed. The three-seed mean final score fell from 0.520918 to 0.498734, a paired loss of 0.022184 against the required gain of 0.002. Seed deltas were +0.020623, -0.027981 and -0.059192. Zaleplon improved by 0.014340 in mean score; decoration hopping, DRD2, median similarity and sitagliptin fell by 0.000898, 0.014919, 0.001324 and 0.108118 respectively.

Unique credit to a fixed edit operator did not remove the failure seen in the earlier breeding-parent experiment: historical success weighting increased progress-event frequency while reducing average gains and final archive value. The effect is especially clear for sitagliptin, where source improvements rose from 109 to 116 while their mean size fell from 0.044884 to 0.029538 and all three final scores declined. Credit conditions on accepted outputs also leave generation costs invisible: bond changes consumed 630 invalid attempts, and overall emission yield fell from 82.31% to 78.56%. Historical counts pool changing source graphs and tabu admission states, so their enrichment is an allocation result rather than a calibrated prediction of future improvement. Distinguishing improvement magnitude, archive progress and generation yield is now a concrete next question; this experiment does not establish which would fix the loss. The molecular assessment still finds sulfur-rich cages, reactive attachments and unresolved stereochemistry. Those persistent liabilities explain why more local-score successes cannot be read as better chemical feasibility.

nodes.hypothesis: Replace only full-pool batch allocation with distinct-support finite-pool DPP-TS: initialize with the inherited masked correlated Thompson batch, form L=I+(F F^T)/(0.05^2) from its actual standardized jittered Cholesky factor F, and execute exactly 20B uniform-position Metropolis proposals from fresh unmasked full-pool correlated posterior maximizers, taking duplicate self transitions and accepting other replacements by the determinant ratio while preserving slot order.
nodes.finding:
All 435 finite chains completed their 200 attempts, and every transition reconstructed. On the same actual candidate pools, average count similarity fell from 0.6660 to 0.5798 and modeled batch log determinant rose from 39.2105 to 41.8934. The effect was aggregate: 83 batches became more similar and 53 finished with a lower determinant. Predicted mean enrichment fell from 0.9888 to 0.7287 pool standard deviations while latent uncertainty rose. Original predictions stayed identical on every emitted identity. More parent-beating cores appeared and entered later breeding, but absolute offspring scores fell from the Parent’s 0.3720 to 0.3353, and total sequential incumbent gain fell from 5.8194 to 5.2470. The complete fifteen-cell endpoint mean was 0.558294 versus 0.596453, a change of −0.038159; all three seed means fell and twelve endpoints lost. The Parent’s late deco_hop breakthrough stays in this primary result. The descriptive other-fourteen-cell mean change is also negative, −0.023254.

The determinant acceptance rule measurably adds separation beyond simply refreshing posterior-maximizer proposals. Replaying the same saved proposals while accepting every valid replacement gives count similarity 0.6540, log determinant 39.6516 and mean enrichment 0.9552, compared with the actual sampler’s 0.5798, 41.8934 and 0.7287. That is a local geometry and predicted-quality tradeoff; those passive alternatives have no observed labels or descendants. Broader productive cores did not supply larger total progress: newly productive typed-core descendants had more incumbent advances but less cumulative gain, while the corresponding generic-core cohort improved, so reuse is mixed rather than absent. The chemistry assessment also finds low-scoring tiny fragments and questionable closures alongside useful aromatic, carbonyl and amine context; fingerprint separation does not establish better functional relationships or feasibility. This fixed recipe activates its intended diversification but fails the performance hypothesis and ends without parameter rescue. Mixing error, true information gain, regret and the chemical or ancestry mediator of the endpoint loss remain unmeasured; this result does not settle other allocation methods or the retained foundation’s contribution.

nodes.hypothesis: Move persistent particles through a frozen deterministic SELFIES VAE latent space using inertia plus independent stochastic attractions toward their own best observed position and the swarm best observed position, and attach accepted molecular scores to the exact generating positions before updating those task-local memories.
nodes.finding:
The two additional seeds reproduced the intended persistent motion, accepted-score memories and information transfer. All 2,932 motion equations and state transitions were verified, including 2,732 reuses of persistent velocity. Cognitive attraction was nonzero in all 1,896 eligible distinct-position opportunities, social attraction in all 2,801 eligible opportunities, and real shared memories influenced other particles 2,700 times. Accepted proposals established 200 personal bests and strictly improved them 658 times; every updated personal memory with a later opportunity was reused. All 2,900 proposals were accepted with no evaluator invalids or duplicates, and every generating position matched its runtime repeated decode. Mean final-best scores were 0.450789 in the original seed, 0.358719 in the first new seed and 0.288163 in the second. The three-seed mean is 0.365890 with a population standard deviation of 0.066585. Most of the variation comes from drd2_docking, whose final scores fell from 0.859171 to 0.476176 and 0.124923. The three-seed means for the other objectives are 0.345495 for zaleplon_mpo, 0.569962 for deco_hop, 0.174178 for median_2 and 0.253060 for sitagliptin_mpo. The decoder learned in each preparation: new-seed heldout reconstruction losses fell from 4.565228 to 0.629885 and from 4.534641 to 0.633075. Exact heldout molecular reconstruction remained only 6/480 and 7/480. None of the 100 initial encoding receipts in the new runs reconstructed its original identity, so all 200 particles correctly began without scored attractors.

The lower scores do not come from omitted inertia, unused personal memory, missing information transfer or score assignment to the wrong logged latent position. The initial identity gate prevented all supplied initial scores from becoming attractors in the new seeds; shared memory was then established from the first accepted batch and used normally thereafter. That separates safe score handling from the decoder's limited ability to recover the supplied molecules. Low token loss and abundant valid outputs coexist with weak exact reconstruction and large structural changes: emitted molecules average about 0.85 Morgan distance from both their decoded source and personal best. The molecular assessment is consistent with this coarse search behavior, finding many polyenes, irregular rings and reactive polar forms, with conventional aromatic/amine arrangements unevenly represented. The loss of the stronger aromatic/basic-amine family accompanies the largest score decline, but the data do not isolate its cause. These replicas vary both the prepared representation and the stochastic search, so they do not establish that encoder quality is the sole constraint or that any swarm component improves scores. Representation quality and motion scale remain separate questions for controlled follow-up. The execution finding is specific to the evaluated CUDA runtime: all runtime repeat-decodes matched, while independent CPU replay changed the decoded identity on 16 of 2,932 new motion attempts. Cross-backend decoder identity is therefore not established.

nodes.hypothesis: Restrict atom-replacement targets to atoms outside existing carbonyl C=O pairs, preserving both carbonyl atoms and their double bond in that operator.
nodes.finding:
All 12,104 successful replacements on carbonyl-bearing sources preserved every original C=O pair. The protected substitutions reached 11,191 pool descendants and 718 actual evaluated descendants. Among products made by a single replacement, carbonyl loss fell from 751 of 7,016 Parent pool products and sixty of 589 Parent emissions to zero of 7,100 pool products and zero of 526 emissions. This did not preserve the whole functional group: 93 evaluated descendants contain replacements that changed an original carbonyl’s neighboring atom class, including 41 that lost an adjacent nitrogen. Across the full emitted stream, acyl-halide-bearing molecules increased from seventeen to 272. All fifteen task/seed runs completed with 4,350 valid novel submitted offspring and no evaluator invalid or duplicate attempts. Mean final score fell from 0.544374 to 0.509621, a paired change of -0.034753. The seed changes were -0.089860, -0.027023 and +0.012624. The mean DRD2 change was -0.146641, while median_2 improved by 0.009198.

The intervention closes the intended destructive replacement channel, but that channel is not sufficient to explain useful graph evolution. Existing carbonyl atoms and their double bond can survive while adjacent amide-like or ester-like connections change, and subsequent operators still remove some carbonyls. Indeed, thirty-six protected replacements introduced an acyl-halide connection by changing an unprotected neighboring atom, and five of those paths reached evaluation. The sole all-protected case correctly retried through another operator rather than substituting a protected endpoint. The Parent also had five source-beating carbonyl-loss emissions, so motif removal was not uniformly harmful. The negative score result therefore narrows the useful question to which complete functional relationships deserve preservation, rather than carbonyl retention alone. The supplied chemistry reinforces that limit: useful aryl amine and indole-carbonyl families coexist with strained aromatic bridges, oversized repeated assemblies and reactive halogen or peroxide connections, with no specified stereochemistry. In particular, the large seed-0 DRD2 decline accompanies bulkier hydroperoxide-containing chemistry; the experiment does not isolate one structural cause of that decline. The inherited representation issue also reached one evaluated pure-crossover product, outside the replacement channel. Neither unchosen sites nor unselected pool molecules have counterfactual scores, so the observed subgroups cannot establish that allowing a particular omitted replacement would have improved the endpoint.

nodes.hypothesis: Allocate the announced batch by greedy maximization of a shared Monte Carlo estimate of the posterior expected maximum over the selected pool members, so each added molecule is valued by its incremental contribution to the batch's predicted best outcome.
nodes.finding:
The batch objective changed the selected set in 434 of 435 batches when compared with the Parent rule on the same candidate pools and posterior draws. Among 3,765 later positions with a distinct positive-gain winner, 3,440 choices differed from the corresponding raw-draw winner under the same mask. Every emitted choice matched the registered acquisition. The internal estimate of the batch maximum rose by 0.00597 on average against the Parent comparator: 418 batches improved, 17 tied and none declined. The finite panel still saturated: 150 later positions across 45 batches had exactly zero gain and followed the declared index tie rule.

On the actual scored searches, strict improvements over the best generating parent rose from 624 to 688 out of 4,350 offspring, and incumbent improvements rose from 241 to 298. Yet the average accepted batch-best score fell from 0.48731 to 0.46096. The three-seed final macro mean was 0.57398 versus 0.57434 for the Parent, a change of -0.00036, below the required +0.002 improvement. One seed improved and two fell; seven of fifteen task/seed endpoints improved. Mean endpoints rose for sitagliptin and median similarity, while decoration hopping, DRD2 and zaleplon declined. Every session completed with valid, novel emissions and no numerical fallback.

Selected-stream prediction MSE fell from 0.01127 to 0.00980, while mean within-batch rank correlation fell from 0.550 to 0.515. Nominal 95% latent intervals covered only 77.6% of outcomes, versus 76.9% for the Parent. On identical Child pools, the changed rule selected slightly more uncertainty than the Parent rule, but average conditional correlation increased slightly and distinct molecular cores fell from 7.17 to 7.06 per batch.

The missing batch-set objective was a real decision difference, but correcting it did not supply the registered final-score benefit. This rules out lack of allocation opportunities or a nonexecuting selector as explanations for the result. It also shows why more parent-beating offspring and more incumbent updates are insufficient evidence of stronger final solutions: they can be more frequent increments along a weaker search history. Here the absolute batch-best scores declined even as those counts rose.

The higher internal objective describes the same finite posterior panel used to choose the batch. It does not reveal the real scores of the unevaluated alternatives. The posterior model itself is unchanged; the lower prediction MSE reflects a changed selected stream and feedback history, and does not establish repaired uncertainty. Coverage remains especially poor on sitagliptin, at 37.4%. Model error, limited tail sampling and the objective’s focus on the next batch rather than future breeding remain plausible limits. Those explanations need separate evidence; the current paired panel does not identify their individual contributions. Greedy maximization is also approximate: on the Parent’s original ten-path panels, its existing batches already captured every path maximum and a passive greedy replacement sometimes lost internal utility.

The molecular assessment finds recognizable ring-rich families alongside recurrent reactive heteroatom bonds, unusual ring closures and unassigned stereochemistry. The slightly narrower core coverage and higher same-pool correlation show that batch-best complementarity need not mean broader or cleaner chemistry. Valid graphs and higher posterior batch utility therefore leave chemical feasibility unresolved. The supported finding is successful allocation activation with no demonstrated final-score gain on these three seeds; transfer to different posterior quality, chemical families or batch sizes remains open.

nodes.hypothesis: At each real suggestion boundary, reweight the unchanged mutation-operator mixture by smoothed bounded gain-magnitude credit from exactly joined earlier accepted ordinary single-call offspring, freezing positive weights throughout that suggestion and preserving every inherited generation route.
nodes.finding:
The credit and allocation mechanism executed as registered. Of 2,567 eligible accepted one-call outputs, 2,473 were consumed at a later real suggestion; 94 terminal outputs remained unused for allocation. Failed internal retries did not become extra credit trials, and composite outcomes remained uncredited raw observations. All 435 frozen weight calculations and 83,314 recorded primitive choices passed independent checks. The first fifteen suggestions matched the Parent, while all 420 later laws changed. Fixed-weight replay on the same recorded random states changed 36,657 primitive choices. These reached 1,700 accepted descendants; 917 later served as parents and 400 remained in final populations.

Within the eligible cohort, source wins rose from 403 to 452 and mean positive gain rose from 0.023041 to 0.025333. Positive gain per eligible observation also rose, from 0.003661 to 0.004461. Yet mean absolute offspring score fell from 0.404728 to 0.374110, and eligible incumbent advances fell from 164 to 147. Across the whole search, wins rose from 629 to 708 while mean positive-win size slipped from 0.024527 to 0.024071 and incumbent advances fell from 258 to 243.

All fifteen task runs completed. Mean final score fell from 0.595670 to 0.566674, a paired change of -0.028996 against the required +0.002. Seed changes were -0.086822, +0.053583 and -0.053749; nine of fifteen task-seed endpoints declined and six improved. Seed population SD rose from 0.026593 to 0.033955. Every pool and announced batch completed, although primitive validity decreased and one call exhausted its twelve internal attempts.

Magnitude-sensitive allocation improved the selected simple-source gain measurements without preserving stronger search progress. This narrows the motivating frequency-versus-size question: the eligible gain-size prediction succeeded, but it did not protect absolute candidate quality, incumbent advances or endpoints. Sources and archive scales were also lower, and the GP selected which outcomes could teach the weights. The result therefore supports a negative contribution from this particular added allocation rule under the tested composition; it does not establish that magnitude credit is worse than binary credit or that any primitive is causally ineffective.

The learned rule also affected failed inner trials, ordinary continuation and crossover finishing, none of which supplies its own credit. A successful one-call output after inner retries can still train its uniquely successful operator. Historical reward enrichment in those choices is an allocation result, not evidence that credit transfers as future efficacy. Rare operators retain optimistic smoothing, and invalid attempts remain invisible to the accepted-only reward. The preserved continuation and crossover channels, as well as terminal survivors, continue to produce useful outcomes outside consumed credit.

The chemical assessment still finds useful compact amines, lactams and aromatic alternatives alongside large repeated assemblies, unusual peripheral bonds, difficult rings and unspecified stereochemistry. A positive source gain or retained descendant can preserve those liabilities. Neither the credit labels nor lineage counts isolate a chemical explanation for the endpoint loss. The experiment supplies an exposed complete score failure under the registered review condition; changing provenance, suppressing composite routes or retuning the reward would be a new intervention.

nodes.hypothesis: Modify only the ordinary single-parent requested mutation-call law at saturation floor one from rng.choices([1, 2, 3], [0.82, 0.15, 0.03]) to rng.choices([1, 2, 3], [0.64, 0.30, 0.06]), using exactly one active length draw in its inherited position. This raises nominal optional-call probability from 0.18 to 0.36 and nominal requested mean from 1.21 to 1.42. When min(6, 1 + member_attempts // 80) exceeds one, retain the original [0.82, 0.15, 0.03] draw and original max(base_length, floor) schedule. Preserve internal mutate retries, break on failed call, original scored generating-parent references, final-only admission and every other generator and posterior rule.
nodes.finding:
All fifteen sessions expose the changed ordinary schedule. There are 8,618 saved draws requesting one extra call, and every extra call succeeds. Successful optional calls per ordinary attempt rise from 0.2097 to 0.4168. Two- or three-call pool finals increase from 7,392 to 14,479, and evaluated ordinary multi-call finals from 310 of 2,860 to 669 of 2,888. The naturally affected cohort delivers 390 evaluated finals; 73 become actual parents of 308 later accepted offspring. These are observed products and descendants, while alternate or intermediate products remain unscored.

Positive gain over the original best generating parent per accepted ordinary product rises slightly, from 0.003979 to 0.004138. Ordinary offspring mean score nevertheless falls from 0.3859 to 0.3476, their best-source mean from 0.4515 to 0.4119, and strict parent beats from 448 to 442. Across all offspring, positive parent-gain mass falls from 17.25 to 15.55 and sequential incumbent-gain mass from 5.819 to 5.235. Productive new typed/generic cores among multi-call finals increase from 28/19 to 61/39. Thus more real longer paths and more productive cores coexist with weaker overall search trajectories.

The complete matched mean falls from 0.596453 to 0.557498, a change of -0.038955 against the required +0.002. Seed macro changes are -0.083591, -0.017451 and -0.015823; 12 of 15 endpoints decrease. Macro population standard deviation decreases from 0.033970 to 0.008909, which does not satisfy the gain claim. The Parent late breakthrough remains in the primary panel; even the separately reported fourteen-cell sensitivity loses 0.024008. Ordinary activation is confirmed and the endpoint-gain falsifier is triggered. Higher-floor rejection escalation receives zero natural exposure.

Keeping occasional continuation and increasing its frequency require different contribution claims. The earlier complete removal control lost endpoint score, while this fixed upward change also loses against the same Parent. Together they narrow the question: useful continuation presence does not establish that more continuation improves this search, and neither contrast locates an optimum or supports a schedule sweep. The longer-path channel clearly reaches labeled products, productive cores and real recursive ancestry, so the endpoint loss cannot be dismissed as failure to expose it. Its small pooled parent-relative gain increase also does not explain endpoint quality: gain rates decrease in eight of fifteen sessions and in the early and late phases, and absolute source and offspring quality are lower. One exposed session supplies fourteen affected finals and a real breeding draw but no accepted descendant; recursive delivery is conditional, not universal.

The chemistry assessment likewise finds broader core coverage without consistently credible alternatives: nitrogen-halogen observations increase from 786 to 1,398, and perceived cyclic cumulated-carbon observations from 6 to 159. Reactive substitution, difficult ring geometry and unresolved stereochemistry remain alongside recognizable amides and amines. These concurrent chemical differences describe the produced graphs; they do not establish which extra call, scaffold or adaptive-history change caused the score loss. The evidence supports a negative incremental contribution of this upward probability variant under the frozen panel, while preserving the earlier positive presence finding. Higher-floor escalation, unlabeled alternate products, component mediation and the catalog’s separate attribution and publication gaps remain open.

nodes.hypothesis: Remove access to nonincumbent first-parent sources by executing the original quantile-group and member draws passively in their original order for every first-parent request, then using the current population[0] accepted record as the actual first parent, while retaining the complete ordinary live population and original score-quantile crossover-partner law with exclusion of that actual first identity.
nodes.finding:
Mean final Top-1 fell from 0.595670 to 0.539853, a paired change of -0.055816 across the three Search seeds. Ten of fifteen task/seed endpoints fell and five rose; seed mean changes were -0.106272, +0.009419 and -0.070597. The restriction executed on every first-parent call: 80,056 of 90,891 passive draws changed identity, and 3,829 accepted products came from those changed draws. Population survival, the original excluded-partner rule, learning and all 435 full proposal pools remained intact. Incumbent improvements increased from 258 to 287, but their mean positive size fell from 0.022510 to 0.017319 and their summed gain fell from 5.807663 to 4.970416. Mean accepted offspring score fell from 0.385256 to 0.334168. The changed products did reach later breeding: 2,037 were used again and 823 produced an accepted immediate descendant; products admitted at the end or superseded within a feedback batch were counted separately as censored.

Access to alternative first sources has positive conditional value under this exact graph-search composition and evaluation profile. Choosing the best current score at every first-parent call raised source quality on each actual state, yet the resulting search histories had lower absolute generating-parent and offspring scores and smaller incumbent gains. More improvement events, continued partner diversity and extensive descendant reach therefore do not establish better endpoint search. The effect is uneven: all three median_2 endpoints improved slightly, while the largest losses were in two sitagliptin seeds and one deco_hop seed. The molecular assessment likewise found distinct leading families and a strongly enlarged series in one seed, rather than a universal loss of chemical variety; that enlarged series slightly improved its matched endpoint. Reactive local bonds, difficult ring connections and unspecified stereochemistry remain in the output, but these observations do not identify the chemical cause of the mean loss. The result answers only the conditional value of permitting nonincumbent first sources, including its changes to source probabilities, partner exclusions, graph randomness and feedback. It does not establish the contribution of the entire evolutionary foundation, separate mutation from crossover first-source effects, or combine this intervention with the partner-exclusion sibling.

nodes.hypothesis: Refine each rooted radius-one motif with binary cycle membership of its root-to-neighbor bonds, so signed occurrence counts and inverse tabu restrictions distinguish cyclic from acyclic instances of an otherwise identical local environment.
nodes.finding:
The observed graphs contained 834 old motif families with multiple cycle contexts, and those distinctions reached live restrictions and scored proposals. A separate unannotated memory replay on the same sources and accepted history shows that 19 evaluated molecules were newly admitted and one evaluated molecule replaced a newly vetoed ring opening, changing 20 of 435 actual batches. Only one of these 20 molecules improved its source, by 0.001295; 19 worsened it and none tied. None immediately improved the best archive. One worsening ring closure became the next walk state, but its 20 later evaluated descendants added no archive gain. The three-seed mean final score fell from 0.521759 to 0.476854, a paired loss of 0.044906 instead of the required gain of 0.002. All three seeds declined. DRD2 and sitagliptin accounted for the largest task losses; zaleplon improved slightly on average.

The result rules out lack of structural activation or lack of evaluated exposure as the explanation for the missing score benefit. The original labels really did pool ring and chain occurrences, and the refined labels still transferred restrictions between distinct molecules during a live memory window. That additional topological distinction alone did not improve this search. It also did more than remove vetoes: resolving opposite changes that previously canceled changed which motif families were retained in nine transitions and created one extra veto. The largely unfavorable outcomes of the newly allocated neighbors show why passive admissions cannot be treated as evidence of useful search. The full trajectories also change when a batch stops on a different draw, so the large final losses do not identify the causal score contribution of any single annotation or unscored alternative. The supplied molecular assessment still finds aromatic and carbonyl arrangements alongside reactive heteroatom bonds, unusual sulfur cages and undefined stereochemistry. Binary cycle membership does not describe ring size, geometry, strain or chemical stability; those limitations remain open after this experiment.

nodes.hypothesis: While the session's own count of consecutive non-improving announced batches is at least K=3, set the effective connected-fragment crossover probability to zero for every breeding attempt of the next announced batch. The original crossover-branch uniform draw stays at its stream position, so each such attempt takes the inherited single-parent mutation walk with its sampled one/two/three-call length, saturation floor and unchanged operators. Crossover, partner selection, fragment construction and post-crossover finishing are untouched before the first trigger and resume unchanged from the batch after the first improving batch.
nodes.finding:
The switch worked exactly as registered. Thirteen of the fifteen task sessions stalled at least once, giving 90 stalled batches in 30 episodes; the two decoration-hopping sessions that never stall reproduced the Parent molecule for molecule, and every other session matched the Parent exactly up to its first stalled batch. Inside stalled batches about 6,900 breeding attempts that would have recombined took the ordinary mutation walk instead, and not one partner draw, recombinant, finishing edit or crossover offspring appeared. Outside them crossover ran at the Parent's rate (45.6% of attempts versus 45.4%).

Stalls did not get longer. The Child spent 90 batches stalled against the Parent's 91 (30 episodes versus 29, four left unfinished in each). Of the 13 first stalls, which start from identical states, 4 lasted longer, 3 shorter and 6 the same. Yield inside stalls barely moved: incumbent gain per evaluated molecule was 0.000492 versus 0.000524 (28 improving molecules in both), and 8.3% versus 8.6% of offspring beat their best parent. What did shrink was the jump that ends a stall: in 8 of the 13 matched first stalls the breaking batch gained less than the Parent's, and the 13 breaks summed to 0.261 versus 0.390, most visibly in sitagliptin seeds 0 and 1 (about 0.033 versus 0.087 and 0.099). Recombinants also became scarcer in the breeding population: at stall ends 17% of the 64 survivors and 17% of the top ten had themselves been made by crossover, versus 26% and 28% in the Parent, and at session end only 1 of 15 best molecules came from crossover, versus 6 of 15. Founder concentration among the leaders stayed as high as in the Parent.

The matched mean fell from 0.5965 to 0.5823, a change of -0.0142, and all three seed scores fell (-0.024, -0.006, -0.013). Ten of fifteen cells fell (one by a negligible 0.00000005), three rose and two (unexposed) were identical. The loss sits mainly in zaleplon seed 0 (-0.074), sitagliptin seed 2 (-0.079), zaleplon seed 1 (-0.034) and sitagliptin seed 0 (-0.027), partly offset by zaleplon seed 2 (+0.022); dropping any single cell leaves a mean between -0.016 and -0.009. Unlike every earlier complete child of this Anchor, it keeps the Parent's late decoration-hopping breakthrough, because that session never stalls. Under the frozen rule this classifies as a positive contribution of crossover during stagnation, and the registered prediction that removal would be harmless is falsified.

Recombination is not dispensable during stalls on this Anchor, but the result does not support the stall-escape story that would most simply explain why. That story needed stalls to lengthen and stall yield to fall; stall length was unchanged and yield fell only about 6%. The theory-based alternative, that crossover stops helping once the population has lost diversity, predicted a harmless removal and is contradicted at the endpoint even though founder concentration stayed at the Parent's level. The one stall-phase difference that tracks the loss is how far a stall break reaches and how much recombinant material the population carries forward afterwards, so crossover may matter more for the size of the escape than for its timing. These are single-realization signatures, not identified causes.

The loss must also be read against departure from the Anchor's own run. Once a session first stalls its future is re-randomized, and the four cells where the Parent gained most after its first stall carry about 83% of the summed loss, exactly where the Anchor's continuation was a favourable draw. Crossover's stall contribution is therefore not separated from departure from the Anchor's realized continuation. Against a pure-departure reading, this Child lost more than each of the three same-trigger siblings, both panel-wide (their changes were -0.010, +0.008 and +0.005) and in those same cells; but the siblings are interventions in their own right, not null controls.

Together with the earlier whole-run removal (-0.044), this shows that switching recombination off costs endpoint score whether it is removed throughout or only while the search is stalled, which closes the idea that stalled batches offer free capacity by switching recombination off. The molecular assessment finds chemistry essentially identical to the Parent's, including the tiny fragments that only the recombination route wastes evaluations on (104 versus 105), so chemistry does not explain the score. This route registered one complete answer, and no threshold or probability sweep is justified. What remains open is the size of the departure effect that every stall-conditioned sibling shares: a stall-triggered change to the random stream alone, or more seeds, would measure it.

nodes.hypothesis: Extend the inherited per-site atom-replacement menu with a direct exchange of a neutral aromatic nitrogen and a hydrogen-bearing aromatic carbon in the same six-member ring, preserving molecular formula and connectivity while changing nitrogen placement.
nodes.finding:
The intended positional edit executed correctly. All 536 sampled exchanges preserved formula and connectivity; 435 changed molecular identity and 101 were symmetry identities. Changed exchanges reached 404 pool entries and 30 evaluated molecules. Twenty-nine evaluations retained the exact immediate isomer; one also changed another atom later, while retaining the exchanged nitrogen placement and aromatic ring. The 22 evaluations containing only the exchange gave five source improvements, nine ties and eight losses. One pyridyl nitrogen relocation raised an accepted score from 0.438799 to 0.460926 and established a new final task best. Across all three seeds, mean final-best score increased from 0.544374 to 0.551771, a gain of 0.007397 above the registered 0.002 threshold; population standard deviation decreased from 0.013310 to 0.008223. Two seed macros improved and one declined. Zaleplon and sitagliptin task means rose, while decoration, DRD2 and median means fell. Every task completed its budget, all pools filled, and all admitted identities and feedback joins remained consistent. Recorded total wall time rose from 2,391 to 4,705 seconds, with both greater oracle time and substantially larger diagnostic logs.

This establishes a useful local alternative under the existing pool generator and learned selector, including an observed incumbent gain, while narrowing the utility claim to particular molecular families. Pure exchanges were often neutral or harmful, and all eight evaluated descendants that also contained other edits lost to their best generating parent. Evaluated exposure was concentrated in zaleplon, decoration and median; neither DRD2 nor sitagliptin evaluated an exchange. The sitagliptin score gain therefore cannot be credited to a directly scored positional isomer, and the aggregate trajectory difference does not isolate the contribution of each swap. Three later reversals were correctly rejected as duplicates, demonstrating why operation counts alone overstate retained alternatives. Formula and connectivity preservation also leave the larger chemical limitations intact: the successful nitrogen relocation retained a reactive N-F substituent, the overall emitted stream grew in mean size, and explicit stereochemistry remained absent. The evidence supports testing nitrogen position as a local chemical variable; it does not establish broader ring-topology coverage, synthetic feasibility, or a uniformly favorable exchange neighborhood.

nodes.hypothesis: Replace the shared seven-operator mutation neighborhood by one fixed CReM-inspired radius-three, single-heavy-bond-cut context-matched fragment substitution prior: uniformly sample an eligible concrete source orientation and then a distinct compatible corpus-derived fragment, assemble it once at the witnessed source attachment, and let the unchanged count-GP graph optimizer evaluate and learn from its actual accepted descendants.
nodes.finding:
The construction mechanism operated in every session. Of 4,350 accepted offspring, 2,867 contain a changed context graft, including 2,570 with a multi-atom fragment on at least one side of the final replacement and 607 with a ring-containing incoming fragment. All 2,770 nonterminal graft products entered the next Gaussian-process fit; 2,278 were retained and 1,571 were later selected as parents. Their accepted direct-child union contains 3,056 molecules, so this was substantial exposure through the real search, not merely successful table lookup.

That exposure did not yield the predicted larger useful gains. Strict wins over the original best generating parent rise slightly, 653 versus 648, but their total positive margin falls to 15.276942 from 17.251535 and their median winning margin falls to 0.005429 from 0.007549. Sequential incumbent advances fall to 231 from 255, with total gain 5.156211 versus 5.819415. The Child also uses somewhat weaker scored parents; its less-negative average child-minus-parent margin is therefore not evidence of greater absolute progress. Positive gain mass improves in two seeds but falls overall, while incumbent progress falls in all three. The complete mean endpoint is 0.552239516 versus 0.596453114, a paired change of -0.044213598 against the required +0.002. Five of 15 endpoints improve and ten decline; all three seed macro scores decline. The Parent’s late decoration-hopping breakthrough remains fully included.

Local context support was sufficient to construct different multi-atom graphs and carry them into accepted feedback and breeding. It was insufficient to make this fixed neighborhood more productive. Typed new-core arrivals fall to 1,058 from 1,820, and fewer of those first arrivals beat their parents or the incumbent. Generic-core first-arrival incumbent wins instead rise to 79 from 71, illustrating why a favorable novelty descriptor cannot substitute for larger realized gains. Each panel has four sessions whose ten leaders trace to a single founder, and every leading set shares at least one founder across all members. Distinct seed-leading chemistries still exist, but their overlapping ancestry does not establish independent family discovery. The late search loses especially much gain mass; the result narrows the problem to generating and developing useful alternatives, rather than merely delivering larger edits.

Both borrowed CReM elements operated: the corpus-derived context/fragment relation supplied compatible alternatives, and the canonical context keys plus mapped attachment produced the recorded accepted graphs. The result applies to the declared single-cut adapter. Its physical-site enumeration and stereo handling differ from the general upstream implementation, so this neither reproduces nor refutes the full CReM family. Chemically, fewer heteroatom-halogen attachments and no observed cyclic cumulene or ring-alkyne flags coexist with persistent reactive attachments, unspecified stereochemistry, tiny fragments and oversized assemblies. Those changes do not establish whole-molecule feasibility or explain the endpoint loss causally. Prospective prediction diagnostics improve on the different acquired stream while the GP itself remains unchanged, again separating a useful proxy from optimization progress.

The registered productive-gain and endpoint falsifiers are triggered despite confirmed construction and feedback activation. This complete exposed result ends the fixed recipe. It does not isolate the contribution of corpus size, radius, cut scope or sampling, and provides no justified parameter sweep or continuation. A materially revised approach would need new failure-specific evidence and planning; the broader constructive-fragment idea remains an open question.

nodes.hypothesis: Repair accepted-feedback trace lookup by using the canonical SMILES obtained after reparsing each generated edit, so proposal bookkeeping and returned molecular structure share the same identity used by the recorded feedback.
nodes.finding:
The previously failing seed-2 feedback now reaches the correct pending proposal. The repaired walk processes all ten scores in that batch and continues to the full 300-evaluation task budget. Both added seeds complete all five tasks: 3,000 evaluations, 2,900 optimizer outcomes and 290 completed walk steps, with no invalid evaluations, duplicates or unresolved feedback. Replaying the original source still reproduces the exact identity-lookup exception, while the repaired replay matches the formal continuation.

The comparison preserves every one of the 4,310 previously recorded molecule/score entries in normalized order. All fourteen complete task logs are identical to the original runs; the failed prefix differs only in the spelling of one molecular identity, whose returned graph is unchanged. The inherited tabu behavior remains active in the two new seeds: 132 of 3,032 valid novel attempts are vetoed, while 1,577 partial inverse matches reach evaluation and supply 153 selected next states.

Macro final Top-1 is 0.518077929779343 for seed 0, 0.527798815337278 for seed 1 and 0.516876739241218 for seed 2. The complete three-seed mean is 0.5209178281192797, with population standard deviation 0.004890242222897396. The previously incomplete zaleplon task finishes at 0.41003927643747895. These are formal evaluation results; the diagnostic replay makes no oracle calls.

The new evidence closes the specific uncertainty left by the recovery run: the identity fix supports the full previously failing seed, beyond the ten batches that could be replayed earlier. Exact preservation of all available successful histories narrows the earlier interruption to proposal-to-feedback identity bookkeeping. The original executable has no completed continuation for the failed task, so this establishes operational recovery and a complete score estimate without establishing a new search advantage. The seed-0 comparison supplied with this replication is the same repaired algorithm, not a separate intervention.

The small spread in macro score also hides task variation: sitagliptin final scores range from 0.4484554129767839 to 0.5903526424693334 across the three seeds. The molecular assessment finds different ring frameworks across the added seeds but persistent reactive heteroatoms, dense cages and unspecified stereochemistry, with late trajectories concentrated within related families. Successful identity handling and stable macro performance therefore leave chemical feasibility and useful scaffold coverage unresolved.

nodes.hypothesis: A corpus-trained frozen SELFIES VAE generates de novo molecules through prior-preserving pCN MCMC whose latent target is the standard Gaussian prior multiplied by a task-local fingerprint Tanimoto GP's probability of exceeding the observed incumbent, with the same deterministic decoded molecule used for prediction and submission.
nodes.finding:
The macro mean of 0.433 places this sixth. It reached 0.868 on drd2_docking, 0.573 on deco_hop and 0.341 on zaleplon_mpo, with 0.212 on sitagliptin_mpo and 0.172 on median_2. Corpus pretraining cut held-out reconstruction loss from 4.225 to 0.161. Every session initialized a fresh Gaussian process on exactly ten scored structures and grew it in steps of ten to 290. Across the five sessions the sampler attempted 36,800 transitions and accepted 19,938, all 145 rounds had nonconstant posterior probabilities, and all 1,450 submitted molecules matched the recorded prediction identity exactly, so no molecule was ever scored that the surrogate had not itself evaluated.

The design goal is met: the surrogate genuinely steers sampling and the prediction-submission identity never breaks, which is a real integrity property that several latent methods in this round cannot claim. The acceptance rate near 54 percent indicates the chain is mixing rather than sticking. What limits it is that a fingerprint Gaussian process fitted to at most 290 points has to generalise across a space the decoder can reach, and its probability estimates flatten out where the incumbent is already high, which shows as a median score of exactly zero on the hardest objective. Whether a different kernel or an incumbent-relaxation would help is untested, on one seed.

nodes.hypothesis: Replace the original dot-product count-Tanimoto GP law on sulfur-gated Parent n-1744a1494180 by the fixed coherent K_E(x,y)=exp(T_DP(x,y)-1), lambda=1, in every active training/training, training/query and query/query Gram block, so both active predictive mean mu_E and conditional residual covariance C_E come from that same exponential GP; preserve the original correlated sampling, masks and all other mechanisms.
nodes.finding:
All 15 task/seed runs completed with 300 observations each. The exponential covariance was used in every training, cross and pool block of all 435 decision pools, and both of its outputs moved in every pool. Compared with the original law recomputed on the same archive, pool and random draws, predicted means shifted by up to 0.55 (0.016 on average, and lower on average in every pool), conditional variances shifted by up to 0.30, and every pool mean and covariance entry changed. The original law would have picked a different set of ten in 417 of 435 pools, and 1,260 of the 4,350 evaluated offspring (29%) were choices it would not have made. Those choices were systematically more local. On identical pools, the exponential law's picks sat at a mean nearest-archive distance of 0.095, versus 0.182 for the original law's picks, with lower uncertainty and slightly larger molecules (35.3 versus 32.6 heavy atoms). The 1,260 candidates it displaced were distant (0.383), small (25 heavy atoms) and uncertain.

On the molecules actually evaluated, the exponential means predicted the real labels slightly better than the original law would have on the same molecules: MSE 0.00790 versus 0.00860, pair-order accuracy 66.8% versus 66.3%, and mean batch Spearman 0.431 versus 0.420. Pair ordering was nevertheless worse on all three deco-hop seeds. Against the Parent's own run, offspring scored higher on average (0.400 versus 0.372), strict wins over the best generating parent rose from 648 to 703, wins carrying a new scaffold rose from 262 to 340, and productive descendant edges rose from 780 to 854. But the wins were smaller (mean gain over the parent 0.0187 versus 0.0266), and total incumbent progress fell from 5.82 to 5.32 summed over the 15 runs, mostly on deco-hop and sitagliptin.

The final macro score was 0.5633 against the Parent's 0.5965, a paired change of -0.0332 against the required +0.002. Seed changes were -0.081, +0.007 and -0.025. Eight of 15 task/seed endpoints improved and seven worsened, with the losses concentrated in deco-hop seed 0 (-0.236), sitagliptin seed 0 (-0.192) and sitagliptin seed 2 (-0.094). Seed-to-seed spread narrowed sharply (population SD 0.0052 versus 0.0340), but around a lower mean. Among the four current laws, the full exponential law (0.5633) sits between the residual-only hybrid (0.5667) and the mean-only hybrid (0.5382), and all three are below the original (0.5965). The descriptive four-law interaction is +0.055, positive in 10 of 15 cells. In one deco-hop seed the selected molecules grew to the 120-atom cap, and that task took 4,635 s of its 7,200 s limit.

The fixed exponential warp is now settled as an endpoint route on this Parent. The mean-only, residual-only and coherent versions all lose between 0.030 and 0.058, as the older ungated full law did, and the registered one-test rule ends this recipe. Coherence did not rescue the hybrids: it cut the mean-only hybrid's loss but landed no better than the residual-only hybrid. The positive four-law interaction is not synergy. It mostly reflects that all three exponential variants reach similar endpoints and miss the same rare Parent discoveries, for example 0.61 to 0.62 against the Parent's 0.856 on deco-hop seed 0, so their losses do not add up.

The run also shows how the warp acts on allocation. Its constant exp(-1) floor ties every candidate to the whole archive. That is consistent with what was measured: the displaced distant candidates lost predicted mean (0.071 lower than under the original law) and some uncertainty, so the law drops far, small, uncertain molecules and samples near what is already known. Its choices track the mean-only hybrid (90% shared) much more closely than the residual-only hybrid (76%), so the mean path drives most of the change. This is the opposite of the broader productive exploration the research brief asks for. The result was more and smaller local wins, a higher offspring average, and less total incumbent progress. It is also one more counterexample showing that better prediction on the selected stream does not carry through to endpoints.

Whether locality causes the loss is still open, and the evidence argues against a simple story: the Parent's largest late jump (deco-hop seed 0, +0.247) was itself a near edit, and the Child gained more than the Parent from distant moves. Locality is a measured signature here, not an identified mediator. The Molecular assessment explains part of the deco-hop gap: this node never built the fused 6-6 diazine bicycle behind the Parent's 0.856. It also identifies chemistry problems that no covariance choice touches: leaders built on N- and O-halogen artefacts, single-atom decoration only, and unbounded molecular size. Worth testing next are allocation rules that preserve or reward uncertainty about distant candidates instead of shrinking it, and generator-side changes such as balanced growth and deletion, fragment-level substitutions and ring annulation, which a kernel change cannot supply.

nodes.hypothesis: Within the inherited selected score band, sample a crossover partner with probability proportional to its accepted-molecule fingerprint Tanimoto similarity to the already selected first parent.
nodes.finding:
The intended pairing mechanism changed actual breeding. Of 34,123 partner draws, 33,350 had unequal similarities and used the registered weights; 7,967 choices (23.35%) differed from the passive uniform choice on the same eligible partners and random variate. On nondegenerate states, expected Tanimoto similarity rose from 0.48313 under uniform selection to 0.51979 under the applied law. Actual mean pair similarity rose from the Parent's 0.48309 to 0.51650. The first-parent rule, greedy survival, graph operators and posterior selection remained unchanged. Both runs evaluated 1,679 crossover and 2,671 mutation offspring. Crossover best-parent beats rose from 172 to 176 and sequential incumbent improvements from 75 to 84. Its mean parent-relative deficit narrowed from -0.15687 to -0.13737, but the mean best generating-parent score also fell from 0.43361 to 0.40325, and absolute crossover-offspring score fell from 0.27674 to 0.26587. Raw invalid crossover attempts increased from 123 to 326. Mutation incumbent improvements fell from 143 to 130, leaving fewer total improvements (214 versus 218). The three-seed macro mean fell from 0.54437 to 0.52840, a paired change of -0.01597; seed changes were -0.00054, -0.06139 and +0.01401. All five task means declined, with the largest mean loss on sitagliptin (-0.06334). Every formal task still completed its full evaluation budget.

The experiment separates selecting related molecules from obtaining more productive chemistry. Similarity enrichment and changed pairings are established, but the smaller parent-relative deficit partly accompanies a weaker reference parent and does not demonstrate stronger absolute offspring. Crossover contributed more local incumbent gains while the inherited mutation stream contributed fewer; mutation is not an unaffected control because new pairings change the accepted population and subsequent random trajectory. Much of the final-score loss came from the second seed's sitagliptin run, so this panel supports negative mean transfer rather than a universal failure of related-parent crossover. Fingerprint relatedness also did not preserve a common core more often: the share of evaluated crossover offspring reusing a generating parent's core fell from 34.25% to 33.00%, while survivor core coverage broadened. The molecular assessment still found repeated large assemblies, reactive halogen connections and strained rings; larger repeated products often offered little score separation from smaller relatives. Thus shared fingerprint features alone did not ensure that the unchanged fragment crossover preserved useful attachment relationships or chemical scale. The conditional-law comparison establishes allocation, but supplies no score for an unchosen partner and no causal attribution for either member of a pair.

nodes.hypothesis: Install and refresh inverse-motif restrictions only when the selected actually accepted neighbor has a strictly higher score than its recorded source; tied and worsening selected transitions still move and age the walk but receive no new memory credit.
nodes.finding:
All 184 tied or worsening selected moves skipped memory installation, omitting 719 attributes while retaining 984 attributes from improving moves. On the Child's recorded history, unconditional credit would veto 188 novel draws; the actual gate vetoed 115. This admitted 74 candidates across all fifteen task sessions, while preserved older provenance caused one additional veto in the opposite direction. Twenty newly admitted candidates became next states. Fourteen improved their source score, thirteen tied and forty-seven worsened it; only two immediately improved the archive. The three-seed macro mean fell from 0.521759 to 0.501486, a paired change of -0.020273, against the registered requirement of +0.002. Two seeds declined and one improved. Task means improved for zaleplon and median_2, but declined for deco_hop, DRD2 and sitagliptin, with the largest loss in DRD2. All runs completed their full budgets and batches.

The experiment establishes that protecting nonimproving moves can block useful fresh variations: newly admitted methyl removal and aryl-fluorine removal both produced immediate archive gains. It also rules out an unexercised gate, missing feedback or changed restriction tenure as explanations for the negative panel result. Those useful cases were sparse, and overall source-improvement frequency and positive-gain magnitude fell. The archive improved slightly more often, but its total improvement was smaller. This narrows the question to the search value of the restrictions: withholding credit based on one move's local gain does not reliably identify protection that is expendable on this panel. Whether protecting nonimproving moves helps diversification remains unresolved because the passive comparison cannot reproduce an alternative walk or score excluded candidates. Preserved overlap provenance matters in practice: an older improving pair survived a skipped refresh and blocked a candidate that unconditional credit would admit. Thus the gate does not create a universal admissibility superset. The supplied molecular assessment still finds reactive heteroatom bonds, unusual sulfur connections and dense ring systems alongside recognizable aromatic/carbonyl and amine families; the changed allocation supplies no evidence that chemical feasibility improved.

nodes.hypothesis: Replace the inherited score-quantile preference with uniform draws over every eligible member of the current live score-greedy survivor population, retaining the original band construction and band-choice draw passively, the existing member-choice call and partner-exclusion fallback, recursive accepted-offspring breeding, and active accepted-label count-GP allocation.
nodes.finding:
All 106,858 Child breeding draws followed the uniform law over eligible current survivors, including partner exclusion. 53,199 draws used ranks that the inherited score bands could never choose, and 92,549 lay outside the passively drawn band. Mean selected topness was 0.500066, close to the exclusion-conditioned uniform expectation of 0.499988, versus 0.884073 under the original law on those same states. Accepted offspring continued to enter survivors and breed: 3,254 distinct offspring were later used, versus 2,401 for the Parent. All 435 accepted-label count-GP fits and full candidate pools remained active on each side.

Mean final Top-1 fell from 0.595670 to 0.549672, a paired change of -0.045998, exceeding the registered 0.002 loss scale. Seed macro changes were -0.063415, -0.038977 and -0.035602. Thirteen of fifteen task-seed endpoints and all five task means declined. The two exceptions were zaleplon seed 0 (+0.010604) and seed 2 (+0.020822); its seed 1 lost 0.059613. Seed-macro population deviation fell from 0.026593 to 0.019687. All three replicas completed without fallback or missing endpoints.

This establishes positive conditional contribution of the inherited score-quantile preference while recursive feedback, greedy survival and the predictive selector remain active. It does not separate the value of restricting support from the value of weighting supported ranks. It also does not repeat the earlier fixed-initial-parent experiment or settle the value of the whole graph-evolution foundation.

The contrast separates participation from productive progress. Previously unsupported parents contributed to 1,427 evaluated offspring, of which 928 later bred. Yet strict generating-parent beats increased from 629 to 1,055 against weaker sources, while sequential incumbent gains fell from 258 to 203. Predictions also had lower error and higher within-batch ordering correlation on the changed evaluated distribution, despite worse endpoints. None of these selected associations establishes a causal mediator or a transferable surrogate-quality gain.

The molecular assessment finds recognizable biaryl amines and useful aromatic/carbonyl combinations alongside inherited reactive bonds, crowded rings and unspecified stereochemistry. The halogen-free carboxamide improvement and a strong carbon-bound-fluorine leader prevent treating unusual bonds or blanket chemical exclusions as the explanation. Broader parent participation therefore did not resolve chemical feasibility or ensure better endpoint search. Terminal admissions and unselected alternatives provide no unobserved descendant outcomes.

nodes.hypothesis: Add the exact archived mean-fantasy within-batch residual projection to the exchange-disabled Parent: condition future sampled residual rows on each earlier selected molecule taking its unchanged posterior mean, using the original jittered sampling covariance and zero innovations only for batch allocation.
nodes.finding:
All 3,915 projections executed correctly and preserved every first choice. They changed 657 later positions and 295 of 435 batch sets, replacing 493 selected memberships. Later selected sampling variance fell by 3.28% on average. These choices entered real feedback: all 482 nonterminal newly selected molecules entered later fits, and 296 of the 493 new selections later bred. Yet the final mean fell from 0.595670 to 0.553927, a paired loss of 0.041742 against the required gain of 0.002. All three seed macros fell; six task/seed endpoints improved and nine declined. Strict parent wins rose from 629 to 642, while absolute offspring mean fell from 0.385256 to 0.359834 and total incumbent improvement fell from 5.807663 to 5.181529. Downstream opportunity also had limits: three newly selected nonterminal molecules had positive breeding support but were never drawn; four task/seed cohorts of new selections produced no positive direct-descendant incumbent increment, while terminal selections had no later opportunity. The molecular assessment still finds chemically varied aromatic and heterocyclic outputs, alongside reactive halogen bonds, difficult ring geometry and unspecified stereochemistry. Those liabilities and inconsistent useful family coverage remain relevant gaps, but these data do not identify chemical mediation, an exchange interaction or the contribution of the retained graph-evolution foundation.

nodes.hypothesis: One posterior-component replacement on n-cf8d309c06de: use a zero-mean, unit-amplitude count-Tanimoto GP latent utility with likelihood product_e Phi(f_w(e)-f_l(e)) over sparse chronological local comparisons. At each inherited refit, retain all canonical accepted records in serial order; for each i>0 choose j<i maximizing the original count-kernel similarity, with earliest accepted serial breaking exact similarity ties. Choose j without scores, orient the one edge by exact raw-score order, and omit it if the two raw scores are exactly tied, without searching for another predecessor. Each pair has a unique later endpoint, at most N-1 edges are stored, and no transitive or repeated likelihood factors are manufactured. The individual preference-noise SD is 1/sqrt(2), so the pairwise probit argument has denominator1. Score magnitudes do not enter this active likelihood. With K+jI=LL^T from the inherited prior jitter ladder, f=L u and A=D L (D has +1 at the winner and -1 at the loser), minimize J(u)=0.5*u^T*u-sum(log Phi(Au)). From deterministic u=0, bounded damped Newton uses the exact gradient and Hessian; only a converged MAP may supply a fitted posterior. Let z=A u, r=phi(z)/Phi(z), W=diag(r*(r+z)), and H=I+A^T W A at MAP. The latent posterior covariance is L H^-1 L^T. For a fresh pool let V=L^-1 K_train,pool; the full predictive mean is V^T u and covariance is K_pool,pool-V^T V+V^T H^-1 V. This retains all cross-candidate terms; neither a diagonal approximation nor the regression noise0.05 enters the active likelihood. Zero non-tied edges produce the explicitly reported zero-mean GP prior. Distinct canonical records with identical count features remain distinct training records and labels. The resulting latent utility distribution, with an optional shared positive raw-location/scale interface wrapper fixed below, feeds the unchanged correlated sampled-row maxima, exact pool-order ties and K=3/M=40 eligibility law. Real raw scores alone continue to govern breeding, survival and stall state. Local ordering can therefore change paid identities and subsequent learning without changing generator support or introducing another acquisition objective; the asserted benefit remains empirical.
nodes.finding:
All 435 preference fits converged, and every purchased batch changed relative to the passive raw-score GP on the same candidate pool. The model bought 3489 identities that its passive comparator would not have selected. On the 19559 non-tied pairs actually purchased, ordering accuracy was 63.79% versus 73.66%; every task/seed cell was worse. Full incumbent gain fell from 5.97807 to 4.45749, triggering both parts of the registered scientific falsifier despite successful execution and feedback. Late gain rose from 1.02241 to 1.69888, but did not recover the full-path loss. The complete endpoint mean fell from 0.60703 to 0.50566 (−0.10137): all three seed averages and all five task means were lower, with 13 of 15 individual endpoints lower. Population seed dispersion rose from 0.03018 to 0.05818. There were no missing tasks, numerical failures, invalid purchases or missing passive predictions.

This settles the specified sparse local probit/Laplace intervention: it runs correctly and changes consequential choices, yet supplies weaker ordering on its own purchased labels and less total useful progress. The borrowed GP-preference and Laplace elements operated; the local edge rule, fixed count prior, unit comparison scale and retained sampled allocator are adaptations, so the result does not generalize to all preference learning or the cited library’s defaults. More parent-beating offspring (762 versus 634) were produced against weaker realized generating parents, which explains why that diagnostic cannot rescue the endpoint loss. The method’s measured limitation is an inferior ranking model on both restricted and unrestricted purchased streams. A different observation/comparison model would be needed to address that limitation; this experiment does not isolate whether sparse edges, discarded score magnitudes or their covariance are responsible. Chemistry shows broader scaffold coverage (1994 typed scaffolds versus 1667) and lower fragment-excluded similarity, alongside 176 molecules above fifty heavy atoms versus 44 and unresolved stereochemistry/reactive connectivity. Thus lack of structural variety is not the demonstrated bottleneck; coherent growth and functional-group-aware proposal operators are a separate capability suggested by the observed oversized assemblies, not a proven cure. The passive comparator supplies no unpurchased rewards or alternative adaptive path, and full gain telescopes to the endpoints. The isolated contribution of each posterior ingredient, alias/zero-edge behavior in real sessions, and whether another comparison model would help remain open.

nodes.hypothesis: Extend the existing change_atom neighborhood with a direct two-site exchange of a neutral aromatic nitrogen and a hydrogen-bearing aromatic carbon in the same six-member ring, producing formula-preserving nitrogen positional isomers without an evaluated single-substitution intermediate.
nodes.finding:
Ten fresh formula-preserving nitrogen positional isomers reached evaluation from thirteen sampled exchanges. All ten changed local signed motifs; three improved their source score and seven worsened it, with no ties. Three became subsequent walk states and one immediately improved the best archive. Every sampled exchange preserved atom count, bonds, molecular formula and qualifying-ring aromaticity. The three-seed macro mean rose from 0.520918 to 0.521759, a paired gain of 0.000841, below the required 0.002. One seed improved, one declined slightly and one was unchanged. The largest task change was deco_hop in the improving seed; DRD2 and sitagliptin endpoints were unchanged in all seeds.

The neighborhood extension is demonstrably usable: the ten evaluated products cannot be reached by any single legacy element substitution from their recorded sources. Unlike the earlier configuration-only experiment, nitrogen relocation changes both the motifs seen by tabu memory and the measured source scores. This rules out identity-only or score-invisible activation as the explanation for the limited panel benefit. Exposure is sparse and local outcomes are mixed: only ten of 4350 evaluated neighbors are exchanges, and most lose to their source. One selected deco_hop exchange leads into later archive improvements, but the whole walk and its random draws also change, so those later gains cannot be assigned to nitrogen placement alone. The evidence supports positional-isomer accessibility and score sensitivity, while the preregistered overall score benefit is refuted for this panel. The molecular assessment still finds the Parent-like aromatic/carbonyl families alongside reactive heteroatom bonds, unusual sulfur and dense cages; formula conservation by itself has not established better medicinal or synthetic quality.

nodes.hypothesis: Within each existing direct-policy sampling call, admit at most the first valid canonically novel molecule for each successfully extracted nonempty atom/bond-typed nonisomeric Murcko scaffold, resetting the scaffold allowance at the next refill call and leaving acyclic or extraction-fallback identities under inherited admission.
nodes.finding:
The admission mechanism executed correctly in all 497 sampling calls. It rejected 459 otherwise novel repeat-core draws before capacity and produced no repeated ring core within a call; the parent emitted 460 such repetitions. Against equal-sized choices from the same actual draws, 154 calls gained a total of 264 family slots: 259 ring-core appearances and five acyclic singleton appearances. Every added family reached evaluation, and six of those molecules improved the incumbent. Across complete runs, distinct evaluated ring cores increased from 2,813 to 3,079, while the largest occupancy of one core in a session fell from 160 molecules to 44. Total strict incumbent improvements nevertheless fell from 149 to 120.

The three-seed mean final score decreased from 0.522705 to 0.508379, a paired change of −0.014326 against the required +0.002 benefit. Seed changes were +0.002392, −0.018880 and −0.026492. All five task means declined, although the DRD2 endpoint difference was only about two millionths near the score ceiling. Recorded mean AUC increased from 0.405593 to 0.427858; about 94% of that aggregate increase came from DRD2, mainly its much earlier progress in seed 2. All fifteen sessions completed their budgets. Batches needing refills increased from 16 to 33, and measured generation time increased from 24.75 to 37.02 seconds. The utility falsifier is triggered; the verified admission mechanism remains confirmed.

This resolves the earlier uncertainty about whether protected alternatives ever reach useful downstream opportunities. Here, all 264 locally added families were scored, and 111 of their molecules entered fitting, making 212 training appearances, including 101 historical replay appearances. Direct admission therefore carried diversification through evaluation and learning. That propagation was insufficient for a final-score benefit. The 337 calls without a quota opportunity reproduced their local no-quota choices exactly, and paired behavior agreed through the first intervention in every session, narrowing the change to admission and the subsequent feedback it altered.

The result supports a tradeoff between early progress and later refinement. The parent obtained fifteen actual incumbent gains from repeated-core analogues, while the child gained only six incumbents from its locally added families. These are observations from separate completed trajectories, so they cannot price the child’s unscored rejected molecules or establish that those particular rejections caused the endpoint loss. The chemical assessment helps explain why counting cores is insufficient: productive attachment positions and combinations of peripheral groups remained uneven despite broader ring coverage. The number of evaluated molecules with potential tetrahedral centres rose from 846 to 1,145, with no assigned configurations in either cohort; the quota supplied neither configuration control nor a guarantee of preserving useful functional roles.

The open question is whether broader early coverage can coexist with sufficient sampling of productive peripheral analogues to retain late improvements. The AUC gain makes that distinction worth testing, while the lower final score rules out treating increased family coverage alone as evidence of better search.
