The selector consistently changes which offspring are evaluated, but this does not establish that uncertainty itself improves final scores. The original direct-submission Parent has only one available seed, so the earlier paired score gain of 0.005848 remains a single-seed comparison; the new results establish repeatable execution and describe score variability without establishing a paired multi-seed improvement. Matched Parent replicas and a same-pool mean-only or direct-order comparison are still needed to isolate score benefit, efficiency and uncertainty's contribution.

Direct nitrogen exchanges fell from 13 proposals, 10 accepted molecules and 3 selected states to zero, despite eligible pairs appearing in 92 child batches. Removing their menu entries changed 65 of 435 submitted batches and 54 selected states, while the retained tabu gate, overlap refresh, graph validation and accepted-maximum walk passed reconstruction. All fifteen tasks completed. Mean final score fell from 0.521759 to 0.520918, a paired change of -0.000841 within the specified 0.002 margin. Seed changes were +0.000374, -0.002898 and zero; the largest task loss was deco_hop seed 1 at -0.014491. Twelve of fifteen final task scores were unchanged. Every complete child trajectory exactly reproduced the historical repaired ancestor. Live exchange enumeration disappeared, but unmatched wall timings do not establish a speedup.

The result confirms the expected reversion and repeatability; it adds no independent seed evidence beyond the historical ancestor. This sparse exchange allocation is not needed to stay within the supplied mean margin on this panel, although individual paths benefit and one replica loses more than the margin. The experiment also shows why the exchange chemistry cannot be credited or blamed alone: in one shared-source batch, the Parent exchange was not selected, but the changed random-draw progression altered a later ordinary carbon extension into an oxygen extension and changed the winner. Removal measures the whole menu allocation policy. Nitrogen-containing molecules remain reachable, and the resulting families retain reactive bonds, unusual sulfur, dense rings and unassigned stereochemistry. The evidence supports a narrower proposal path in this particular walk, without demonstrating better chemistry or general dispensability of nitrogen relocation.

nodes.hypothesis: Remove the rejection-conditioned minimum on the number of successive graph-mutation calls taken by the ordinary single-parent mutation route of the Anchor's breeder. In the Parent that route performs max(sampled_length, min(6, 1 + member_attempts // 80)) successive mutate calls, where sampled_length is drawn once per attempt from [0.82, 0.15, 0.03] over one, two and three calls and member_attempts counts the consecutive construction attempts since this announced batch last admitted a pool member; after the removal it performs exactly sampled_length calls. Nothing else is touched: the sampled law, the break at the first failed mutate call, the discard of an attempt that produced no edit, the member_attempts counter itself with its increment per attempt and its reset to zero on pool admission, the separate halving of crossover probability while member_attempts exceeds forty, crossover and its finishing edit, the sulfur gate, identity admission, both duplicate scopes, the attempt bound and its partial-pool break, the accepted-only count-Morgan Gaussian process, the correlated draw with its sequential availability masks, the stall-conditioned top-forty eligibility mask with K=3 and M=40, the archive and the greedy survivor population all remain exactly as inherited. The causal claim has two steps. First, the removed term is the only consumer of the escalation threshold and draws no randomness, so if member_attempts never reaches eighty the deleted expression returned its neutral value 1 at every evaluation, the realized call length is identical at every position, every random stream is consumed at the same positions, and all fifteen sessions must reproduce the Anchor record for record. Second, this is the measurement the catalog gap needs: an exactly reproducing panel with an exposure receipt showing the threshold was never approached classifies this mechanism's conditional total endpoint contribution as no-material-effect on this composition, while any record-level divergence falsifies the recorded unreached-threshold claim and the same receipt names the slot count at which the floor bound.
nodes.finding:
The exposure audit is the primary reading and it is unambiguous. Reconstructing the per-member rejection counter from this node's own breed receipts over all fifteen sessions gives 76,057 in-loop construction attempts (69,600 pooled, 6,316 duplicate, 138 sulfur-rejected, 3 invalid). The counter takes the value 1 in 69,600 attempts, 2 in 5,781, 3 in 607, 4 in 61 and 5 in 8; its maximum anywhere is 5 and the longest preceding rejection run is 4, against a first escalation threshold of 80. Per session the maximum is 3 to 5, never higher. Not one of the 76,057 attempts reached 80, and in the 41,688 attempts that actually took the ordinary single-parent mutation route there are zero positions at which the inherited floor would have exceeded that position's sampled call length. Recomputing the same audit read-only over the Parent's fifteen sessions returns every one of those figures identically, so the catalog's recorded unreached-threshold condition is now measured rather than inferred from code.

With the floor gone the ordinary route's realized call count is exactly the separately sampled length: 34,210 one-call, 6,245 two-call and 1,233 three-call runs over 41,688 positions, empirical shares 0.8206 / 0.1498 / 0.0296 against the declared 0.82 / 0.15 / 0.03 law, with zero runs stopped early by a failed edit and 78,396 operator calls in total - all identical to the Parent position by position.

The divergence check finds no divergence anywhere. All fifteen trajectory files are byte-identical to the Parent's published trajectories: the same 150 initial records, the same 4,350 optimizer proposals in the same order with the same scores, the same best-so-far path and the same final Top-1. All fifteen session logs are identical line for line - 164,935 lines per side, about 740 MB - once the four wall-clock timing fields are removed, which means every pool, every posterior fit, every selected index, every sampled value and every gate decision matched: 435 pools at 160 of 160 with no truncation and 76,057 breeding attempts, 435 batches each emitting ten unique identities with no posterior fallback, 4,350 selection receipts, and the stall regime restricting the same 88 of 435 announced batches in the same 13 of 15 sessions with deco_hop seeds 0 and 2 again never restricted. The configuration block logged at session start is identical key for key.

The endpoint panel is therefore equal cell for cell: all fifteen cells complete with 300 oracle calls and 290 accepted proposals, seed macros 0.649701 / 0.585234 / 0.586156 and macro mean 0.607030, paired delta exactly 0.000000 on every seed and every task, which at the 0.002 descriptive scale is read as no material effect and never as statistical equivalence. On the implementation side the diff against the Anchor is exactly the two deleted lines, restoring the one statement reproduces the Anchor's source hash byte for byte, no occurrence of the escalation term survives, and no configuration key, receipt field, asset or dependency changed.

The campaign now has an experimental answer where it had an empty evidence list: rejection-conditioned mutation-call escalation contributes nothing on this Anchor, and it contributes nothing for a specific and checkable reason - its trigger is sixteen times further away than this benchmark's rejection statistics ever get. The admission path is simply too permissive for it: 69,600 of 76,057 attempts are admitted on the first try, so a candidate slot almost never fails twice in a row, let alone eighty times. This is a dormancy result, which is stronger than a measured null under exposure: the removed expression returned its neutral value at every one of its 41,688 opportunities, so no random draw moved and the reproduction is exact rather than merely similar. It also closes the one contribution gap on this Anchor that could be paid without buying path departure - the four other candidate removals all sit inside the law-free departure band, where a removal's loss cannot be separated from the cost of leaving the Parent's trajectory.

Two corollaries come free. First, complexity accounting: every later arm on this composition has been carrying this law in its retained-mechanism list and can now drop it, and the same audit shows the second law keyed to the same counter - the halving of crossover probability above forty consecutive failures - was likewise never reached, since the counter never passed five. That is an exposure finding, not a contribution measurement of that law, but it says a removal of it would also be a dormancy test rather than a search-behaviour change. Second, the only way this identity could ever be priced on this method is to change the admission statistics it reads - a much harsher gate, a far larger pool target or a stricter identity rule - which is a different experiment, and nothing here transfers to the L07 variant with its threshold of eight, to a lower threshold or to a different cap. A reproduction this exact is also a second, independent confirmation that this harness is deterministic under a fixed seed and profile, which is what makes future removals on this Anchor readable at all.

Because the molecules are the Parent's molecules exactly, the molecular reading is a second look at the same output and it is where the real limitation sits. Each session collapses onto one substituted scaffold - 12 to 21 distinct Murcko scaffolds in the top-scoring decile against 187 to 560 over the full proposal set, with 83 of one objective's best 87 molecules coming from a single seed - and then keeps editing it. This node's own receipts show why: of the 5,830 generating-parent entries behind those 4,350 proposals, 4,349 come from the population's top quantile, 1,211 from the second and 270 from the third; 1,595 of the 4,350 proposals were bred entirely from molecules first seen in the immediately preceding announced batch, the mean age of the oldest generating parent is 2.9 batches, only 2.6 percent reach back ten or more batches and just 198 descend from an initial-population member, so the search is a short-memory walk around the current leader. The late budget is spent on relabelling: 253 of 4,350 evaluations improved their session's best, 62 percent of the total gain lands in the first third against 12 percent in the last, and one session (zaleplon_mpo, seed 1) made its last improvement at evaluation 87 and then spent 203 further evaluations with 32 of its last 98 proposals sitting in five-way-or-larger exact score ties - families that differ only in whether a position carries F, Cl or Br. The surrogate is not the thing that is broken: within each announced batch the posterior mean's ranking of the ten molecules it selected agrees with their realized scores at a mean Spearman of 0.515 (median 0.553, negative in only 30 of 435 batches), consistent with the Anchor's own recorded pair-ordering accuracy of 0.799. What the evidence supports is a proposal-and-population limitation, not a ranking-model limitation: the method has no way to hold several structurally distinct families alive at once and no skeleton-level edit available at comparable frequency to peripheral substitution. The kind of method that would remove it is a population with explicit structural niching or scaffold-distance-aware admission, together with proposal operators that act on the skeleton (ring replacement, linker length, fusion pattern, scaffold hop) and with constructive introduction of whole functional-group classes - not a retuned threshold anywhere in the existing laws. The nine other recorded contribution gaps on this Anchor stay open and condition-mismatched, and this node says nothing about any of them.

nodes.hypothesis: Renew an inverse-motif restriction for exactly one additional inherited tenure when that specific live entry has actually participated in a same-transition bidirectional veto during its initial tenure, retaining its original selected-transition provenance and allowing no further renewal.
nodes.finding:
The intended lifetime and evaluation changes both happened. All 343 used restrictions that survived to their original deadline renewed once, adding 1206 completed restriction-steps; none exceeded the eight-step limit. Renewed entries caused 65 additional vetoes in 53 batches and displaced 62 candidates from complete, reconstructed ten-member comparator batches. All 62 replacements were evaluated, seven became walk states, eight beat their source and two improved the best archive. Renewal changed at least one batch in every task/seed session, while credit selection, overlap replacement and provenance remained intact. All fifteen sessions completed their full budgets. The three-seed macro mean fell from 0.521759 to 0.513767, a paired change of -0.007992 against the required +0.002. Seeds 0 and 2 improved by 0.018110 and 0.028962, but seed 1 fell by 0.071049. Mean DRD2 score fell by 0.068863 and deco_hop by 0.008789; gains in zaleplon (+0.022797), sitagliptin (+0.013894) and median_2 (+0.000999) did not offset those losses. The renewal mechanism is confirmed; its preregistered score benefit failed.

This rules out a merely larger memory table or a lack of later recurrence as the explanation for the result: renewed restrictions changed both evaluated membership and selected states. Recurrence remains a weak guide to value. Of 343 renewals, 240 never participated in another qualifying veto during their observed extension, and partial matches alone accounted for 103 of those cases. More concretely, at the first DRD2 divergence in seed 1, the renewed memory excluded a neighbor that the actual Parent had scored from the identical source and selected as its winner, improving that source by 0.059783. The Child instead made a worsening move. This is direct evidence that extending an exercised restriction can remove a useful opportunity; the later endpoint loss cannot be assigned to that one veto because subsequent draws and walks diverge. The molecular assessment also finds reactive heteroatom bonds and complex sulfur cages among strongly scored structures, so this recurrence signal provides no demonstrated improvement in chemical stability or makeability. The open question is whether a task-independent signal can distinguish harmful revisits from productive reuse; actual veto participation alone did not supply that distinction in this panel.

nodes.hypothesis: Modify only active tree eligibility using C={F,Cl,Br}. closed(i) is true if and only if occurrence i has an exact canonical identity in C, its stored graph is the corresponding ordinary neutral single atom, and each identity in C has an actual accepted receipt in this Objective Session. Ordinary means exactly one atom, zero bonds, matching atomic number 9/17/35, zero formal charge/isotope/radicals/atom map/explicit H, nonaromatic, unspecified chirality, implicit H enabled and one total H, matching the checked round-trip graph for that canonical key. No score value, task identity, fixed evaluation index or rejection count enters this predicate. Under the unchanged operator menu replacement can only swap the other two halogens; append and fragment/crossover have no eligible attachment or cut, deletion has no legal atom, and insertion/bond/ring operations have no support. Thus accepted coverage of C certifies no novel reachable terminal, by induction over all successful paths. Remove exactly these occurrences from active child selection and its sibling-kernel support, and count only nonclosed children in widening occupancy. The widening threshold itself stays max(1,floor(1.5*(N+O+1)**0.5)). Refuse action attempts from closed sources before any RNG draw; allow the unchanged bounded controller to route to live ancestors/alternatives. Keep topology, all allocated-node capacity counts and exact N/W/O/M/receipt storage. Newly generated closed aliases may still be admitted from live sources under the unchanged admissions, but cannot subsequently become active support. This is one eligibility intervention, including its effect on kernel support and width occupancy; their individual effects are not separately identified.
nodes.finding:
The rule activated in one of fifteen sessions, after all three reachable halogen identities had been accepted and with 170 paid proposals still available. It eliminated all 14,480 post-certificate actions from that exhausted class, left the fourteen unexposed sessions exactly unchanged, and preserved the common prefix of the exposed session. Across all 4,350 paid proposals, outer actions fell from 19,286 to 4,842 and unproductive actions from 14,759 to 313. In the late half, the corresponding counts fell from 16,937 to 2,491 and from 14,645 to 197. Twelve widening decisions gained permission to expand live branches, and exclusions were associated with 84 actual paid outputs. None improved the incumbent; 43 distinct later descendants of newly widened routes also produced no gain. Full and late incumbent gains remained 4.365063 and 1.367463, with 148 and 42 improvements, respectively. Every task/seed endpoint stayed unchanged: mean 0.499496, a paired difference of zero and 0.107534 below the formal Anchor. Closure, accounting and efficiency checks pass, but both registered strict useful-conversion increases fail. The protocol verdict is refuted at that downstream layer, not a technical failure or a failure to execute the routing change.

This experiment separates a real computation bottleneck from the cause of the score plateau. Exhausted branches wasted substantial action effort, and removing that waste recovered live alternatives, but the paid proposal budget was already completed by the Parent. The exposed session still bought 170 proposals after activation without improving its incumbent. That makes insufficient remaining opportunity an inadequate explanation here; improving internal action efficiency alone was insufficient to improve the purchased search on this panel. Only one session exposed the predicate, so the evidence establishes a precise local efficiency benefit and no measured endpoint contribution under these conditions, not broad transfer or an end to the tree approach. Selection/kernel exclusion and widening changes remain a joint intervention whose separate effects were not isolated.

The method still has a proposal-quality limitation after the closed class is removed. In the exposed session, 167 evaluation positions changed but none of the later proposals beat the existing incumbent. Across the panel, proposals below six heavy atoms increased from 425 to 447 and those above fifty from 301 to 302, while nonempty typed scaffold coverage fell from 1,704 to 1,693 distinct scaffolds. Fragment-excluded within-session similarity changed only slightly, from 0.3888 to 0.3883 overall and from 0.4332 to 0.4315 late; this does not establish scaffold collapse. The Molecular assessment finds that useful ring, amino and carbonyl arrangements are reachable but are inconsistently preserved through graph changes, alongside reactive heteroatom linkages and unspecified stereochemistry. A proposal operator or search scheme that can preserve and recombine informative structural relationships could address this limitation; the present experiment does not test its utility or justify a general small-molecule ban. Wall time fell in the exposed session, but matching Parent suggestion timers and complete instrumentation overhead are absent, so the action-count result is stronger than a causal runtime claim.

nodes.hypothesis: Replace the Parent's exposure-weighted squared residual with an exposure-weighted Huber residual whose transition is the detached starting weighted root-mean-square residual of each update, floored at the square root of the inherited stopping tolerance and held fixed through that update, thereby capping individual residual influence while preserving selected members, augmented targets and exposure coefficients.
nodes.finding:
The cap executed in all 450 updates. In the 420 historical updates followed by new proposals, it reduced influence on 1,465 of 4,200 selected row exposures at update start, including 1,092 current elites and 373 historical elites. The capped rows' mean share of absolute scalar influence fell from 69.22% to 59.37% on those same inputs. Every one of these updates changed the combined gradient direction even after global norm clipping, and every real first backward matched the Huber diagnostic exactly. Huber loss fell in 419 of the 420 updates, although 928 of 2,100 individual historical row exposures ended with larger residuals. All replicas completed. The three-seed final mean fell from 0.517655 to 0.508373, a paired change of -0.009283, with seed changes -0.026055, +0.032442 and -0.034235. The endpoint gain expected by the intent was not observed. Recorded mean AUC nevertheless rose from 0.406769 to 0.458439 and improved in every seed. The largest endpoint changes were a sitagliptin decrease of 0.080247 and a zaleplon increase of 0.035486. Raw duplicates rose from 36.22% to 48.80%, and batches needing additional sampling doubled from 29 to 58, while all 4,350 submitted proposals remained valid and novel.

Global gradient clipping did not make the row-level cap redundant: relative learning direction changed measurably in every prospective fitting opportunity. That establishes a real learning intervention, but more balanced residual influence did not provide the proposed final-score benefit. Faster discovery and the final endpoint separated: much of the AUC gain came from reaching strong DRD2 molecules earlier, where the parent already finished near the score ceiling, while sitagliptin lost substantial endpoint value. The molecular assessment found its stronger compact lactam–sulfonamide family in only one seed; broad core coverage in the other seeds did not supply equally useful structures. The cap also left target feasibility unresolved: historical exposures with positive, unattainable log-probability targets increased from 489 to 752 on the resulting trajectories. Starting caps affected current elites much more often than history, yet accepted-score averages and AUC increased, so the prediction of uniformly weaker early exploitation is not supported either. What remains open is how to preserve these early gains while reducing later repetition and avoiding the task-dependent loss of useful molecular families. The evidence does not isolate a particular suppressed row, token change or chemical feature as the cause of the endpoint loss.

nodes.hypothesis: Extend the existing change_bond neighborhood with relocation of an intact single-attachment acyclic branch from an aromatic carbon to its adjacent hydrogen-bearing aromatic carbon, directly exposing substitution-position isomers while preserving the branch, ring framework and molecular formula.
nodes.finding:
Ten fresh positional isomers reached evaluation from thirteen sampled branch relocations, with all atoms, the complete branch, molecular formula and aromatic ring framework retained. Six moved one-heavy-atom groups and four moved larger groups. One thiol position change improved its source score; the other nine lost. None won its batch, updated the best archive or produced a later walk descendant. The three-seed macro mean nevertheless rose from 0.520918 to 0.525257, a paired gain of 0.004339 that exceeds the 0.002 target. One seed improved and two declined; the largest endpoint gain was in one DRD2 seed, while median_2 and sitagliptin endpoints were unchanged throughout.

Direct positional accessibility is established: none of the ten scored products is reachable by a single original bond-order change, and each changes local motifs and measured score. Intact-group retention therefore avoids the necessary atom loss of branch deletion, but it does not reliably make a stronger neighbor. All four evaluated larger-branch relocations lose to their sources, including the methoxy and carboxyl shifts. The distinction between a successful panel and useful new molecules matters here: since no relocation is selected, the panel gain cannot be credited to descendants carrying a moved group. The expanded menu also changes proposal choices and batch competition among the original operators. The evidence supports a working positional channel and one local thiol-position gain, while leaving a reproducible score benefit from retaining a new position unresolved. The stronger sulfur-free aryl-amine series identified by the molecular assessment is an original-operator outcome and still contains strained nitrogen rings; other populations retain unusual sulfur and reactive heteroatom bonds. Conserving the existing group and ring has not established better stability or synthetic accessibility.

nodes.hypothesis: Among exact accepted-score batch maxima, select the candidate with the fewest heavy atoms before applying the inherited canonical lexical fallback, so an equally scored larger neighbor cannot become current solely because of its canonical spelling.
nodes.finding:
The rule changed six of 435 accepted transitions, all on equal-score plateaus in deco_hop seeds 0 and 2. Each selected an already scored maximum with one or two fewer heavy atoms than the lexical alternative, saving 10 atoms across those same-batch comparisons. All selected identities reached the actual current state and memory update. The other 429 choices, the immediate maximum score, canonical fallback and independent archive rule passed reconstruction checks. The three-seed panel mean fell from 0.521759 to 0.520655: paired change -0.001104 against the preregistered +0.002 minimum. Deco_hop endpoints fell by 0.001632 in seed 0 and 0.014925 in seed 2; every other task/replica scored trajectory was identical. The local tie mechanism is confirmed, while its expected score benefit was not observed.

Canonical ordering did sometimes choose unnecessary growth at an exactly tied score, so this experiment establishes a real selection opportunity. Avoiding that growth did not preserve a permanently compact or more productive walk: every changed choice was followed by a later growth move, and the six-transition plateau containing the first seed-2 change kept its original length. Mean proposal size in the affected task decreased by only 0.30 heavy atoms, with the median unchanged at 38. Smaller also did not mean chemically simpler: one changed choice introduced a carbon-sulfur triple bond, and the molecular assessment still finds reactive heteroatom attachments and questionable complete structures. Half of the changed choices altered bonds or elements without shrinking their own source; the other half deleted one atom. The poorer later results therefore concern changed chemical neighborhoods and memory provenance, not an isolated effect of size. In the seed-2 continuation, accepted source-beating neighbors fell from 19 to nine. The evidence narrows the opportunity to sparse exact ties in one objective family and makes chemically meaningful tie preferences or persistence of compact states worth testing separately; neither has a demonstrated score benefit here.

nodes.hypothesis: Replace the generation path of a preregistered quarter of the Anchor's unchanged 160-candidate pool: for every admitted pool member whose index satisfies index mod 4 == 3 (40 of 160 slots), draw one scored parent with the inherited score-quantile law, tokenize that parent's canonical isomeric SMILES with the prior's Cl|Br|. token regex, keep the first ceil(T/2) content tokens as a fixed prefix, and sample a continuation from the frozen corpus-pretrained autoregressive SMILES prior at temperature 1.0 until the end-of-sequence token or the 192-token content cap; the decoded prefix-plus-continuation string is then offered to exactly the inherited admission path (checked_molecule, pool_identity_admission, both duplicate scopes, and the sulfur gate evaluated against that same single conditioning parent). At most twelve sampled continuations are spent on one prior-origin slot, after which that slot falls back to the inherited graph-edit path and the fallback is recorded. The prior is trained only during prepare, only on the supplied unlabeled corpus, and its weights are frozen for the whole session: no accepted score, no oracle label, no task identity and no gradient update ever reach it, and its only session-dependent input is the parent prefix. Every other Anchor component - the seven graph operator families and their probabilities, two-parent connected-fragment crossover and its optional finishing, the floor-one continuation law [0.82, 0.15, 0.03] with the rejection-conditioned escalation, score-quantile parent sampling, greedy-64 survival, the bounded refill and its attempt limits, the sulfur envelope and rejection bookkeeping, the accepted-only count-Morgan Gaussian process with its generalized Tanimoto kernel, normalization, noise, jitter ladder and finite guards, and the correlated Thompson allocation with its availability masks and first-index ties - is retained exactly, and the pool target stays 160 so prior-origin candidates displace graph-edit slots rather than widening the field.
nodes.finding:
Supply changed exactly as registered. Across all fifteen sessions the frozen corpus prior filled 17,302 of the 69,600 admitted pool slots (realized share 0.2486 against the registered 0.25; every session at or above 0.231, every single pool at or above 0.194, 98 of 17,400 prior slots falling back to the graph path after the registered twelve attempts). The chemistry it supplied is much farther from its conditioning parent than the inherited graph edits of the same sessions: median count-Morgan Tanimoto 0.609 against 0.833, 82.7% of prior members at or below 0.70 against 24.0%, median heavy-atom change four atoms against one, 70.3% changing at least three heavy atoms against 30.5%, and a changed Murcko core in 97.2% against 69.8%. The graph arm itself stayed inside the Anchor's own reference (accepted products: median 0.892 and 14.8% changing three or more atoms, against the Anchor's 0.889 and 13.1%). Preparation behaved: holdout token loss fell from about 4.56-4.59 to 0.563-0.566 on 1,268,755 corpus sequences per seed, with no oracle label, no stored molecule, and a parameter hash identical at the first and last batch of all fifteen sessions. None of the 231 accepted prior products is a verbatim corpus molecule.

The failure is at the point where the surrogate decides what to evaluate. The inherited correlated Thompson allocation spent 231 of 4,350 evaluations on prior-origin candidates, 5.3% of picks against a 24.9% share of the supply, and the registered range of 0.5 to 5 picks per batch of ten was missed in ten of fifteen sessions. 292 of 435 batches bought none at all, and sitagliptin_mpo seed 2 bought none in any of its 29 batches, which is the registered allocation falsifier. The reason is visible in the posterior: in 433 of 435 batches both the median and the maximum predicted score of the prior-origin group sat below the graph-edit group, and that gap widened from 0.026 in the first ten batches to 0.115 and then 0.150 as each session's own accepted prior scores entered the archive; picks decayed accordingly, 140 then 55 then 36. The prior candidates that were bought were bought for their uncertainty, not their predicted value: median uncertainty percentile 0.78 and median predicted-score percentile 0.42 inside the pool, against 0.26 and 0.93 for graph-edit picks.

Conversion then failed on its own terms. Prior-origin products beat their own scored parent 25 times in 231 (0.108 against the graph arm's 0.148), produced 13 incumbent improvements against the graph arm's 241, and carried 0.1405 of the 5.0403 total realized incumbent-increment mass (2.8%). Eight of fifteen sessions saw no prior-origin incumbent improvement at all, against the registered requirement of at least one per session. Survival was weaker too: 67.5% of prior products entered the greedy-64 population against 79.6% of graph products, and prior-origin molecules were the conditioning parent in only 2.07% of the node's 111,107 parent draws. At node level the realized increment mass fell from the Anchor's 5.8194 to 5.0403 and incumbent improvements were 254 against 255, so the extra chemistry bought no extra realized gain.

Scores, complete and paired on seeds 0/1/2: panel mean 0.544512 against the Anchor's 0.596453, delta -0.051941, which sits just below the ungated law-free reference band's lower edge of -0.050871. Seed macros moved -0.096582, -0.049216 and -0.010026. Task means: deco_hop 0.617335 against 0.706940 (-0.089605, margin 0.02 breached, and this includes the known inherited seed-0 departure cell, 0.628292 here against 0.856148, worth about -0.0152 of the panel), sitagliptin_mpo 0.470835 against 0.604768 (-0.133933, margin breached), drd2_docking 0.955889 against 0.991017 (-0.035128, margin 0.03 breached), zaleplon_mpo 0.444399 against 0.456810 (-0.012411, inside its margin), median_2 0.234102 against 0.222732 (+0.011370, with all three cells above the Anchor's: +0.021327, +0.011740, +0.001043). The median_2 move is the only one that clears its registered band (upper edge +0.006695) and the only task mean above the Anchor. Interfaces were untouched: 160 candidates in all 435 pools, ten emitted in every batch, both duplicate scopes and a sulfur receipt on every valid novel candidate of both origins, 435 accepted-only model fits with no uncertainty escalation and no fallback batch, crossover share 0.432 against the Anchor's 0.429 and walk-length shares 0.817/0.152/0.030 against 0.814/0.155/0.031.

The campaign has now changed what this Anchor can propose, and learned that proposal supply was not the binding constraint. The limitation has moved one stage downstream: the accepted-only count-fingerprint surrogate systematically prices unfamiliar chemistry below the incumbent's own neighbourhood, so a second, genuinely different generator can occupy a quarter of the supply and still receive one evaluation in twenty. That pricing is not a prior-origin artifact that fades; it hardens as the session proceeds, because each cheap prior evaluation that lands below the incumbent band teaches the same kernel to down-price its neighbours. This is the first measurement on this lineage that separates 'the generator cannot propose a scaffold jump' from 'the allocator will not pay for one', and it says the second is now the active obstacle.

The chemistry explains why the allocator was right in its own terms and still wrong for the campaign. The prior's products are farther and more makeable (median synthetic-accessibility score 2.4-4.1 against 3.0-5.2 for the edit path, almost no heteroatom-halogen bonds) but they land off the incumbent's scoring ridge: their median accepted score is 0.185 against 0.289, and not one of them appears in the highest-scoring thirty molecules of any of the fifteen sessions. A raw continuation keeps half of a scored parent's string and rewrites the rest, which is enough to leave the narrow composition window these objectives reward. The two origins were therefore not complementary at the level that matters here; one was chosen and the other was measured.

Two further limitations were measured rather than assumed. First, an unconditional prior prompted with a prefix degrades exactly where the population leaves corpus-like chemistry: sample parse rate ran 0.875 down to 0.232 across sessions, and the worst session (sitagliptin_mpo seed 2, 3,853 unparsable samples of 5,018, 88 slot fallbacks, 4.7 attempts per admitted member) is precisely the session that bought zero prior candidates. Prefix-conditioning an unconditional model is cheap but brittle off-distribution. Second, the inherited search behaviour that motivated this round is unchanged by a supply change alone: the molecular report still shows late search re-pricing one decorated framework (top-thirty sets spanning 3-16 Murcko scaffolds, up to 82% of a session's last hundred evaluations on one generic framework) and graph-edit products still at median Tanimoto 0.89 with a one-atom median change.

What this rules out and what it makes worth trying. It rules out 'the pool has the wrong chemistry in it' as the explanation for this Anchor's plateau, and with it the whole family of share, temperature, truncation and model-size variants of this recipe: exposure was already at the registered quarter and the structural prediction was met in full, so no parameter of this recipe is the missing piece. It points instead at method classes that change who gets evaluated or how a distant proposal is finished: an allocator that reserves evaluations by proposal family or prices novelty explicitly rather than one joint posterior over a mixed pool; a surrogate or ranking model whose uncertainty is comparable across chemotypes instead of a similarity kernel anchored on the archive; or a refinement stage that locally edits a continuation, or conditions on a longer prefix, so the prior's chemistry arrives already on the scoring ridge instead of competing raw against the incumbent's neighbourhood. Of the route's three reserved follow-ups, the retention and breeding-membership arm is the one that attacks the measured obstacle; unconditioned de novo sampling is contraindicated, because it would move proposals even farther from the archive, which is the direction this selector demonstrably refuses to buy; and a score-driven policy update would change the prior's distribution rather than the allocator's pricing, at a budget of 300 evaluations per task where the source method uses one to ten thousand.

Still open: the median_2 gain. It is the only task above the Anchor, it clears both its +0.010 bar and its reference band, and all three cells rose, but it cannot be attributed to the prior from this panel. Prior-origin products carry 0% of that session's increment mass on seed 0, 34.5% on seed 1 and 25.7% on seed 2, and the same intervention also cut the inherited graph field from 160 to about 120 candidates per batch, so the joint recipe, not the prior, is what moved. The complementary explanation Curate already recorded for median_2 - a compressed scoring band re-priced by near score-identical single-atom swaps - remains consistent with a 0.011 move. Also open is whether the panel loss is the prior's own cost or the ordinary price of leaving this Anchor's lucky realization: the panel sits 0.0011 below the ungated band edge, and its known deco_hop seed-0 departure cell alone is worth about -0.015.

nodes.hypothesis: Replace any-single-attribute tabu vetoes with same-transition bidirectional inverse-attribute matching: veto a valid novel graph edit only if its signed motif changes match at least one active positive restriction and at least one active negative restriction originating from the same selected accepted transition.
nodes.finding:
Across the two added replicas' observed streams, the original any-match rule would veto 1,578 of 2,831 valid novel attempts (55.74%); the paired rule vetoed 121 (4.27%) on the same candidates and live memory. All 1,457 newly admitted proposals reached evaluation, accounting for 53.76% of optimizer evaluations. Of these, 141 beat their current source (9.68%), and their mean neighbor-minus-source score was -0.09247. They supplied 141 actual next-current states and 60 strict incumbent-improving observations. The remaining restrictions vetoed 112 distinct task/run molecular identities, changed 79 of 271 batches and produced nine selected next states absent from the passive unfiltered batch. Matching and memory-lifecycle checks agreed with the intended rule throughout the observed execution.

The first added replica completed all five tasks at 300 evaluations each, scoring 0.5277988 in macro final Top-1 versus 0.5180779 in the earlier screening replica of this same algorithm. The second added replica completed four tasks but crashed on zaleplon after 110 evaluations. Its completed final scores were 0.6092183 for decoration hopping, 0.9148144 for DRD2, 0.2018564 for median_2 and 0.4484554 for sitagliptin. The evaluator reports 1,310 total calls and no macro score for that replica, so there is no complete three-seed score estimate.

The crash occurred after the evaluator scored a full ten-molecule batch. The first accepted molecule's canonical spelling changed between generation and feedback, so its pending record could not be found. All ten evaluations are visible in the trajectory, but none of that batch's feedback was ingested and no next state was selected.

The narrower reversal test reproducibly changes oracle allocation and the walk while retaining active structural memory. Correct same-transition matching, intact four-step expiry and the surviving fresh-identity vetoes rule out erased memory as the source of easier admission. Most newly admitted neighbors still score below their source, so greater admissibility has not established better average neighborhood quality. The useful effects arise from a minority of admitted moves; the separate value of the remaining vetoes remains unmeasured because rejected alternatives were never scored.

The identity lookup failure previously seen only in the supplied smoke evidence now occurs in a formal replica. Its cause is localized: the generator keys pending proposals by a molecular spelling that changes when the evaluator canonicalizes it. The failing proposal was one of the newly admitted partial matches. This exposes an inherited execution limitation on the newly accessible trajectory and prevents a claim of complete or repeatable score benefit. A stable identity join and a complete replica are needed before assessing that benefit.

The molecular assessment shows that partial-overlap admission still explores recurring ring-rich families with unusual sulfur bonding, dense ring junctions and unspecified geometry. Memory selectivity does not establish chemically plausible alternatives or broad useful scaffold coverage; those limitations remain separate from the verified matching effect.

nodes.hypothesis: Quadruple only the fresh offspring pool target per announced batch member, from sixteen to sixty-four (160 to 640 candidates per announced batch of ten), so the unchanged accepted-only count-Tanimoto GP correlated Thompson selector takes its ten sequentially masked joint-draw maxima over a four-times larger field of fresh de novo offspring produced by the unchanged breeder, operators, continuation, crossover and finishing, sulfur gate and stable identity admission.
nodes.finding:
The enlarged field was built and used. Every one of the 435 batches across the complete fifteen-cell panel ranked exactly 640 fresh offspring, never truncated, at a modest generation cost of 1.147 breeding attempts per admitted member against the Parent's 1.093; the inherited escalation branches never fired and the longest struggle for a single pool member anywhere was nine attempts. The extra candidates genuinely competed: 73.3 percent of the 4,350 oracle calls went to members generated beyond position 160, the selection index distribution is nearly flat over all 640 positions, and the first 160 positions took 26.7 percent of the choices against the 25 percent expected if all members were interchangeable. That last number is the whole result in miniature: the later-generated members behaved exactly like the earlier ones. They beat their own generating parent at 0.152 and improved the incumbent at 0.063, against 0.153 and 0.067 for the members inside the Parent-sized prefix.

The screening-quality prediction failed. The registered test was that selected candidates should sit further above their own pool in posterior mean than the Parent's +1.054 standard deviations. They sat at +1.043, slightly lower, and fell in eight of fifteen cells, while the pool's own best available candidate did improve (+1.841 against +1.735). So the wider field did offer better candidates and the unchanged Thompson rule did not take them: it drew relatively more uncertain members (selected posterior SD 0.897 of the pool average, against 0.849 in the Parent), disagreed with the posterior-mean argmax in 92.8 percent of choices instead of 86.5, and picked members ranked on average 135th of 640 by posterior mean, 76.6 percent of them outside their pool's top ten. This is the registered failure mode for this intervention: four times more candidates means four times more chances for an extreme residual draw on an uncertain molecule, and that is what the enlarged field was spent on.

Downstream effects were real but tiny, and they went both ways. Parent-beating rose from 0.149 to 0.152 and incumbent improvement from 0.0586 to 0.0644, prediction error on emitted members fell slightly (batch MSE 0.0106 against 0.0112) and within-batch rank correlation rose from 0.526 to 0.546. Against that, the molecules actually evaluated were worse on average (mean offspring score 0.360 against 0.372) and larger (30.7 against 28.4 heavy atoms), with 181 emissions of five heavy atoms or fewer against 105.

The endpoint moved the wrong way. The complete matched panel mean fell 0.016060, from 0.596453 to 0.580393, against the registered requirement of at least +0.002; seed macros moved -0.044984, -0.012371 and +0.009174, six of fifteen cells improved, and the mean AUC fell from 0.4710 to 0.4555. Dispersion across seeds narrowed (population SD 0.0211 against 0.0340), which is not a substitute for the endpoint. Most of the panel loss is one cell: deco_hop seed 0 at -0.2459. The two runs were level there until evaluation 280 (Child 0.6088, Parent 0.6096), and then the Parent made its single rare late jump to 0.8561 while the Child finished at 0.6102. Excluding only that cell the panel would be close to flat. The largest gains were sitagliptin_mpo seed 2 at +0.0922 and zaleplon_mpo seed 0 at +0.0515. Compute behaved as predicted: non-oracle work rose about fourfold to a mean of 106 seconds per task, the worst task used 10.8 percent of its timeout and the worst node 2.9 percent, with no fallback, no truncation and every Cholesky succeeding at the smallest jitter.

Candidate-set breadth is now measured on this lineage and it is not the lever. The pool multiplier had been 16 in every node since the screening layer was introduced, and the Parent's near-uniform use of all 160 positions had been read as evidence that the selector was field-limited. Quadrupling the field falsifies that reading: the selector spreads over 640 positions just as evenly, which means the uniformity was never a sign of hunger for more candidates, only of how flat the sampled posterior is across fresh offspring of one population. At a cost of four times the generation work per evaluation, the panel mean fell 0.016 and not one intermediate quantity moved enough to matter. Breadth under this selector is exhausted as a direction; the remaining headroom in this component is in the posterior and the acquisition rule, not in how many molecules they are shown.

The sharpest thing learned is the split between the field and the choice. The best candidate available in the pool improved measurably when the pool grew, yet the chosen candidate did not: the enlarged field's extra quality went into the tail of the sampled draw rather than into what was evaluated. With unit prior amplitude and a fixed noise SD of 0.05, a joint Thompson draw over a larger correlated field gets its maximum increasingly from residual extremes on uncertain members, and the diagnostics show exactly that drift. This makes a concrete, cheap next test available: hold the pool at 640 and shrink the effective residual scale, or take the posterior-mean argmax for a fraction of the ten slots, and see whether the improved pool maximum can be converted into improved selections. It also sharpens the reading of the earlier removal results, which showed the composite selector worth 0.128 on this Parent: that contribution is about having a posterior-ranked fresh field at all, not about its size.

The chemistry explains why extra screening could not help. The molecular review of this node finds the generator producing ring-rich frameworks finished with N-Cl, O-Cl, S-F and N-F bonds, free imines and thiocarbonyls, no trifluoromethyl group in 4,350 molecules, no formal charge and no assigned stereocentre, and on the flattest objective it grows oligomers to a mean of 43 heavy atoms and QED 0.19 rather than finding alternatives. A larger pool samples that same vocabulary more densely; it widens the degenerate tail along with the useful one, which is visible here as 181 near-trivial fragments emitted against the Parent's 105, and as the deco_hop seed-0 cell where mean emitted size reached 55.7 heavy atoms and 600 crossover products were rejected as invalid. Scaffold diversity, distinct scaffolds among the best fifty, and late-phase pairwise distance are all unchanged from the Parent, so the wider field did not produce collapse and did not produce discovery either; it produced more of the same chemistry.

Two things stay open. The deco_hop seed-0 contrast is dominated by the Parent's single late breakthrough at evaluation 281, which no Child in three rounds has reproduced, so the size of the loss is fragile even though its sign holds on two of three seeds; a trustworthy reading of that cell needs more seeds, not more analysis. And this result constrains one multiplier at one announced batch size. It does not establish that 16 is optimal, does not rule out that a much smaller field would do as well for a quarter of the compute, and says nothing about breadth under a different acquisition rule. The compute-efficiency question is now the interesting one in the other direction: if 640 buys nothing over 160, it is worth asking what 4 would cost.

nodes.hypothesis: Remove optional second and third successive GraphOperators.mutate calls from ordinary single-parent proposals when the inherited saturation floor is one, retaining the original sampled base-length draw and the full max(base length, saturation floor) schedule whenever that floor exceeds one.
nodes.finding:
Ordinary second and third mutation calls disappeared under real requests for longer walks. The Child made one call in all 41,665 ordinary attempts; 7,373 requests would have allowed continuation, suppressing 8,589 requested calls. The Parent actually executed 8,737 continuation calls. Of the affected first-call products, 6,980 entered the candidate pools and 518 reached accepted evaluation; 100 beat their generating parent and 35 improved the incumbent. Internal retries, crossover finishing mutations and correlated posterior selection remained active. Neither side exercised saturation recovery.

The complete matched three-seed panel fell from mean final Top-1 0.595670 to 0.568802, a paired change of -0.026868, exceeding the registered 0.002 loss scale. Seed changes were -0.047714, -0.009154 and -0.023735. Population dispersion decreased from 0.026593 to 0.012088, but every seed macro was lower. Ten task-seed endpoints declined and five improved: all three median_2 endpoints, zaleplon_mpo in seed zero, and sitagliptin_mpo in seed one. Three task means declined and two rose. Correct execution and the predicted endpoint loss support a positive contribution from retained ordinary continuation in this composition.

The removal exposed useful first products, yet useful local steps did not preserve final search quality. Across the whole Child, parent beats increased from 629 to 714 and incumbent improvements from 258 to 299 while endpoints fell. Those counts depend on changing ancestors and incumbents; they cannot tell us what the omitted continuations would have scored. This resolves the previously open current-composition contribution question, separately from the earlier exchange-enabled experiment. It does not make the separate crossover and posterior-component losses additive.

The molecular assessment helps narrow the next question to coverage of useful structural arrangements. The Child still finds varied aromatic, carbonyl and amine families, but its leading repeated aza-aryl family does not recover the Parent’s compact carbonyl-thione organization. Some other families improve, and reactive bonds, difficult ring geometries and unspecified stereochemistry persist on both sides. Fewer calls therefore do not establish chemically simpler or more feasible output. These associations do not identify which omitted product or molecular feature caused the score loss. Saturation recovery remains untested, and fewer calls did not yield an observed speedup: total wall time was about 1,778 seconds versus 579, alongside much greater oracle time on the changed molecules.

nodes.hypothesis: Replace the accepted-prefix categorical reference penalty KL(policy || frozen prior) with KL(frozen prior || policy), preserving the existing coefficient, sequence normalization, score-ranked replay and trajectory-balance objective.
nodes.finding:
The reference gradient changed in all 7,185 updates after the policy and prior differed; the 15 identical initial states correctly showed no gradient difference. That activation did not produce better measured retention. Across 230,400 replay occurrences, prior-to-policy KL rose from 0.473648 before updates to 0.475468 afterward, and total variation rose from 0.215919 to 0.216668. Both average changes were unfavorable in every task-seed session. The inherited policy-to-prior diagnostic was also higher than the parent overall, although the two runs followed different histories.

Raw valid novel emission increased slightly, from 7,991 to 8,050 of 12,000 draws, or 66.59% to 67.08%. Mean accepted policy-origin score increased from 0.204941 to 0.222083, and graph feedback continued to affect later generation. Nevertheless, the three-seed mean final score fell from 0.550198 to 0.543814, a decrease of 0.006384. Paired seed changes were +0.000428, -0.027151 and +0.007572. The main final-score losses were in zaleplon_mpo and median_2, whose task means fell by 0.024000 and 0.020793. All fifteen task replicas completed their 300 evaluations.

A restoring component on nearly abandoned prior-supported alternatives was present, yet that component alone did not preserve conditional support under these joint score-driven updates. This rules out an unchanged KL orientation, a drifting prior, missing graph feedback or altered replay labels as explanations for the outcome. The registered retention-benefit falsifier is triggered even though mechanism execution is confirmed. The loss can improve while its reference-divergence component worsens; changing direction at the inherited coefficient therefore does not establish the intended protection.

The small gain in valid novel strings cannot be credited to demonstrated support retention. Its seed dependence, the missing parent prior-to-policy diagnostic and the different search histories leave that causal connection unresolved. Graph-bearing policy movement and later scaffold matches increased, which also argues against explaining the score loss as a simple shutdown of graph-to-policy learning. The molecular assessment still found a mixture of plausible compact molecules and oversized or chemically questionable assemblies. The experiment therefore narrows the next question to how joint training can retain useful conditional support without losing objective progress; changing the reference gradient alone did not settle it.

nodes.hypothesis: Replace dot-product count Tanimoto covariance by exact min/max count Tanimoto K(x,y)=sum_i min(x_i,y_i)/sum_i max(x_i,y_i) on unchanged folded Morgan occurrence rows, with empty/empty=1 and empty/nonempty=0.
nodes.finding:
The changed posterior reached every batch: all 435 selection orders changed against the passive original GP, and 433 selected sets changed. All 4,350 emitted offspring were accepted with their logged identities. On those same scored offspring, pair-order accuracy was 70.68% versus 71.51% for the passive original model, mean batch Spearman was 0.522 versus 0.536, and prediction MSE was 0.009562 versus 0.009146. Productive search also weakened overall: 623 offspring beat their best generating parent versus 629 for the actual Parent; sequential incumbent gains fell from 258 to 232, and beats of the whole-batch pre-feedback incumbent fell from 346 to 311. Mean offspring and source scores fell, while generic-core novelty on parent-beating events rose slightly from 190 to 195. Final macro mean fell from 0.595670 to 0.547424, a matched change of -0.048245 rather than the required +0.002. Seed macro differences were -0.083646, -0.018090 and -0.043000. Three of fifteen task/seed endpoints improved; twelve declined. Seed dispersion narrowed from 0.026593 to 0.007300 around the lower mean.

This was an exposed covariance intervention: repeated counts were present, all three Gram systems moved, the inherited allocator delivered different candidates, and the numerical and identity audits found no execution failure. Its activation is confirmed; its predicted ranking and endpoint benefit is contradicted under this Parent and profile. Lower MSE against the actual Parent stream did not signify better search: the child sampled lower absolute offspring/source scores, and the original GP fit to the exact same child state predicted its chosen scores better overall. Farther-from-archive accepted pairs and some individual task/seed cells provide positive ranking or local-win counterexamples, but they do not rescue the failed complete gain test or reveal rewards of unselected candidates. Rich aromatic, carbonyl and amine organization remained alongside reactive nitrogen attachments, difficult bridges and unspecified stereochemistry; the molecular evidence does not isolate a covariance-mediated chemical cause. The result closes this exact min/max law without transferring the failure to all count kernels or to those generator gaps. Mean-versus-covariance mediation, independent plausible scaffold supply and broader contribution remain open; terminal records and overlapping ancestry limit continuation claims.

nodes.hypothesis: Select the reusable prior checkpoint by fixed-noise ancestral valid-connected-unique molecular emission yield among unlabeled checkpoints that improve the initial holdout loss, breaking ties by lower original-string holdout NLL while preserving the Parent training and stopping rules.
nodes.finding:
The rule selected different prior weights in all three preparations. On the fixed selection samples, the chosen checkpoints produced 243, 245 and 238 valid, distinct molecules out of 256, compared with 232, 236 and 229 for the lowest-loss checkpoints from the same training trajectories. The independent diagnostic changed those counts by -1, +10 and 0; its pooled gain was only 9 of 768 draws, compared with 29 of 768 on the selection samples. Thus checkpoint choice and its selection-sample advantage are established, while an independent yield advantage appeared in only one seed. All training runs completed the same 29,742 updates, and the ordinary lowest-loss weights exactly matched the published parent weights, so no training-length difference explains the choice. The selected checkpoints incurred small token-loss increases of 0.001852, 0.002624 and 0.003124.

During optimization, valid terminated neural draws fell from 8,441 of 12,000 to 8,156 of 12,000, or 70.34% to 67.97%. Nevertheless, the complete three-seed endpoint mean rose from 0.520669 to 0.550198, with paired gains of 0.026285, 0.051553 and 0.010747. The mean gain, 0.029528, exceeds the registered 0.002 target. Deco hop, median and sitagliptin task means improved; zaleplon was nearly unchanged and DRD2 declined slightly. Every task completed the supplied evaluation panel. The new checkpoints therefore changed useful downstream search outcomes, but the score increase cannot be explained as a consistent increase in valid molecular emission.

The minimum token-loss checkpoint is not the only useful prior along the same unchanged learning trajectory. This experiment cleanly separates checkpoint choice from changes to training representations, gradients or the online search algorithm. It also exposes the limitation of the selection criterion: choosing among 60 checkpoints with one fixed 256-draw sample creates a selection-sample advantage that mostly disappears on fresh diagnostic randomness in two seeds. That pattern is compatible with selection noise and supports only limited generalization of the measured yield gain. The lower online raw validity shows that valid prior sampling and useful adaptation should remain separate measurements; even the first online batch follows accepted-score policy updates.

The molecular assessment gives the same distinction a chemical interpretation. Useful aromatic, amine and carbonyl arrangements coexist with unusual sulfur bonding, nitroso groups, peroxide bonds and unresolved stereochemistry. Valid connected uniqueness does not distinguish those liabilities, and higher endpoint scores do not establish better synthetic plausibility. The campaign now has evidence that an earlier checkpoint can improve the reciprocal search without a reliably better valid-emission rate. Whether a more representative unlabeled diagnostic can predict that downstream usefulness remains open.

nodes.hypothesis: Freeze a corpus-trained bidirectional masked discrete denoiser over SAFE fragment sequences, then repeatedly select high-ranked task-local observed molecules, replace one fragment with a variable-length mask chunk, iteratively denoise the missing tokens while preserving the surrounding context, and use accepted scores to update which whole molecules supply future contexts.
nodes.finding:
The macro mean of 0.495 is second of thirteen. It is the only root above 0.20 on every single objective: 0.908 on drd2_docking, 0.591 on deco_hop, 0.424 on zaleplon_mpo, 0.344 on sitagliptin_mpo and 0.207 on median_2. Context selection enrichment was positive on every objective and held under a tie-midrank sensitivity check. Every remasking attempt decoded with an unchanged prefix and suffix, a nonempty retained subgraph, exactly one replacement block and fixed outside attachment labels. One registered measurement came back against expectation: the mean score of a completion minus its generating context is negative in aggregate and on every task, so individual completions usually score worse than the molecule they came from.

Consistency, not peak performance, is what this node contributes. Its sitagliptin_mpo score of 0.344 is the best in the round and its drd2_docking of 0.908 is third, which no other method combines. The negative context-beating delta is the interesting result: the search improves by keeping the rare good completion and discarding the rest, rather than by proposing better molecules on average. That means throughput of attempts matters more here than proposal quality, which is a different tuning direction from every other lineage. One seed, and the fragment vocabulary itself has not been varied.

nodes.hypothesis: Modify only the support of the existing crossover-donor law. After inherited retirements/restarts have finished and before either regional fit/generation, snapshot both current accepted centers once for the announcement. For region r, construct exactly its original at-most-eight nearest episode-owned donors excluding its current center. Append frozen center c_(1-r) once if its canonical identity differs from c_r and is absent from that menu. Sort the resulting at-most-nine records by the inherited (-score, accepted serial) key, and use the unchanged quantile edges, weights, within-group random draw and per-action current-walk-source exclusion. Eligibility of the extra accepted graph permits the existing crossover branch, including at an otherwise donorless singleton, but does not force a crossover or purchase. The branch probability and fragment constructor remain inherited. New accepted products retain their generating region and episode ownership. The opposite label is used only by the pre-existing donor ordering and already-shared amplitude archive, never imported into the receiving GP or credited to its controller. The predicted path is admitted donor support -> actual opposite-center recombination -> valid noncopy paid products -> owned feedback and useful full/late conversion.
nodes.finding:
The structural access and feedback links worked. Across all fifteen Search sessions, the other accepted center was added at 864 of 870 regional boundaries; at the remaining six it was already present. The original donor set, independent training ownership and auction rules were preserved. There were 19,430 opposite-center draws and 261 paid products with a witnessed final noncopy two-fragment join, appearing in every session. Another 116 purchases had a successful earlier cross-region recombination followed by edits. Of these 377 products, 346 entered a later owned fit; 25 arrived at the final boundary and six belonged to an episode retired before another fit. No eligible product missed feedback use.

That access failed the registered useful-conversion prediction. Total global improvement fell from 5.64182 to 5.22074 across 4,350 paid evaluations, so gain per purchase fell from 0.001297 to 0.001200. Late-half gain fell from 0.83221 to 0.63777 across 2,175 purchases, or 0.000383 to 0.000293 per purchase. Mean endpoint fell from 0.58461 to 0.55654, a loss of 0.02807 against the code Parent rather than the required gain of 0.002. All three seed means declined; seven task/seed cells improved and eight worsened. Four task means fell, with median_2 the exception. The result is also 0.05049 below the formal Anchor. Every task completed its budget, with no evaluator invalid or duplicate submission and no model fallback. The verdict refutes the frozen utility prediction while preserving the established activation and feedback results.

Missing donor access was a real structural restriction, but removing it was not sufficient to buy more useful global progress. Direct and earlier-cross products supplied only 0.22972 of the total global gain. Their descendants were productive in some cases: 2,015 unique later purchases were linked through actual accepted roots or successful donors. That ancestry cannot be converted into incremental causal credit, because the donor-free alternatives and their future trajectories were never evaluated.

The measured bottleneck moves beyond simple access. Direct recombinants were overpredicted by 0.10293 score units on average, compared with 0.03075 for remaining purchases; their prediction MSE was higher in 13 of 15 cells. Late in search the 148 direct products were overpredicted by 0.17822 on average and generated only two strict global gains, totaling 0.00229. The 59 earlier-cross-only late purchases generated none. A ranking model that can calibrate recombinations outside local training support is therefore a relevant method class for this observed limitation, although these selected-stream errors do not establish that misranking caused the score loss or tell us which unpurchased alternatives were better.

The chemistry also limits what broader access means. The accepted output broadened from 1,880 to 2,038 typed scaffolds and from 1,234 to 1,300 generic scaffolds, so this is not whole-search scaffold collapse. Yet high-score cohorts still contain only 7–25 generic scaffolds per task, 2,113 of 2,175 late purchases make no strict global improvement, and many outputs elaborate recurring ring/carbonyl families into strained or reactive arrangements. Small fragments increased from 134 to 177 accepted outputs while oversized graphs fell from 245 to 153; peroxide-containing outputs increased from 48 to 237, and 2,705 products had potential tetrahedral centers with no assigned configuration. Those observations support a gap in proposal operators that preserve coherent, chemically explicit frameworks while changing them. They do not establish a chemistry filter, size threshold or score-mediated benefit. What this node settles is that this exact donor-support rule activates without satisfying its full-and-late utility criterion. Better structural proposals, calibrated pricing and the wider regional approach remain open; no retained component or entire route is rejected by this single intervention.

nodes.hypothesis: At natural restarts only, condition the regional count-GP on the deduplicated union of its owned episode records and a predictor-only context fixed at restart. Start context S with the chosen root. Let F be that region first actually generated field and A the unique already accepted current-session archive excluding identities in S. Greedily add min(9,|A|) distinct records: at each step choose z maximizing |F|^-1 sum_{x in F} cov(x,z|S)^2/[var(z|S)+0.05^2], using the inherited fixed count-Morgan generalized-Tanimoto covariance and noisy conditioning solve, with exact equal reductions broken by earliest accepted serial. Recompute conditional covariance after each addition. This targets nonredundant predictor support over actual proposals, restores nonconstant conditional means, and can change the existing posterior auction. Context selection reads features and acceptance identity only, without optimizing on the candidate labels or using selected z scores in its criterion. Only fitting uses their already accepted scores. Context never transfers donor eligibility, ownership, center status or progress. Predictive design activation is separate from subsequent purchased global gain.
nodes.finding:
The intended selection and conditioning operated at all 18 natural restarts. Every context differed from the same-state nearest-neighbor set, all 162 greedy additions lowered candidate-field variance, and all first-reset predictions became nonconstant; the Parent had 19 singleton restarts with constant first predictions. Average normalized field variance fell from 0.34138 with the root alone to 0.25660, versus 0.31394 with nearest context. Ordered purchases changed in 87 of 101 exposed announcements against owned-only predictions and 93 of 101 against nearest context. On the 989 actual post-reset labels, RMSE was 0.19675 versus 0.21031 for owned-only and 0.19557 for nearest context. Paired within-announcement rank correlation improved more often than it worsened: 52 versus 21 against owned-only, and 52 versus 39 against nearest context. All 18 restarts received first-field feedback. Post-reset global gain per evaluation increased from 0.116910/950 = 0.000123063 to 0.129368/989 = 0.000130807, while late gain mass fell from 0.832207 to 0.814778. Across all fifteen completed task/seed cells, mean score rose from 0.584614 to 0.585197, a gain of 0.000583; paired seed changes were +0.002152, -0.001374 and +0.000970. The mean remains 0.021834 below the formal Anchor. Execution and direct behavior are established, but the registered joint conversion prediction is refuted because the complete-panel score gain missed 0.002. This is a small observed gain below the criterion, not an execution failure or missing-data result.

The experiment separates useful conditioning from sufficient optimization benefit. Selecting context for the actual field reduces uncertainty and changes decisions more strongly than geometric proximity alone; it also improves observed ranking on this selected stream. Those changes still produce only a small increase in global progress. Lower predictive variance did not guarantee lower overall prediction error than nearest context, and better selected-label ranking did not deliver the registered endpoint gain. The Parent comparison tests the joint addition of context selection and conditioning; passive replays cannot isolate the optimization contribution of choosing variance-based rather than nearest context because their alternative molecules were never scored.

The limiting behavior is continued local search with scarce global returns, rather than blanket restart starvation: only 19 of 989 post-reset purchases made a new global incumbent, and eight of eighteen reset episodes contributed no global gain. Molecular assessment finds recurring aromatic carbonyl, aza/dicarbonyl and cyclic-amine families; typed/generic scaffold coverage fell from 1,880/1,234 to 1,824/1,176, and within-batch similarity among nonfragment accepted molecules rose from 0.73151 to 0.73656. Fragments, oversized recombinations, unconventional heteroatom connectivity and unresolved stereochemistry persist. These observations support a limitation in the useful proposal repertoire, without proving that context selection caused the chemical liabilities or that all search collapsed to one scaffold. A proposal operator or search scheme that reaches alternative complete frameworks, or a ranking model better aligned with realized improvement, could address the remaining limitation; their benefit is untested. This node settles the registered finite-panel conversion claim and leaves the broader restart-context approach open.
