nodes.hypothesis: Reduce only the fresh-pool target of the inherited pool loop from 160 to 120 candidates per announced batch of ten, by setting the single constant CONFIG['posterior_selector']['pool_multiplier'] from 16 to 12, so the unchanged accepted-only count-Morgan Gaussian process takes its ten sequentially masked correlated-draw maxima over a complete 120-member field instead of a 160-member one, with the breeder, operator families and probabilities, continuation law, sulfur gate, identity admission, both duplicate scopes, the attempt bound, partial-pool break, exhaustion raise, fallback routing and the emission of exactly ten identities per batch all unchanged.
nodes.finding:
The narrower field was built exactly as registered and nothing else moved: all 435 pools reached 120 of 120 candidates with no truncation and no exhaustion, 52,200 fresh admitted graphs against the Anchor's 69,600, every batch still emitted ten unique molecules, no batch fell back to generation order, and reversing the single constant reproduces the Anchor source byte-for-byte. The removed slice is gone from the choice set: no evaluated molecule came from positions 120-159, where the Anchor had taken 1,023 of its 4,350 picks, and the mean selected position fell from 78.2 to 58.5. Generation work fell with the field, 76,081 breeding attempts to 56,457, at an unchanged attempt bound and an unchanged worst case of six consecutive attempts for one member.

The endpoint fell 0.055666 on the complete fifteen-cell paired panel (0.540787 against the Anchor's 0.596453), which is below the pre-registered ungated reference band whose lower edge is -0.050871, by 0.004795. Three of the four protected task margins are breached: deco_hop -0.095127, drd2_docking -0.075492 and sitagliptin_mpo -0.096585 against margins of 0.02, 0.03 and 0.02; zaleplon_mpo -0.015740 stays inside its 0.02 margin. median_2 is the one favourable task mean, +0.004614 with two of its three cells above the Anchor, but it sits inside the median_2 reference band of [-0.007767, +0.006695]. The loss is heavily one seed: seed 0 contributes -0.138296 while seeds 1 and 2 move only -0.009732 and -0.018969, both inside the reference band, and three seed-0 cells (deco_hop -0.232107, drd2_docking -0.217570, sitagliptin_mpo -0.256325) carry almost the whole panel delta. The deco_hop task mean lands inside the registered departure range of [-0.116414, -0.084946] that all thirty previous ungated children occupy, and the inherited seed-0 endpoint of 0.856148 was again not reproduced, so that cell is the known departure signature rather than anything about breadth.

The productive-use receipts moved in a split direction. The smaller field produced more gains, each smaller: parent-beating rose from 14.9 to 17.3 percent of evaluations and incumbent improvements from 255 to 290, yet the realized increment mass fell from 5.8194 to 4.9844 and the largest single increment from 0.4620 to 0.2690. Splitting each session into thirds locates the whole deficit in the first third, 3.7484 to 2.3991, while both later thirds match or beat the Anchor. One registered observable is only partly met: in raw score units the best of the field fell as predicted (per-batch maximum posterior mean 0.4485 to 0.3761, selected joint-draw value 0.4760 to 0.3897), but recomputed in each fit's own standardized units the top of the field did not fall at all (1.610 to 1.664), so the raw drop tracks the lower score levels the diverged runs reached rather than a clean order-statistic effect.

The control answers the loss half of the round-42 attribution question and refuses the gain half. A pure quarter-cut of the graph field, with no prior and no second proposal stream, costs 0.055666 - as much as the entire round-42 panel delta of -0.051941, which was in fact 0.003725 less negative than this control. So the round-42 loss needs no explanation beyond the field reduction it imposed on its own breeder as a side effect, plus ordinary departure, and the prior-origin supply carries no additional panel penalty. The favourable median_2 movement is a different matter: the field reduction alone yields +0.004614 with two of three cells above the Anchor and stays inside the reference band, where the round-42 arm reached +0.011370 with all three cells above and outside it. Breadth therefore explains less than half of that movement, and the open question about whether median_2 can be read as approached stays open and now points at the prior-origin path or at departure rather than at breadth.

The breadth evidence on this Anchor is now firmly non-monotone and should stop being treated as a curve: 640 candidates cost 0.016060, 120 cost 0.055666 and 40 cost 0.062417, so a quarter-cut is nearly as damaging as a fourfold cut and clearly worse than a fourfold widening. With 83 percent of this panel delta coming from one seed and three cells, one realization per field size cannot resolve a breadth coefficient against this level of path noise; the missing measurement is repeated seeds at a level already run, not another level.

What the increment-mass decomposition adds is a mechanism for why breadth matters at all here, and it is not the one the field-size framing suggests. The endpoint on this Anchor is set by a few rare large early jumps, not by the rate of small refinements: the narrower field lost 36 percent of its first-third increment mass and its best single increment dropped from 0.462 to 0.269, while its later thirds actually improved and its parent-beating rate rose. A smaller field lowers the chance of drawing one of those rare high-value members, and the extra late refinements cannot repair a Top-1 endpoint once the chance is missed.

That makes the binding limitation a search-behaviour one, and the trajectories and chemistry show it directly. Improvement continues to the end of the budget in both panels (mean last improving evaluation 272 of 300 here, 275 for the Anchor), so nothing stops early; what happens instead is basin lock. Every seed settles on one scaffold family within the first 100-150 evaluations and then spends the remaining budget on single-atom swaps, with up to 284 of an objective's 870 proposals merely reproducing a score an earlier proposal already reached and one Murcko scaffold covering up to 34.6 percent of a panel. The clearest case is drd2_docking seed 0, which locked onto a bridged chloro N,O-acetal cage of 36 heavy atoms and plateaued at 0.7737 while seeds 1 and 2 reached 0.9729 and 0.99999 on a compact aminergic series; the score gradient there is unambiguous and the generator can follow it, so this is a basin the method cannot leave, not a gradient it cannot read. Meanwhile the surrogate carries real signal but ranks only moderately well (chronological prediction MSE 0.00669 against an archive-mean baseline of 0.03022, but a within-batch rank correlation of just 0.482) while taking 90.8 percent of its picks from beyond the first ten generated positions. Candidate supply is not the constraint; which basin the run is trapped in, and how well the ranker orders within it, are.

The method classes that could remove that limitation are therefore not field sizes. Worth trying: a basin-aware proposal and allocation scheme - an archive partitioned by scaffold with per-niche evaluation budget, or an explicit novelty or diversity term in the acquisition over scaffold space - instead of one correlated Thompson draw over a single undifferentiated field; a restart or niche-reallocation operator that can abandon a stalled basin, which the inherited floor-one continuation law cannot do; and a ranking model whose uncertainty is comparable across chemotypes, since the round-42 arm already showed this accepted-only count-Morgan kernel systematically down-prices chemistry unlike its archive. The chemistry report adds operator-vocabulary gaps in the same spirit: the generator can never build a polyhalogenated carbon, places halogen directly onto ring nitrogen in up to 72 of 87 top-decile molecules, closes strained three- and four-membered rings onto aromatics, and cannot rebuild a multi-atom functional group once it is mutated away. None of that is addressable by changing how many candidates are built per batch.

nodes.hypothesis: Condition the retained connected-fragment crossover donor-cut distribution on reciprocal endpoint-context compatibility with the unchanged first-parent cut whenever compatible support exists, preserving the inherited donor behavior otherwise.
nodes.finding:
The conditional donor law worked exactly on 26,727 informative crossover attempts. On those same states, the inherited chance of a reciprocal context match averaged 9.55%; the applied law made it 100%. Independent reconstruction found no key, weighting, support, sampling or product-identity discrepancy. The resulting channel was usable: 354 compatible products that differed from both parents reached evaluation, including 257 pure crossovers. They produced 70 strict best-parent beats and 32 incumbent gains; 268 later served as parents. However, 22,117 of the 26,727 conditioned immediate products reproduced a parent. Of 850 evaluated conditioned descendants, 496 became novel only through finishing mutation. No informative nonidentical product reached evaluation in any of the three median-task runs.

Total crossover evaluations rose slightly from 1,492 to 1,549, but novel crossover pool entries fell from 29,730 to 22,962. Evaluations following genuinely nonidentical immediate crossover fell from 1,368 to 1,023, and pure crossovers fell from 961 to 725. All fifteen task runs completed, with every announced batch valid and unique. The complete matched endpoint mean fell from 0.595670 to 0.575399, a change of -0.020271 against the required +0.002. Seed changes were -0.061941, +0.019643 and -0.018514; ten of fifteen task-seed endpoints declined. Seed population SD fell from 0.026593 to 0.008463. Overall local parent beats nevertheless increased from 629 to 654, and incumbent gains from 258 to 277.

Constructing compatible donors avoided the earlier hard gate’s near-elimination of evaluated crossover, but retaining the route count did not retain its composition. Exact local correspondence often selected a fragment that rebuilt an existing parent; subsequent mutation then supplied novelty. This separates three claims that a matching percentage conceals: correct donor allocation, exposure to genuinely new recombination, and improvement of the complete search. The first is established, the second survives in a smaller channel with a clear task boundary, and the endpoint improvement prediction is contradicted. The experiment supports a negative mean contribution from this particular refinement under the tested composition; it does not overturn the separate evidence that crossover itself is useful.

Local correspondence also fails to certify chemistry. The output remains rich in aromatic, carbonyl and amine families, with conventional alternatives alongside reactive halogen bonds, doubtful ring geometry and unspecified stereochemistry. In the fluorinated family, fewer nitrogen-halogen molecules accompany more oxygen-halogen molecules, so one reduced alert would hide a changed liability. Finishing mutations can also remove the matched attachment environment. The useful next distinction is whether donor choices preserve favorable complete molecular relationships while producing a distinct, chemically credible product. Neither excluding reproduced parents nor filtering unusual bonds has been tested here. Which change in ancestry, pool competition or later feedback caused the endpoint loss remains open; the scored cohorts do not provide labels for unchosen donors.

nodes.hypothesis: One joint replacement: persistent prefix-conditioned, all-observed-terminal-return MCTS with progressive action widening and WU-UCT-style pending-aware direct batch selection. Prefix occurrences retain molecular states and route-specific completed counts N, observed return sums W, and pending counts O across observe boundaries. Actual terminal rewards, including non-improving and low returns, are backed up exactly once on their recorded route. UCT uses W/N only from completed observations and N+O only in its exploration term. The selected forest itself emits the announced batch of distinct valid terminal molecules, exposing tree feedback without the old GP or stall mask. The causal prediction is that real terminal feedback changes subsequent existing-prefix choices, revisits unscored intermediates, and delivers useful evaluated descendants through those intermediates; those descendants may increase realized incumbent progress and the full-panel endpoint.
nodes.finding:
All 15 sessions completed. The tree delivered 3,044 of 4,350 evaluated proposals through 2,296 intermediate occurrences retained unscored across batches. Every accepted return was backed up correctly, including 4,302 non-improving returns. Freezing values at their pre-feedback level changed 2,681 actual choices, including 382 below the root selector; pending counts changed 3,930 same-state selections. Retained-prefix descendants produced 24 incumbent improvements totaling 0.6483. Yet full-panel improvement mass fell from 5.9781 to 1.4670, or from 0.00137427 to 0.000337234 per evaluation, triggering the registered useful-progress falsifier. Mean final Top-1 fell from 0.607030 to 0.306290 (paired difference −0.300740, against a required +0.002). All three seed macros and all five task means fell; 14 of 15 endpoints were lower, and every task mean exceeded its allowed regression margin. These results establish activation and refute this intervention’s predicted conversion to better search.

Loss of prefix memory, positive-only credit and an intervening GP filter do not explain this run: persistent memory, all-return feedback and direct purchases all operated. The limitation is how the activated method uses its limited feedback. Of 13,049 non-root occurrences, 10,584 finished with only one terminal return; 2,299 of the 2,681 feedback-sensitive decisions were still choices among the ten original roots. Real deeper reuse occurred, but it did not sustain useful refinement: late-half evaluations produced 12 incumbent improvements versus the Parent’s 76. Chemistry supports diffuse exploration rather than scaffold collapse: typed/generic scaffold counts rose from 1,667/951 to 2,718/2,085 and fragment-excluded similarity fell on every task, while scaffold coverage fell and both tiny and oversized tails expanded from 91/44 to 350/472. Favorable combinations of rings and polar functionality were reachable but less consistently preserved; broader scaffold variety alone did not solve the search problem. A proposal or ranking model that generalizes feedback across related graph states and preserves useful local arrangements is the kind of method that could address this sparse, weakly focused refinement; this run does not test such a method. The literature-derived persistence, backup, pending accounting and widening elements all operated in their registered molecular adaptations, so this is an informative failure of their bound conversion prediction. Because the replacement also removed the Parent’s predictor and scored breeding concentration, the evidence identifies a negative result for the joint controller and cannot isolate the contribution of tree credit, widening, pending accounting or the removed components. It leaves broader tree-search approaches open and supplies no counterfactual scores for unchosen routes.

nodes.hypothesis: Fit a task-local regularized linear score model on exact molecular count descriptors, then construct new bounded peripheral regions of scored molecules by maximizing that predictor in a mixed-integer graph program whose atom, bond, attachment, valence, connectivity and descriptor constraints jointly define the submitted molecular graph.
nodes.finding:
All five tasks completed on the screening seed. The optimizer supplied 145 full batches and 1,450 novel accepted molecules from feasible integer assignments, with zero discrepancies across their 384 count descriptors. All 150 ridge fits reconstructed from accepted task-local scores, and the 140 feedback refits with later opportunities changed subsequent construction objectives. Accepted constructions were selected again as sources 525 times. Of 1,450 proposals, 1,400 had positive predicted gains over their source; 578 of those predictions became actual gains. Overall, 598 proposals beat their source and 36 improved the running best, although mean child-minus-source score was negative on three of the five tasks. The final five-task Top-1 mean was 0.286518. Initial to final Top-1 changed from 0.305105 to 0.395373 for zaleplon_mpo, 0.548381 to 0.583606 for deco_hop, 0.019041 to 0.189601 for drd2_docking, 0.167839 to 0.175888 for median_2, and 0.002094 to 0.088123 for sitagliptin_mpo. This root has no Parent, and one screening seed does not establish comparative advantage.

The construction and adaptive feedback mechanisms happened. This result establishes that exact count realization and sufficient integer-construction throughput are attainable in this bounded peripheral-edit domain; the remaining predictive errors cannot be attributed to a mismatch between optimized descriptors and submitted graphs. The representational limit is visible in the accepted data: different molecules with identical full descriptor vectors received different scores on every task. In the docking trajectory, the two fluorine-position variants highlighted by the chemistry assessment share all 384 counts but score 0.124071 and 0.189601. No refit of this descriptor-only linear predictor can distinguish that pair. The chemistry assessment also finds familiar inherited rings carrying many reactive or unconventional appendages, alongside simpler high-scoring alternatives. Together, these observations make richer chemical-environment representation and constraints on functional-group compatibility worth testing while keeping exact realization as a control. They do not establish that either change will improve scores. Current evidence covers neutral, unspecified-stereochemistry peripheral trees and retained ring frameworks; new ring construction, broader chemistry and reliable advantage across replicas remain open.

nodes.hypothesis: Remove nonuniform score-rank weighting only from actual crossover-partner requests, choosing uniformly from the increasing-rank union of the inherited positive-probability groups after original first-parent exclusion and empty-group fallback; keep the original band draw passive for that role and preserve every first-parent request under its original weighted band and within-band law.
nodes.finding:
All 75,472 first-parent draws retained the original rule. Partner selection preserved exactly the original eligible identities but changed 32,483 of 34,304 choices when replayed against the inherited choice from the same random state. On those same populations, expected partner score fell from 0.365128 to 0.342519. Changed choices reached 1,439 accepted crossover offspring; 797 of those offspring later bred. Greedy survival, complete accepted-score learning and all 435 full candidate-pool selections remained active.

Mean final Top-1 fell from 0.595670 to 0.543862, a paired change of -0.051808 against the registered 0.002 scale. Seed-average changes were -0.087771, -0.005118 and -0.062534. Eleven of fifteen task/seed endpoints declined; zaleplon seed 0, median similarity seeds 1 and 2, and sitagliptin seed 1 improved. Task means rose for zaleplon and median similarity but fell for decoration hopping, docking and sitagliptin. Seed-average population deviation fell from 0.026593 to 0.008407. Every task completed its full oracle budget.

The score-ranked crossover partner has positive conditional value even when the first-parent rule and eligible partner set are preserved. Earlier removal in both roles could not localize that value; this control answers the partner question. It leaves first-parent contribution, support-only value and the value of the complete graph-evolution system open. Shared-baseline results cannot be added or subtracted into those answers.

More local success did not mean better search. Strict best-parent wins rose from 629 to 702, accepted offspring later reused rose from 2,401 to 2,619, and incumbent advances rose from 258 to 265. But the generating reference weakened: mean best-parent score fell from 0.470456 to 0.386162, mean offspring score fell from 0.385256 to 0.325006, and the average positive incumbent increment fell from 0.022510 to 0.018983. These results rule out treating local win counts, reuse or lower dispersion as sufficient evidence of productive exploration.

The molecular assessment describes substantial aromatic, amine and carbonyl chemistry, including a comparatively conventional nitrile ketone in the improved zaleplon run. The largest losses include failure to recover the Parent’s compact high-scoring decoration-hopping arrangement, while much larger decorated structures, reactive nitrogen/oxygen–halogen bonds, difficult ring geometry and unspecified stereochemistry persist. Those associations suggest a gap in useful feasible alternatives, but neither the cleaner counterexample nor the liabilities identify the chemical cause of the loss. Partner identities, subsequent graph randomness and adaptive feedback remain inseparable parts of this measured total effect.

nodes.hypothesis: Remove only original sampled residual influence on successful pool allocation by choosing the maximum original count-GP posterior mean on each inherited available mask, resolving exact ties by the first pool index, while retaining full original covariance, Cholesky, normal-array consumption and correlated sampled arrays as passive computations with unchanged failure routing.
nodes.finding:
Every mean-only choice followed the original model mean, with no non-tied mean-loss decisions. The original sampled rule preferred a different identity at 3,958 of 4,350 actual mask positions. A separately masked replay changed all 435 batch orders and 434 selected sets; 2,731 actual accepted molecules were outside its sets. On these same Child pools, mean-only selection raised the average sum of ten predicted means from 3.16569 to 3.42482, lowered selected latent SD from 0.03059 to 0.01583, and raised count-Tanimoto redundancy from 0.58199 to 0.82801. The model uncertainty and original draws remained intact. All 15 task/seed evaluations completed. Macro score fell from 0.59645311 to 0.48013623, a loss of 0.11631688. Paired seed changes were −0.22680180, −0.03988971 and −0.08225913. Twelve task cells lost; median-2 seeds 0 and 2 and sitagliptin seed 1 improved. Local parent wins rose from 648 to 668, but mean best-generating-parent score fell from 0.45530 to 0.37127 and mean offspring score from 0.37205 to 0.33081. Total incumbent gain fell from 5.81942 to 4.07466; new nonempty generic cores with a strict parent-beating member fell from 168 to 101. These complete, exposed results support positive conditional contribution of original sampled residual presence at the registered 0.002 scale.

The loss cannot be explained by a missing intervention, absent natural choice exposure, altered original model arithmetic, broken accepted-feedback joins or a changed sulfur admission rule: those checks passed. Higher predicted means and lower error on the acquired stream did not preserve the best observed outcome. Selected-stream MSE was lower than Parent in all 15 cells, yet pair ordering and Spearman were worse in 14; the only favorable ranking cell was zaleplon seed 2. Those comparisons describe different adaptively acquired streams. On identical Child identities and labels, active and passive original-mean prediction/ranking contrasts are exactly zero. The narrower selected cores and the Molecular assessment's repetitive connected families are consistent with restricted exposure, while reactive attachments remain in both methods; they do not identify why residual sampling helped or establish chemical mediation. Lack of later breeding is also insufficient as a general explanation: 657 of 659 nonterminal parent-winning Child sources were actually drawn, versus 636 of 639 in Parent. However, 390 drawn Child winners had no productive direct accepted descendant, versus 343 in Parent. Each panel's 150 final-batch offspring remain censored. This answers the current gated residual-presence criterion as one total adaptive removal contrast. It does not establish constituent additivity, sulfur interaction, the value of covariance dependence, independent validation, a complete optimizer foundation or transfer from older ungated Parents; those questions remain open.

nodes.hypothesis: Remove nonuniform score-rank weighting conditional on the original same-state positive breeding support: choose uniformly from the increasing-rank union of the inherited positive-probability eligible quantile groups after original partner exclusion and empty-group fallback, retaining the original band-choice call as passive and the original member-choice call as the sole active parent allocation.
nodes.finding:
The control preserved the exact original positive breeding support in all 108,254 parent requests. Every request offered a nonuniform-law comparison, and 103,018 actual parent identities differed from the inherited choice made from the same saved post-band random state. Mean selected topness was 0.756082 versus the original same-state expectation of 0.883924, and mean parent score was 0.348279 versus 0.373596. Changed choices reached 4,020 of 4,350 accepted offspring; 2,269 of those offspring later bred. Greedy recursion, complete accepted-score learning and all 435 full candidate-pool selections remained active.

Mean final Top-1 fell from 0.595670 to 0.538667, a paired change of -0.057003, beyond the registered 0.002 scale. Seed macro changes were -0.113955, -0.012930 and -0.044124. All five task means declined, but four of fifteen task-seed endpoints improved: zaleplon seed 0 (+0.031351), decoration hopping seed 1 (+0.003856), sitagliptin seed 1 (+0.008015) and median similarity seed 2 (+0.006814). The other eleven declined. Seed-macro population deviation fell from 0.026593 to 0.019563. Every formal session completed with its full oracle budget and no fallback.

Nonuniform weighting has positive conditional value even when the set of eligible parents is held fixed. This separates the weight question from the earlier uniform-live control, which also admitted previously unsupported survivors. It does not identify support-only value or the value of the whole graph-evolution foundation, and the two shared-baseline controls cannot be subtracted into independent component effects.

The extra local wins used a weaker reference. Strict best-parent beats rose from 629 to 936, and distinct offspring later reused rose from 2,401 to 2,521. Yet mean best-generating-parent score fell from 0.470456 to 0.383214 and mean offspring score from 0.385256 to 0.321688; sequential incumbent gains fell from 258 to 238 and their average size also fell. Broader use therefore did not preserve absolute search quality. Founder ancestry, chemical core coverage and later use are distinct descriptions, and none establishes the causal route to the score loss.

The molecular assessment finds more generic core identities on four tasks but fewer on median similarity, alongside recognizable aromatic/carbonyl and amine chemistry. Useful-looking structural variety still includes reactive local bonds, demanding bridges and unresolved stereochemistry, with conventional-bond and less-bridged counterexamples. The high-scoring Parent decoration-hopping arrangement was not recovered in the most affected seed. These observations narrow plausible explanations but do not show that a specific chemical defect caused the loss or that a universal chemical restriction would help. The registered weight-only question is answered for this composition, budget and three-seed panel; support-only effects, chemical mediation and broader foundation value remain open.

nodes.hypothesis: Rank each selected transition's changed motifs first by absolute occurrence-count change divided by the larger of its before and after counts, then by the Parent's existing rank, so the unchanged bounded sign-balanced inverse installation prioritizes complete motif turnover over partial changes to recurring motifs.
nodes.finding:
The new ranking changed the retained key set at 104 of 435 installations and replaced 114 attributes. On those same recorded transitions, mean selected occurrence turnover rose from 0.931289 under the old ranking to 0.965876, without reducing it at any installation or changing the number of slots assigned to either sign. Partly changed motifs occupied 110 of 1,707 slots, down from 221 under the old ranking. Separate memory histories on the recorded candidate stream yielded 28 newly admitted evaluated molecules and four new vetoes. Three vetoes caused evaluated replacements; one occurred beyond the alternative batch cutoff. This establishes changes to 26 complete scored batches. The recorded stream resolves all ten alternative legacy members in three of those batches; the other 23 alternatives remain incomplete. Among the 31 affected evaluated molecules, seven improved their source, one tied and 23 worsened it; six became next states and three immediately improved the archive. The complete three-seed macro mean fell from 0.521759 to 0.519304, a paired change of -0.002456 against the required +0.002. One seed improved and two declined. Mean DRD2 performance increased by 0.034439, while sitagliptin decreased by 0.048248.

This rules out absent exposure, mere reordering and failure to change evaluated allocation as explanations for the missed score target. More complete turnover demonstrably changes which local attributes receive memory and which fresh molecules are tested. It also changes admissibility in both directions, so it is not a general relaxation of tabu. The full stream produced slightly more source improvements and archive improvements than the Parent, but their average positive gains were smaller; those event counts did not translate into better final search. The largest loss is not explained by rejecting the best immediate neighbor at the first divergence: in the affected sitagliptin seed, both runs chose the same next molecule after replacing a losing proposal, and their later histories separated. Nine of eleven first batch divergences similarly preserved the next state. Later archive gains are therefore evidence of actual descendants, not isolated causal rewards for particular retained motifs or missing alternatives. Turnover measures how much of a motif multiset changed, without identifying a physical edit site. The molecular assessment still finds reactive heteroatom bonds and dense sulfur cages alongside more conventional aromatic families; the improved memory proxy has not established better chemical plausibility. The unresolved question is which local environments deserve exclusion for useful search, rather than whether fractional ranking can redirect it.

nodes.hypothesis: Restart-local accepted-context conditioning. Only when the existing controller naturally restarts a region, retain the unchanged selected root plus the nine nearest distinct records already accepted in this Objective Session, ordered by descending inherited count-Morgan generalized Tanimoto to that root and then ascending accepted serial. Freeze this auxiliary context for the whole episode. Fit the unchanged local GP on the canonical-identity union of that context and the current episode-owned records. The context provides local score variation and changes conditional means/covariance before the raw-unit Thompson auction; the shared accepted-archive amplitude law is unchanged. Borrowed membership conveys no ownership, donor access, new feedback, center update or progress-counter credit.
nodes.finding:
The conditioning and decision mechanism is confirmed on the observed executions. All 13 natural restarts used the root plus nine previously accepted neighbors; first-fit training rose from one owned label to ten predictor labels, and all 13 first fields became nonconstant. The context stayed fixed, with no detected ownership, donor or controller contamination. Across 64 post-reset fields, exact posterior and sample reconstruction passed the registered tolerance; 54 of 60 exposed auctions changed the purchased set. On 129 actual first-reset labels, RMSE fell from 0.317030 with the owned-only replay to 0.294915 with context, and MAE fell from 0.211978 to 0.189050. Across all 597 post-reset labels, RMSE fell from 0.257217 to 0.254237. For complete seeds 0 and 2, post-reset global gain was 0.099398 over 597 evaluations, or 0.000166496 per evaluation, versus the matched Parent’s 0.054802 over 599, or 0.000091490. The available macro mean was 0.581637577 with population SD 0.011614516; its matched improvement was 0.004459570, comprising essentially no change in seed 0 and +0.008919195 in seed 2. Four task/seed endpoints improved, one declined and five tied. Seed-2 sitagliptin supplied 88.9% of positive endpoint gains. Both complete seed macros remained below the formal Anchor, with a matched mean deficit of 0.036290989. Seed 1 ended with Slurm time-limit cancellation, exit 143, after only ten recorded optimizer evaluations in zaleplon and before any observed restart. Its remaining tasks and all five final endpoints are unavailable. This technical interruption does not refute the executed mechanism, but the complete-panel +0.002 test, full-panel useful-context falsifier and formal task-safety result remain unevaluable.

Nearby accepted observations really can restore predictive variation at a restart without giving borrowed labels control over the search. This settles the registered information-loss intervention at the execution and direct-behavior layers; it does not settle reliable three-seed benefit or rehabilitate the earlier full-controller conversion hypothesis. The literature-derived local-conditioning element operated, but this fixed molecular nearest-neighbor subset did not implement the source paper’s sequential design criteria or establish that geometric neighbors are the best subset. Better prediction error is only a partial explanation of search usefulness. On the 48 batches where both rank correlations were defined, average selected-label correlation was 0.409289 with context versus 0.406474 without it; 20 batches improved, 25 worsened and three tied. Only eight of 597 post-reset evaluations increased the global best, and one first-reset sitagliptin purchase supplied 62.1% of all post-reset gain. That molecule was also selected by the owned-only replay at the same Child state. The changed choices therefore establish a decision effect, while the passive replay cannot assign unbought outcomes or establish which earlier changes produced the later score advantage. The complete-panel causal contribution remains open. The molecular evidence also limits the method diagnosis. Formal scaffold variety coexists with repeated local chemical families: the median task generated 393 typed scaffolds in the two complete seeds, yet its strongest values remained in closely related nitrogen-rich dicarbonyl/amine structures. Conventional amine chemistry is reachable, but the other high-scoring series frequently retain N-halogen bonds, and both very small fragments and oversized recombinations remain. Restart memory alone does not supply coherent alternative functional-group arrangements. A context-selection or surrogate method that improves ranking would address the predictive limitation; a proposal operator that makes coherent scaffold and linker substitutions would address the chemical limitation. The present evidence identifies those distinct capabilities, not a demonstrated score benefit from either. The unchanged no-reset streams also bound applicability: this mechanism cannot affect a session before a natural restart.

nodes.hypothesis: Reject a complete, RDKit-valid, canonically novel policy draw before emission when it contains a neutral divalent C-O-C linkage whose adjacent neutral tetrahedral carbon has a single bond to terminal neutral Cl, Br or I; continue the inherited bounded direct-policy refill with all learning and token sampling unchanged.
nodes.finding:
Across 435 completed batches, the raw policy stream contained four molecules with the specified oxygen-adjacent saturated carbon–heavy-halogen attachment. Two arrived after the batch was full and were discarded anyway. The other two—a chloromethyl ether and a cyclic oxygen-adjacent carbon bearing fluorine and bromine—were actively withheld and replaced by nonmatching samples from the same draw stream. No targeted form reached any of the 4,350 optimizer evaluations, compared with five matching appearances in the parent. Both replacements entered the next training update with their original sampled strings and real accepted scores.

All fifteen task sessions finished. Mean final Top-1 remained 0.522705, with population seed deviation 0.020072; the paired change was exactly zero in each seed and task. Mean recorded AUC remained 0.405593, and every recorded best-so-far trace was unchanged. This meets the registered 0.002 endpoint non-inferiority allowance on the complete panel. Thirteen sessions reproduced the parent's entire molecular records; the affected sessions retained identical prefixes through evaluations 248 and 286 before diverging.

Both active batches filled without another sampling call. Overall raw generation stayed at 35,568 draws, including 32,647 valid strings; extra calls remained 23 across sixteen batches. Duplicates rose by seven, so exclusion did not improve raw generation quality. Measured batch-generation time totaled 32.164 seconds versus 24.745 for the parent, including 6.324 seconds in the structural predicate and 0.471 seconds in recorded receipt regions. These measurements describe the runs, rather than isolating a causal overhead.

The evidence distinguishes direct admission changes from later search changes. Only two molecules were directly rejected; the other three matching parent appearances disappeared after accepted feedback and learning changed. Positive raw draws and the two same-stream replacements show that exclusion was exercised, while exact no-action sessions and pre-rejection prefixes locate the intervention at admission. This narrows the earlier attachment question: a carbon-bound halogen can still require a specific oxygen/carbon neighborhood test, while ordinary aryl halides, carbon-fluorine bonds and oxygen linkages continue to be admitted.

Preserved scores have a limited but clear explanation. Both interventions were late, the removed parent examples had not improved their incumbents, and neither replacement nor any of the 48 identities appearing only in the child's affected sessions produced a new incumbent. The test establishes delivery of the specified chemistry without losing observed progress. It does not establish a reward gain or show that earlier, more frequent exclusions would be equally inexpensive. Iodine and haloalkyl-ester contexts had no observed opportunities.

The molecular assessment still describes ring-rich medicinal scaffolds with unresolved size, linker and reactive-form variation, and 843 generated appearances with unassigned perceived tetrahedral centres. Eliminating this attachment leaves those gaps open. The useful next question is whether precise form control can preserve incumbent progress when opportunities occur more often. Reduced raw motif prevalence, greater stability and practical synthesis remain separate claims requiring their own evidence.

nodes.hypothesis: Center accepted trajectory-balance policy coefficients within each replay minibatch while routing the detached common residual exclusively to the learned normalizer, preserving score-ranked replay and the original categorical prior penalty.
nodes.finding:
All 7,200 replay updates used the intended centered policy credit. Independent differentiation verified that the common term had no policy gradient and that the normalizer retained its original direct derivative. The change reversed 99,068 of 230,400 policy-credit signs while preserving pairwise differences and the scalar loss value within numerical precision. Nevertheless, the common mismatch became much larger in the resulting histories: its mean squared contribution was 44.130, compared with 4.418 in the parent, accounting for 62.59% rather than 14.95% of trajectory-balance loss.

Raw valid novel yield fell from 7,991/12,000 draws (66.59%) to 6,861/12,280 (55.87%). The first adapted policy batches improved in validity, but later yield fell from 64.00% to 51.82%. Mean accepted policy-origin score fell from 0.204941 to 0.172874, and later emitted molecules matching previously trained graph scaffolds fell from 53 to 15. The three-seed mean final score fell from 0.550198 to 0.542654, a decrease of 0.007543; paired changes were -0.009239, -0.029845 and +0.016454. All fifteen task replicas completed their 300 evaluations.

The common policy-credit component was not merely an expendable normalization error in this setting. Removing it left the scalar objective unchanged at a given state, yet shifted much more unresolved error onto the normalizer and weakened later transfer of graph feedback into neural proposals. This happened while graph-origin replay share increased from 73.54% to 75.43%, so dilution of graph records is not the explanation. Greater emitted scaffold variety and the disappearance of duplicate raw draws also failed to compensate for lower valid yield and policy-origin scores.

The early-versus-late reversal narrows the problem to continuing accepted-score adaptation rather than a different prepared prior: the checkpoint identities and preparation were unchanged. Preserving the direct normalizer derivative was insufficient to preserve its trajectory, because the policy state and shared clipping changed. The improved sitagliptin endpoint must also be read alongside the molecular assessment, which found prominent peroxide-linked, stereochemically undefined structures; broader graph coverage does not establish better chemical quality. Mechanism execution is confirmed, while the registered search-advantage condition is unsupported. The remaining question is how to control common and relative learning jointly without discarding the useful molecular transfer observed in the parent.

nodes.hypothesis: Replace independent first-parent requests within each suggestion by uniformly permuted systematic blocks of length equal to the inherited fresh-pool target, preserving the exact inherited prospective categorical rank probabilities and positive support while leaving every second-parent request on the original quantile law.
nodes.finding:
The scheduler preserved the original prospective rank preference and balanced all 870 preallocated blocks. It consumed 75,411 of 139,200 records; the other 63,789 were unused. Each suggestion actually used every supported first parent, raising mean distinct first-parent coverage from 24.32 to 29.00. More accepted offspring beat their generating parents (720 versus 629), and more accepted records were later used for breeding (2,636 versus 2,401). Yet average offspring score fell from 0.385256 to 0.352623, and the average positive incumbent increment fell from 0.022510 to 0.018417. All fifteen task/seed runs completed on each side. Macro mean fell from 0.595670 to 0.553508, a paired change of -0.042161 against the required +0.002 gain. Every seed macro declined; eleven task/seed endpoints declined and four improved. The improved cells were zaleplon seeds 0 and 2 and median-2 seeds 1 and 2. Macro dispersion also decreased, from 0.026593 to 0.018224, without meeting the performance prediction.

Balanced prospective allocations transmitted into real accepted descendants and more complete breeder coverage. That exposure makes this a useful negative result: coverage and local parent-win counts are insufficient evidence of endpoint benefit for this fixed scheduler. The Child’s generating parents had lower absolute scores, so its extra local wins were measured against weaker references; more incumbent advances also came in smaller steps. The largest losses involved decoration hopping and sitagliptin, while median-2 and zaleplon task means improved. The chemistry assessment found substantial formal scaffold variety and useful aromatic, amine and carbonyl arrangements, alongside reactive bonds, strained closures and unspecified stereochemistry. Plausible alternative leading families remain limited even where graph counts are broad. Those descriptions do not establish which chemical feature caused the score loss. The fixed scheduling approach has a complete adverse result under this profile. The respective roles of changed parent sequences and their associated graph-RNG paths in producing those losses remain unresolved, as does contribution of the broader graph-evolution foundation.

nodes.hypothesis: Give the existing stall regime a success-counter exit. The entry rule is untouched: one integer counter of consecutive announced batches whose accepted members fail to raise the session best-so-far held when that batch was announced, and the regime is entered when it reaches K=3. Once entered, the regime now latches and governs every following announced batch - each of them ranks the Parent's 640-member fresh offspring field instead of 160 - until this session has produced tau_succ=2 consecutive improving announced batches, at which point the Parent's inherited 160-member behaviour is restored exactly and both the non-improving counter and the in-regime success counter reset to zero. A single improving announced batch no longer ends the regime; it only advances the success counter, and one non-improving batch sets that counter back to zero. One tau_succ is bound before evaluation: no mid-run adaptation, no per-task value, no sweep. The width stays at the Parent's bound 64 per announced member, the threshold stays at 3, both counters are read only from this session's own accepted scores, the bookkeeping consumes no random numbers and changes no other law, so every session reproduces the Parent exactly until the first announced batch the Parent would have un-widened and the two sessions that never reach K=3 reproduce it completely.
nodes.finding:
The new exit rule ran exactly as designed. Across the 15 task/seed sessions, 169 of 435 announced batches screened a 640-member offspring field instead of 160, up from the Parent's 86 and close to the 163 projected; 76 of them were batches the old rule would already have released. Every one of the 13 episodes that ended did so only after two improving batches in a row, the logged counters matched an independent recount in all 435 batches, nothing changed before the first held batch, and the two deco_hop sessions that never stall reproduced the Parent molecule for molecule. The target task received the most new exposure: median_2 spent 30 of its 87 batches in the wide state, against 7 in the Parent. The extra candidates did compete: in the held batches 75 percent of the picks came from beyond the first 160 positions, which is what interchangeable candidates would give.

The payoff did not follow. The held batches were the least productive batches of the run: they raised the session best 30 percent of the time and added about 0.003 per batch, against 53 percent and 0.019 for ordinary batches. Over the whole wide state the share of batches that raised the best stayed exactly at the Parent's level (0.314 against 0.314), offspring beat their best parent less often (9.3 against 12.4 percent), and when each session's first held episode is compared with the Parent over the same batches from the same starting state, the total gain is the same (0.710 against 0.711; the Child ahead in 6 sessions, behind in 6). Requiring two improvements in a row made the wide state nearly permanent where improvements are rare: 10 of the 23 episodes were still held when the session ended, and they contain 119 of the 169 wide batches; two zaleplon sessions stayed wide from batch 4 and batch 8 to the end. Non-oracle run time rose from 41 to 57 seconds per task on average but stayed under 2 percent of the task limit.

Scores: the three-seed mean fell from 0.6011 to 0.5965, a paired change of -0.0047 (seeds -0.0144, -0.0044, +0.0049; 5 task cells up, 7 down, 3 unchanged). median_2 fell from 0.2312 to 0.2277 (seeds -0.012, -0.012, +0.013). Against the Anchor the node is flat (+0.00001 where +0.002 is required), and median_2 gains +0.0049 where +0.010 is required, with seed 1 below the Anchor. The four protected tasks all stay within their margins of the Anchor: zaleplon -0.0087 of an allowed 0.02, drd2 -0.0009, deco_hop +0.0015, sitagliptin +0.0033.

Holding the wide field longer does not scale the Parent's small gain; it erased it. The Parent's +0.0047 over the Anchor becomes +0.00001 here, and on the 13 sessions that ever stall it goes from +0.0054 to zero. Either the stall-only widening never had an effect beyond path noise, or whatever value it has sits in short bursts and is diluted when the wide state is held. Either way, more exposure of this 640-member field is not a route to a better panel, and the three-success exit, which would hold it longer still, is not worth running. The route of scaling this element by exposure should stop here.

The receipts show why holding fails. With no way out except two consecutive improvements, the hold is one-way on exactly the sessions that improve rarely, so there the rule turns into the always-on wide field that was already measured to lose. The borrowed trust-region rule has a counterweight this transplant leaves out: a region that keeps failing shrinks and eventually restarts. The extra candidates were not worse choices by the model's own measure (picks in held batches sat 1.16 pool standard deviations above the field average, as in the Parent's wide batches, 1.17), but they were not better molecules. A field four times larger, bred from the same parents on a plateau, gives more of the same. The chemistry review agrees: this node is almost indistinguishable from its Parent, and median_2's leaders remain a single architecture, a quinoline joined to a bridged bis-lactam cage that the search keeps enlarging instead of changing the aromatic partner. The median_2 session held wide for 12 batches found 2 improvements where the Parent found 6 over the same stretch.

Still open: this round's law-free path reference and the parallel arm that applies the same exit rule to a different stall-time element. Neither can turn this into a gain, because -0.0047 is below the only path-noise realization measured so far (-0.0017). They will decide whether this result counts as noise or as a real loss, and whether the exposure law fails on both elements. For median_2 the evidence now points away from candidate breadth and toward changing which parents and fragments get combined.

nodes.hypothesis: On actual code Parent n-e4b751133c75, remove only off-diagonal completed-count influence on the exploration denominator and zero-started priority at deeper selections (parent_id != 0). For the exact eligible sibling set and inherited nonnegative count-Tanimoto K, keep D_i=sum_j K_ij N_j, P_i=sum_j K_ij O_j and B_i=sum_{j:N_j>0} K_ij N_j M_j. Keep V_i=B_i/D_i when D_i>0 and the inherited neutral default otherwise, even when own N_i is zero. Replace only started_i=D_i+P_i by started_i=N_i+P_i below the virtual root. The active bonus is inherited beta*sqrt(2*log(max(2,N_parent+O_parent))/started_i) when started_i>0; otherwise bonus/index remain null and unvisited priority is true. Retain the exact lexicographic winner (unvisited_priority, index-or-zero, -occurrence_id). Root selections keep D_i+P_i. Since D_i>=N_i on this nonnegative diagonal-one kernel, the deeper bonus cannot decrease where both denominators are positive; previously unstarted own branches may regain priority when N_i=P_i=0 despite D_i>0. The hypothesis is that this separation changes deeper choices and their actual purchased descendants without changing shared peak valuation or pending discouragement. It addresses the frozen question of completed-density contribution with those other consumers retained. The working score prediction is non-inferiority, not an established benefit: the exposure audit has no unpurchased outcomes.
nodes.finding:
The isolated removal ran as registered. It changed 2,198 of 4,310 deeper decisions and reached 1,964 of 4,350 accepted optimizer purchases across all 15 task/seed cells; shared value, pending credit, virtual-root choices and fresh-incumbent restarts reconstructed without discrepancies. Mean final score fell from 0.499496 to 0.484258, a paired change of -0.015238. Eleven of fifteen endpoints improved, but all three seed means declined (-0.000409, -0.042194 and -0.003112): the three sitagliptin losses outweighed gains elsewhere. The registered non-inferiority expectation therefore failed, and the isolated, exposed removal meets the criterion for positive conditional contribution of the retained completed-density consumer. Full incumbent gain fell from 4.365063 to 4.136487 over 4,350 purchases, despite 162 rather than 148 strict improvements. Late gain increased from 1.367463 to 1.758650 over 2,175 purchases, with 59 rather than 42 improvements. The formal Anchor remains ahead by 0.122772, so its separate +0.002 target is unmet. All sessions completed without technical failure.

Borrowed completed support was not simply redundant with shared peak values or pending support in this configuration: removing its exploration influence reached real purchases and reduced the complete paired endpoint mean. This answers the registered conditional consumer question; it does not price all sharing, isolate an interaction, establish an additive decomposition, or overturn the Parent's fresh-root result. Activation is confirmed while the score expectation is contradicted. The result is limited to this adaptive Search panel and does not establish reliable generalization or end the broader approach.

The method still concentrates late search around related structures. Fragment-excluded within-cell similarity increased from 0.2238 over the full Child stream to 0.2945 late, compared with the Parent's 0.1923 and 0.2421, and 2,116 of 2,175 late Child purchases added no incumbent gain. Broad scaffold production and fewer size extremes did not secure the endpoint: below-six and above-fifty heavy-atom purchases fell from 425/301 to 281/244 overall, yet the largest task losses remained. The Molecular report identifies local substitution plateaus, reactive linkages and unspecified stereochemistry rather than a uniquely missing target scaffold. These observations support a limitation in local graph-edit proposal quality and sustained exploration of distinct structural basins. A topology-changing proposal operator that preserves useful functional-group arrangements, or a search scheme that maintains alternative scaffold basins, could address that type of limitation; neither is tested here, and these associations do not explain the removal loss by causal mediation.

Late improvement and reduced internal failed routing are real descriptive changes, but they do not compensate for the lower final mean. Measured wall time was 321.32 seconds versus 663.81, while oracle time alone was 185.10 versus 500.05; the data cannot assign that difference to selection efficiency. Complete selection/proposal/diagnostic timing, empirical RNG-state equality and trusted task-safety margins remain unmeasured. The inherited chemistry prose overstates the Parent late fragment count: the underlying receipts establish 195, making the Child's reduction to 113 an 82-purchase difference; this correction leaves the mechanism and contribution conclusions unchanged.

nodes.hypothesis: Reject an otherwise valid canonically novel close_ring neighbor before tabu testing unless its source shortest path overlaps the existing ring graph in zero atoms, one atom, or exactly one existing ring edge, thereby redirecting new-cycle proposals away from extended or separated ring overlap while retaining the Parent's edit sampling and accepted-score walk.
nodes.finding:
The gate rejected 275 valid, fresh ring-closure attempts. Independent reconstruction of the current tabu table shows that 257 of these would otherwise have been admitted; each was replaced by a different neighbor from the same scored source before feedback. Emitted closures with extended or separated overlap fell from 241 to zero. Ring growth remained active through 40 permitted closures: six paths outside existing rings, three with a single old ring atom and 31 sharing one old ring edge. Nine permitted closures beat their source score and seven improved the best archive.

The overall molecules also lost much of the targeted complexity. Among 4,350 emitted neighbors, the number with a pair of RDKit-perceived rings sharing at least three atoms fell from 1,867 to 10, while mean ring-atom participation changed only from 62.89% to 61.70%. This preserved substantial ring content while removing most extensive ring overlap. All batches completed, requiring 12.83 attempts per ten submitted molecules versus 12.15 for the parent. The complete three-seed mean fell from 0.520918 to 0.517522, a paired change of -0.003396 that exceeds the allowed 0.002 loss. Seed changes were +0.004044, -0.024305 and +0.010073. DRD2 improved on average; the other four task means declined.

The experiment establishes that a narrow source-path rule can strongly control ring-junction growth without disabling all closures or disturbing identity, memory and feedback. Most evaluated rings remain, and the admitted closure repertoire still produces improvements. The score cost is nevertheless real on this panel: the parent had 37 source-improving and 19 selected closures in the now-excluded class. Those historical observations explain why score retention required a test, but they do not provide scores for the newly rejected structures or identify which missing transition caused a later loss.

The chemical assessment shows what the topology restriction leaves unresolved. Less elaborate ring cages still contain unusual sulfur coordination, reactive heteroatom-halogen bonds and unspecified configurations. The permitted classes do not establish accessible three-dimensional geometry or synthetic plausibility, and the rule neither removes complexity already present in a source nor constrains other edit types. The campaign now has evidence that extensive ring overlap can be suppressed selectively, alongside evidence that this degree of suppression did not retain the registered mean-score margin. Ring topology and local chemical bonding remain separate limitations.

nodes.hypothesis: Select oracle-bound offspring by maximizing independent joint posterior function draws from a task-local fingerprint Gaussian process over a fresh pool generated by the Parent's unchanged graph evolution operators.
nodes.finding:
The two additional runs reproduce posterior selection and feedback. All 2,900 selected offspring maximize their reconstructed correlated function draws, uncertainty changes 2,693 choices (92.86%) compared with choosing the highest posterior mean, and all 2,800 eligible predictions on the same molecules change after accepted feedback. All 290 fits use only earlier accepted observations. Mean final-best score across the five objectives is 0.558863 in the first additional run and 0.526723 in the second, compared with 0.547535 in the original run of this selector. Across all three seeds, mean score is 0.544374 with population standard deviation 0.013310. The intended offspring-efficiency improvement does not appear: only 371 of 2,900 new offspring beat their best generating parent (12.79%), and their mean child-minus-parent score is -0.100465. The original direct-submission Parent's single-seed references are 13.86% and -0.084154. Across all three selector runs, 565 of 4,350 offspring beat their best parent (12.99%). The original paired screening-score gain of 0.055880 remains a one-seed comparison because matched additional runs of the direct-submission Parent are unavailable.

The experiment now separates reliable selector execution from the hoped-for improvement in offspring yield. The new runs' posterior means contain useful predictive information on the selected molecules: pooled prediction MSE is 0.017182 versus 0.036613 for the same-fit archive mean, with average within-batch rank correlation 0.412. Yet this information and widespread uncertainty-driven choice do not produce a higher parent-beating fraction. The remaining question is how to turn predictive information into more productive evaluations relative to already strong parents. Prediction quality is also uneven: on sitagliptin_mpo it is worse than the archive-mean predictor in two of three seeds, and that objective has the largest final-score variation. The chemistry assessment shows ample aromatic amides, cyclic amines and carbonyl-containing rings, alongside reactive substitutions and destructive edits; access to recognizable molecular families is established, while reliable discrimination among useful, chemically credible alternatives remains open. The unused pool members have no scores, so these runs cannot identify which rejected alternatives would have been better. Matched Parent replicas and same-pool comparisons with mean-only and generation-order selection are needed to isolate score benefit, efficiency, and uncertainty's contribution.

nodes.hypothesis: At objective initialization, refine each identity-mismatched initial encoding by bounded gradient descent on frozen-decoder target-token margin loss, and replace its particle starting position and admit its real initial score only when unchanged deterministic decoding exactly recovers that initial canonical molecule.
nodes.finding:
Exact starting coverage increased from one to two of the ten supplied molecules. The same additional molecule was recovered in all five objective sessions after 168 latent updates: its mean target-margin loss fell from 0.168312 to 0.019830, and its checked position was installed in two particles per session. This doubled scored initial particle memories from two to four out of twenty. All ten recovered particle copies supplied actual motion sources; their memories produced 44 nonzero personal-attraction terms and 252 nonzero attractions from other particles. Eight other mismatched molecules reached the 256-step limit and retained their original positions, while the original exact match stayed unchanged. These five sessions reuse one fixed ten-molecule set and are not five independent reconstruction tests. The frozen model and exact score-position provenance remained intact. On the supplied seed, the mean final Top-1 score fell from 0.450789 to 0.347733. Zaleplon improved from 0.374833 to 0.390441 and median_2 from 0.167839 to 0.202143; deco_hop fell from 0.592706 to 0.553113, drd2_docking from 0.859171 to 0.412549, and sitagliptin from 0.259395 to 0.180421. At least one missing starting identity was already representable by the frozen decoder: correcting its coordinates recovered that identity without changing neural weights or transferring a score to a different molecule. The causal path from recovery to installation, motion and scored attraction is therefore established. That repairs a real coverage defect, but this run does not support the expectation that doubling the initially scored particles improves overall search quality. On drd2_docking and sitagliptin, both recovered personal memories were replaced after their first proposals, before they could supply a nonzero personal pull; their shared memory still influenced other particles. On deco_hop, the recovered shared attractor was referenced in 210 motions and both recovered personal memories survived to the end, yet the task score was lower. The amount of attractor reuse alone is therefore insufficient evidence of useful search guidance. All nine optimization attempts lowered their best visited mean loss, but only one recovered its molecule, so the token-margin proxy cannot replace the production identity check. The eight failures do not establish that those molecules lack an inverse: the bounded local optimizer may simply have failed to find one. Mean decoded fingerprint distance from the source remained large, increasing from 0.854 to 0.864. The molecular assessment likewise finds abundant rings alongside long unsaturated chains, labile polar linkers and irregular ring arrangements. Exact initialization does not control those downstream structural changes. Broader inversion coverage and the usefulness of moves around a recovered position remain separate open questions; this single seed establishes activation and an observed score loss, without establishing a reproducible score effect.
